huichang: 845 CE, Chang'an: outside a great Buddhist monastery with a wooden pagoda, officials in robes and caps supervise workers lowering bronze Buddha statues and bells onto carts to be melted for coin, while long lines of monks and nuns in grey robes walk out of the gate carrying small bundles. Autumn trees, quiet dusty street, tiled roofs. Painted in late Tang court painting style, ink and muted mineral colours on silk, many small figures.
zhang-yichao: 848 CE, Dunhuang: a grand procession of mounted soldiers with banners, drummers and musicians escorts a commander on a white horse across the desert toward the oasis city gates, while Tibetan garrison troops withdraw into the distance; poplars, sand dunes and the Mogao cliff on the horizon. Bright desert morning. Painted in the style of the Zhang Yichao procession mural in Mogao Cave 156, mineral greens, reds and ochre on plaster, rhythmic rows of horsemen.
diamond-sutra: 868 CE, a printing workshop near Dunhuang: an artisan carves a large pear-wood block while another inks it and lifts a sheet of paper printed with a frontispiece picture of the Buddha preaching to monks under a canopy; finished panels are glued into a long scroll, characters too small to be legible. Oil lamp light, brushes and ink pots. Painted in late Tang Dunhuang mural style, warm ochre and mineral blue, softly worn surface.
huang-chao: 875 CE, Caozhou in Shandong: on the flat drought-stricken plain, a crowd of ragged peasants with hoes, staves and banners gathers around salt smugglers' carts piled with sacks, a leader on horseback addressing them from a dike; cracked fields, withered trees and a distant walled county town under a dusty yellow sky. Painted in late Tang style ink and light colour on silk, loose expressive brushwork, many small figures.
guangzhou-sack: 879 CE, Guangzhou on the Pearl River: seen from across the water, columns of smoke rise over the walled southern port, while ocean-going ships with matting sails and Arab dhows crowd the harbour and some flee downriver; rebel soldiers swarm along the riverbank and city gates, warehouses and banyan trees beyond. Humid, hazy afternoon. Painted as a late Tang ink-and-colour handscroll on silk, mineral greens, figures small and distant.
huang-chao-changan: 880 CE, Chang'an in winter: a huge rebel army in mixed armour and plain clothes enters the main gate of the Tang capital under banners, as officials in court robes kneel along the avenue to greet it; in the far distance a small imperial party on horseback hurries through snowy hills toward the mountain roads to Sichuan. Grey sky, empty wards. Painted in late Tang court style, ink and mineral colours on silk, panoramic composition.
end-of-tang: 907 CE, Bianzhou (Kaifeng): in a great hall of a palace, ranks of officials in purple and red robes and black caps stand in rows as Tang court officers present the imperial seals and regalia on lacquered trays to a powerful warlord seated small and distant on a dais; armed guards line the hall, red pillars, bronze incense burners. Dim formal light. Painted in Five Dynasties court figure-painting style, as in The Night Revels of Han Xizai, fine line and rich colour on silk.
abaoji: 916 CE, the Khitan heartland near Shangjing (Linhuang): on a broad grassland by a river, Khitan nobles with shaved crowns and side locks, wearing left-closing robes and boots, gather before a great felt tent with banners and tall drums for an enthronement ceremony; horsemen, ox carts with felt covers, herds of horses and a white horse and grey ox for sacrifice. Wide sky, late summer. Painted in the style of Hu Gui's Khitan horsemen paintings, ink and colour on silk, fine detailed figures.
later-tang: 923 CE, Bianzhou (Kaifeng): Shatuo Turkic cavalry in lamellar armour with bows and lances ride in a long column through the gate of the walled city on the Bian canal, banners streaming, while townspeople watch from tiled houses and boats on the canal; the old palace roofs in the distance. Autumn, clear light. Painted in Five Dynasties style like Hu Gui's horsemen, fine ink line with light colour on silk, energetic horses.
shu-conquered: 925 CE, Sichuan: a Later Tang army in armour winds along cliffside plank roads through the dramatic Jianmen Pass, then descends toward the green Chengdu Plain where the walled city of Chengdu stands among rice paddies and rivers; officials come out of the gate with offerings to surrender. Misty mountains, early winter. Painted as a monumental Five Dynasties landscape in the manner of Jing Hao and Guan Tong, ink on silk with light colour, tiny figures.
balhae-falls: 926 CE, Sanggyeong (near Ning'an, Heilongjiang): Khitan cavalry with shaved crowns and side locks surround the stone-founded walls and palace halls of the Balhae capital in a forested river valley, smoke rising from the gates, while a long line of Balhae officials in robes comes out to submit. Snow on the hills, cold winter light, wide northern landscape. Painted in the style of Hu Gui's Khitan scenes, ink and light colour on silk.
later-shu: 934 CE, Chengdu: a calm, prosperous court scene in a palace garden on the Chengdu Plain, a new ruler seated small on a dais among officials in robes; around the palace walls lie rice fields, brocade workshops with silk drying on frames, river boats and green hills. Spring sunshine, peaceful mood. Painted in Five Dynasties court style of the Shu painters such as Huang Quan, fine line, bright colours on silk, flowering trees.
sixteen-prefectures: 936 CE, near Youzhou (modern Beijing): in a Khitan felt-tent camp below the mountain passes of the north, envoys in Chinese court robes bow and present bundled maps and registers on trays to Khitan nobles with shaved crowns and side locks, while Khitan horsemen stand in ranks and carts of tribute silk wait nearby. Rugged Yanshan ridges and walled towns in the distance, autumn. Painted in Five Dynasties ink and colour on silk in the manner of Hu Gui.
southern-tang: 937 CE, Jinling (Nanjing): a palace of the new Southern Tang beside the Qinhuai River, with the Purple Mountain behind and the broad Yangtze in the distance; courtiers in elegant robes gather in a hall with painted screens and musicians, while boats glide on the river below. Soft spring evening light. Painted in the refined style of Southern Tang court painting like The Night Revels of Han Xizai, fine line, rich mineral colours on silk.
bach-dang: 938 CE, the Bạch Đằng River estuary in northern Vietnam: at low tide, rows of iron-tipped wooden stakes emerge from the muddy river, and a fleet of Southern Han warships with matting sails is caught and tilted among them, while small Vietnamese boats close in from mangrove banks under limestone hills. Grey morning mist, distant. Painted in a traditional ink and light colour handscroll style on silk, loose wet brushwork, small boats and figures.
min-divided: 945 CE, Fuzhou in Min: the walled city between its three hills and the White Pagoda, the Min River and its boats below, with armies of Southern Tang soldiers in lamellar armour approaching from the western mountains and a Wuyue fleet arriving by sea; smoke rising over a city worn by civil war. Subtropical green hills, cloudy sky. Painted in Five Dynasties monumental landscape style, ink and light colour on silk, tiny figures.
liao-takes-kaifeng: Early 947 CE, Bianzhou (Kaifeng): Khitan horsemen with shaved crowns and side locks, fur-lined robes and bows ride through the wide snowy streets of the walled capital toward the palace, while officials of the defeated Later Jin kneel along the road in robes; camel carts with felt covers follow. Cold winter light, bare willows along the canal. Painted in Hu Gui's Khitan style, ink and colour on silk, fine detailed horses.
later-han: 947 CE, Taiyuan (Jinyang): the walled city on the Fen River below the Lüliang mountains; inside the gate, Shatuo Turkic troops in lamellar armour and Chinese officials in robes stand in ranks as their governor is acclaimed before a hall, banners and drums raised. Spring, loess terraces and willows beyond the walls. Painted as a Northern-style Five Dynasties landscape in the manner of Guan Tong, ink and colour on silk, small figures.
later-zhou: 951 CE, Bianzhou (Kaifeng): a column of soldiers escorts a mounted general through the city gate, one soldier having draped a torn yellow banner over his shoulders like a robe, while officials in court dress await him at the palace gate; canal boats and tiled roofs line the Bian River. Winter morning, pale light. Painted in Five Dynasties court style, fine ink line with light colour on silk, many small figures.
chu-falls: 951 CE, Changsha on the Xiang River: Southern Tang war boats with sails and oars come up the river toward the walled city of Chu, while soldiers march along the bank below Yuelu Mountain; smoke rises from a palace district damaged by fighting between rival princes. Lush green hills, humid haze. Painted in the manner of Southern Tang river landscapes like Zhao Gan's Along the River, ink and light colour on silk.
gaoping: 954 CE, Gaoping in southern Shanxi: on a valley floor among loess hills, the Later Zhou army in lamellar armour charges under red banners, a young ruler on horseback leading the guard at the front; the opposing Northern Han infantry and Khitan cavalry with shaved crowns waver and break in the dust. Seen from a hillside at a distance, spring. Painted as a Northern Song style battle handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, many small horsemen.
huainan-campaign: 956 CE, Shouzhou (Shouxian) on the Huai River: the Later Zhou army besieges the strong walled city, siege towers and battering rams at the gates, war boats blocking the river, camps and banners covering the plain; defenders on the walls with bows. Rain clouds, flooded fields, spring. Painted as a Five Dynasties monumental landscape in the manner of Guan Tong, ink and colour on silk, small figures in a broad scene.
chenqiao: 960 CE, Chenqiao post station north of Kaifeng: at dawn in a camp of tents and horses, armoured soldiers crowd around their general in front of the station gate and drape a yellow robe over his shoulders, officers kneeling, banners raised, frosty fields and bare willows beyond. Figures small, seen from a distance. Painted in early Northern Song figure-painting style, ink and light colour on silk, fine line, crisp winter light.
gaoliang: 979 CE, by the Gaoliang River outside Youzhou (Beijing): a Song army retreats in disorder across marshy plains as Khitan Liao cavalry with shaved crowns and side locks sweep in from both flanks, dust and smoke rising; the walled city of Youzhou and the Western Hills in the distance. Late summer evening, dramatic sky. Painted as a Northern Song battle handscroll in ink and light colour on silk, figures tiny within the landscape.
chanyuan: 1005 CE, Chanzhou (Puyang) on the Yellow River: Song and Liao envoys in contrasting robes meet beneath a pavilion between two armies encamped on either side of the river, while carts loaded with bolts of silk and silver ingots wait nearby; the Song emperor stands small on the city wall under a yellow canopy. Winter, ice on the river, pale sun. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
xixia: 1038 CE, Xingqing (Yinchuan): beneath the rugged Helan Mountains, the walled Tangut capital with its palace and white brick pagodas; Tangut nobles with shaved crowns and fringe hairstyles, in narrow-sleeved robes, assemble in a palace courtyard for a coronation, horsemen and camels outside the walls, the Yellow River and irrigated fields nearby. Clear autumn light. Painted in the style of Western Xia murals at the Yulin caves, mineral greens and earth reds on plaster.
movable-type: 1041 CE, a printer's workshop in Hangzhou: a commoner in a plain robe sets small fired-clay type pieces into an iron frame on a heated iron plate coated with pine resin and wax, trays of type pieces sorted in wooden cases, a second plate being inked, paper sheets drying on a line; characters are too small to read. Lattice windows, soft daylight. Painted in Northern Song genre style like the Qingming scroll, ink and light colour on silk, fine detail.
zizhi-tongjian: 1084 CE, Luoyang: in the study pavilion of a quiet scholar's garden with bamboo and a pond, an elderly scholar-official in a plain robe and cap sits at a desk surrounded by tall stacks of manuscripts and scroll boxes, assistants sorting drafts; the pages are blank or illegible. Autumn evening, lamp light through lattice windows. Painted in Northern Song literati style, ink and light colour on silk, delicate line and soft washes.
jurchen-jin: 1115 CE, Huining near the Anchuhu River in Manchuria: Jurchen warriors with shaved crowns and long braids, in fur and leather, gather on horseback in a forest clearing before a chieftain's hall of logs, raising banners and bows to acclaim their leader; birch and pine forests, a river, snow on the ground. Cold clear morning. Painted in Jin-dynasty figure-painting style like Zhang Yu's Wenji Returning to Han, ink and colour on silk, detailed horses and costume.
jingkang: 1127 CE, Kaifeng in winter: seen from a distance, a long column of Jurchen Jin cavalry escorts carts loaded with treasure, books and ritual bronzes and a line of captive courtiers north out of the city gate across a snowy plain; smoke rises over the walls and palace roofs of the fallen capital. Grey sky, falling snow. Painted as a Song-dynasty handscroll in ink and light colour on silk, tiny figures in a vast bleak landscape.
linan: 1138 CE, Lin'an (Hangzhou): West Lake surrounded by misty hills, pagodas, temples and willows on the causeways; pleasure boats on the water, and the walled city with crowded streets, shops and the palace on Phoenix Hill stretching toward the Qiantang River. Morning mist, spring. Painted in Southern Song style after Li Song's West Lake handscrolls and Ma Yuan's one-corner compositions, ink and pale colour on silk.
yue-fei: Winter 1142 CE, Lin'an (Hangzhou): a quiet, snow-covered courtyard of a government prison at night, a single lantern glowing under the eaves; inside an empty cell, a general's armour, helmet and spear lie set aside on a wooden rack, while outside the city walls West Lake and bare hills lie under snow. Solemn and still, no figures close up. Painted in Southern Song style after Ma Yuan and Xia Gui, ink washes on silk, much empty space.
caishi: 1161 CE, the Yangtze at Caishi below the Ma'anshan cliffs: Song treadle-powered paddle-wheel warships with wooden superstructures ram and scatter small Jin boats crossing the wide river, gunpowder thunderclap bombs bursting in clouds of lime smoke; Jin cavalry and tents crowd the far northern bank. Late autumn, windy sky. Painted in Southern Song style after Xia Gui, ink and light colour on silk, distant boats and figures.
genghis: 1206 CE, the source of the Onon River in Mongolia: a great assembly of Mongol chiefs and warriors on horseback surrounds a large white felt ger and a white standard of nine yak-tail banners; a small figure in fur-trimmed robe stands at the centre as nobles kneel. Rolling green steppe, river, distant mountains, herds of horses. Clear summer day. Painted in Yuan-dynasty handscroll style like Liu Guandao's Kublai Khan Hunting, ink and colour on silk.
caizhou: 1234 CE, Caizhou (Runan): the walled city under siege in winter, Mongol cavalry camps and Song army tents with banners on opposite sides, siege engines at the gates and a breach in the walls; dark smoke rises from a palace hall inside the city. Snow on the plain, grey dawn light, seen from a distance. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll in ink and light colour on silk, small figures.
liangzhou-meeting: 1247 CE, Liangzhou (Wuwei) in the Hexi Corridor: an elderly Tibetan lama in red monastic robes and a pointed scholar's hat, with young novices, is received in a large Mongol tent palace by a Mongol prince and his court in fur-trimmed robes; Buddhist offerings and silk hangings, camels and horses outside, snowy Qilian Mountains beyond. Painted in Tibetan thangka style of the Sakya tradition, mineral pigments, gold highlights, flat figures, no inscriptions.
xuanzheng: 1264 CE, the Mongol court at Yanjing (later Dadu, Beijing): in a palace hall hung with Buddhist banners, a young Tibetan lama in red robes is honoured by Mongol officials in fur-trimmed robes and Chinese scribes, while Tibetan monks and envoys bearing scarves wait in rows; lamps, gilded Buddha images, guards at the door. Painted in a Yuan-dynasty court style blended with Tibetan thangka colouring, mineral pigments and gold on silk.
kublai: 1271 CE, Dadu (Beijing): construction of a vast new capital, labourers raising rammed-earth walls and gates on a planned grid, palace halls with glazed roofs rising beside the Taiye Lake and the island of Qionghua; Mongol officials on horseback and Chinese architects inspect the work, camel caravans and carts bring timber. Clear autumn sky, Western Hills behind. Painted in Yuan-dynasty ruled-line architectural painting style, ink and colour on silk.
xiangyang: 1273 CE, Xiangyang on the Han River: huge counterweight trebuchets built by Muslim engineers hurl stones at the walls and towers of the fortress city from across the river, while Mongol armies and boats surround it, and Fancheng on the opposite bank has already fallen; dust and smoke at the walls, seen from a distance. Winter, hazy light. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, small figures.
marco-polo: 1275 CE, Shangdu (Xanadu) on the Inner Mongolian grassland: the summer capital's walls and palace with a great tent pavilion; a small group of European travellers in Venetian tunics and caps, dusty from the road, kneel among a crowd of Mongol nobles, Tibetan monks and Persian officials before the distant throne. Horses, white mares, green steppe and blue summer sky. Painted in Yuan-dynasty court painting style like Liu Guandao, ink and colour on silk.
yamen: 1279 CE, Yamen on the coast of Guangdong: seen from a high headland, a great fleet of Song ships lashed together in the bay is broken by Yuan warships; burning sails and smoke drift over grey waves, and sea cliffs rise on both sides of the inlet. Stormy dusk, dramatic clouds, figures tiny and distant. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty ink landscape handscroll, ink washes and light colour on silk, mournful atmosphere.
japan-invasion: 1281 CE, Hakata Bay in Kyushu: a violent typhoon strikes a vast Yuan fleet of Chinese and Korean junks with matting sails at anchor near the islands; masts snap, ships collide and founder in towering waves, while samurai behind a long stone defensive wall on the shore watch from afar. Dark storm sky, rain, night falling. Painted in the style of the Japanese thirteenth-century Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba handscroll, ink and colour on paper, no inscriptions.
red-turbans: 1351 CE, the Yellow River dikes near Yingzhou: thousands of conscripted labourers with baskets, shovels and carrying poles repair a vast earthen dike, while some throw down their tools and gather around leaders wearing red headcloths, red banners raised; Yuan overseers on horseback in the distance. Muddy river, grey spring sky, flat plain. Painted in late Yuan to early Ming woodblock-print illustration style, bold black lines with light colour washes.
sam-boyaca: 1819, the stone bridge of Boyacá in the green Andean highlands of Colombia: patriot infantry in ragged blue coats and straw hats, with mounted llaneros carrying long lances, close in on a column of Spanish royalist troops in white and red uniforms at a small stone bridge over a narrow stream, gunsmoke drifting across rolling pastures and steep hills, figures small and distant, no wounded shown. Painted as an early nineteenth-century South American oil history painting, warm earth tones, wide panoramic composition, soft afternoon light.
sam-peru-independence: 1821, the Plaza Mayor of Lima: a large crowd of townspeople in cloaks, shawls and broad hats gathers before the cathedral and carved wooden balconies of colonial houses, while a small group of officers in dark blue coats with bicorne hats stands on a raised platform unfurling a new red and white flag; soldiers line the square, church bells in towers, pale grey coastal sky. Painted as a nineteenth-century Peruvian oil history painting, crowded, festive, figures seen at a distance.
sam-brazil-independence: 1822, beside the small Ipiranga stream on a hill near São Paulo: a mounted prince in a dark uniform, seen small and from a distance, raises his hat amid an escort of horsemen in blue and white dragoon uniforms who lift their swords, while ox-cart drivers and country folk watch from the roadside; red earth road, tall grass, scattered palms and araucaria trees, wide afternoon sky. Painted as a nineteenth-century academic Brazilian oil history painting, luminous colour, panoramic.
sam-guayaquil: 1822, the river port of Guayaquil in Ecuador: a whitewashed colonial house with wooden balconies on the waterfront of the broad Guayas river, sailing ships and canoes at anchor, palm trees and tropical haze; through an open doorway two officers in dark uniforms with gold epaulettes, seen from behind and small, sit at a table in private while sentries wait outside. Painted as a nineteenth-century South American watercolour, humid soft light, muted greens and ochres.
sam-ayacucho: 1824, the high plain of Quinua near Ayacucho, Peru: patriot troops in blue coats and lancers on horseback advance across a grassy Andean pampa beneath a steep mountain slope where Spanish royalist columns descend, puffs of musket smoke drifting, snow-dusted peaks and clear thin-aired sky behind; all figures small, seen from far off, no wounded. Painted as a nineteenth-century Latin American oil battle painting, panoramic, golden morning light, earthy browns and Andean blues.
sam-bolivia: 1825, the colonial town of Chuquisaca (Sucre) in Upper Peru: delegates in dark frock coats and cravats gather in a whitewashed hall with carved wooden ceilings and arched windows, standing in rows to vote, while outside red-tiled roofs, church towers and dry hills under a bright Andean sky; townspeople in ponchos and wide felt hats wait in the courtyard. Painted as a nineteenth-century Bolivian oil painting, restrained palette, soft window light, many small figures.
sam-paraguayan-war: 1864-1868, the riverside fortress of Humaitá on a bend of the Paraguay River: long earthwork batteries and a brick church overlook the wide brown river, where ironclad steam gunboats with tall funnels approach in the distance, smoke rising from the banks; Paraguayan soldiers in red shirts and white trousers man cannons among palms and marsh grass, all seen small from afar. Painted as a nineteenth-century documentary engraving coloured by hand, wide river panorama, humid hazy light.
sam-war-of-the-pacific: 1879, the desert port of Antofagasta on the Atacama coast: Chilean soldiers in blue kepis and red trousers land from rowing boats onto a stony beach, steam warships at anchor offshore, a small wooden town with nitrate warehouses and a railway pier behind, bare brown coastal mountains rising above, utterly dry under a hard blue sky. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving with light watercolour tint, many small figures, crisp desert light.
sam-lei-aurea: 1888, the square outside the imperial city palace in Rio de Janeiro: a joyful crowd of Afro-Brazilian and white townspeople in straw hats, white dresses and dark suits fills the plaza, waving hats and handkerchiefs and throwing flowers toward the palace balcony, where tiny distant figures stand; colonial facades, palm trees, Guanabara Bay and green mountains behind. Painted as a nineteenth-century Brazilian lithograph illustration with soft colour, festive, bright tropical afternoon.
sam-vargas: 1930, Rio de Janeiro: revolutionary soldiers and gaúcho horsemen from the south in broad hats and red neckerchiefs tie their horses to the obelisk on Avenida Rio Branco, a wide boulevard lined with Beaux-Arts buildings, trams and palm trees; crowds of men in white suits and boaters watch, Sugarloaf Mountain faint in the haze. Painted as a 1930s Brazilian watercolour illustration, loose brushwork, warm light, figures small and anonymous.
sam-peron: 1946, Buenos Aires: a vast crowd of workers in shirtsleeves and flat caps fills the Plaza de Mayo before the pink Casa Rosada, holding up rolled banners without lettering and Argentine sky-blue and white flags; the domed Cabildo and tall jacaranda trees in bloom, a distant tiny balcony with indistinct figures. Painted as a 1940s Latin American lithograph illustration in muted blues, pinks and greys, high viewpoint, dense crowd, soft spring light.
sam-brasilia: 1960, Brasília on the red-earth central plateau: the twin towers and the upturned and inverted white bowls of the new National Congress rise above a vast empty esplanade, ministries in a long row, wide new roads and young trees, construction workers in hats and a few cars below, big cumulus clouds over the flat cerrado horizon. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration of mid-century modernism, clean geometry, sunlit whites against ochre earth.
sam-chile-coup: 1973, Santiago, Chile: seen from a distance across a wide plaza, the neoclassical La Moneda Palace sends up dark smoke from its roof, while small military aircraft cross a grey sky and tanks wait on an empty street lined with leafless trees; the Andes faint and snow-capped behind, no people in close view. Painted as a sombre documentary watercolour, desaturated greys and ochres, restrained, quiet and neutral tone.
sam-falklands: 1982, Stanley in the Falkland Islands: a small harbour town of white houses with coloured tin roofs and a little church on a windswept slope, grey warships far out on the cold sea, helicopters low over treeless moorland and rocky ridges, soldiers in winter gear small on a distant hillside, peat smoke and low cloud. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, cold blues, greens and greys, wide South Atlantic sky.
sam-chile-plebiscite: 1988, Santiago, Chile: long orderly queues of citizens in coats, men and women of all ages, wait outside a school used as a polling station, cardboard ballot boxes on tables inside, rainbow-coloured paper decorations without writing in the streets; the snow-capped Andes rise beyond plane trees and low buildings in clear spring light. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, calm, anonymous figures seen at a distance.
sam-colombia-peace: 2016, Bogotá: a white open-air ceremony in a plaza, with rows of people dressed in white seated before a low stage under a large white canopy, white doves and white balloons rising, the green Andean ridge of Monserrate with its hilltop church above the brick city behind; all figures tiny and anonymous. Painted as a gentle documentary watercolour, soft whites and greens, hopeful morning light.
sa-kot-diji-culture: c. 2800 BCE, Kot Diji in Sindh: a fortified farming town on a low limestone ridge above the green Indus flood plain, with stone-and-mudbrick defensive walls and bastions enclosing flat-roofed mud-brick houses, women grinding grain, men driving humped zebu cattle, painted pottery jars drying in the sun, fields of barley along the river. Painted in an earthy ochre-and-red palette inspired by early Indus painted pottery and rock art, flat forms, warm sunlight.
sa-kalibangan-ploughed-field: c. 2800 BCE, Kalibangan on the Ghaggar plain in Rajasthan: a farmer behind a pair of humped zebu oxen pulls a simple wooden plough, cutting criss-cross furrows in a grid across a flat field beside a mud-brick walled settlement; other plots show furrows in two directions, sparse trees, a dry river bed and wide pale sky. Painted in a palette inspired by Harappan black-on-red pottery, flat ochre and brown forms, clear early morning light.
sa-dholavira-settled: c. 2650 BCE, Khadir island in the Rann of Kutch: early settlers cut stone and build walls of local sandstone and mud brick on a low rise, digging a large rock-cut reservoir to catch monsoon runoff from two seasonal streams; salt flats shimmer around the island, goats and zebu graze on scrub, a few reed huts. Painted in an earthy palette inspired by Harappan painted pottery, flat stylised figures, bright dry light.
sa-harappa-city: c. 2600 BCE, Harappa on the Ravi river in Punjab: a planned city of uniform baked-brick houses laid out on straight streets with covered drains, a raised citadel mound, granary platforms and workers carrying bricks and grain; bullock carts with solid wheels, men in simple draped cloth, women in jewellery of shell and beads, river and fields beyond. Painted in a palette inspired by Harappan red pottery and terracotta figurines, warm red-browns, gentle afternoon light.
sa-great-bath: c. 2500 BCE, the citadel of Mohenjo-daro: a rectangular sunken pool of finely fitted baked bricks with steps descending at each end, surrounded by a colonnaded brick verandah and small rooms; men in draped robes stand at the edge, water reflecting a pale sky, flat brick rooftops and the Indus plain beyond. Painted in a style inspired by Harappan terracotta and black-on-red pottery decoration, warm ochres and brick reds, calm still morning.
sa-lothal-dockyard: c. 2400 BCE, Lothal in Gujarat: a long rectangular baked-brick basin filled with water, linked by a channel to a river, holds small wooden sailing boats with square sails; workers unload bales and jars, bead makers drill carnelian at nearby workshops, a raised warehouse platform and mud-brick town, flat estuary land under a hazy sky. Painted in a palette inspired by Harappan pottery and seal imagery, flat earthy colours, many small figures.
sa-decline-of-indus-cities: c. 1900 BCE, Mohenjo-daro: half-empty baked-brick streets with crumbling walls and silted drains, a few families loading bundles onto a bullock cart with solid wheels and leading goats away, the citadel mound behind; the river has shifted and dry cracked earth lies where fields were, a pale dusty sky. Painted in a muted palette inspired by Harappan terracotta and pottery decoration, faded ochres and greys, quiet melancholy light.
sa-ghaggar-drying: c. 1900 BCE, Banawali on the Ghaggar-Hakra: a broad river bed now dry and sandy with only scattered pools, a small mud-brick walled town on its bank, villagers driving zebu cattle and carrying grain jars eastward along a dusty track toward distant green woodland; withered trees and hot white haze. Painted in an earthy palette inspired by Harappan painted pottery, flat stylised forms, sun-bleached colours.
sa-indo-aryan-migration: c. 1700 BCE, the Swat valley in the northwest mountains: bands of herders in wool cloaks drive cattle and horses down a green river valley between pine-covered slopes, a few light two-wheeled spoked chariots pulled by horses, families on foot with bundles, smoke from campfires, snowy peaks above. Painted in a style inspired by ancient Central and South Asian rock carvings and petroglyphs, red ochre and charcoal on a stone-coloured ground, simple stylised figures.
sa-rigveda: c. 1500 BCE, the Punjab plain of the Seven Rivers: bearded priests in white unstitched cloth sit cross-legged around a square fire altar at dawn, pouring ghee into the flames and chanting, young pupils listening; cattle, grass huts and a wide river beyond, morning mist and a rising sun. Painted in a style inspired by early Indian painting on cloth and later Ajanta murals, earthy reds, ochres and soft greens, flowing lines, serene light.
sa-battle-of-ten-kings: c. 1400 BCE, the Ravi river in Punjab: on a broad flooded river, light two-wheeled horse chariots and warriors with bows rush along the bank as rival tribal bands flounder across the high water in the distance, dust and spray, cattle herds on the far shore, open plain and big sky; all figures small and stylised, no bloodshed. Painted in a style inspired by ancient Indian rock paintings, red ochre and white on stone ground, dynamic simple forms.
sa-kuru-kingdom: c. 1200 BCE, Kurukshetra in Haryana: a large village of thatched timber halls within a wooden palisade, where priests tend a series of fire altars laid out for a royal ritual, a chieftain seated under a canopy surrounded by warriors and horses, cattle and grey painted pottery vessels arranged as offerings, fields and forest beyond. Painted in a style inspired by early Indian painting traditions, ochre, red and white with flowing outlines, warm afternoon light.
sa-varna-system: c. 1000 BCE, a village on the Ganges plain: a single panoramic scene of village life with priests at a fire altar, warriors with bows beside a chariot, merchants and farmers with cattle and grain baskets, and labourers carrying loads, arranged in separate groups around a thatched settlement under a large banyan tree; the broad river beyond. Painted in a style inspired by Ajanta murals and early Indian narrative art, earthy reds and greens, calm, balanced composition.
sa-upanishads: c. 800 BCE, a forest hermitage in Videha, Bihar: a bearded sage in simple cloth sits on a deerskin under a large tree, teaching a small circle of seated pupils and a few visitors; thatched huts, a sacred fire, grazing deer and cattle, dappled light through the forest canopy. Painted in a style inspired by Ajanta cave murals, soft ochres, greens and terracotta, flowing outlines, serene contemplative mood.
sa-sixteen-mahajanapadas: c. 600 BCE, Rajgir in Bihar: a walled city in a ring of rocky green hills, with long cyclopean stone walls, timber gateways and thatched and tiled houses; merchants in a market exchange small bent-bar and punch-marked silver coins, ox carts and an elephant on the road, soldiers on the walls. Painted in the style of early Indian relief sculpture (Bharhut and Sanchi gateway reliefs), rendered in warm stone tones with gentle colour.
sa-buddha-born: c. 563 BCE, the garden of Lumbini in the Nepal Terai: a grove of flowering sal trees beside a pond, attendants holding parasols and cloth screens around a resting place, women in draped garments carrying water jars, lotus flowers in bloom, the Himalayan foothills faint behind; the birth is shown only symbolically by a small pair of footprints on a lotus and an empty space. Painted in the style of early aniconic Buddhist relief (Sanchi and Bharhut), soft stone tones with gentle colour.
sa-buddha-enlightenment: c. 528 BCE, Bodh Gaya in Bihar: a great pipal (Bodhi) tree spreads over a simple empty stone seat by the Niranjana river, a halo of light in its branches, deer resting nearby, devotees in the distance bowing with flowers, villagers and palms beyond; the enlightenment is shown symbolically by the tree and the empty seat, with no figure of the Buddha. Painted in the aniconic style of Sanchi gateway reliefs, warm sandstone tones, golden dawn light.
sa-buddha-parinirvana: c. 483 BCE, Kushinagar: a grove of twin sal trees showering pale blossoms over an empty stone couch, mourning monks in saffron robes and lay followers kneeling around it, and in the distance a small brick stupa being raised over relics, with princes bearing caskets on elephants; the Buddha himself is not shown. Painted in the style of early aniconic Buddhist relief carving from Sanchi and Bharhut, soft sandstone tones, quiet evening light.
sa-hydaspes: 326 BCE, the monsoon-swollen Jhelum river in Punjab: Macedonian infantry with long sarissa pikes and cavalry on horseback face a line of Indian war elephants and archers with tall bows across a muddy plain, rain clouds overhead, the wide river behind with boats; all figures small, seen from a distance, no bloodshed. Painted in the style of a Hellenistic mosaic (like the Alexander Mosaic), small stone tesserae, earthy reds, ochres and greys.
sa-maurya-founded: c. 321 BCE, Pataliputra on the Ganges: a great timber-palisaded city with wooden towers and gates beside the river, where a victorious army with war elephants, chariots and foot soldiers carrying bows and long shields marches in through the gate, crowds watching from wooden balconies, boats on the river. Painted in the style of early Indian relief sculpture from the Sanchi gateways, with soft added colour, crowded procession, warm daylight.
sa-seleucid-maurya: c. 303 BCE, near Pataliputra: a long line of five hundred caparisoned war elephants with mahouts is led along a riverside road past a camp of Greek soldiers in helmets and cloaks, who stand beside their tents, while Indian officials in turbans and draped garments oversee the exchange; the timber walls of the city and the Ganges beyond. Painted in the style of early Indian relief carving, warm sandstone colour, long processional composition.
sa-megasthenes: c. 302 BCE, Pataliputra: a Greek traveller in a short chiton and cloak, seen from behind, walks with Indian guides along the great timber walls of the Mauryan capital, past a wooden palace hall with polished stone pillars, busy markets of cloth and spices, elephants and ox carts, the Ganges full of boats beyond. Painted in a style that blends Hellenistic fresco and early Indian relief art, warm earth colours, panoramic city view.
sa-kalinga-war: c. 261 BCE, the plain near Dhauli in Odisha: seen from a hill, a vast Mauryan army with war elephants and chariots spreads across the green coastal plain by the Daya river, smoke rising from burnt villages in the distance; abandoned weapons and broken chariot wheels in the foreground, no bodies shown, sombre grey sky. Painted in the style of early Indian relief sculpture, muted stone tones, solemn mood.
sa-ashoka-buddhism: c. 260 BCE, Pataliputra: in a pillared Mauryan palace hall of polished stone, a king seen small and from behind kneels before a group of Buddhist monks in saffron robes, attendants holding parasols and fly-whisks; through the doorway a new stupa rises, and people carry flowers. Painted in the style of the Sanchi gateway reliefs with soft added colour, warm sandstone tones, calm light.
sa-edicts-of-ashoka: c. 258 BCE, Girnar in Gujarat: stonemasons on wooden scaffolding carve lines of shallow, indistinct marks into the face of a great granite boulder at the foot of a forested hill, while a royal official in a turban and draped garments supervises and villagers watch; a polished sandstone pillar with a lion capital stands in the distance. Painted in the style of early Indian relief carving, warm stone colours, sunlit; no legible writing.
sa-mahinda-lanka: c. 250 BCE, Mihintale in Sri Lanka: on a rocky, forested hilltop, a group of shaven-headed monks in saffron robes stand on a flat rock ledge, meeting a royal hunting party of a king with attendants, bows and dogs, who has paused and lowers his bow; jungle canopy, distant tanks and plains, morning mist. Painted in the style of ancient Sri Lankan murals (Sigiriya), warm ochres and greens, flowing outlines.
sa-shunga-coup: c. 185 BCE, Pataliputra: a vast army review on a parade ground outside the timber city walls, rows of infantry with spears, war elephants and chariots, a royal parasol over a small platform in the distance where confusion breaks out among a cluster of officers; dust and banners, no bloodshed shown. Painted in the style of Bharhut stone reliefs of the Shunga period with soft colour, crowded composition, harsh noon light.
sa-menander: c. 155 BCE, Sagala (Sialkot): in a Hellenistic-Indian palace courtyard with Corinthian columns and Indian wooden balconies, a king in a Greek diadem and cloak, seen from behind, sits on a bench conversing with a seated Buddhist monk in a robe, courtiers in Greek and Indian dress listening; fruit trees, a fountain and mountain light. Painted in a Greco-Indian style mixing Hellenistic fresco and early Gandharan relief colour, warm and calm.
sa-gandhara-art: c. 100 CE, Takht-i-Bahi monastery on a hilltop in Gandhara: sculptors in a stone workshop carve grey schist reliefs with flowing Greek-style drapery and Indian ornaments, unfinished panels of monks and stupas around them; the terraced monastery courtyard with small votive stupas, rugged hills and valley beyond. Painted in the style of Gandharan schist relief, rendered in soft grey stone tones with faint traces of original paint.
sa-kanishka: c. 127 CE, Purushapura (Peshawar): a Kushan court on a terrace before a towering wooden-and-stone stupa under construction, nobles in long belted tunics, felt boots and tall caps, Buddhist monks in robes, and camel caravans loaded with silk and goods arriving from the Khyber hills beyond; the king seen small among courtiers. Painted in the style of Gandharan relief and Kushan art, grey schist tones with ochre and red highlights.
sa-gupta-founded: c. 320 CE, Pataliputra: a royal wedding procession winds through the city, a prince and a Licchavi princess on an elephant beneath a parasol, seen small and from behind, musicians with drums and conch shells, women throwing flowers from balconies of brick and timber houses, the Ganges and boats beyond. Painted in the style of Ajanta cave murals, flowing lines, rich reds, ochres and greens, festive daylight.
sa-samudragupta: c. 335 CE, Prayagraj at the meeting of the Ganges and Yamuna: a tall polished sandstone pillar stands by the riverbank, while envoys of southern kings in silk cloth and jewels arrive by boat and on elephants, bringing gifts of gold and horses to a royal pavilion; soldiers with bows and banners, sacred bathers in the rivers. Painted in the style of Ajanta murals, rich mineral colours, panoramic, warm morning light.
sa-chandragupta-ii-saka: c. 395 CE, Ujjain in Malwa: Gupta cavalry and war elephants enter a walled city on the Shipra river, temple spires and brick mansions behind, while merchants load bales and spices onto ox carts headed for the western ports; townsfolk in fine muslin watch from terraces. Painted in the style of Gupta-era Ajanta murals, flowing figures, rich reds, yellows and greens, bright afternoon light.
sa-nalanda-founded: c. 427 CE, Nalanda in Bihar: rows of red-brick monastery buildings with courtyards, cells and a tall brick temple rise among palm trees and a lotus pond, while monks in saffron robes carry palm-leaf manuscripts, students sit in a circle around a teacher, and builders lay bricks for a new hall. Painted in the style of Ajanta cave murals, warm terracotta reds, ochres and greens, flowing outlines, soft morning light.
sa-ajanta-caves: c. 460 CE, the horseshoe-shaped ravine of the Waghora river at Ajanta: craftsmen carve pillared cave halls into a basalt cliff while painters on bamboo scaffolding by lamplight lay mineral colours onto plastered walls inside, showing palaces, elephants and forest scenes; monks watch, a waterfall and green monsoon forest outside. Painted in the style of the Ajanta murals themselves, rich reds, lapis blues and ochres, graceful outlines.
sa-aryabhata: 499 CE, Kusumapura (Pataliputra): a scholar in white cloth, seen from behind, sits on a rooftop terrace at night with pupils, arranging small pebbles on a board and using a simple shadow stick and a water bowl to observe the stars; a huge starry sky, the moon, brick rooftops and temple spires below. Painted in the style of Gupta-era Indian murals, deep indigo night, ochre and white highlights, quiet contemplative mood; no writing.
sa-harsha: c. 606 CE, Kannauj on the Ganges: a royal assembly in a vast open-air pavilion, where a king, small among his courtiers, presides over a gathering of Buddhist monks, Brahmin priests and poets, while a play is performed on a wooden stage with dancers and drummers; elephants with howdahs, city walls and the river behind. Painted in the style of Ajanta-period Indian murals, rich reds and greens, crowded festive composition.
sa-pulakeshin-harsha: c. 618 CE, the banks of the Narmada river: Chalukya warriors with shields and spears hold the southern shore and the ghats of the wide river, while across the water a great northern army with war elephants halts in the dust; forested Vindhya hills, morning haze, figures small and seen from far off, no bloodshed. Painted in the style of Deccan cave-temple murals (Ajanta and Badami), earthy reds, greens and ochres, panoramic.
sa-xuanzang-india: 631 CE, Nalanda in Bihar: a Chinese monk in grey Tang robes with a bamboo pack of scrolls, seen from behind, enters the brick gateway of the great monastery and is welcomed by Indian monks in saffron robes; tall brick temples, courtyards, students with palm-leaf books and lotus ponds in soft light. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural blended with Ajanta colour, mineral blues, greens and ochres.
sa-shore-temple: c. 700 CE, Mahabalipuram on the Bay of Bengal: a granite temple with two tapering pyramidal towers stands on the beach, waves breaking at its base, while stonemasons carve monolithic rathas and a huge relief panel on a granite boulder nearby; wooden trading ships with lateen sails off the coast, palms and fishing boats. Painted in the style of South Indian temple murals, warm ochres and blues, bright sea light.
sa-arab-sindh: 712 CE, the port of Debal (Banbhore) on the Indus delta: an Arab army in mail and turbans with horses and camels, and a large wooden siege engine, encamps before the city's stone walls and a tall temple spire, Arab dhows with lateen sails anchored in the creek; dust and smoke rise over the walls, all seen at a distance, no bloodshed. Painted in the style of a Persian manuscript miniature, bright mineral colours, flat perspective.
sa-kailasa-temple: c. 760 CE, Ellora in Maharashtra: hundreds of workers with chisels and hammers cut downward into a basalt cliff, freeing a huge multi-storeyed temple with towers, pillars and life-sized carved elephants from the solid rock, baskets of rubble carried away along ramps; the cliff walls tower around the deep trench, monsoon clouds above. Painted in the style of Deccan cave murals, earthy ochres and greys, dramatic scale with tiny figures.
sa-tripartite-struggle: c. 786 CE, Kannauj on the Ganges: a walled city of temples and palaces on the riverbank, with three armies approaching from different directions across the plain, each with war elephants, cavalry and banners of different colours, dust clouds rising; boats on the river, all figures small and distant. Painted in the style of an early medieval Indian palm-leaf manuscript painting (Pala style), flat red, yellow and green, stylised forms.
sa-rajaraja: c. 985 CE, Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu: a Chola king, small beneath a white parasol, receives returning soldiers and war elephants in a palace courtyard, while in the background the foundations of a great granite temple are laid, and Chola ships with square sails are moored on a river; dancers and musicians celebrate. Painted in the style of Chola-period temple frescoes at Thanjavur, rich reds, ochres and greens, flowing outlines.
sa-brihadisvara: 1010, Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu: the newly finished granite temple with its towering pyramidal vimana of many tiers, capped by a great dome-shaped stone, rises over a walled courtyard; a huge seated stone bull under a pavilion faces the shrine, priests with lamps, temple dancers, drummers and crowds of pilgrims in white cloth fill the court, palms beyond. Painted in the style of Chola-period frescoes from the Brihadisvara temple itself, rich ochre, red and green, flowing lines, festive daylight.
sa-somnath-sacked: 1025, Somnath on the Gujarat coast: seen from a distance across the shore, a great stone temple with a tall carved spire stands by the Arabian Sea, smoke rising from its precincts, while a long train of laden camels and horsemen in turbans and mail moves away inland across the sand with chests of treasure; waves and a grey sky, no bloodshed. Painted in the style of a Persian manuscript miniature, flat bright colours, fine detail.
sa-second-tarain: 1192, the plain of Tarain in Haryana: seen from a low rise, mounted archers in Central Asian armour and turbans wheel and loose arrows at a long line of Rajput war elephants with howdahs and armoured horsemen with lances, dust clouds rising over the flat dry plain, banners and parasols, all figures small; no bloodshed. Painted in the style of an Indo-Persian manuscript miniature, flat bright colours, decorative composition, golden light.
sa-nalanda-destroyed: 1193, Nalanda in Bihar: seen from far across a lotus pond, smoke rises in tall columns from the red-brick monastery halls and temples of the great university, a few monks in saffron robes hurrying away along a palm-lined road carrying bundles of palm-leaf manuscripts, horsemen faint on the horizon; ash drifts over a dim orange sky, no bodies. Painted in the style of a Pala-period palm-leaf manuscript illustration, flat red, ochre and green, sombre mood.
sa-qutb-minar: c. 1199, Mehrauli, Delhi: builders on wooden scaffolding raise the first storey of a great fluted red sandstone tower beside a new mosque courtyard with reused carved stone pillars and a pointed stone screen of arches; masons cut stone blocks, labourers carry baskets, an elephant hauls a stone, dry plain and scrub trees around. Painted in the style of a Mughal-era architectural miniature, fine detail, warm red and ochre, clear light; carved bands shown as abstract patterns, no legible script.
sa-delhi-sultanate: 1206, Delhi: in a courtyard of red sandstone arcades beside the rising Qutb tower, a newly crowned sultan, seen small and from behind on a raised dais, receives the homage of Turkic nobles in long robes, turbans and boots, horsemen and guards with spears standing in rows, war elephants at the gate; dry plain and city walls beyond. Painted in the style of an Indo-Persian court miniature, flat bright colours, gold accents.
sa-razia-sultana: c. 1236, Delhi: a sultan on horseback, seen from a distance, rides at the head of a procession in a turban-like cap and cloak through the gate of a red sandstone fortress, with nobles, archers and an elephant behind, crowds watching from flat rooftops; the ruler is a woman, shown small and partly from behind, dressed like her nobles. Painted in the style of an Indo-Persian manuscript miniature, flat jewel-like colours, decorative clarity.
sa-alauddin-markets: c. 1303, Delhi: a busy grain market in a walled city square, merchants with sacks of wheat, rice and lentils measured on large balance scales under the eyes of market officers in turbans, granaries and caravans of bullock carts arriving, soldiers buying provisions; the battlements of the Siri fort behind. Painted in the style of an Indo-Persian manuscript miniature, bright flat colours, many small figures, clear daylight.
sa-daulatabad: 1327, the road to Daulatabad in the Deccan: a long column of townspeople with bullock carts, camels, bundles and children trudges across a dusty plain toward a great conical rock fortress with rings of walls and a moat; travellers rest in shade by the roadside, palaces and gateways atop the hill. Painted in the style of a Deccani manuscript miniature, rich colours with gold, stylised hills and trees, hazy afternoon.
sa-vijayanagara: 1336, Hampi on the Tungabhadra river: amid a landscape of giant granite boulders and palm groves, workers build the stone walls and a temple gateway of a new royal city, while two princes, small and seen from behind, stand with a sage by the riverbank; coracles float on the river, monkeys on the rocks. Painted in the style of the Vijayanagara murals at Lepakshi, warm ochres, reds and black outlines, bright southern light.
sa-timur-delhi: 1398, outside Delhi: seen from a distance, the walls and domes of the city send up columns of smoke while Timurid horsemen in conical helmets and mail and long camel trains laden with booty stream out across the plain; war elephants captured and led away, all figures small, no bloodshed shown. Painted in the style of a Timurid Persian manuscript miniature, rich lapis blue, gold and vermilion, high horizon.
sa-first-panipat: 1526, the plain of Panipat in Haryana: a Mughal army stands behind a line of carts chained together, small bronze field cannons puffing white smoke, while mounted archers sweep around the flanks of a huge opposing army of war elephants and cavalry; dust over the flat plain, banners and tents, all figures small and distant. Painted in the style of a Mughal Baburnama manuscript miniature, vivid colours, high viewpoint, fine detail.
sa-sher-shah: c. 1540, northern India: a long straight road lined with shade trees and stepped wells runs across the Gangetic plain, with a walled caravanserai, distance markers, and travellers, ox carts and royal couriers on horseback; in a town market merchants weigh newly minted silver coins, the domed tomb rising in a lake at Sasaram on the horizon. Painted in the style of an early Mughal manuscript miniature, fresh greens and ochres, panoramic.
sa-akbar: 1556, Kalanaur in Punjab: in an open garden, a boy king, seen small and from behind, sits on a simple brick platform under a canopy, surrounded by nobles in jamas and turbans and his guardian general, a crowd of soldiers and horses around, mango trees and a camp of tents beyond. Painted in the style of an Akbarnama Mughal manuscript miniature, bright colours, gold highlights, lively crowd composition.
sa-talikota: 1565, the plain near Talikota in the Deccan: two vast armies meet on open ground, war elephants with armoured howdahs, cavalry and gun crews with cannons in clouds of white smoke, while far away on the horizon the boulder-strewn city of Hampi burns; all figures small and distant, no bloodshed. Painted in the style of a Deccani manuscript miniature, rich colours with gold, dramatic sky, stylised hills.
sa-din-i-ilahi: c. 1582, the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri: in a red sandstone hall with carved pillars and lattice screens, scholars of many faiths in different robes and turbans — Muslim ulama, Hindu pandits, Jain monks, Parsi priests and Jesuit fathers in black cassocks — sit in groups debating, an emperor seen small and from behind presiding; courtyard fountains beyond. Painted in the style of a Mughal court miniature, rich colours, fine detail; no figure of any prophet.
sa-taj-mahal: c. 1632-1643, Agra on the Yamuna: thousands of workers, masons and elephants build a white marble tomb on a raised platform, its great dome rising inside brick scaffolding, carvers inlaying coloured stones, carts of marble blocks arriving, gardens laid out with water channels before it, boats on the river. Painted in the style of a Mughal court miniature, luminous whites, soft pinks and greens, fine detail, golden morning light.
sa-aurangzeb: 1658, Agra Fort on the Yamuna: seen from across the river, the red sandstone walls and white marble pavilions of the fort, with an elderly figure tiny on a marble balcony gazing toward the distant Taj Mahal, while soldiers stand guard at the gates and an army encampment with tents fills the plain; evening light on the water. Painted in the style of a Mughal court miniature, soft colours and gold, melancholy calm.
sa-shivaji-crowned: 1674, Raigad fort on a high flat-topped hill in the Sahyadri mountains: a coronation in a stone courtyard, a king seen small and from behind seated on a golden throne under a canopy, Brahmin priests pouring sacred water, Maratha warriors in turbans and sashes holding saffron banners, cannons fired in salute, steep cliffs and monsoon clouds around. Painted in the style of a Deccani or Maratha miniature painting, saffron, green and gold, festive.
sa-aurangzeb-death: 1707, a military camp near Ahmednagar in the Deccan: a vast sprawl of tents and red canopies on a dry plain, quiet and still at dusk, a simple white tent at the centre with courtiers in white mourning robes gathered outside, horses and elephants idle, distant rocky hills and a fortress. Painted in the style of a late Mughal miniature, muted earth tones with gold, sombre evening light, figures small and anonymous.
sa-karnal: 1739, Delhi after the battle of Karnal: a long caravan of Persian soldiers in tall red-topped caps, camels and elephants leaves the city carrying chests of jewels and a jewelled throne under a canopy, the walls and domes of the Red Fort behind; townspeople watch silently from rooftops, dust over the road. Painted in the style of a Persian Safavid-Afsharid miniature, rich colours and gold, crowded procession, no bloodshed.
sa-plassey: 1757, the mango grove at Plassey in Bengal: red-coated British infantry and Indian sepoys in rows shelter in a grove of mango trees by the Bhagirathi river, small cannons firing white smoke, while across the plain a great army of the Nawab with war elephants and cavalry stands, part of it idle; monsoon rain clouds above, figures small. Painted in the style of a Company painting by an Indian artist, gouache on paper, soft watery greens.
sa-buxar: 1764, the plain near Buxar on the Ganges in Bihar: Company infantry in red coats and sepoys in white form neat lines with cannons, facing a large allied army of Mughal and Nawabi cavalry, elephants with howdahs and camel-mounted guns; the river and the walls of a small fort behind, smoke drifting, all figures small. Painted as an eighteenth-century Company-style gouache painting by an Indian artist, panoramic, soft colours.
sa-seringapatam: 1799, Srirangapatna on an island in the Kaveri river: British and sepoy troops wade across the river in a stormy afternoon toward a breach in the massive stone walls and bastions of the fortress, cannon smoke drifting over minarets and a temple tower inside; palms on the banks, all figures small, no bloodshed shown. Painted as a late eighteenth-century British engraving with watercolour tint, panoramic, dramatic clouds.
sa-third-anglo-maratha: 1818, Pune: the British flag is raised over the Shaniwar Wada, the Peshwa's palace with its massive stone walls and great teak gateway studded with spikes, while red-coated troops and sepoys stand in ranks in the square and townspeople in turbans and saris watch from wooden balconies; hills beyond. Painted as an early nineteenth-century Company painting, gouache on paper, soft colours, calm daylight.
sa-rebellion-1857: 1857, the cantonment at Meerut: at dusk, sepoys in red coats and white trousers gather on a dusty parade ground beside low whitewashed barracks with tiled roofs, shouting and raising muskets, while smoke rises from bungalows in the distance and horsemen ride off along the road toward Delhi; neem trees and a red sky, figures small, no bloodshed. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving with sepia wash.
sa-inc-founded: 1885, Bombay: in a high-ceilinged college hall with tall windows, cloth punkahs hanging from the ceiling and wooden benches, some seventy delegates in long coats, turbans, Parsi hats and Western suits sit in rows listening to a speaker, papers on a long table; through the windows palm trees and colonial Gothic buildings. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine cross-hatching, soft daylight, figures anonymous.
sa-jallianwala: 1919, Amritsar: the Jallianwala Bagh, an enclosed garden surrounded by high brick house walls with one narrow entrance passage, an old well and a few trees, shown empty and still in the evening after the event, scattered turbans and shoes on the dusty ground, bullet marks on a wall, a single marigold garland; the tall white towers of the city beyond. Painted as a sombre Bengal School watercolour, muted wash, quiet mourning mood, no people or bodies shown.
sa-salt-march: 1930, the seashore at Dandi in Gujarat: a long line of marchers in white homespun khadi, many with walking sticks, walks along the mud flats to the edge of the Arabian Sea at dawn, a slight elderly figure at the front seen only from behind and far off, villagers watching, salt crust glittering on the flats. Painted in the style of a 1930s Bengal School watercolour, soft washes of grey, white and pale gold, gentle dawn light.
sa-quit-india: 1942, Bombay: a huge open-air meeting at the Gowalia Tank maidan, tens of thousands of people in white caps and saris seated on the ground before a distant platform under a canopy, tricolour flags of saffron, white and green flying, rain clouds over the city, palm trees and apartment blocks; all figures tiny and anonymous. Painted in the style of a 1940s Indian woodcut print, black and white with spot colour, dense crowd.
sa-independence-partition: 1947, the Punjab plains: an endless column of refugees with bullock carts, bundles, children and cattle walks along a dusty road under a hot sky, while a crowded train passes slowly with people on its roof; in the far distance, on a city skyline, a new saffron, white and green flag is raised over a sandstone building at dawn. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, dusty ochres and greys, solemn mood, no violence shown.
sa-kashmir-war-1947: 1947, the Kashmir valley near Srinagar: Dakota transport planes land on a small airfield amid poplar trees, soldiers in greatcoats and helmets file off, while snow-covered Himalayan peaks rise behind, wooden houseboats on Dal Lake and wooden houses of the old city in the distance; autumn chinar trees in red and gold. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, cold blues and warm autumn colours, figures small and anonymous.
sa-gandhi-assassinated: 1948, New Delhi: the garden of Birla House at dusk, a lawn and a path with a small raised stone platform, quiet and empty, a single pair of simple sandals and a walking stick resting beside it, marigold petals scattered, mourners gathered far off in white, the colonnaded house and trees softly lit. Painted as a gentle Bengal School watercolour, soft grey-green washes, quiet mourning mood, no figure shown up close and no violence.
sa-ceylon-independence: 1948, Colombo: a ceremonial parade on the Galle Face green beside the sea, with soldiers in white uniforms, Kandyan dancers and drummers in costume, elephants decorated with cloth, and a flag with a lion raised on a tall mast; crowds in white sarongs and saris, palms bending in the sea breeze, colonial buildings behind. Painted as a mid-century watercolour illustration, bright tropical colours, festive and calm.
sa-constitution-of-india: 26 January 1950, New Delhi: one single interior view of the domed, wood-panelled Constituent Assembly chamber, members in white homespun kurtas and Gandhi caps seated in curved rows of benches facing a raised presiding desk, a thick bound volume lying open on a table in the foreground, soft daylight from high windows under the dome. No exterior view, no split composition, no portraits, no legible writing. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration in warm sandstone and wood tones.
sa-bengali-language-movement: 1952, Dhaka: the campus of Dhaka University beneath tall trees, where a crowd of students in white kurtas and saris gathers peacefully, some carrying blank placards, beside a small simple memorial of bricks covered with red flowers; the old red-brick university buildings behind, early spring morning light. Painted as a muted Bengal School watercolour, soft greens and reds, calm, solemn mood; no violence shown.
sa-sino-indian-war: 1962, the high Himalaya near Tawang: a monastery with whitewashed walls and golden roofs perches on a mountain ridge above deep snowy valleys, small columns of soldiers in winter coats struggling along narrow mountain paths far below, prayer flags snapping in the wind, a grey winter sky over jagged peaks. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, cold blues and whites, figures tiny and anonymous, no fighting shown.
sa-indo-pak-1965: 1965, the Punjab plain near Lahore: flat green fields of wheat and sugar cane crossed by an irrigation canal, with a few tanks and army trucks moving along a tree-lined road in the distance, dust and smoke on the horizon, a village of mud houses and a Sikh gurdwara nearby; afternoon haze. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, earthy greens and greys, figures and vehicles small, no fighting shown.
sa-green-revolution: 1966, near Ludhiana in Punjab: endless fields of golden high-yield wheat ready for harvest, a tractor and threshing machine working, a tube-well pumping water into a channel, farmers in turbans gathering sheaves, sacks of grain piled high near a village; bright blue sky over flat fertile land. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, warm golds and greens, cheerful daylight, figures small and anonymous.
sa-bangladesh-liberation: 1971, Dhaka: on a green racecourse field under a December sky, rows of soldiers stand at a formal ceremony around a small table, while a large crowd of civilians gathers at a distance waving flags of green with a red disc; trees and low city buildings beyond. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft greens and reds, calm, figures small and anonymous, no fighting shown.
sa-smiling-buddha: 1974, the Thar desert near Pokhran in Rajasthan: a vast flat desert of sand and scrub at dawn, a small cluster of army trucks, huts and measuring masts in the far distance, the ground beginning to heave and rise in a broad dust dome, camels and a thorn tree in the foreground. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, pale sands and pinks, quiet dramatic stillness, no people in view.
sa-emergency: 1975, New Delhi: a quiet broad avenue with sandstone government buildings and a domed Parliament, a printing press in a newspaper office in the foreground with its machines silent and blank sheets stacked, police jeeps parked on the street outside; overcast summer sky, few people visible. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, grey and sandstone tones, still and subdued mood, no individuals shown.
sa-sri-lanka-civil-war: 1983, the Jaffna peninsula in northern Sri Lanka: flat sandy land with palmyra palms, a Hindu temple tower and small houses, smoke rising faintly on the horizon, a road with an army checkpoint and families with bicycles and bundles moving along it; lagoon and grey monsoon sky. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, sombre greens and greys, figures small and anonymous, no violence shown.
sa-blue-star: 1984, Amritsar: the Golden Temple seen from across its square sacred pool at dawn, gilded upper storeys reflected in still water, the marble walkway and surrounding white buildings with some scarred and damaged, a few army trucks far off at the entrance, pigeons in flight; muted and still. Painted as a sombre documentary watercolour, gold and grey washes, quiet mood, no people up close and no fighting shown.
sa-liberalisation: 1991, New Delhi: the long sandstone North Block ministry building with its domes and colonnades in morning light, a ministry corridor where officials carry files, and outside on the street new imported cars, auto-rickshaws and a busy crowd, a container port crane suggested far off; ordinary office workers seen from behind. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, warm sandstone and cool blue tones, calm everyday scene, figures anonymous.
sa-nuclear-tests-1998: 1998, the Thar desert near Pokhran: a wide empty desert at noon with a distant shallow crater and a low rising dust cloud over the dunes, a few army vehicles and huts far away, a thorn tree and a herd of camels in the foreground watching the horizon. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, pale yellows and greys, still and quiet, no people visible.
sa-nepal-republic: 2008, Kathmandu: the old royal palace compound with its pagoda-roofed buildings and a modern palace façade in the background, a large calm crowd of people of all ages gathered outside carrying red flags without symbols, prayer flags strung over the street, the Himalayan foothills beyond under a clear sky. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, warm reds and soft greens, figures small and anonymous.
sa-chandrayaan-3: 2023, the lunar surface near the south pole: a small four-legged gold-foil-wrapped lander resting on grey cratered regolith, a tiny six-wheeled rover rolling down a ramp, long low shadows from a sun near the horizon, rugged crater rims and a black starry sky with the blue Earth faint above. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, silvery greys and soft golds, calm and precise, no people.
sa-hasina-ousted: 2024, Dhaka: a vast calm crowd of students and townspeople fills a wide boulevard at dusk, carrying blank placards and red-and-green flags, rickshaws parked along the edges, the dense city skyline with apartment blocks and a large modernist parliament building far in the background; all figures tiny and anonymous. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, warm dusk tones, neutral and peaceful, no individuals depicted.
sea-austronesian-expansion: c. 2200 BCE, the Cagayan Valley in northern Luzon: outrigger canoes with woven sails are drawn up on a river beach, families of seafarers unloading pigs, dogs, rice seedlings, red-slipped pottery and stone adzes, building stilt houses with thatched roofs at the edge of green forest, mountains behind. Painted in a style inspired by ancient Southeast Asian rock art and Austronesian bark-cloth patterning, red ochre, black and cream, simple stylised figures.
sea-ban-chiang: c. 2100 BCE, Ban Chiang in northeast Thailand: a village of thatched stilt houses among rice paddies, women shaping and painting buff pottery with red swirling patterns, men working wet fields with water buffalo, pigs and chickens beneath the houses, a small group casting bronze bracelets over a fire. Painted in a style inspired by Ban Chiang pottery decoration, red spiral designs on buff, flat earthy colours.
sea-dong-son-culture: c. 1000-500 BCE, the Red River plain in northern Vietnam: in a village of boat-roofed stilt houses, craftsmen pour molten bronze into a mould for a huge drum, while finished drums decorated with concentric bands of birds, boats and dancers stand nearby; long canoes with feathered rowers on the river, rice fields and limestone hills behind. Painted in the style of Đông Sơn bronze drum engravings, dark bronze tones with green patina.
sea-sa-huynh-culture: c. 500 BCE, the coast of central Vietnam near Đức Phổ: villagers bury large lidded pottery jars in sandy dunes behind the beach, with offerings of iron tools, glass beads and double-headed animal ear ornaments of jade; boats with sails on the South China Sea, coconut palms, distant green mountains. Painted in a style inspired by ancient Southeast Asian pottery decoration, earthy browns, greens and cream, simple flat forms.
sea-plain-of-jars: c. 500 BCE, the Xiangkhouang plateau in northern Laos: hundreds of huge stone jars, some as tall as a man, stand scattered across a grassy upland plain under a misty sky, a group of villagers rolling a newly carved jar into place with logs and ropes, stone discs nearby, low hills and pines around. Painted in a style inspired by ancient Southeast Asian rock art, earthy ochres and greys with misty atmosphere.
sea-au-lac: c. 257 BCE, Cổ Loa near the Red River: a great citadel of three spiralling earthen ramparts with moats, workers carrying baskets of earth and building bamboo palisades, bronze-armed warriors with crossbows on the walls, boats in the moats, rice paddies and villages beyond. Painted in the style of Đông Sơn bronze drum engravings blended with simple ink, bronze-green and earthy tones, stylised figures.
sea-pyu-city-states: c. 200 BCE, Beikthano in central Myanmar: a walled city of fired brick with circular corner bastions on the dry Irrawaddy plain, brick buildings and a cylindrical reliquary mound inside, farmers driving ox carts and irrigating rice fields from channels, sugar palms and distant hills. Painted in the style of early Burmese temple mural painting, warm reds, ochres and greens, flat forms.
sea-han-jiaozhi: 111 BCE, Luy Lâu in the Red River delta: Han officials in long robes and black caps arrive at a walled commandery town of rammed earth and timber, soldiers with halberds and crossbows, local Lạc Việt villagers with tattoos and short hair bringing rice, ivory and tortoiseshell as tribute; river boats and paddies. Painted in the style of a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, with soft added ochre colour, flat procession.
sea-oc-eo: c. 150 CE, the port of Óc Eo in the Mekong delta: wooden stilt houses and warehouses along canals, ships with woven sails and outriggers moored at jetties, merchants from India and further west in draped garments trading beads, glass and gold, local craftsmen making jewellery; a few gold and Roman-style coins on a mat. Painted in the style of an Angkor-period bas-relief with soft colour, crowded market scene.
sea-chenla-conquers-funan: c. 550 CE, Sambor Prei Kuk in Cambodia: a forest city of brick temple towers with carved sandstone door frames, a Khmer king seen small on an elephant beneath a parasol leading an army of spearmen, while dignitaries kneel in submission before him; ponds and tall trees around. Painted in the style of a Khmer bas-relief (as at Angkor and Bayon), sandstone tones with faint added colour, processional composition.
sea-yijing-srivijaya: c. 671 CE, Palembang on the Musi river in Sumatra: a Chinese monk in grey Tang robes, seen from behind, steps off a large Persian-style merchant ship onto a wooden jetty, met by Buddhist monks in saffron, wooden stilt houses and a monastery with palm trees along the broad river. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, tropical setting.
sea-srivijaya-rise: 683 CE, the Musi river near Palembang: a great royal expedition sets out with hundreds of boats crowded with warriors and thousands of soldiers marching along the bank, a king under a parasol on a decorated barge, stilt villages and tropical forest; a carved standing stone by the river with indistinct marks. Painted in the style of Borobudur bas-reliefs, warm volcanic stone tones, crowded flowing composition, no legible writing.
sea-mai-thuc-loan: 722 CE, Nam Đàn in Nghệ An: rebel peasants armed with spears and bows gather at the foot of a green mountain, their leader small on horseback in dark clothes, behind them rice paddies and thatched villages, smoke from a Tang garrison fortress in the distance; dark rain clouds over the hills. Painted in the style of traditional Vietnamese Đông Hồ woodblock prints, flat colours on textured paper, simple bold figures.
sea-borobudur: c. 780-830 CE, Borobudur in Central Java: thousands of workers lift andesite blocks with ropes and wooden frames to build a great stepped stone monument shaped like a mountain mandala, carvers shaping reliefs on its terraces and bell-shaped stupas at the top, volcanoes and palm groves around, morning mist. Painted in the style of the Borobudur bas-reliefs themselves, grey volcanic stone tones with soft green surroundings.
sea-khmer-empire: 802 CE, the sacred Phnom Kulen plateau above Cambodia: on a forested mountain top beside a stream, a consecration ceremony with Brahmin priests in white chanting around a stone lingam, a king seen small under a gold parasol, nobles and elephants nearby, the plain below stretching to the horizon. Painted in the style of an Angkor-era Khmer bas-relief, sandstone tones with soft added colour, solemn composition.
sea-prambanan: c. 856 CE, Prambanan in Central Java: a cluster of tall, slender stone Hindu temple towers rises in a courtyard among palm trees, the central Shiva temple soaring above the rest, priests and devotees in sarongs bringing offerings of flowers and fruit, Mount Merapi smoking faintly in the distance. Painted in the style of the Ramayana reliefs of Prambanan, grey stone tones with soft greens, festive procession.
sea-yasodharapura: c. 889 CE, Angkor: workers drag sandstone blocks on rollers up the natural hill of Phnom Bakheng to build a stepped temple pyramid, a vast rectangular reservoir being dug below, elephants hauling logs, rice fields and forest stretching across the flat plain. Painted in the style of an Angkor bas-relief, sandstone tones with soft green surroundings, busy construction scene with many small figures under a bright sky.
sea-dai-co-viet: 968, Hoa Lư in Ninh Bình: a royal citadel nestled among dramatic limestone karst peaks and winding rivers, with timber palace halls with curving tiled roofs, an emperor seen small and from behind on a throne in the courtyard receiving bowing officials in robes, soldiers with banners, boats on the river. Painted in the style of traditional Vietnamese silk painting, soft ink and colour, misty karst landscape.
sea-thang-long: 1010, the Red River at Thăng Long: a fleet of royal boats with dragon prows sails up the wide river toward a new capital site, while legend's golden dragon rises from the water into the morning sky, timber palaces being built on the bank, crowds of people watching. Painted in the style of traditional Vietnamese silk painting with Đông Hồ woodblock colours, gold and red on soft green, festive.
sea-chola-srivijaya: 1025, the port of Kedah on the Malay peninsula: a Chola fleet of large wooden ships with square sails and painted eyes enters the estuary, soldiers wading ashore with spears and shields, smoke rising from the port warehouses in the distance, green mountain Gunung Jerai behind; all figures small, no bloodshed. Painted in the style of South Indian Chola fresco, warm reds, ochres and blues.
sea-pagan-empire: 1044, Bagan on the Irrawaddy plain: a king seen small on a white elephant leads a procession of warriors and monks past the first brick stupas and temples rising over a dry plain dotted with toddy palms, the wide river with wooden boats beyond and blue hills on the horizon. Painted in the style of Bagan temple murals, warm reds, ochres and greens, flat stylised forms, golden sunlight.
sea-pagan-thaton: 1057, the road from Thaton to Bagan: a long procession of elephants carrying gilded caskets of palm-leaf scriptures, Mon monks in saffron robes, artisans and craftsmen walking behind, and Burmese soldiers with spears escorting them away from a walled Mon city with golden stupas near the sea; green rice fields and palms. Painted in the style of Bagan temple murals, warm reds, ochres and greens, flat processional composition, gentle morning light.
sea-temple-of-literature: 1070, Thăng Long (Hanoi): a walled temple compound with a series of courtyards, a large square pond and wooden halls with curved tiled roofs, scholars in long dark robes and black hats walking under old trees, students reading bamboo-bound books on a veranda, an elegant gate pavilion; misty morning. Painted in the style of traditional Vietnamese ink and colour on silk, soft greens and reds, calm scholarly atmosphere; no legible writing.
sea-angkor-wat: c. 1113-1150, Angkor: thousands of labourers and elephants haul sandstone blocks along a causeway across a wide moat to build a vast temple with five lotus-bud towers rising from galleried terraces, carvers working on long relief galleries, rafts carrying stone on the water, palm trees and forest around. Painted in the style of the Angkor Wat bas-reliefs themselves, golden sandstone tones with soft green surroundings, dawn light.
sea-jayavarman-vii: c. 1181-1200, Angkor Thom: a new walled city with a monumental gate topped by great serene stone faces looking in four directions, a causeway lined with stone figures pulling a serpent, the many-towered Bayon temple rising at the centre; travellers, ox carts and a rest house along the road, monks and villagers. Painted in the style of Bayon bas-reliefs, grey-gold sandstone tones, crowded everyday scenes, soft afternoon light.
