Small distant figures, no violence shown. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, fine line, muted mineral colours on silk.
pingliang-ambush: 787 CE, Pingliang in Gansu: a treaty pavilion on a high loess plateau, Tang officials in red robes and Tibetan delegates, Tibetan cavalry suddenly charging out of a hidden ravine, a Tang general on horseback galloping away; banners falling. Distant panoramic view, no gore. Overturned altar tables and scattered silk gifts lie on the ground. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
tea-tax-introduced: 793 CE, a river port near tea-growing hills: merchants unload bales and bricks of tea from boats, government officials in black caps weigh them on scales and collect a tenth in a warehouse, porters carry loads; tea terraces on the hills behind. Bright day. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground.
cangshan-alliance: 794 CE, the Cangshan mountains above Erhai Lake: a solemn oath ceremony at a mountain shrine, a Nanzhao king in local dress, seen small, and Tang envoys in red robes sacrifice at an altar, attendants and warriors around them; mist on the peaks and blue lake below. Painted in the style of the Nanzhao Picture Scroll, fine line, mineral colours on paper.
eunuchs-command-shence: 796 CE, Chang'an: the Shence Army parade ground inside the palace's northern park, rows of armoured soldiers with banners, two beardless palace eunuch officers in robes and caps reviewing them from a pavilion while ministers in black caps watch from afar. Bright day. Willows and pavilions of the palace park frame the scene. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, mineral colours on silk, many small figures.
tongdian-completed: 801 CE, Yangzhou: a scholar-official's study in a southern garden residence, an elderly official in robes surrounded by piles of paper rolls and bound volumes, assistants arranging documents into boxes, brush and ink stone on a low table. Calm daylight through lattice windows. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Zhou Fang, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
wei-gao-defeats-tibet: 801 CE, Weizhou (Lixian) in the mountains of western Sichuan: Tang troops in lamellar armour storm Tibetan stone watchtowers in a steep river gorge, Tibetan soldiers retreating up the valley; snowy peaks above. Distant panoramic view, no gore, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Zhaodao, mineral colours on silk.
kukai-arrives: 804 CE, Chang'an: two Japanese monks in dark robes with a few companions, seen small, arrive at the gate of the Qinglong Temple, welcomed by Chinese monks; pagoda and halls behind, Japanese embassy officials in court dress at a distance. Spring blossoms. A tiled stupa and courtyard of cypress trees stand behind the gate. Painted in the style of a Japanese Kamakura-period emakimono biography scroll, fine line, mineral colours.
yongzhen-reform: 805 CE, Chang'an: in a palace office hall, a small group of reform-minded officials in black futou caps and green and red robes confer intently around a low table spread with memorials, while in the shadow of a long corridor beardless eunuch officers in robes watch them; outside, an ailing emperor's empty throne under a canopy. Spring light, tense quiet mood. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Zhou Fang, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
classical-prose-movement: 805 CE, Chang'an: a gathering of scholars in a courtyard garden of a residence, an older scholar in plain robes reading aloud from a paper roll while younger literati in black caps listen, some writing with brushes at low tables; pine trees, a rock garden and a simple pavilion. Calm autumn afternoon light. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, fine line, soft mineral blues and greens on silk, small figures.
flying-cash: 806 CE, Chang'an: inside a government office in the Western Market, merchants in round-collared robes and caps hand strings of square-holed bronze coins across a counter to clerks, receiving folded paper certificates in return; outside, a busy market street with camels, shops and travellers. Bright daylight, crowded but orderly. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural of market scenes, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, lively small figures.
everlasting-regret: 806 CE, Zhouzhi county near the Qinling mountains: a young official and two friends in scholar's robes, seen small, sit on a temple terrace among pines at dusk, sharing wine and talking; in a dreamlike mist above the mountains float faint images of a Tang palace and a court lady in flowing robes on a cloud. Melancholy evening light. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Zhaodao, mineral colours on silk.
liu-pi-suppressed: 806 CE, Chengdu: an imperial army with banners advances across the green Sichuan plain through rice fields and bamboo groves towards the walled city, after crossing the steep plank roads visible in the mountains behind; the city gates open as defenders surrender. Distant panoramic view, misty light, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk.
niu-li-factional-strife: 808 CE, Chang'an palace: in a great hall with red columns, two groups of officials in black futou caps and robes of purple, red and green stand on opposite sides of the hall, turned away from each other, some gesturing in argument, memorials in their hands; an empty space between them on the stone floor. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral colours on silk.
yuanhe-junxian-tuzhi: 813 CE, Chang'an: in a chancellor's office, officials and draughtsmen in black caps kneel around a vast map painted on silk spread across the floor, showing rivers, mountains and walled towns without any writing; scribes compile notes on paper rolls at side tables. Soft daylight through lattice windows. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, fine line, mineral blues and greens on silk.
wu-yuanheng-assassinated: 815 CE, Chang'an: before dawn on a broad, dark avenue between walled wards, a chancellor's small procession with lanterns and a horse is scattered, lanterns lying on the ground, shadowy figures fleeing over a ward wall; distant guards running with torches. No gore, small distant figures. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, darkened mineral colours on silk, night atmosphere.
pipa-xing: 816 CE, Jiangzhou by the Xunyang River: an autumn night with maples and reeds along the bank, a moored boat with a lantern where a woman in faded fine robes plays a pipa, while on a second boat a small group of officials in robes listen, one weeping into his sleeve; the moon reflected on the water. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape, fine line, soft mineral colours on silk.
li-su-takes-caizhou: 817 CE, Caizhou in Henan: a snowy night, a column of Tang soldiers wrapped against the cold marches silently through a blizzard towards a walled city, geese and ducks on a pond beside the walls covering the sound; soldiers climbing over the walls with ropes. Dark blue and white, small distant figures. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, darkened lapis, white and ochre.
han-yu-buddha-bone: 819 CE, Chang'an: a grand procession carries a jewelled reliquary casket on a canopied carriage along a broad avenue towards the palace gate, crowds of devotees bowing and burning incense; in the corner, a lone official in robes, seen small from behind, rides away southward on a horse into the mountains. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues, greens and ochre.
li-shidao-killed: 819 CE, Yunzhou in Shandong: a provincial governor's walled headquarters, armed officers in lamellar armour opening the gates to an approaching imperial army, banners being lowered on the towers; townspeople watching from the streets. Grey winter morning, distant view, no violence shown. Rammed-earth walls, watchtowers and bare trees line the flat Shandong plain. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
xianzong-murdered: 820 CE, Chang'an palace: a dark night in a palace pavilion, small bottles of alchemical elixir and a cinnabar furnace on a table beside an empty couch, eunuchs in robes hurrying away along a covered corridor lit by a single lamp; the palace roofs under a cold moon. No figures in close-up, no violence shown. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, darkened mineral colours on silk.
tang-tibet-treaty: 821 CE, Lhasa: a tall plain stone pillar stands before the Jokhang temple in a city square, its surface uncarved in view, with Tibetan monks, nobles in fur-lined robes and a Tang envoy's party in black caps and red robes gathered before it; whitewashed buildings and mountains behind. Bright high-altitude sunlight. Painted in the style of a Tibetan thangka painting, mineral colours, flat perspective, fine outlines.
hebei-revolts-821: 821 CE, Youzhou (Beijing): soldiers in lamellar armour mutiny in the courtyard of a governor's headquarters, waving banners and gathering with spears, while an imperial envoy's party hurries out of the gate on horseback; smoke rising from a building nearby. Distant view, winter light, no gore. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
ganlu-incident: 835 CE, Chang'an: in the Daming Palace courtyard, a pomegranate tree said to bear sweet dew stands before a hall; curtains blowing aside reveal hidden armed men, while beardless eunuchs in robes rush the emperor's palanquin away through a gate; officials scattering across the vast courtyard. Distant small figures, no gore. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, mineral colours on silk.
ennin-travels: 838 CE, the Grand Canal near Yangzhou: a Japanese monk in dark robes with a companion, seen from behind, travels by small boat along a willow-lined canal, writing in a notebook; Tang farmhouses, temples and a pagoda along the banks, boats with cargo. Misty morning light. Painted in the style of a Japanese Heian-period Yamato-e emakimono, fine line, soft mineral colours on paper.
uyghur-collapse: 840 CE, Ordu-Baliq on the Orkhon River: a walled steppe city with a tall citadel and Manichaean temples on the grassland, smoke rising above the walls as Kyrgyz horsemen in fur caps pour in; Uyghur families flee with carts and herds across the plain. Distant panoramic view, no gore. Painted in the style of a Uyghur Manichaean manuscript painting from Turfan, rich blue and gold, outlined figures.
li-deyu-zelu: 843 CE, Luzhou (Changzhi) in the Shanxi highlands: a walled city in a mountain basin, imperial armies with banners closing in from several valleys, defenders on the walls opening the gate; loess terraces and mountain passes. Distant panoramic view, autumn haze, many small figures. Supply carts wind along the mountain roads behind the troops. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
gunpowder-formula: 850 CE, a Daoist alchemist's workshop in the hills near Chang'an: an alchemist in Daoist robes and topknot cap steps back startled as a small mixture of yellow and black powders in a ceramic bowl flares with bright flame and smoke, an assistant dropping a fan; furnaces, mortars and jars around, mountain pines outside. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
guiyi-circuit: 851 CE, Shazhou (Dunhuang): before the great cave temples on the cliff above the oasis, a Han general on horseback leads a grand procession of armoured cavalry, musicians and banners, celebrating the return of the region to Tang; desert dunes and poplars. Bright sunlight. Painted in the style of the Dunhuang Mogao Cave 156 procession mural of Zhang Yichao, mineral blues, greens and ochre, many small figures.
qiu-fu-rebellion: 859 CE, Shan county in Zhejiang: a peasant army with hoes, staves and makeshift banners pours from wooded green hills towards a small walled county town on a river; terraced rice fields and bamboo groves. Misty spring light, distant panoramic view, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk.
nanzhao-takes-jiaozhi: 863 CE, Jiaozhi (Hanoi) in the Red River delta: Nanzhao warriors with long spears and shields and local fighters storm a walled Tang protectorate city surrounded by rice paddies and palms, smoke rising over the walls; river boats fleeing downstream. Distant panoramic view, humid haze. Painted in the style of the Nanzhao Picture Scroll, fine line, mineral colours on paper.
pang-xun-mutiny: 868 CE, the road to Xuzhou: a column of weary garrison soldiers in worn armour marching home along a river through southern hills, banners raised in defiance, boats carrying their gear; they approach the walls of Xuzhou on the plain. Autumn light, distant panoramic view, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre.
famen-relic-873: 873 CE, Famen Temple near Fufeng: a magnificent procession carries a nested gold and silver reliquary on a jewelled palanquin from a brick pagoda, monks chanting, court officials and crowds kneeling along the road strewn with flowers; silver incense burners and silk banners. Bright spring sunlight. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues, greens and gold.
qin-fu-yin: 883 CE, the road near Luoyang: a lone young woman in faded Tang dress, seen small from behind, walks along a willow-lined road past ruined farmhouses, a poet in robes resting beneath a tree nearby listening; smoke on the distant horizon where Chang'an lies. Melancholy spring light. Painted in the style of a late-Tang Dunhuang manuscript illustration, ink and light colour on paper.
li-keyong-retakes-changan: 883 CE, Liangtianpo near Weinan: black-clad Shatuo Turkic cavalry with bows and lances sweep across a plain beside the Wei River, the rebel army breaking and fleeing towards Chang'an's distant walls; dust clouds. Distant panoramic view, many small figures, no gore. Black banners stream above the horsemen and the loess terraces rise behind the river. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, black, lapis and ochre.
huang-chao-dies: 884 CE, Langhu Valley near Laiwu in Shandong: a narrow mountain valley with pine forests, a small band of exhausted rebels with tattered banners hiding among rocks, while pursuing cavalry appear at the valley mouth; grey dusk. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties monumental landscape in the manner of Jing Hao, ink and light colour on silk.
shangyuan-inn-incident: 884 CE, Bianzhou (Kaifeng): night at a large inn with tiled roofs and courtyards, fire and torches as soldiers attack, a few riders fleeing over a wall into a sudden rainstorm; lightning illuminating the scene. Distant view, small figures, no gore. Rain pours on tiled roofs, and horses rear in the inn's stable yard as lanterns swing in the wind. Painted in the style of a late-Tang Dunhuang cave mural, darkened lapis and ochre.
wang-jian-takes-chengdu: 891 CE, Chengdu: an army with banners at the gates of the walled city on the Sichuan plain, defenders surrendering, troops marching in along broad streets lined with timber houses and hibiscus trees; mountains on the horizon. Misty light, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties court painting in the manner of Huang Quan, fine line, rich colour on silk.
yang-xingmi-yangzhou: 892 CE, Yangzhou: a once-great canal city in ruins, burned warehouses and broken bridges along the Grand Canal, a governor's army entering the gate while a few surviving townspeople return with bundles; willows sprouting among ruins. Grey sky, melancholy. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Zhou Wenju, fine line, soft colour on silk.
wang-chao-fuzhou: 893 CE, Fuzhou on the Min River: an army arrives at the walled city among green subtropical hills, river junks and sampans crowding the waterfront, banners rising on the city walls; lychee trees and mountains. Warm humid light. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Fishing nets dry along the riverbank and townspeople watch from the waterfront. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties blue-green landscape, mineral colours on silk.
changan-abandoned: 904 CE, Chang'an: labourers dismantle palace halls, stripping roof tiles and lowering great timber beams into the Wei River to float downstream, crowds of townspeople with carts trailing eastward along the road; the vast grid city half empty, smoke over abandoned wards. Grey winter light. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties monumental landscape in the manner of Jing Hao, ink and light colour on silk.
baima-incident: 905 CE, Baima Station on the Yellow River: a desolate post station on the muddy riverbank at dusk, a row of official black futou caps and fallen court tablets scattered on the ground, soldiers with spears standing guard, the broad yellow river flowing past under a heavy sky. Symbolic, no bodies shown. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties ink landscape, ink and pale wash on silk.
wuyue-founded: 907 CE, Hangzhou: beside the West Lake and the Qiantang River, a ceremony at a palace on Phoenix Hill, a king in robes seen small receiving envoys from the north who present a seal; boats on the lake, pagodas on the hills. Spring mist. Courtiers in robes line the terrace and attendants hold parasols and banners. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties blue-green landscape, mineral colours on silk.
former-shu-founded: 907 CE, Chengdu: a palace hall in Sichuan where a governor, seen small and from behind, mounts a throne, scholars and officials in Tang-style black caps and robes, some newly arrived from the north, bow in rows; hibiscus flowers in the courtyard. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties court painting in the manner of Huang Quan, fine line, rich colour on silk.
ma-yin-king-of-chu: 907 CE, Changsha on the Xiang River: tea merchants load bales and bricks of tea onto river boats at a busy waterfront, porters with shoulder poles, a royal palace on the hill behind; tea-covered green hills. Bright day. Clerks with scales tally the loads and northern merchants wait beside their carts. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties handscroll, fine line, ink and light colour on silk, many small figures.
battle-of-luzhou: 908 CE, Luzhou (Changzhi): a thick morning fog fills a mountain basin as cavalry in lamellar armour charge through earthwork siege lines and wooden palisades surrounding a walled city; enemy camps in confusion, banners emerging from the mist. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties monumental landscape in the manner of Jing Hao, ink and light colour on silk.
yang-wo-murdered: 908 CE, Yangzhou palace: night in a palace residence, armed generals in lamellar armour walking down a dark corridor towards a lamplit bedchamber hung with curtains; guards look away. Small distant figures, no violence shown. Moonlight falls on tiled roofs and a silent garden pond outside. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties court painting in the manner of Gu Hongzhong, fine line, rich colour on silk.
wang-shenzhi-prince-of-min: 909 CE, Quanzhou harbour in Fujian: a busy seaport with sea-going junks and Arab and Persian merchant ships, porters unloading spices and ivory, a modest prince's procession passing along the quay; temples and green hills behind. Warm light. Warehouses with tiled roofs line the quay, and townspeople in simple dress crowd the waterfront to watch. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties handscroll, fine line, ink and light colour on silk.
qian-liu-seawall: 910 CE, Hangzhou on the Qiantang River: workers sink huge bamboo cages filled with stones and drive timber piles along the riverbank as a tidal bore surges up the estuary; archers on the dyke shoot arrows at the wave in ritual defiance. Dramatic grey sky. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties monumental landscape, ink and light colour on silk, many small figures.
battle-of-boxiang: 911 CE, Boxiang in Hebei: on a frozen plain, Jin cavalry in lamellar armour charge across the river ice against a Later Liang army, the Liang lines breaking; snow-covered fields and willows. Distant panoramic view, many small figures, no gore. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties monumental landscape in the manner of Jing Hao, ink and light colour on silk.
zhu-wen-murdered: 912 CE, Luoyang palace: a dark palace bedchamber at night seen from across a courtyard, armed men slipping in through a side gate, lamps flickering behind paper screens, an ominous empty corridor. Small distant figures, no violence shown. Moonlight falls on tiled roofs, bare trees and a silent garden pond, and a guard's lantern lies abandoned by the gate. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties court painting, fine line, darkened colours on silk.
jin-conquers-yan: 913 CE, Youzhou (Beijing): a Jin army with banners storms the walled northern city below the Yanshan mountains, defenders surrendering, a small figure in imperial robes led out of the gate; winter trees. Distant panoramic view, no gore. Snow lies on the rooftops, and Jin banners are being raised on the gate towers as townspeople watch from the streets. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties monumental landscape, ink and light colour on silk.
weibo-joins-jin: 915 CE, Weizhou (Daming) in Hebei: mutinous soldiers in lamellar armour on the city walls lower the old banners and raise new ones, while a Jin army approaches across the plain; townspeople cheering. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Supply carts and horses crowd the road outside the gate, and willows line the moat. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties handscroll, fine line, ink and light colour on silk.
southern-han-founded: 917 CE, Guangzhou: a palace on the Pearl River, a governor seen small and from behind enthroned in a hall, officials bowing; in the harbour, Arab and Persian merchant ships and Chinese junks unloading pearls and spices; banyan trees. Warm light. Courtiers in silk robes line the hall, and porters carry chests along the quay. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties court painting, fine line, rich colour on silk.
battle-of-huliupo: 918 CE, Huliupo near Puyang: two armies clash on a wide plain near the Yellow River, both sides exhausted, a hill fought over in the middle, scattered banners and riderless horses; dusk light. Distant panoramic view, no gore, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties monumental landscape in the manner of Jing Hao, ink and light colour on silk.
xu-zhixun-killed: 918 CE, Yangzhou: in a palace courtyard during a banquet, an arrogant young official in rich robes sits apart while armed men wait behind a screen; a calm young man in robes stands aside in the shadow. Small distant figures, no violence shown. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties court painting in the manner of Gu Hongzhong, fine line, rich colour on silk.
battle-of-langshan-river: 919 CE, Langshan at the Yangtze mouth: a Wuyue fleet of warships with matting sails scatters burning ashes and sand upwind onto an enemy fleet, the opposing ships in confusion and fire; a lone hill on the riverbank. Distant view, many small figures. Smoke drifts over the broad estuary. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
khitan-script: 920 CE, Shangjing on the steppe: in a felt tent palace beside a walled city, Khitan scholars with shaved crowns and side locks and Chinese advisers in caps sit at low tables writing unfamiliar characters with brushes on paper, illegible; horses and herds outside. Painted in the style of a Liao steppe painting in the manner of Hu Gui, fine ink and light colour on silk.
battle-of-wangdu: 922 CE, Wangdu in Hebei: Jin cavalry in lamellar armour fight Khitan horsemen in fur caps on a snowy plain, the Khitan host turning back north; abandoned tents. Distant panoramic view, many small figures, no gore. Bare trees and frozen streams cross the plain. Painted in the style of a Liao steppe painting in the manner of Hu Gui, fine ink and light colour on silk.
gao-jixing-jingnan: 924 CE, Jiangling on the Yangtze: a small riverside walled city, envoys from several neighbouring states arriving by boat and horse, a modest ruler seen small receiving them at the gate with gifts; the wide river and green hills. Porters carry chests of tribute, and river junks crowd the waterfront below the walls. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties handscroll, fine line, ink and light colour on silk.
jing-hao-bifaji: 925 CE, Mount Taihang: a hermit painter in plain robes sits on a rock beneath towering cliffs and ancient pines, brush in hand, painting on silk spread on a stone; a thatched hut beside a waterfall, mist in the valleys. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties monumental landscape in the manner of Jing Hao's Mount Kuanglu, ink on silk.
zhuangzong-killed: 926 CE, Luoyang palace: smoke rising from a palace gate tower as mutinous soldiers with spears storm the palace courtyard, actors' masks and musical instruments scattered on the ground; distant figures, no gore. Palace attendants and court actors flee along covered galleries, and dark smoke drifts across tiled roofs under a grey spring sky. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties court painting, fine line, rich colour on silk.
mingzong-accession: 926 CE, Luoyang: an elderly general seen small and from behind takes the throne in a modest palace hall, officials bowing in rows in black caps and robes; outside, farmers working peaceful fields. Calm daylight. Officials hold court tablets before them, guards line the steps, and willows and tiled roofs frame the scene of a quieter reign. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties court painting, fine line, soft colour on silk.
abaoji-dies: 926 CE, Fuyu in Jilin: a Khitan camp of felt tents in the northern forest-steppe, the khagan's great tent draped in white mourning, a widowed empress in Khitan robes seen from behind standing before it, Khitan nobles kneeling; horses and banners. Grey autumn light, no injury shown. Painted in the style of a Liao steppe painting in the manner of Hu Gui, fine ink and light colour on silk.
guo-chongtao-killed: 926 CE, Chengdu: a general's headquarters in a palace hall, a messenger arriving with a sealed edict, armed guards in the shadows, soldiers' camps in the courtyard beyond; tense mood. Small distant figures, no violence. Hibiscus trees and rooftops of Chengdu frame the scene. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties court painting in the manner of Huang Quan, fine line, rich colour on silk.
nine-classics-printed: 932 CE, Luoyang: a busy printing workshop, craftsmen carving wooden blocks with knives, others inking blocks with brushes and pressing paper sheets, stacks of printed pages drying on racks, no legible text; scholars in caps proofreading. Daylight. Shelves of finished blocks line the walls, and apprentices carry bundles of printed sheets to a binding table. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties handscroll, fine line, ink and light colour on silk.
death-of-qian-liu: 932 CE, Hangzhou: a funeral procession of white-clad mourners and officials winds along the shore of the West Lake, past seawalls and irrigated fields along the Qiantang River, pagodas on the hills; misty light. Banners and parasols lead the long procession, boats on the lake carry more mourners, and farmers pause in the fields to bow as it passes. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties blue-green landscape, mineral colours on silk.
li-congke-takes-throne: 934 CE, Luoyang: a rebel army from Fengxiang marches into the eastern capital as the court's troops lay down their banners and join them, officials bowing at the city gate. Distant view, autumn light, many small figures. Cavalry ride beneath tall banners, while townspeople line the streets and watch from doorways. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties monumental landscape, ink and light colour on silk.
later-tang-falls: 936 CE, Luoyang: a tall palace tower wrapped in smoke and fire seen from afar, the palace walls deserted, Khitan-backed troops approaching the city across the plain; dark winter sky. Symbolic, no figures in the flames. Courtiers and townspeople flee along the roads out of the city with carts and bundles. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties monumental landscape, ink and light colour on silk.
kaifeng-capital-938: 938 CE, Bianjing (Kaifeng): a busy canal city on the plain, grain barges crowding the Bian canal past bridges and warehouses, a new palace being expanded, crowds in the streets; flat landscape. Daylight. Officials in black caps oversee the building works, porters carry goods across arched bridges and shops line the waterfront. Painted in the style of a Northern Song Qingming-scroll-style handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, many small figures.
liao-southern-capital: 938 CE, Youzhou (Beijing): Khitan horsemen in fur caps and long robes ride through the gates of a walled northern city, Han officials in caps welcoming them; the Yanshan mountains behind, felt tents outside the walls. Winter light. Painted in the style of a Liao steppe painting in the manner of Hu Gui, fine ink and light colour on silk.
huajian-ji: 940 CE, Chengdu: an evening banquet in a garden pavilion, poets in robes, singing girls in high-waisted dresses with pipa and flutes, a scholar compiling song lyrics on paper rolls; flowers, lanterns and willows. Servants carry wine jars and dishes along a covered corridor. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties court painting in the manner of Gu Hongzhong's Night Revels, fine line, rich colour on silk.
zhang-yuxian-rising: 942 CE, eastern Guangdong near Huizhou: peasant rebels with bamboo spears and banners gather in green hills above rice paddies and a riverside walled town; subtropical trees, misty mountains. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Smoke rises over the town where tax granaries burn, and southern troops with banners approach along a river road in the distance. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties blue-green landscape, mineral colours on silk.
li-jing-succeeds: 943 CE, Jinling (Nanjing): a palace hall of Southern Tang with elegant halls, a new ruler seen small and from behind ascending the throne steps, officials bowing; on a side table lie alchemical bottles of the late emperor. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties court painting in the manner of Zhou Wenju, fine line, soft colour on silk.
min-civil-war: 943 CE, Jianzhou (Jian'ou) in northern Fujian: two armies face each other across a mountain river in steep green valleys, banners of each side on opposite banks, river boats; mist on the peaks. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Walled towns sit on hilltops above the river, and refugees with bundles trudge along the mountain paths. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties blue-green landscape, mineral colours on silk.
old-book-of-tang: 945 CE, Bianjing (Kaifeng): a palace archive hall where historians in caps and robes sit among tall stacks of paper rolls and court records, compiling history; a senior official presenting bound volumes on a lacquer tray. Calm daylight. Scribes copy pages at low tables, and assistants carry bundles of rolls from tall wooden shelves. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties court painting, fine line, soft colour on silk.
battle-of-yangcheng: 945 CE, Yangcheng near Baoding: a yellow sandstorm sweeps across a Hebei plain as an army breaks out of its encirclement and routs Khitan cavalry; a lone rider in the distance flees on a camel. Distant panoramic view, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Liao steppe painting in the manner of Hu Gui, ink and ochre wash on silk.
du-chongwei-surrenders: 946 CE, Zhongdu Bridge near Zhengding: a great army on the bank of the Hutuo River lays down its weapons and banners in neat piles, Khitan horsemen in fur caps receiving them; a stone bridge across the river, winter fields. Distant view, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties monumental landscape, ink and light colour on silk.
kr-armistice: 1953, Panmunjom, Korea: a plain wooden hut in a bare field of trampled grass, with two long tables inside and small groups of uniformed delegates, military officers in khaki and olive drab, seated apart; army trucks and jeeps parked outside, a few guards, low autumn-brown hills and leafless trees beyond under an overcast summer sky. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour illustration, soft greys and khaki, loose brushwork, calm and neutral, many small figures seen from a distance.
kr-juche: 1955, Pyongyang, Korea: one single unified wide view across the broad Taedong River toward a city rising from postwar rubble, plain new concrete apartment blocks wrapped in timber scaffolding, small workers in padded jackets carrying bricks on shoulder poles along the embankment, a low modest lecture hall at the riverside with a few cadres filing in, distant hills under a pale spring sky. Rendered as one continuous restrained black-and-white woodcut print with fine gouged lines and grey wash, a single scene with no borders, panels or insets, neutral documentary mood, no banners, no portraits, no text, small figures only.
kr-april-revolution: 1960, Seoul, Korea: a wide boulevard lined with low Japanese-era stone buildings and leafy plane trees, crowds of university and high-school students in dark uniforms and caps marching shoulder to shoulder, seen from a distance, a few trams halted and onlookers on pavements, spring blossoms and the granite peaks of Bukhansan beyond. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, warm April daylight, many small figures, calm and neutral composition with no blank placards.
kr-may-16: 1961, Seoul, Korea: before dawn, a column of army trucks and soldiers in steel helmets crosses the Han River bridge into a quiet sleeping city, headlights glowing in mist, a few tanks waiting near low government buildings with tiled roofs, empty streets, Namsan hill dark against a lightening sky. Painted as a subdued documentary watercolour in grey-blue and olive tones, distant small figures, still and neutral atmosphere, no flags or insignia shown in detail.
kr-han-miracle: 1962, Ulsan, South Korea: a coastal bay where a new industrial complex is being built, bulldozers levelling rice fields, the steel skeleton of a refinery and tall chimneys going up, workers in caps and cotton jackets pushing carts, fishing boats in the harbour and green hills behind, smoke drifting over the sea in bright morning light. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, broad flat colour planes, many small figures, optimistic but neutral tone.
kr-saemaul: 1970, Cheongdo, rural South Korea: a farming village in a green valley where villagers in work clothes widen a dirt lane, lay a small concrete bridge over a stream and replace straw-thatched roofs with new slate and tin roofs, children watching, persimmon trees and terraced rice paddies around, an ox cart nearby, low mountains under a clear summer sky. Painted as a soft documentary watercolour echoing Joseon genre-painting composition, earthy greens and browns, many small figures.
kr-park-assassinated: 1979, Seoul, Korea: an October night outside a quiet walled compound of low traditional-style buildings near the presidential grounds, warm light glowing behind paper screens, black sedans parked in the courtyard, a few guards standing in the shadows, autumn ginkgo leaves on the ground and the dark ridge of Bugaksan above. Rendered as a sombre documentary watercolour in deep blues and amber, no people shown up close, still and restrained, conveying tension only through the empty night scene.
kr-gwangju: 1980, Gwangju, South Korea: a calm wide view of the city's central square in late May, the granite fountain and the old provincial government building with its clock, crowds of townspeople gathered at a distance, scattered shoes and leaflets on the paving, green hills of Mudeungsan behind under a hazy spring sky. Painted as a quiet black-and-white woodcut with grey ink wash, solemn and neutral, many tiny figures, no weapons or violence shown.
kr-june-struggle: 1987, Seoul, South Korea: a broad avenue in front of modern office towers and an old cathedral on a hill, filled from end to end with crowds of students and office workers in white shirts, seen from high above, traffic stopped, a faint haze in the June air and scattered paper on the asphalt. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, soft summer light, thousands of small figures, calm and neutral, no banners with lettering.
kr-seoul-olympics: 1988, Seoul Olympic Stadium, South Korea: the curved white concrete stadium with its sweeping roof by the Han River, packed stands of spectators, athletes in colourful tracksuits parading on the red running track, a large flock of white doves rising into a clear autumn sky, the city's apartment towers and mountains in the distance. Painted as a bright documentary watercolour illustration, crisp September light, thousands of tiny figures, no logos or lettering.
kr-kim-il-sung-dies: 1994, Pyongyang, North Korea: a broad empty plaza beside the Taedong River in midsummer, long lines of mourners in dark clothes laying flowers at a distance, monumental grey buildings and a tall stone tower across the water, overcast sky, and beyond the city a stretch of dry, thin rice fields hinting at hard times ahead. Painted as a subdued documentary watercolour in muted greys and greens, tiny figures, no statues or portraits shown, calm and neutral.
kr-summit-2000: 2000, Pyongyang airport, North Korea: a white passenger jet parked on a broad grey tarmac in June, a small group of officials in dark suits gathered at the foot of the stairway seen from far away, rows of welcoming people in bright traditional hanbok holding paper flowers, low hills and the hazy city skyline beyond. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, soft summer light, small anonymous figures, calm and neutral.
kr-nuclear-test: 2006, Punggye-ri, North Korea: a remote rugged mountain range of granite peaks in autumn, with a small tunnel entrance and gravel road cut into a slope, a few low sheds and parked trucks, a faint plume of dust drifting from the hillside, bare larch forests and a cold grey sky. Painted as a sober documentary watercolour in slate, ochre and grey, empty landscape, no people in close view, no explosion or flames.
kr-panmunjom-2018: 2018, Panmunjom, Korean Demilitarized Zone: the row of pale blue conference huts straddling a low concrete strip on the border line, a neat lawn and a small pine tree newly planted with a spade beside it, grey stone buildings on both sides, empty of people, a soft April spring sky and green hills beyond. Painted as a quiet documentary watercolour in pale blues and greens, a calm landscape-only composition with no figures.
kr-martial-law-2024: 2024, Seoul, South Korea: a cold December night outside the National Assembly building with its large green dome, floodlit on the bank of the Han River, a crowd of citizens in winter coats gathered on the lawns at a distance, police buses parked along the road, city lights and bridges reflected in the dark water. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, deep blues and warm lamplight, tiny anonymous figures only, calm and neutral.
mx-maize-farming-spreads: c. 3000 BCE, the Tehuacán Valley, Puebla, Mexico: a dry valley of cactus and thorn scrub ringed by mountains, a small family group in simple woven plant-fibre garments tending small plots of early maize with short cobs, digging sticks in hand, baskets of seeds and grinding stones near a rock shelter, squash vines on the ground, warm afternoon light. Painted in the flat outlines and earthy reds and ochres of a Mixtec-codex-style painting on deerskin.
mx-paso-de-la-amada: c. 1650 BCE, Paso de la Amada, Chiapas, Mexico: a village of thatched wattle-and-daub houses on low earthen mounds near the Pacific coastal plain, a long flat earthen court with raised side embankments where young men play with a heavy rubber ball using their hips, villagers watching from the slopes, palms and mangroves around, golden evening light. Painted in the style of Mesoamerican ceramic painting, red and cream slip with dark outline figures.
mx-el-manati-rubber-balls: c. 1600 BCE, El Manatí, Veracruz, Mexico: a sacred freshwater spring at the foot of a low hill in tropical forest, villagers in loincloths kneeling at the water's edge and setting dark rubber balls, jadeite axes and wooden objects into the clear pool, rubber trees with cut bark nearby, morning mist over the water. Painted in the style of Olmec-era earthy murals as reimagined in a codex palette, red ochre, black and green, simple bold outlines.
mx-san-lorenzo: c. 1400 BCE, San Lorenzo, Veracruz, Mexico: a great artificial earthen plateau above the Coatzacoalcos river floodplain, with clay platforms topped by thatched buildings, stone drain channels, and a large carved basalt monument being set in place by workers with ropes, canoes on the river below, tropical forest all around. Painted in the style of a Mesoamerican mural, flat red, ochre and green pigments, bold dark outlines, many small figures.
mx-olmec-colossal-heads: c. 1200 BCE, San Lorenzo, Veracruz, Mexico: teams of workers haul a huge rough basalt boulder on log rollers and a balsa raft along a river from the distant blue Tuxtla mountains, while nearby sculptors with stone hammers shape a colossal head wearing a helmet-like headdress, its broad face turned away; thatched huts and forest around. Painted in an earthy Mesoamerican mural style, ochre, black and jade-green, flat forms and bold outlines.
mx-la-venta: c. 900 BCE, La Venta, Tabasco, Mexico: an island city among swamps and rivers, with a tall fluted clay pyramid, long plazas and low mounds, priests in feathered headdresses laying polished jade celts and serpentine blocks into a buried offering pit, colossal stone heads standing in the plaza, palm-thatched houses and canoes in the waterways. Painted in an Olmec-inspired Mesoamerican mural style, jade green, red ochre and cream, bold outlines.
mx-zapotec-writing: c. 600 BCE, San José Mogote, Oaxaca, Mexico: a hilltop village of adobe houses and a stone-faced temple platform overlooking the green Valley of Oaxaca, a carver kneeling to cut glyphs and a simple calendar sign into a flat stone slab set as a threshold, onlookers in cotton mantles behind, dry mountains beyond. Painted in Zapotec-Mixtec codex style, flat red, yellow and black on cream deerskin, stylised figures, no legible writing.
mx-monte-alban: c. 500 BCE, Monte Albán, Oaxaca, Mexico: on a mountaintop high above the broad Valley of Oaxaca, crowds of Zapotec workers level the summit with baskets of earth and stone, laying out a long plaza with the first terraced stone platforms and stairways, smoke from valley villages far below, blue mountains and clear dry-season sky. Painted in the style of a Mixtec-Zapotec codex, flat bright colours on cream ground, bold black outlines, many small figures.
mx-olmec-decline: c. 400 BCE, La Venta, Tabasco, Mexico: the abandoned Olmec island city, its clay pyramid overgrown with grass and young trees, a colossal stone head half-sunk in mud and vines, the river channel silted and shifted away, a few families with bundles paddling canoes off into the swamp, herons and dawn mist. Painted in an earthy Mesoamerican mural style, faded ochre, jade green and grey, quiet and melancholy.
mx-el-mirador: c. 300 BCE, El Mirador, Petén, Guatemala: a vast Preclassic Maya city in dense rainforest, the immense La Danta pyramid with stucco-plastered terraces painted red rising above the canopy, raised white limestone causeways stretching off through the jungle, crowds of workers and traders walking along them, smoke rising from plastered plazas at sunrise. Painted in the style of a Maya mural, Maya blue, red and ochre with fine black outlines.
mx-long-count-date: 36 BCE, Chiapa de Corzo, Chiapas, Mexico: a town of stone platforms and thatched houses above the Grijalva river canyon, a scribe-priest in a cotton mantle and simple headdress standing beside a newly carved stone stela with columns of bar-and-dot numerals, villagers gathered in the plaza around it, river and green hills beyond in morning light. Painted in Maya codex style, red and black on cream bark paper, stylised figures, no legible glyphs.
mx-pyramid-of-the-sun: c. 100 CE, Teotihuacan, Valley of Mexico: the enormous terraced Pyramid of the Sun under construction with workers carrying baskets of earth and stone up ramps, the long straight Avenue of the Dead stretching toward the distant Pyramid of the Moon and Cerro Gordo mountain, plastered apartment compounds spreading in a grid, dry-season blue sky. Painted in the style of a Teotihuacan mural, flat red, green and ochre, stylised figures with bold outlines.
mx-feathered-serpent-temple: c. 200 CE, Teotihuacan, Valley of Mexico: inside the great walled Ciudadela enclosure, a stepped temple faced with rows of carved stone feathered-serpent heads and goggle-eyed headdress masks painted in red, green and white, priests in feathered costumes on the stairway and a crowd in the plaza below, mountains on the horizon. Painted in the style of a Teotihuacan mural, flat red ground, green and ochre, bold outlines, no violence shown.
mx-siyaj-kak-tikal: 378 CE, Tikal, Petén, Guatemala: a column of warriors in Teotihuacan-style goggled headdresses and feathered shields, carrying atlatl spear-throwers, marching along a white causeway into the Maya city of stuccoed temple-pyramids rising from the rainforest canopy, Maya nobles in jade and quetzal plumes waiting on the plaza steps. Painted in the style of a Classic Maya mural, Maya blue, red and ochre, fine black outlines, many small figures.
mx-copan-dynasty: 426 CE, Copán, Honduras: a green river valley ringed by forested hills, with a small new temple-platform painted red and decorated with stucco masks, a new Maya ruler in a feathered headdress and goggle-like eye ornaments seen from behind as nobles bow, cornfields and thatched houses along the river, morning mist. Painted in the style of a Classic Maya mural, Maya blue, red and cream, fine black outlines.
mx-teotihuacan-falls: c. 550 CE, Teotihuacan, Valley of Mexico: plumes of smoke rising from the temples and palaces lining the long Avenue of the Dead, charred roof beams and toppled sculptures on the stairways, the great Pyramid of the Sun standing above, small groups of people leaving the city with bundles toward the dry hills, a hazy orange sky. Painted in the style of a Teotihuacan mural, faded red, ochre and grey, stylised figures, no bodies.
mx-caracol-defeats-tikal: 562 CE, Caracol, Belize: on a jungle-covered plateau, Caracol's great Caana pyramid-palace rises above plazas where victorious Maya warriors in jaguar-skin tunics and feathered headdresses return with captured war banners and bundles of tribute, nobles watching from the stairs, terraced maize fields around and rainforest rolling to the horizon. Painted in the style of a Maya mural like Bonampak, Maya blue, red and ochre, fine outlines, no bloodshed.
mx-pakal: 615 CE, Palenque, Chiapas, Mexico: a white limestone palace with corbel-vaulted galleries and mansard roofs on a forested hillside above the plain, a young boy king, seen small from behind, receiving a jade-and-feather headdress from his mother on a throne platform while nobles kneel, waterfalls and jungle around. Painted in the style of a Classic Maya mural and stucco relief, Maya blue, red ochre and cream, fine black outlines.
mx-temple-of-inscriptions: 683 CE, Palenque, Chiapas, Mexico: a stepped limestone pyramid temple against a forested hill, a procession of nobles carrying torches down a narrow vaulted stairway inside, and in a deep stone crypt a great carved limestone sarcophagus lid with a jade mosaic mask and jade beads laid beside it, flickering torchlight. Painted in the style of a Classic Maya mural, red, Maya blue and ochre, fine outlines, no body shown.
mx-bonampak-murals: c. 790 CE, Bonampak, Chiapas, Mexico: inside a small three-room stone temple in the rainforest, Maya painters on wooden scaffolds by torchlight brush brilliant murals onto plastered walls, showing processions of musicians, nobles in white mantles and warriors; bowls of Maya blue, red and ochre pigment at their feet, apprentices grinding colour. Painted in the style of the Bonampak murals themselves, Maya blue ground, bright figures with fine black outlines, no violence shown.
mx-classic-maya-collapse: c. 800-900 CE, Tikal, Petén, Guatemala: the great stone temple-pyramids of Tikal standing silent above plazas overgrown with grass, a half-finished stela lying uncarved beside its quarry, dried-up reservoirs cracked in drought, a few families carrying bundles along an empty causeway into the forest, vines creeping up the stairways, pale dusty sky. Painted in a faded Classic Maya mural style, muted red, ochre and Maya blue, melancholy mood.
mx-chichen-itza: c. 900 CE, Chichén Itzá, Yucatán, Mexico: the four-sided stepped pyramid of El Castillo with serpent balustrades on its stairways rising over a flat scrub-forest plain, beside it the long Great Ballcourt with high walls and stone rings, crowds of Maya and Toltec-style warriors and traders filling the plaza, white sacbe roads and a cenote nearby, bright midday sun. Painted in the style of a Maya mural, red, Maya blue and ochre, fine outlines.
mx-el-tajin: c. 900 CE, El Tajín, Veracruz, Mexico: a city in green hills near the Gulf coast, with the Pyramid of the Niches, its many terraces lined with small square recesses painted red and dark, and several stone ballcourts with carved walls, players in padded yokes and spectators on the slopes, tropical forest and drifting rain clouds. Painted in Gulf-coast Mesoamerican mural style, red, black and cream, bold scrolling outlines.
mx-tula: c. 950 CE, Tula, Hidalgo, Mexico: on a ridge above a dry valley, the Toltec temple pyramid crowned by four tall basalt warrior columns wearing butterfly breastplates and feathered headdresses, colonnaded halls below, Toltec warriors in quilted cotton armour and merchants crossing the plaza, cactus and maize fields around, bright dry-season sky. Painted in the style of an Aztec codex such as the Codex Mendoza, flat colours on cream paper, bold black outlines.
mx-eight-deer: c. 1100 CE, Tilantongo, Oaxaca, Mexico: in the rugged pine-covered mountains of the Mixteca, a Mixtec ruler wearing a jaguar-claw headdress leads warriors with round shields and spears toward a hilltop town of stone platforms, enemy lords kneeling with gifts of quetzal feathers and gold, rivers winding through terraced valleys. Painted in the style of a Mixtec screenfold codex like the Codex Zouche-Nuttall, flat red, yellow and blue on white deerskin, no legible glyphs.
mx-tula-falls: c. 1150 CE, Tula, Hidalgo, Mexico: smoke rising from the burned temples and colonnaded halls of the Toltec capital, the stone warrior columns toppled and broken on the ground, and on the dry plain below bands of northern Chichimec migrants in hide garments carrying bows and bundles walk southward past the ruins. Painted in Aztec-codex style, flat ochre, red and turquoise on cream paper, bold outlines, stylised figures, no bodies.
mx-mayapan: c. 1220 CE, Mayapán, Yucatán, Mexico: a walled Maya city on the flat limestone plain, a smaller copy of El Castillo pyramid rising over crowded thatched houses and stone-walled house lots, Maya lords in feathered headdresses gathering in a colonnaded council hall, the long encircling stone wall with gateways, scrub forest and cenotes beyond, hot afternoon light. Painted in the style of a Late Postclassic Maya codex, red, blue and black on cream.
mx-mexica-arrive: c. 1250 CE, Chapultepec, Valley of Mexico: a rocky wooded hill with cypress trees beside the shining Lake Texcoco, a band of Mexica migrants in simple maguey-fibre cloaks carrying bundles, bows and a wrapped sacred effigy, setting up reed huts at the foot of the hill, lakeside towns and volcanoes Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl in the distance. Painted in the style of an Aztec migration codex such as the Codex Boturini, sparse red and black on cream.
mx-tarascan-state: c. 1300 CE, Tzintzuntzan, Michoacán, Mexico: on the shore of the blue Lake Pátzcuaro, Purépecha lords gather at a hillside town of T-shaped stone yácata platforms, a ruler in a feathered headdress, seen from behind, receiving chiefs who arrive by dugout canoe with nets and copper goods, pine-covered volcanic hills around, misty morning. Painted in the style of the Relación de Michoacán colonial manuscript illustrations, ink line and soft watercolour.
mx-tenochtitlan-founded: 1325 CE, Lake Texcoco, Valley of Mexico: a small rocky island amid reeds and shallow blue water, where a golden eagle perches on a prickly-pear cactus, and a group of Mexica people in maguey-fibre cloaks stand and kneel in their dugout canoes gazing up at it, distant snow-capped volcanoes and lakeside towns. Painted in the style of an Aztec codex like the Codex Mendoza frontispiece, flat turquoise, green and red on cream paper, bold outlines.
mx-triple-alliance: 1428 CE, Valley of Mexico: three groups of Nahua lords in feathered cloaks, jewelled headdresses and turquoise ornaments, from Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan, meet on reed mats beside the lake, warriors with feathered shields and obsidian-edged clubs behind them, the city of Azcapotzalco smoking across the water after its defeat, volcanoes beyond. Painted in Aztec codex style, flat bright colours on cream amate paper, bold outlines, no legible glyphs.
mx-moctezuma-i: c. 1440 CE, Tenochtitlan, Valley of Mexico: the island city with whitewashed temples and canals, porters with tumplines carrying tribute of cotton mantles, cacao beans, jaguar skins, feathers and jade into the palace courtyard, officials on mats keeping tallies, the emperor seated far back on a reed throne under a canopy, canoes crowding the lake. Painted in the style of the Codex Mendoza tribute pages, flat colours on cream paper, bold outlines.
mx-flower-war: c. 1450 CE, near Tlaxcala, central Mexico: on a broad grassy plain below the Malinche volcano, two lines of warriors in feathered jaguar and eagle suits with round shields and wooden clubs edged with obsidian meet at a distance in ritual combat, captives being led away with ropes, the hill towns of Tlaxcala beyond. Painted in Aztec codex style like the Codex Mendoza, flat red, ochre and turquoise, bold outlines, no blood shown.
mx-templo-mayor: 1487 CE, Tenochtitlan, Valley of Mexico: the enlarged Great Temple, a massive stepped pyramid with twin shrines on top, one painted red and white for Huitzilopochtli and one blue and white for Tlaloc, smoke of copal incense rising, huge crowds of people in white mantles filling the sacred precinct, canals and causeways beyond. Painted in Aztec codex style like the Codex Durán, bright flat colours, many small figures, no blood or sacrifice shown.
mx-moctezuma-ii: 1502 CE, Tenochtitlan, Valley of Mexico: a great palace courtyard of whitewashed stone and carved cedar beams, nobles in feathered cloaks bowing barefoot with eyes lowered toward a canopied throne where a ruler sits small and distant wearing a turquoise diadem, attendants with feather fans, gardens and canals beyond. Painted in the style of an Aztec codex like the Florentine Codex illustrations, flat colours with ink outline, no face in detail.
mx-cortes-lands: 1519, Veracruz, Gulf coast of Mexico: eleven Spanish carracks and caravels anchored off a hot sandy beach, small boats landing soldiers in steel morion helmets and breastplates, horses, bronze cannon and crates, a cross being raised and timber huts begun, Totonac people watching from the dunes with palm-leaf shade, tropical forest behind. Painted in the style of the Lienzo de Tlaxcala, a colonial-era native pictorial manuscript, ink line with soft colour on cloth.
mx-noche-triste: 1520, Tenochtitlan, Valley of Mexico: a rainy night on the long causeway across Lake Texcoco, Spanish soldiers with horses and their Tlaxcalan allies hurrying west, gaps in the causeway where bridges are gone, Aztec warriors in war canoes approaching through the dark water, the city's temples behind lit by torches. Painted in the style of the Lienzo de Tlaxcala native manuscript, ink line and muted colour, stylised small figures, no bodies or blood.
mx-smallpox-1520: 1520, Tenochtitlan, Valley of Mexico: a quiet neighbourhood of adobe houses and canals, people lying wrapped in cotton blankets on reed mats under awnings, others tending them with water jars and herbs, empty canoes drifting in a canal, smoke of incense rising from a small shrine. Painted in the style of the Florentine Codex illustrations, sixteenth-century native ink line with soft watercolour, restrained and sorrowful, no visible sores or bodies in close view.
mx-fall-of-tenochtitlan: 1521, Tenochtitlan in the Valley of Mexico: smoke rising over the shattered island city, its stepped temples and houses partly demolished. On the lake float a few small Spanish brigantines, low open boats about a dozen metres long with a single mast and lateen or square sail and rows of oars, no tall three-masted ships and no ocean galleons. Armoured Spanish soldiers and thousands of Tlaxcalan allies with feathered shields fill the causeways; a lone canoe of Aztec nobles is intercepted in the distance. Painted in the style of the Lienzo de Tlaxcala, ink line and flat colour, no bodies. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-conquest-of-guatemala: 1524, Iximche, Guatemala highlands: a Kaqchikel Maya hilltop city of stone temples and palace platforms on a plateau between deep ravines, a column of Spanish cavalry in steel helmets and breastplates with lances and their Nahua allies in cotton armour arriving across a pine-covered plain, volcanoes on the horizon. Painted in the style of the Lienzo de Quauhquechollan, a colonial-era native painted cloth map, ink line and soft colour.
mx-grito-de-dolores: 1810, Dolores, Guanajuato, Mexico: before dawn on 16 September, a modest baroque parish church with a bell tower in a small town plaza, an elderly priest in a black cassock seen from behind on the church steps, villagers in sarapes and straw sombreros gathering with lanterns, farm tools and machetes, the bell ringing in the tower, dark hills behind. Painted as a nineteenth-century Mexican oil history painting, warm lantern light and deep shadows.
mx-mexican-independence: 1821, Mexico City: the Army of the Three Guarantees enters the great central plaza on 27 September, columns of cavalry and infantry in tall shakos and sashes riding past the baroque cathedral and the long viceregal palace, crowds of townspeople on balconies and rooftops waving, church bells ringing, volcanoes faint in the distance. Painted as a nineteenth-century Mexican oil history painting, festive bright daylight, many small figures, flags without emblems.
mx-mexican-american-war: 1847, Mexico City: blue-uniformed United States infantry and artillery march into the vast central plaza before the baroque cathedral and the National Palace, Mexican townspeople in rebozos and sarapes watching silently from the edges, smoke drifting from distant Chapultepec castle on its hill, grey September sky. Painted as a nineteenth-century lithograph after a war artist's drawing, hand-coloured, many small figures, no fallen soldiers shown.
mx-battle-of-puebla: 1862, Puebla, Mexico: on 5 May, French infantry in red trousers and kepis advance up the slopes toward the hilltop forts of Loreto and Guadalupe, Mexican soldiers in dark uniforms and peasant volunteers defending the stone walls, cannon smoke drifting across the hills, the domed city of Puebla below and the volcanoes Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl beyond. Painted as a nineteenth-century oil battle panorama, figures small and distant, no bodies.
mx-porfiriato: c. 1890, central Mexico: a steam locomotive with a long train crossing a new iron trestle bridge over a dry ravine, telegraph poles along the track, a grand hacienda with arcades and fields of maguey where barefoot peasants in white cotton and wide sombreros labour, top-hatted visitors on a station platform, mountains behind. Painted in the style of José María Velasco's nineteenth-century Mexican landscape oils, clear luminous light, small figures.
mx-mexican-revolution: 1910, northern Mexico: a dusty railway station on a high desert plain, bands of rebels in wide sombreros, white cotton shirts and crossed cartridge bandoliers mounting horses and climbing onto boxcars, women with rebozos handing up baskets, a steam locomotive puffing smoke, cactus and dry mountains under a vast blue sky. Rendered as an early twentieth-century Mexican woodcut print in the manner of the Taller de Gráfica Popular, bold black gouged lines, small figures, no flags with lettering.
mx-plan-of-ayala: 1911, Ayala, Morelos, Mexico: sugar-cane fields and a stone hacienda with an aqueduct in a green valley under volcanoes, a gathering of peasant farmers in white cotton clothes and broad straw sombreros, some on horseback with rifles, standing in a village square around a simple table where a paper is being read aloud, a whitewashed chapel behind. Painted in the style of a Mexican muralist fresco, earthy reds, ochres and greens, sturdy simplified figures, no faces in close view.
mx-constitution-1917: 1917, Querétaro, Mexico: the interior of a neoclassical theatre with tiers of red-velvet boxes and gilded balconies, rows of delegates in dark suits and some in military uniforms seated in the stalls facing a long table on the stage, papers stacked on it, winter light falling through high windows. Painted as a restrained early twentieth-century oil history painting, warm reds and gold, many small figures seen from the back of the hall, no legible documents.
mx-oil-expropriation: 1938, Mexico City: in front of the baroque cathedral and the long colonial National Palace, a vast crowd of townspeople, workers in overalls and women in rebozos filling the Zócalo, some carrying hens and small household goods as contributions, while beyond the city, oil derricks and storage tanks are glimpsed on a distant plain. Rendered as a 1930s Mexican linocut print, bold black and white with touches of red, many small figures, no lettering.
mx-zapatista-uprising: 1994, San Cristóbal de las Casas, Chiapas, Mexico: on a misty New Year's morning, the colonial town plaza with its yellow cathedral and arcaded municipal palace, small groups of indigenous people in dark wool tunics and knitted caps standing quietly at a distance, pine-covered highland mountains behind, scattered townspeople watching from doorways. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft grey and ochre tones, tiny anonymous figures, calm and neutral, no weapons shown in detail.
me-cuneiform-matures: c. 3000 BCE, Uruk, southern Mesopotamia: inside a mud-brick temple storeroom, Sumerian scribes with shaved heads and fleece-tufted kilts sit cross-legged pressing reed styluses into small damp clay tablets, baskets of tablets and sealed jars of barley around them, sunlight through a doorway showing the white-plastered temple platform outside. Painted in the style of an inlaid Sumerian shell-and-lapis panel, flat figures in profile, lapis blue, red and cream, no legible signs.
me-gilgamesh-of-uruk: c. 2700 BCE, Uruk, southern Mesopotamia: hundreds of workers in fleece kilts carry baskets of mud bricks and lay them in long courses to raise a great city wall with towers, a bearded king in a long robe and tall cap watching small and distant from atop the rampart, date palms, canals and the Euphrates marshes beyond. Painted in the style of a Sumerian shell-inlay panel, lapis blue background, flat profile figures in registers.
me-royal-cemetery-of-ur: c. 2600 BCE, Ur, southern Mesopotamia: a deep mud-brick-lined burial pit by torchlight, filled with grave goods laid out in rows: a lyre with a gold bull's head, gold cups and headdresses of gold leaves, carnelian and lapis beads, a wooden panel inlaid with shell scenes, an ox-drawn sledge, attendants in fine robes standing at a distance at the pit's edge. Painted in Sumerian inlay style, lapis blue, gold and red, flat forms, no bodies shown.
me-stele-of-the-vultures: c. 2450 BCE, Lagash, southern Mesopotamia: a phalanx of Sumerian soldiers in leather caps behind a wall of tall rectangular shields with spears levelled, marching across flat irrigated fields and canals toward a distant enemy city, a king in a chariot drawn by onagers at their head, vultures circling high in the sky. Rendered in the style of a Sumerian limestone stele relief, low flat carving in registers, pale stone tones, no bodies shown.
me-sargon-founds-akkad: c. 2334 BCE, Mesopotamia: a long column of Akkadian soldiers with bows, axes and javelins marches along the Euphrates past conquered Sumerian cities with ziggurats and walls, envoys bringing tribute of cedar logs and metal ingots, a bearded king in a tall headdress walking small and distant at their head, palms and canals around. Painted in the style of an Akkadian stone victory relief, warm sandstone tones with touches of lapis and red.
me-enheduanna: c. 2285 BCE, Ur, southern Mesopotamia: on the terrace of a mud-brick temple of the moon god, a high priestess in a flounced woollen robe and a rolled-brim headdress, seen small in profile, leads a procession of attendants carrying offerings of dates and libation vessels toward an altar, a crescent moon rising over the city and palms at dusk. Rendered in the style of a Sumerian carved alabaster disk relief, cream stone with touches of lapis.
me-naram-sin-stele: c. 2250 BCE, Zagros Mountains: Akkadian soldiers with spears and standards climb a steep forested mountain slope in ranks, defeated Lullubi mountain warriors in short tunics retreating and kneeling above, a king in a horned helmet small near the summit, a great rock peak with stars in the sky above. Rendered in the style of the Akkadian sandstone victory stele, warm pinkish stone relief, diagonal composition, no bodies or blood shown.
me-gutian-conquest: c. 2190 BCE, Akkad, Mesopotamia: under a dusty sky after drought, cracked dry irrigation canals and withered barley fields surround a mud-brick city, while bands of mountain warriors from the Zagros in sheepskin cloaks, with axes and bows, ride donkeys down from the hills toward its gates, smoke rising from outlying villages. Painted in the style of a Mesopotamian cylinder-seal impression and stone relief, flat profile figures, earth and sand tones.
me-ur-nammu-founds-ur-iii: c. 2112 BCE, Ur, southern Mesopotamia: the great stepped mud-brick ziggurat of Ur under construction, with three long stairways and terraces, workers with baskets and bricks, scribes with tablets recording rations, provincial officials arriving by reed boat along the canal, date palm groves and the Euphrates beyond. Painted in the style of a Neo-Sumerian stone relief of the Ur-Nammu stele, flat registers, warm buff stone with lapis-blue sky.
me-fall-of-ur: c. 2004 BCE, Ur, southern Mesopotamia: columns of smoke rising from the walls and temple quarter of Ur, its ziggurat dark against an orange sky, Elamite soldiers with spears and bows leading a long line of captives and carts of loot away along a canal, palm groves burning in the distance. Painted in the style of a Mesopotamian stone relief, flat profile figures in registers, ochre, black and pale stone, no bodies shown.
me-kanesh-trade: c. 1950 BCE, Kanesh, central Anatolia: a caravan of black donkeys laden with tin ingots and bales of woollen textiles arriving at a busy merchant quarter of stone-and-mud-brick houses below a high citadel mound, Assyrian traders in fringed robes greeting local Anatolians, a merchant inside a house sealing clay letters in envelopes, dry hills and snowy Mount Erciyes behind. Painted in the style of an Old Assyrian cylinder-seal impression and Anatolian pottery painting, earth reds and buff.
me-hammurabi-unites: c. 1763 BCE, southern Mesopotamia: a Babylonian army of spearmen and archers with chariots camped outside the walls of Larsa, engineers diverting a canal to flood the plain, envoys from the city coming out to kneel, palm groves and flat fields stretching to the horizon, the Babylonian king small and distant before his tent. Painted in the style of an Old Babylonian terracotta plaque and stone relief, warm earth tones, flat profile figures.
me-code-of-hammurabi: c. 1754 BCE, Babylon, Mesopotamia: in a temple courtyard of mud brick, a tall polished black basalt stele stands with a carved scene at its top of a seated sun god handing a rod and ring to a king, its lower surface densely covered in tiny lines of carving, citizens in fringed robes gathered to look at it, scribes nearby. Rendered in the style of an Old Babylonian relief, black basalt and buff stone, no legible writing.
me-hittite-old-kingdom: c. 1650 BCE, Hattusa, central Anatolia: a rocky ridge above a gorge with new massive stone and mud-brick fortification walls being built, a Hittite king in a long robe and skullcap seen from behind, surveying the works with officers, war chariots with six-spoked wheels parked below, rolling grassland and distant hills. Painted in the style of a Hittite stone orthostat relief, flat profile figures, grey stone and ochre tones.
me-hittites-sack-babylon: c. 1595 BCE, Babylon, Mesopotamia: a Hittite army with light two-horse chariots and spearmen withdrawing upriver along the Euphrates, carrying away cult statues and carts of treasure, smoke rising from the walls and temple of Babylon behind, palm groves along the riverbank and boats on the water. Painted in the style of a Hittite stone relief, flat profile figures and chariots in registers, grey stone and ochre, no bodies shown.
me-kassite-babylon: c. 1531 BCE, Babylon, Mesopotamia: Kassite horsemen and chariots from the Zagros mountains enter a partly ruined Babylon, priests in long fringed robes greet them at the gate, workers begin repairing temple walls, and a carved boundary stone with divine symbols stands beside a field, the Euphrates and palms beyond. Painted in the style of a Kassite kudurru boundary-stone relief, symbolic carved motifs, black stone and buff tones, no legible writing.
me-suppiluliuma: c. 1344 BCE, Carchemish, upper Euphrates: a Hittite army of three-man chariots and infantry with sickle swords besieging a walled city on a mound above the river, siege ramps against the walls, Mitannian envoys bringing out tribute and horses, smoke on the plain and hills of northern Syria beyond. Painted in the style of a Hittite stone orthostat relief from Carchemish, flat profile figures, basalt grey and ochre tones, no bodies.
me-battle-of-kadesh: c. 1274 BCE, Kadesh, on the Orontes River, Syria: thousands of chariots sweep across a broad plain beside the walled city of Kadesh on its mound encircled by river channels, light Egyptian two-man chariots facing heavier Hittite three-man chariots, dust clouds rising, the Egyptian camp with tents and shields in the distance. Painted in the style of an Egyptian temple relief of the battle, painted sunken carving, ochre, blue and red, many small figures in registers.
me-destruction-of-ugarit: c. 1185 BCE, Ugarit, Syrian coast: smoke and flames rising over the walled port city on its mound by the sea, the palace and stone temples burning, ships of the Sea Peoples with bird-headed prows beached in the harbour, townspeople fleeing inland with bundles and donkeys, an unfired clay tablet left in a kiln. Painted in the style of a Late Bronze Age Levantine ivory carving and Egyptian relief, flat profile figures, ochre and sea blue, no bodies.
me-fall-of-hattusa: c. 1180 BCE, Hattusa, central Anatolia: the great Hittite capital on its rocky ridge abandoned, the Lion Gate and temple walls blackened by fire, dry cracked fields around, a last file of people with ox carts leaving along a dusty road, crows on the ruined walls under a pale drought sky. Painted in the style of a Hittite stone relief, flat profile figures, ash grey and ochre tones, melancholy mood, no bodies.
me-phoenician-alphabet: c. 1050 BCE, Byblos on the Lebanese coast: a harbour town of flat-roofed stone houses climbing to a rocky promontory topped by a Phoenician temple, a walled courtyard with a plain cubic shrine and standing stone obelisks, with no Greek columns, no colonnade and no pediment. Cedar-clad mountains behind. A Phoenician scribe in a conical cap writes on a papyrus scroll while merchants load cedar logs and jars onto round-hulled ships with horse-headed prows. Painted in the style of a Phoenician carved ivory panel, ochre and Tyrian purple, no legible letters. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-kingdom-of-david: c. 1000 BCE, Jerusalem: a small walled hill town of stone houses on a narrow ridge between deep valleys, terraced olive groves and threshing floors on the slopes, Israelite tribesmen in fringed wool tunics arriving with flocks and donkeys, a few musicians with lyres at the gate, the Judean hills under a golden evening sky. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated Hebrew manuscript, flat gold and lapis tones, small figures, no individual central figure.
me-battle-of-qarqar: 853 BCE, Qarqar, on the Orontes River, Syria: an Assyrian army with heavy chariots, cavalry and archers advances across a plain toward a large coalition force of chariots, infantry and a band of camel riders, the Orontes river and a walled town beyond, dust clouds rising. Rendered in the style of an Assyrian bronze gate-band relief like those from Balawat, embossed bronze figures in narrow registers, golden-brown metal tones, no bodies shown.
me-tiglath-pileser-iii-reforms: c. 745 BCE, Nimrud, Assyria: on the banks of the Tigris, ranks of a standing Assyrian army drill before the great palace walls, soldiers with conical helmets and round shields, scribes with tablets and wax boards counting tribute, and lines of deported families with ox carts and bundles being led to new lands. Rendered in the style of a Neo-Assyrian palace alabaster relief from Nimrud, low carved registers in pale stone, no violence shown.
me-fall-of-samaria: 722 BCE, Samaria, central hill country of Israel: on a hilltop city with a stone palace and walls breached, Assyrian soldiers in conical helmets lead long lines of deported families with ox carts, donkeys and bundles down the terraced slopes toward the east, olive groves and hills under a grey sky. Rendered in the style of a Neo-Assyrian palace alabaster relief, low carved registers in pale stone, many small figures, no violence shown.
me-library-of-ashurbanipal: c. 650 BCE, Nineveh, Assyria: inside a palace hall with carved alabaster wall reliefs of lion hunts, scribes in long fringed robes sort thousands of clay tablets on wooden shelves and in baskets, others copying texts by lamplight, a courtyard and the Tigris visible through a doorway. Painted in the style of a Neo-Assyrian palace relief, flat profile figures in pale stone tones with touches of red and blue paint, no legible signs.
me-fall-of-nineveh: 612 BCE, Nineveh, Assyria: the immense walled city on the Tigris engulfed in smoke, Median horsemen and Babylonian infantry pouring through breached gates and across a flooded moat, palace roofs burning, the river and the ziggurat silhouetted against an orange sky. Rendered in the style of a Neo-Assyrian palace relief depicting a siege, carved registers of small figures in pale stone with touches of red, no bodies shown.
me-babylonian-captivity: 586 BCE, Jerusalem: smoke rising from the stone walls and the great temple on the hilltop, Babylonian soldiers in tall caps leading long lines of Judean families with bundles, donkeys and ox carts down into the Kidron valley and away along the road east, olive trees and Judean hills under a hazy sky. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript, gold leaf sky, flat jewel tones, small figures, no bodies.
me-ishtar-gate: c. 575 BCE, Babylon: the towering Ishtar Gate faced with deep blue glazed bricks bearing rows of golden aurochs and dragons in relief, the long processional way lined with blue walls of striding lions leading through it, priests and citizens in a festival procession, terraced gardens with palms rising over the city behind. Rendered in the style of Neo-Babylonian glazed-brick relief, rich cobalt blue, gold and white, flat profile figures.
me-fall-of-babylon: 539 BCE, Babylon: Persian soldiers in pleated robes and fluted hats, Median troops in tunics and trousers, march in orderly ranks through the open blue-glazed city gate, Babylonian citizens and priests lining the street calmly to watch, palms and ziggurat behind, the Euphrates under a clear autumn sky. Rendered in the style of an Achaemenid stone relief from Persepolis, rows of profile figures in pale grey limestone.
me-ionian-revolt: 499 BCE, Miletus, Anatolian coast: a Greek harbour city with marble temples, stoas and a theatre on the hillside above the Aegean, citizens in himations gathered in the agora, hoplites in bronze helmets and round shields mustering, triremes with eye-painted bows in the harbour ready to sail. Painted in the style of a Greek red-figure vase painting, terracotta figures on black ground, fine line, small figures.
me-mausoleum-of-halicarnassus: c. 350 BCE, Halicarnassus, Anatolian coast: a monumental marble tomb rising high above a harbour city, a tall podium with sculpted friezes, a ring of Ionic columns, a stepped pyramid roof crowned by a four-horse chariot sculpture, workers and sculptors on scaffolding, ships in the bay below. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco from Pompeii, warm ochre, terracotta and sea blue, soft architectural perspective.
me-battle-of-issus: 333 BCE, Issus, near the Gulf of Iskenderun, Anatolia: Macedonian cavalry in bronze helmets and a phalanx with long sarissa pikes charge across a narrow coastal plain by a river, the Persian army in colourful trousers and tiaras breaking, a Persian royal chariot turning in flight, mountains and sea on either side. Rendered in the style of the Roman Alexander Mosaic from Pompeii, tesserae in ochre, red and black, dense dynamic figures, no bodies shown.
me-battle-of-gaugamela: 331 BCE, Gaugamela, northern Mesopotamia: on a vast flat dusty plain, the Macedonian phalanx bristling with long pikes and companion cavalry wedge advancing, the Persian army with scythed chariots, war elephants and archers stretched to the horizon, dust clouds and banners, low hills beyond under a hot sky. Painted in the style of a Hellenistic battle fresco, ochre, red and black, many small figures, no bodies shown.
me-antioch-founded: c. 300 BCE, Antioch on the Orontes, Syria: Greek surveyors with measuring rods and ropes lay out a grid of streets on the plain between the Orontes River and Mount Silpius, workers raising colonnades and walls, colonists arriving with ox carts, a priest sacrificing at an altar, cypress and olive trees around. Painted in the style of a Hellenistic Roman fresco, warm ochre, terracotta and soft green, light architectural perspective, small figures.
