xingan-dayangzhou-tomb: c. 1200 BCE, Xin'gan in the Gan River valley of Jiangxi: inside a timber-lined burial pit in a sandy riverside mound, hundreds of bronze vessels, bells, weapons with tiger-shaped handles and jade ornaments are carefully arranged by attendants in hemp robes, while a chief's funeral gathering watches from above; green subtropical hills and the broad river behind. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, jade greens and bronze browns.
four-goat-square-zun: c. 1200 BCE, Ningxiang in the hills of Hunan: in a foundry clearing under tall trees, bronze casters in hemp tunics lift away sections of a clay piece-mould to reveal a large square wine vessel, four curly-horned goats projecting from its corners and shoulders with dragon motifs; charcoal furnaces glow, clay mould fragments lie around, misty green hills beyond. Close but not of any face. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, warm metallic sheen.
houmuwu-ding: c. 1190 BCE, Yin near Anyang: in a large foundry yard, dozens of workers in hemp tunics pour molten bronze from many clay crucibles at once into a giant rectangular clay mould for a four-legged ding cauldron, others pump skin bellows at furnaces; a finished heavy rectangular cauldron stands nearby. Smoke and sparks rise, overseers in robes watch from a platform, palace roofs beyond. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, fiery orange and soot black.
wu-yi-shoots-heaven: c. 1140 BCE, the plain between the Yellow and Wei rivers: a king in a chariot draws a bow at a leather bag hanging from a tall wooden pole, courtiers watching, a human-shaped wooden effigy set on a board nearby; on the horizon storm clouds churn and a bolt of lightning strikes a distant hunting ground. Late afternoon, ominous dark sky over yellow grass. Figures small, no injury shown. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
gugong-danfu-zhouyuan: c. 1130 BCE, the Zhouyuan plain below Mount Qi: a long migration of Zhou people on foot crosses a river and climbs onto fertile loess land, elders leading, families carrying children and bundles, oxen pulling wooden carts, flocks of sheep; an elder chief points to the plain at the foot of the mountain where first huts and fields are laid out. Clear morning, golden loess slopes. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
wen-ding-kills-jili: c. 1101 BCE, Yin near Anyang: inside the walled Shang palace compound, a foreign leader in Zhou-style robes is led by Shang guards with dagger-axes through a courtyard toward a closed timber hall, his attendants held back at the gate; nobles watch from the steps of a hall on a high earthen platform. Grey, tense evening light. Figures small, no violence shown. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
king-zhou-excesses: c. 1070 BCE, Zhaoge: a lavish Shang palace garden at night, a large rectangular pool of wine where revellers in fine robes drink from bronze vessels, and racks of hanging meat like a grove of trees; musicians play bronze bells and stone chimes, dancers whirl, a raised terrace of rammed earth glows with torches, while far beyond the walls grain stores rise at Juqiao. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, deep red and gold.
di-xin-dongyi: c. 1060 BCE, the Huai River and Shandong region: a Shang army of chariots and foot soldiers marches along a marshy river plain toward distant eastern hills, supply ox carts and captured war-banners in the long column; tired soldiers rest by campfires and a commander's chariot halts on a rise. Reeds, water, low clouds, broad landscape seen from afar. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, frieze-like.
jiang-ziya-joins-zhou: c. 1060 BCE, Panxi on the Wei River near Baoji: an old man in a simple hemp robe and straw hat sits on a rock by the clear river with a long fishing rod; on the riverbank above, a chieftain in fine robes has stepped down from his chariot with attendants and bows respectfully toward him. Willows, misty mountains, gentle morning light. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, soft blue-greens.
king-wen-imprisoned-youli: c. 1056 BCE, Youli near Tangyin: a modest rammed-earth prison compound with a thatched hut and guards with dagger-axes at the gate; inside, a captive lord in plain robes sits on a mat, laying out yarrow stalks and drawing patterns of broken and unbroken lines on the ground; outside, Zhou envoys arrive with horses, jade and fine goods as ransom. Quiet evening. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
zhou-conquers-li: c. 1052 BCE, the state of Li near Changzhi in the Shanxi highlands: a Zhou army of chariots and foot soldiers under red banners stands outside the opened gates of a small rammed-earth walled town on a mountain plateau, townspeople kneeling in surrender, smoke rising from a burnt watchtower. Rugged Taihang ridges and a pale sky; in the far east a road descends toward the Shang plain. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
king-wen-builds-feng: c. 1050 BCE, Feng on the Wei River plain: a new Zhou capital rises by the Feng River, workers tamping rammed-earth walls and raising timber palace halls on platforms, ox carts bringing timber, a ruler and ministers in robes inspecting a ritual hall; fields, willow-lined river and the Qinling mountains to the south. Bright spring day, broad bird's-eye view. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, fresh greens.
mengjin-gathering: c. 1048 BCE, the Mengjin ford on the Yellow River: a vast host of allied lords and their chariots and foot soldiers gathers on the south bank under countless banners, boats ferrying troops across the wide muddy river; on a riverbank platform, a young Zhou king in robes addresses the lords, then gestures back westward. Mid-morning, windswept river under broad sky. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, many small figures.
bigan-killed: c. 1047 BCE, Zhaoge: in a Shang palace hall on a high platform, an aged nobleman in long robes kneels and raises his hands in earnest remonstrance before a throne-dais, guards standing by; outside the gate other nobles slip away at dusk with bundles, one of them wandering with unkempt hair as if mad. Scene of tension, no violence shown. Dark red and black, lamplight. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
taigong-founds-qi: c. 1045 BCE, Yingqiu near Linzi on the Shandong coast: a new walled town of rammed earth close to the sea, fishermen hauling nets from wooden boats, salt workers boiling seawater in large pans along the shore, merchants with bundles; an elderly lord in plain robes surveys the scene from a low rise with attendants. Bright coastal light, gulls, blue sea. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
duke-of-shao-founds-yan: c. 1045 BCE, Liulihe near modern Beijing: a small Zhou walled outpost of rammed earth on the northern plain below the Yan mountains, a lord and his retainers arrive by chariot carrying bronze ritual vessels; workers build halls and a cemetery outside the walls, local people in fur and hide watch from the edge of the woods. Cool autumn light, mountains to the north. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
jizi-goes-to-joseon: c. 1045 BCE, the road east toward the Korean peninsula: a Shang prince in dark robes leads a long column of followers on foot and in ox carts, carrying bronze vessels and seeds, along a coastal route between pine-covered hills and the sea; far ahead lies a river valley with thatched villages. Overcast, contemplative mood, figures small and seen from behind. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, cool greys and greens.
boyi-and-shuqi: c. 1045 BCE, Mount Shouyang near Yongji: two aged men in worn robes, seen small from behind, gather wild ferns on a steep rocky mountainside among bare trees, a simple shelter of branches nearby; far below, the Yellow River winds across the plain where Zhou banners and settlements can be seen. Cold autumn wind, thin mist. Ink and light colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, sparse and austere.
zhou-enfeoffment: c. 1044 BCE, Haojing: in a Zhou ancestral temple courtyard, a king seated on a dais presents bronze vessels, jade tablets and baskets of soil to kneeling kinsmen and allies in robes and caps, each receiving a banner; outside the gate, chariots and retainers wait to set out east. Ritual musicians with bells and chimes, pine trees, clear morning. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, formal symmetrical composition.
three-guards-rebellion: c. 1042 BCE, the former Shang capital region near Anyang: a Zhou army under a regent moves across the eastern plain in a long column of chariots and foot soldiers toward distant walled towns where rebel banners fly; smoke rises on the horizon, a commander's chariot halts on a rise. Seen from afar, no bloodshed. Late autumn, grey skies over harvested fields. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
cheng-kang-peace: c. 1042 BCE, the Wei plain near Haojing: a peaceful Zhou countryside, farmers ploughing with wooden spades and harvesting millet in well-ordered fields, villagers with oxen, children by a stream, an empty stocks frame overgrown with grass by the road, and in the distance the palace halls of the capital. Warm late-summer light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, gentle greens and golds.
conquest-of-yan-state: c. 1039 BCE, Yan near Qufu in Shandong: a Zhou army camps outside a captured rammed-earth town, its walls breached, banners of the victors raised; long lines of chariots and soldiers move eastward toward the hills, captives and surrendered nobles walk behind. Smoke drifts from the town, rivers and fields around. Viewed from afar. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
he-zun: c. 1038 BCE, Chengzhou near Luoyang: in a ritual hall of timber posts on a rammed-earth platform, a nobleman kneels before a young king, receiving gifts of cowrie shells, while bronze casters display a tall wine vessel with flaring mouth and beast-mask decoration on a stand; the Luo River plain and the new eastern capital's walls visible through the open doors. No visible writing. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
rites-and-music-of-zhou: c. 1037 BCE, Haojing: a grand Zhou ancestral rite in a temple courtyard, nobles in layered robes and caps arranged by rank, a frame of graded bronze bells and stone chimes struck by musicians, dancers with feather wands and shields moving in rows, ritual bronze vessels with grain and meat on altars; a regent in dark robes directs, seen from behind. Clear dawn. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, symmetrical formal composition.
duke-of-zhou-returns-power: c. 1036 BCE, Haojing: in a Zhou palace hall with timber pillars, a young king ascends to the central seat on a dais while an older minister in dark robes steps down and turns to face him, bowing, taking his place among rows of kneeling officials; jade tablets held in hands, bronze vessels on stands. Calm morning light. Figures small and formal. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
shu-yu-enfeoffed-tang: c. 1033 BCE, a Zhou palace garden: under a large paulownia tree, a boy king playfully hands a leaf cut into the shape of a jade tablet to his younger brother; nearby a court historian in robes steps forward solemnly, and officials watch. Background shows a distant river valley in Shanxi with a small walled town. Gentle spring light. Figures small, no faces in close-up. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
king-zhao-southern-campaign: c. 977 BCE, the Han River: a Zhou royal army attempts to cross the wide swollen river on rafts and wooden boats under grey storm clouds; several boats have broken apart and drift in the current, chariots and banners stranded on the northern bank, soldiers struggle in the shallows, the far southern shore lined with dark forest. Seen from a distance, no bodies. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, cold greys and muddy greens.
king-mu-travels: c. 964 BCE, setting out west from Haojing: a king's chariot drawn by eight fine horses races along a road through yellow loess hills toward distant snow-capped western mountains, followed by a small train of chariots and riders of the escort on foot; on the far horizon, a legendary jade-green mountain palace floats among clouds. Dawn light, sense of immense distance. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, flowing cloud scrolls.
king-yan-of-xu: c. 960 BCE, Xu near Sihong in the Huai River lowlands: a mixed Zhou and Chu army of chariots and foot soldiers advances across marshy fields toward a town of thatched halls behind earthen walls, while Huai Yi warriors with bows and shields fall back among reeds and lakes; banners of both sides in the haze. Viewed from afar, no bloodshed. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, frieze composition.
lu-xing-penal-code: c. 950 BCE, Haojing: in a Zhou court hall, an elderly marquis in robes kneels before a king, presenting bundles of bamboo slips tied with cord; scribes with brushes sit at low tables preparing more slips, and in the courtyard officials weigh lumps of bronze on balance scales to show fines in place of punishments. No legible writing. Morning light through the hall. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, ochre and dark red.
shi-qiang-pan: c. 900 BCE, Zhuangbai near Fufeng on the Zhouyuan plain: in a noble family's ancestral hall, a scribe in robes and cap kneels before a large shallow bronze basin on a low stand, its inner surface densely covered with tiny unreadable incised marks, while bronze-casters and family members look on; other vessels, bells and offerings fill the hall. Lamp and morning light mix. No legible characters. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
feizi-granted-qin: c. 890 BCE, Qin near Qingshui in eastern Gansu: wide grassy uplands between the Wei and Qian rivers where herds of horses graze; a horse breeder in short tunic and trousers with herders leads fine horses before a Zhou royal envoy in robes, who presents him a jade token and a banner; a small earth-walled settlement and pens on a hill. Big sky, rolling hills. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
xiong-qu-proclaims-kings: c. 880 BCE, Danyang near Xichuan in the Han River valley: in a Chu hall of timber and thatch on a riverside hill, a ruler in southern-style robes with a tall cap presents three young men with bronze axes and banners, while warriors with painted shields stand around; the mighty Yangtze region of green mountains and mist stretches southward. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, swirling cloud motifs, black and red.
duke-ai-of-qi-boiled: c. 868 BCE, Haojing: in the courtyard of a Zhou palace, a huge bronze cauldron sits over a fire, steam billowing up; officials and nobles stand in uneasy rows with heads lowered, the king seated far off on a dais in a hall above, a lone eastern lord's empty cap and robe lying on a mat. No person in the cauldron, no body shown. Dark smoky dusk. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
king-li-silences-critics: c. 845 BCE, Haojing: a street in the Zhou capital lined with rammed-earth walls and thatched gates; townspeople pass one another in silence, exchanging only sideways glances, while a shaman in a fringed costume and guards with dagger-axes watch from a corner; a royal palace roof rises behind. Overcast, heavy atmosphere, figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, muted greys and browns.
king-xuan-restoration: c. 827 BCE, Haojing: a newly crowned Zhou king on a raised rammed-earth palace terrace reviews returning armies, two-wheeled war chariots drawn by teams of horses rolling in through the city gate under banners, foot soldiers with bronze dagger-axes marching beside them, generals on foot presenting captured bronze weapons and led chariot horses, ministers in rows; the Wei plain, renewed fields and the Qinling range behind. No one rides on horseback and there are no saddles. Bright clear morning, crowds lining the road. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, ceremonial frieze composition, no text.
xianyun-campaign: c. 823 BCE, near Pengya in the Baishui valley of Shaanxi: a line of Zhou war chariots, each pulled by four horses with bronze fittings, rolls across a dusty loess plain, archers standing in the cars drawing bows. Far ahead, Xianyun raiders on foot, driving herds of sheep and unridden pack horses laden with bundles, retreat northward toward distant hills. Seen from a distance, dust clouds, setting sun. No one rides on horseback, no saddles, no stirrups. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, ochre and dark red.
qin-zhong-dies-fighting-rong: c. 822 BCE, Quanqiu near Tianshui: on windswept grassy uplands, a small Western Zhou-era Qin force of two-horse chariots, each carrying a driver, an archer and a spearman, with foot soldiers holding bronze dagger-axes and hide shields, clashes with Rong tribal warriors on foot among the hills. Nobody rides on horseback; horses only pull chariots. Single scene viewed from afar, no bloodshed, stormy sky filling the whole picture with no border. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
zheng-founded: c. 806 BCE, Zheng near Huazhou in Shaanxi: a new noble estate on the Wei plain below Mount Hua, a lord in robes reviewing his households; in the foreground, ox carts loaded with bronze vessels, bolts of silk and grain chests set off along a road eastward, his family and retainers walking beside them toward the distant plains. Morning light, majestic granite peaks. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
mao-gong-ding: c. 800 BCE, Qishan in the Zhouyuan: in a bronze workshop yard, casters lift a newly cast round tripod cauldron with two upright handles from its clay mould, its inner wall covered with dense tiny unreadable marks; a nobleman and his household in robes look on with satisfaction, charcoal smoke rising, Mount Qi behind. No legible characters. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, warm bronze tones.
battle-of-qianmu: c. 789 BCE, Qianmu: on a broad open plain, the remnants of a Zhou royal army in disarray, broken chariots and abandoned banners scattered across the field, survivors retreating toward a distant walled camp; on far hills, Jiang Rong warriors with banners watch. Smoke and dust under a red evening sky. Seen from afar, no bodies. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
census-at-taiyuan: c. 788 BCE, Taiyuan near Guyuan in the northwest uplands: royal officials in robes sit at low tables under awnings in a village square, tallying households with bundles of bamboo slips and counting sticks, while lines of farmers and families wait; an elder minister nearby gestures in protest to a figure in a chariot. Dry hills, autumn grass. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, no legible writing.
three-rivers-earthquake: c. 780 BCE, the Qishan region: a great earthquake shakes the Zhou homeland, hillsides of loess collapse, a river is blocked and floods, the walls of a village crack and thatched halls lean; people flee into the fields; on a terrace an astrologer in robes gazes at the sky. Dramatic grey and ochre sky, dust clouds rising. No injuries shown. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
king-you-and-bao-si: c. 779 BCE, Haojing: at night, beacon fires blaze on a chain of watchtowers along the hills; lords' chariots rush in confusion to the gates of the capital, while on a high palace terrace a king and a lady in silk robes watch from afar, seen small from behind. Torchlight, dark blue night. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, fiery orange against indigo.
qin-becomes-state: 770 BCE, the road from the ruined western capital to the east: a Qin lord's chariot and armed escort guard the royal carriage of a young Zhou king travelling east through the Wei valley; behind, smoke rises over the abandoned western capital, and to the west lie the Rong-held hills beyond Mount Qi. Dusty road, grey sky. Figures small. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
qin-begins-keeping-records: c. 753 BCE, the confluence of the Qian and Wei rivers near Baoji: inside a modest Qin palace hall of timber and rammed earth, newly appointed historians in robes kneel at low tables writing on bamboo slips, bundles stored on shelves, while a lord in robes watches; outside, the two rivers meet below hills. No legible characters. Calm light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
spring-autumn-annals-begin: 722 BCE, Qufu in the state of Lu: in a quiet archive room of the Lu court, a historian in robes and cap kneels at a low table writing a brief entry onto a bamboo slip with a brush, bundles of slips stacked on shelves, a window showing spring blossoms then autumn leaves on two trees in the courtyard. No legible characters. Warm light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
zheng-defeats-duan-at-yan: 722 BCE, Yan near Yanling: the army of the duke of Zheng, war chariots and foot soldiers under banners, surrounds a walled town on the plain; rebel troops pour out of the gate and scatter while townspeople open their doors to the duke's forces. Viewed from afar, spring fields, light haze. No bloodshed. Painted with the black, cinnabar and ochre palette of Spring and Autumn period lacquerware.
zhou-zheng-exchange-hostages: 720 BCE, Luoyi: at the gates of the Zhou royal city, two small processions meet on a stone-paved approach, each escorting a young prince in robes accompanied by attendants and chariots, passing in opposite directions; officials on both sides bow stiffly. Overcast sky above timber gate towers. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
zhouxu-kills-duke-huan-of-wey: 719 BCE, the Wey capital at Zhaoge: an elderly minister in dark robes stands in a palace courtyard pointing firmly, while guards lead away two men in fine robes toward the gate; nobles watch in silence. A setting sun behind tiled gate-towers casts long shadows. No violence shown. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, sombre browns and reds.
hua-du-kills-duke-shang-of-song: 710 BCE, Shangqiu in the state of Song: a palace hall at night where armed men break through the doors and courtiers flee along a veranda; outside the walls, envoys from neighbouring states arrive with carts piled with bronze vessels and gifts. Torchlight and shadows, figures small, violence implied by fleeing figures only. Black, cinnabar and ochre palette of Spring and Autumn period lacquerware.
battle-of-xuge: 707 BCE, Xuge near Changge: on a broad plain, Zheng chariots form a fishscale formation and break the Zhou royal army's lines; the king's chariot with tall royal banner turns back, arrows in the air, dust rising. Seen from afar, no bloodshed. Winter fields under pale sky. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, ochre and cinnabar accents.
xiong-tong-declares-king: 704 BCE, Ying near Jingzhou: on a raised timber terrace by the Yangtze lakes, a Chu ruler in flowing southern robes and tall cap stands before warriors with painted shields and crowds of people, raising a bronze axe as drums and bells sound; banners with dragons and phoenixes, misty green hills. Seen small from behind. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, swirling clouds, black and red.
duke-huan-of-lu-murdered: 694 BCE, Linzi in the state of Qi: after a night banquet, a powerful strongman lifts a drunken guest into a carriage outside a palace gate; servants look away, lanterns glow, and an empty wine cup lies by the steps. No violence shown, figures small, the shadowy tiled roofs of the Qi capital behind. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, dark blue night.
chu-moves-capital-to-ying: 689 BCE, Ying near Jingzhou: a great procession of the Chu court arrives by river boats and chariots at a new walled city among lakes near the Yangtze; workers raise rammed-earth walls and moats, timber palaces with steep roofs rise, boats unload bronze vessels. Lush green country, humid haze, broad view. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, rich black, red and gold.
qin-creates-first-counties: 688 BCE, Gui near Tianshui: a Qin official in robes arrives by chariot with a few soldiers at a small earth-walled frontier town among the western hills, presenting a bronze tally to the assembled villagers and Rong herders; new granaries and a gate tower being built. Dry grassland, distant ridges, morning light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, ochre and green.
gongsun-wuzhi-kills-duke-xiang: 686 BCE, Linzi: in the dark woods of a hunting ground, armed officers emerge from among the trees around a lone empty chariot and a dropped silk shoe on the path; in the far distance the palace of the Qi capital is lit by torches. Night, mist and moonlight, figures small, no violence depicted. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, cool blue tones.
guan-zhong-reforms: 685 BCE, Linzi in the state of Qi: the busy capital, salt workers boiling seawater in great clay pans by the coast, officials weighing salt and recording at tables, farmers and craftsmen organised in neat quarters, soldiers drilling with chariots on a parade ground; a minister in robes oversees from a gate tower. Bright day. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, many small figures.
battle-of-changshao: 684 BCE, Changshao in the hills of Shandong: two armies face each other across a valley; the Qi side beats great war drums three times, its chariots surging forward, while the Lu chariots wait quietly; a man beside the Lu duke's chariot raises his hand. Seen from afar, dust in the air, no bloodshed. Painted with the black, cinnabar and ochre palette of Spring and Autumn period lacquerware.
covenant-at-ke: 681 BCE, Ke near Yanggu: on a raised earthen altar for a covenant ceremony, a soldier in short armour holds a short bronze dagger close to a duke in robes, as surrounding attendants freeze; ritual bronze vessels and a sacrificial ox stand below, banners of two states. Figures small, tense moment, no blood. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
quwo-supplants-yi: 678 BCE, Yi in the Fen River valley of Shanxi: a victorious army from Quwo enters the gates of the old Jin capital under banners, chariots rolling in; meanwhile carts loaded with bronze vessels and treasures depart along a road toward the distant royal capital. Loess hills, late autumn light. Viewed from afar. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
chen-wan-flees-to-qi: 672 BCE, arriving at Linzi: a young prince in fine but travel-worn robes and his few retainers arrive by chariot at the gates of the Qi capital, greeted by officials; behind them lies a long road from the south. The towers of the city and the sea in the distance. Late afternoon. Figures small, seen from behind. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
qi-attacks-shanrong: 664 BCE, Lingzhi near Lulong in the north: a long Qi army column of chariots and foot soldiers marches through mountain passes and wild grasslands, banners flying, guided by a horse; in the distance the Shanrong camps burn, and Yan people greet the soldiers. Autumn colours, cold wind. Viewed from afar, no bloodshed. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
di-destroy-wey: 660 BCE, Zhaoge: the capital of Wey burns in the distance as Di warriors stream through the gates; in the foreground, elegant cranes ride in small ornate carriages abandoned on the road, and refugees cross the Yellow River in boats. Smoky orange sky over the plain. No bodies shown. Painted with the black, cinnabar and ochre palette of Spring and Autumn period lacquerware.
covenant-of-zhaoling: 656 BCE, Zhaoling near Luohe: two great armies stand in formation on a plain, the coalition of eight states on one side and Chu's army before a fortified camp on the other; in the middle, envoys and a duke stand at an earthen altar, smearing their lips with sacrificial blood from a bronze vessel. Banners, chariots, midday sun. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
lady-li-and-shensheng: 656 BCE, Jiang in the state of Jin: in a palace hall, a dog lies still beside a dish of sacrificial meat on the floor, courtiers recoil, a lady in silk stands to one side, a duke rises angrily from his seat; outside, two princes slip out of the gates by night in chariots with retainers. Lamplight and deep shadows. No people harmed. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
covenant-of-kuiqiu: 651 BCE, Kuiqiu near Lankao: a grand assembly of lords on a plain, a high earthen altar with ritual bronze vessels, a royal envoy presents sacrificial meat to a duke in robes, the lords standing in ranks around, chariots and banners of many states arrayed at a distance. Clear sky, sense of order. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, symmetrical composition.
boat-relief-to-jin: 647 BCE, the Wei and Fen rivers: a long convoy of wooden grain boats stretches upstream along the winding rivers, boatmen poling and hauling ropes along the banks, sacks of millet stacked high; crowds of hungry Jin villagers gather on the riverbank to receive the grain. Dry loess hills, late autumn light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, many small figures.
battle-of-hanyuan: 645 BCE, Hanyuan near Hancheng: on a field by the Yellow River, a Jin war chariot has become stuck in mud, its horses rearing, as Qin chariots close in; banners of both sides, dust rising, the great river and loess cliffs behind. Seen from afar, no bloodshed. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, ochre and dark red.
death-of-duke-huan-of-qi: 643 BCE, Linzi: an abandoned inner palace chamber, its doors sealed and a curtained couch untouched, while outside in the courtyards princes and their armed followers confront one another; weeds grow between the paving, and crows circle above the tiled roofs. Gloomy grey light. No body shown. Painted with the black, cinnabar and ochre palette of Spring and Autumn period lacquerware.
battle-of-hong: 638 BCE, the Hong River near Zhecheng: the Chu army is crossing the river in boats and through the shallows, half on each bank; on the near shore, the Song army waits in neat ranks, its duke in his chariot raising his hand to hold them back. Midday light on water, banners. Seen from afar. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
chonger-returns: 636 BCE, crossing the Yellow River into Jin: a Qin army escorts a middle-aged prince and his loyal companions, who ride in chariots across a ford of the Yellow River; on the far bank, Jin officials and people kneel to welcome them, towns and loess hills beyond. Early spring, fresh light. Figures small, seen from behind. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
covenant-of-jiantu: 632 BCE, Jiantu near Yuanyang: a newly built palace on a rise above the Yellow River plain; lords gather in the courtyard as a royal envoy presents a red bow, black bow, chariots and sacred wine to a duke, kneeling in ritual robes; captured Chu chariots displayed outside. Bright day, ceremonial grandeur. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
zhu-zhiwu-persuades-qin: 630 BCE, Xinzheng: at night, an old man in plain robes is lowered on a rope down the outer face of the besieged city wall of Zheng, while campfires of the Qin and Jin armies glow on the surrounding plain; in the Qin camp, a duke's tent is lit. Moonlit indigo sky, figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
battle-of-xiao: 627 BCE, the Xiao mountains near Sanmenxia: a long Qin army column of chariots and foot soldiers winds through a narrow rocky gorge between steep cliffs; Jin troops in white-dyed mourning garments rise from ambush positions on the ridges, rolling stones and loosing arrows. Seen from high above, small figures, dust and confusion, no bodies. Autumn trees on the slopes. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, dramatic mountain forms.
shangchen-kills-king-cheng: 626 BCE, Ying near Jingzhou: armed soldiers with dagger-axes and painted shields surround a Chu palace of tall timber halls at dusk, torches lit, the gates shut; inside, through an open window, a cooking pot steams on a brazier on an empty table set for a meal. Lake mists, cypress trees. No violence or bodies shown, figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, black and red with swirling cloud motifs.
qin-dominates-rong: c. 623 BCE, the western frontier beyond Yong: a Qin duke in robes stands on a hill in his chariot as chiefs of many Rong tribes in fur hats and hide garments come forward with horses, sheep and gifts; Qin banners rise over newly taken earth-walled settlements in the grassy hills, the Wei valley behind. Wide golden landscape at sunset. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
three-good-men-buried: 621 BCE, Yong near Fengxiang: a vast Qin funeral at a great earthen tomb pit with stepped ramps, a long procession of mourners in white hemp robes winding down to it, chariots, bronze vessels and coffins carried in; yellow birds perch on thorny jujube trees nearby, mourners weeping at the edge. Grey, sorrowful sky. No bodies shown. Ink and light colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, muted tones.
halleys-comet-record: 613 BCE, Qufu in the state of Lu: at night on the flat roof of a high earthen observation terrace, two court astronomers in robes and caps look up at a bright comet with a long sweeping tail crossing the seven stars of the Northern Dipper; one points while the other holds a bamboo slip. The sleeping city roofs below. Deep indigo sky full of stars. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
chu-destroys-yong: 611 BCE, Yong near Zhushan in the mountains of northwest Hubei: allied armies of Chu, Qin and Ba, their varied banners and painted shields visible, advance through steep forested gorges and river valleys toward a hill town of wooden halls behind palisades; smoke rising, defenders retreating. Seen from afar, no bloodshed. Mist in the gorges. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, rich black and cinnabar.
zhao-chuan-kills-duke-ling: 607 BCE, Jiang in the state of Jin: in the archive of the Jin palace, a court historian in robes kneels at a low table writing a brief entry on a bamboo slip, while a senior minister stands at the doorway, gesturing in protest; through the window, the peach garden of the palace. No legible writing, no violence. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, calm daylight.
chu-asks-about-cauldrons: 606 BCE, near Luoyi: a vast Chu army parades on the plain outside the Zhou royal capital, chariots and soldiers under dragon and phoenix banners; in front of the army, a southern king in tall cap stands in his chariot speaking with a royal envoy in plain court robes, who gestures calmly. The capital's walls and towers behind. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
classic-of-poetry: c. 600 BCE, Luoyi at the Zhou court: in a timber hall, court musicians play bronze bells, stone chimes, zithers and pan pipes while a singer performs, and scribes gather bundles of bamboo slips; outside, travelling officials collect songs from peasants harvesting millet and women picking mulberry leaves. No legible text. Golden afternoon light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
xia-zhengshu-kills-duke-ling-of-chen: 599 BCE, Wanqiu near Huaiyang: at night outside the stables of a noble house, a duke is seen fleeing toward his chariot as an archer draws his bow from a dark gateway; the house lit by lanterns, figures small and distant, the moment before any harm. Later in the scene, banners of the Chu army appear on the horizon. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
battle-of-bi: 597 BCE, Bi north of Zhengzhou by the Yellow River: the Chu army sweeps forward with massed chariots and foot soldiers while the Jin army breaks and crowds the riverbank, soldiers scrambling into boats to cross the wide muddy river. Seen from a high distance, dust and spray, no bodies. Dusk light. Painted with the black, cinnabar and ochre palette of Spring and Autumn period lacquerware.
lu-land-tax: 594 BCE, near Qufu in Lu: officials in robes with measuring cords and wooden rods survey farmland divided into irregular private plots, a scribe records on bamboo slips, farmers stand beside their fields of millet and wheat, ox-drawn ploughs, villages with thatched roofs. Clear autumn day, gentle hills. No legible writing. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
chu-besieges-song: 594 BCE, Shangqiu: the walled Song capital is encircled by a long Chu siege camp with tents and earthworks; at night, a lone official in robes climbs secretly into the Chu commander's tent, lamplight within, while famine-gaunt defenders stand on the city walls. Moonlight and campfires, figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, deep blues and ochres.
battle-of-an: 589 BCE, An near Jinan: on a plain beneath Mount Hua near Jinan, Jin chariots pursue a Qi duke's chariot around the mountain's foot; in the chariot, the duke and his driver in matching armour have exchanged places, and the driver stands in the place of honour. Dust and banners, figures small, no bloodshed. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
jin-forms-six-armies: 588 BCE, Jiang in the state of Jin: a vast military review on a parade ground below loess hills, six great divisions of war chariots and foot soldiers arranged in ordered blocks, each with its own banner and ministerial commander in a chariot; the duke watches from a high earthen platform. Bright morning, dust. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, many tiny figures.
jin-moves-to-xintian: 585 BCE, Xintian near Houma: a new Jin capital on the Fen River plain, rammed-earth walls and palace halls rising, great bronze foundries smoking outside the walls where workers make clay moulds and cast bells and vessels; carts bring goods from the old capital. Wide bird's-eye view, afternoon light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
wu-learns-chariot-warfare: 584 BCE, Meili near Wuxi in the land of Wu: on a training ground beside canals and rice paddies, a northern officer in robes teaches Wu warriors with tattooed arms and short hair to drive two-horse chariots and draw bows; boats on the waterways, thatched houses and Lake Tai beyond. Humid, bright day. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, greens and blues.
orphan-of-zhao: 583 BCE, Xintian: at night, a loyal retainer in a plain hooded robe slips quietly out of a back gate of a noble mansion, carrying a swaddled infant hidden in a medicine chest, past sleeping guards; the mansion lies dark and silent, lanterns extinguished. Moonlit indigo sky, figures small. No violence shown. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
lu-xiang-severs-qin: 578 BCE, Masui near Jingyang: an allied army of eight states, many banners and hundreds of war chariots, advances across the Jing River plain into Qin territory while the Qin army falls back to distant hills. Dust clouds, seen from a high distance, no bloodshed. Late spring, green fields. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, frieze-like composition.
battle-of-yanling: 575 BCE, Yanling in Henan: two great armies clash across a wide plain in the morning, Jin chariots pressing forward against the Chu lines; the Chu king's tall chariot with royal banner turns away, an arrow in flight above. Seen from far above, dust and fluttering banners, no bodies. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, cinnabar accents.
duke-dao-revives-jin: 573 BCE, Xintian: in a palace hall, a teenage duke in formal robes sits on a raised mat as ministers in caps kneel in rows before him, presenting bamboo slips of new regulations; outside the hall, granaries are opened to the people and soldiers drill. Bright, orderly morning. No legible writing, figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
wei-jiang-peace-with-rong: 569 BCE, the Jin frontier near Xintian: in a frontier market on open grassland, Jin officials in robes exchange bolts of silk, bronze vessels and grain with Rong and Di herders in fur and hide who bring horses and sheep; tents and earth-walled towns in the distance. Bright day, peaceful mood. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, ochre and green.
qi-lai: 567 BCE, the Shandong peninsula: the Qi army, chariots and foot soldiers under banners, marches along the coast toward the walled town of Lai near the sea; the town's gates open and people surrender, fishing boats and rocky headlands behind. Bright day, waves, seen from afar. No bloodshed. Painted with the black, cinnabar and ochre palette of Spring and Autumn period lacquerware.
three-huan-divide-lu: 562 BCE, Qufu: in a palace courtyard, three noblemen in fine robes stand before three groups of soldiers and stacks of grain and bronze tallies being divided among them, while a duke sits alone and small on a dais in a half-empty hall behind. Cool overcast light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
cui-zhu-kills-duke-zhuang: 548 BCE, Linzi: in the court archive, a historian in robes calmly writes a short line on a bamboo slip while soldiers stand at the door; behind him a younger brother waits with brush in hand, and outside another historian hurries toward the gate carrying slips. No violence shown. Dim lamplight. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, no legible writing.
conference-of-song: 546 BCE, Shangqiu in the state of Song: delegates from fourteen states in robes and caps gather around an earthen altar outside the city walls, chariots and tents of each state arranged around a plain, the Jin and Chu envoys facing each other at the centre. Bright day, many banners, peaceful formality. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, symmetrical composition.
ji-zha-observes-music: 544 BCE, Qufu: in a Lu palace hall, musicians play bronze bells, stone chimes, zithers and drums, and dancers in rows perform; a visiting prince from Wu in elegant robes sits listening intently beside his hosts, attendants serving wine. Warm lamplight. Figures small, no faces in close-up. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, rich red and gold.
zichan-governs-zheng: 543 BCE, Xinzheng: a village in Zheng with neatly divided fields and irrigation ditches; farmers pay grain into an official's tally baskets, and in a village school beneath trees, townspeople gather and argue animatedly about government while a minister in robes passes by without interfering. Clear day. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, many small figures.
conference-at-shen: 538 BCE, Shen near Nanyang: a proud Chu king in a tall cap and flowing robes receives lords of many states before a raised terrace, Chu warriors with painted shields lining the approach; beyond, an army prepares to march east toward Wu. Banners with phoenix designs, blue sky. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, black, red and gold.
zichan-law-code: 536 BCE, Xinzheng: in a square in the capital of Zheng, a large bronze cauldron stands on a stone base, its sides covered in dense tiny unreadable marks; townspeople gather to look, some pointing, officials nearby, while an elderly minister watches from a gate. No legible writing. Bright daylight. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
king-ling-of-chu-dies: 529 BCE, Qianxi near Bozhou: an abandoned royal camp in a river plain, tents half-collapsed, chariots left behind, as soldiers drift away along the roads; a lone king in fine robes wanders into the wild marshes, seen small from behind. Grey sky, reeds and willows. No body shown. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, subdued greys and reds.
king-jing-casts-large-coins: 524 BCE, Luoyi: at a Zhou royal workshop, craftsmen cast heavy bronze spade-shaped coins in clay moulds; in the courtyard, an elderly minister in robes speaks earnestly to the king, gesturing toward ordinary townspeople in a market outside who handle small coins. Bright afternoon. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, no legible writing.
wu-zixu-flees: 522 BCE, the Zhao Pass in the hills of Anhui: at dawn, a tall man in a travel cloak, seen from behind, slips through a narrow mountain pass guarded by a small fort, hiding among villagers; below, a river where a fisherman's boat waits to ferry him across. Mist and pine-covered hills. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, cool blue-greens.
rebellion-of-prince-zhao: 516 BCE, Luoyi: a single continuous view outside the southern gate of the Zhou royal city, rammed-earth walls with a plain timber gate tower; a long procession of ox carts loaded with bamboo slip bundles and bronze vessels winds away toward distant hills, escorted by spearmen on foot and a few two-horse chariots with banners. Smoke rises faintly behind the walls. One unified landscape, no dividing lines or borders, figures small, no riders on horseback, no text. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
duke-zhao-of-lu-flees: 517 BCE, Qufu: on a hill above the capital, a duke and a small band of loyal followers in chariots retreat along a road away from the walls, looking back; below, the troops of three great clans with banners stand in the city. Grey autumn sky, figures small and seen from behind. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
zhuan-zhu-assassinates-liao: 515 BCE, Gusu near Suzhou: a Wu palace banquet hall, guards with spears lining both walls, the king seated at the head, a servant in plain robes carrying a large platter with a whole grilled fish toward him; a prince slips quietly out of a side door. Tense moment before any action, no violence shown. Lamplight. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
helu-builds-gusu: 514 BCE, Gusu (Suzhou): a grand new capital being built in the canal country, workers raise rammed-earth walls with water gates through which boats sail, canals laid out in a grid, palaces with steep roofs at the centre; a minister in robes oversees from a gate tower. Rice paddies and lakes around. Bird's-eye view. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, blues and greens.
jin-penal-cauldron: 513 BCE, the state of Jin: at a smoky foundry yard, workers pour molten iron into a large clay mould for a cauldron; a finished dark cauldron with dense tiny unreadable markings stands nearby, and two ministers in robes inspect it as townspeople gather at the gate. Fire glow against dusk sky. No legible writing. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
art-of-war: c. 512 BCE, Gusu (Suzhou): in the courtyard of a Wu palace, a scholar-general in robes presents bundles of bamboo slips to a king seated on a dais; beyond, palace women in two companies hold halberds and practise drill formations to the sound of drums. Bright day, canals and roofs behind. Figures small, no legible writing. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
laozi-writes-tao-te-ching: c. 510 BCE, the Hangu Pass near Lingbao: an old man in simple robes rides a water buffalo along a narrow road through a deep loess gorge toward a gate tower; at the gate, a keeper in robes bows and offers bundles of bamboo slips and a brush. Purple morning mist drifts from the east. Figures small, seen from the side. Ink and light colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
shen-baoxu-weeps: 505 BCE, Yong near Fengxiang: in the courtyard of the Qin palace, a Chu minister in torn robes leans against a wall, weeping, seen small from behind; guards and officials watch from steps, and finally, beyond the walls, a long column of Qin chariots sets out toward the south. Grey dawn light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
yang-hu-controls-lu: 505 BCE, Qufu: in the mansion of a noble clan, armed retainers stand guard at the gate of a courtyard where a nobleman is confined to a small room; a strong-faced steward in robes holds a bronze tally as officials bow to him. Dim interior light, tension. Figures small, no violence shown. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
conference-at-jiagu: 500 BCE, Jiagu near Laiwu: on an earthen platform for a meeting between Lu and Qi, a group of Qi warriors with weapons and painted faces approach a duke; an advisor in plain scholar's robes stands between them, raising his hand firmly; officials and chariots of both states watch from below. Bright day. Figures small, no close-up faces. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
demolishing-three-cities: 498 BCE, Lu territory near Qufu: workers with wooden spades and rams tear down the rammed-earth walls of a walled clan town, dust rising, while in the distance another fortified town on a hill stands firm with defenders on its walls; an official in scholar's robes oversees from a chariot. Bright day. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
confucius-travels: 497 BCE, a road leaving Lu toward Wey: a small group of travellers, a teacher in plain robes and his disciples, ride in an ox cart and walk along a dusty road through rolling hills and millet fields, seen from behind; a distant walled town on the horizon. Clear autumn morning, long journey ahead. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, warm ochres.
jin-six-ministers-war: 497 BCE, Jinyang near Taiyuan: a strong walled city on the Fen River plain is besieged by armies with banners of rival clans, chariots and foot soldiers encamped; defenders on the walls watch the siege camps below. Seen from afar, dust and smoke, no bloodshed. Autumn hills, the Fen River glinting, supply carts on the roads. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
battle-of-zuili: 496 BCE, Zuili near Jiaxing in the canal country: two armies face each other across a flat field between waterways; the Yue lines advance with banners and boats on the canals, while the Wu army in neat ranks turns in confusion toward a disturbance at the front. Seen from far away, no blood or bodies, smoke over reeds. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
battle-of-fujiao: 494 BCE, Fujiao on Lake Tai: a large Wu war fleet of oared wooden ships with banners sweeps across the lake, driving back the smaller Yue fleet toward the misty southern hills; spray, oars, banners. Seen from a distance, no bodies. Overcast day, choppy grey water. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, blues and greys.
goujian-serves-wu: c. 492 BCE, Gusu (Suzhou): in the stable yard of the Wu palace, a defeated king in coarse clothing tends horses and carries water while Wu guards watch; later, back in his own humble hall in Yue, he sleeps on a bed of brushwood beneath a hanging gall bladder. Two scenes in one handscroll, muted greys and browns. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
han-canal: 486 BCE, Han near Yangzhou: thousands of labourers dig a long canal through flat lowland between lakes and rivers, carrying earth in baskets on shoulder poles; boats loaded with troops and supplies begin to sail north along the finished section, and a newly built walled town rises beside it. Wide bird's-eye view, spring light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, many small figures.
battle-of-ailing: 484 BCE, Ailing near Laiwu: the combined Wu and Lu armies surround the Qi forces on a hilly plain, Wu warriors with short hair and tattooed arms pressing forward with bronze swords and dagger-axes, Qi chariots overturned in the distance. Seen from afar, dust and banners, no bodies. Painted with the black, cinnabar and ochre palette of Spring and Autumn period lacquerware.
wu-zixu-forced-suicide: 484 BCE, Gusu (Suzhou): an aged minister in dark robes stands alone on the high eastern gate tower of the Wu capital, holding a sheathed bronze sword, gazing toward the southeast where Yue lies beyond lakes and mist; a royal envoy departs below. Grey dusk, seen from behind. No violence shown. Ink and light colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
meeting-at-huangchi: 482 BCE, Huangchi near Fengqiu: a grand assembly of lords on the Yellow River plain, a Wu king in fine robes on a high earthen altar, the Jin delegation facing him, ranks of Wu soldiers in white, red and black formations; meanwhile, on the far horizon to the south, a thin column of smoke rises where the undefended Wu capital lies. Bright day. Figures small. Painted with the black, cinnabar and ochre palette of Spring and Autumn period lacquerware.
tian-family-qi: 481 BCE, Linzi: armed retainers of the Tian clan on foot, carrying halberds and banners, pour through the gate of the Qi palace compound with two-horse war chariots rolling behind them; rival nobles flee down a street of rammed-earth walls and timber halls, and a nobleman in fine robes stands on the palace terrace as officials bow. Smoke over one corner of the city. Seen from afar, no bloodshed, nobody riding on horseback, no text. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, cinnabar and ochre.
capture-of-the-lin: 481 BCE, Daye Marsh near Juye: hunters in short tunics with nets and spears gather around a strange gentle creature with a single horn, deer-like body and scaled hide, lying quietly in the reeds of a wide marsh; an elderly scholar in plain robes stands nearby, sleeve raised to his face in sorrow. Grey sky, wild geese overhead. Figures small. Ink and light colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
death-of-confucius: 479 BCE, north of Qufu: a simple earthen grave mound under ancient trees beside the Si River, with small thatched huts built around it where disciples in white hemp mourning robes sit in quiet contemplation, some reading bamboo slips, one tending a plant. Misty morning, muted greens and greys, figures small, seen from a distance. Ink and light colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
rebellion-of-duke-bai: 479 BCE, Ying near Jingzhou: rebel troops with painted shields occupy the gates of the Chu capital among its lakes; in the distance, a relief army led by a lord in a chariot approaches along a causeway as townspeople open the gates to welcome them. Seen from afar, no bloodshed. Misty air, banners with phoenix designs. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, black and red.
battle-of-lize: 478 BCE, the Li Marsh near Wujiang: at night, Yue soldiers in small boats with torches cross a wide river from both flanks, drums sounding, while the Wu camp on the opposite bank wakes in confusion; reeds and water lit by flames. Seen from a distance, no bodies. Dark indigo night with orange reflections. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
chu-destroys-chen: 478 BCE, Wanqiu near Huaiyang: Chu officials in southern robes and tall caps arrive at the gates of a walled city on the Huai plain, replacing the old banners with Chu ones, while local people gather; a Chu army camp stands outside. Calm overcast day, quiet transition. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, swirling cloud motifs, black and red.
chu-destroys-cai: 447 BCE, Xiacai near Fengtai on the Huai River: a Chu army of chariots and foot soldiers enters a small walled town by the broad river, Chu banners raised on gate towers, local nobles in robes bowing; boats on the river and flat green fields beyond. Clear spring day, seen from afar. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black ground with cinnabar and ochre figures.
marquess-wen-of-wei: c. 445 BCE, Anyi near Xia County: in a hall of the Wei court, a ruler sits on a mat with scholars, strategists and officials in robes arranged before him, discussing bamboo slip documents; outside, irrigation channels, orderly fields and soldiers drilling. Warm afternoon light. No legible writing, figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
mozi-stops-chu-attack: c. 440 BCE, Ying near Jingzhou: in a Chu palace hall, a lean thinker in coarse plain clothing and straw sandals faces a master craftsman across a low table, playing a war game with a belt laid out as a city wall and small wooden blocks as siege engines; a Chu king watches from a dais. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, black and red.
marquis-yi-zeng: c. 433 BCE, Suizhou in Hubei: inside a great wooden tomb chamber, a set of 65 bronze bells hangs in three tiers from a lacquered wooden frame supported by bronze figures, alongside stone chimes, zithers and lacquered coffins; attendants in robes carefully arrange the burial goods by torchlight. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, rich black, red and bronze.
chu-destroys-ju: 431 BCE, Ju in eastern Shandong: Chu troops with painted shields and dagger-axes stand outside the opened gates of a hilly walled town, local nobles surrendering; banners of Chu raised on walls, hills and fields of the Shandong countryside behind. Seen from afar, no bloodshed. Bright autumn day. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
ximen-bao-governs-ye: c. 422 BCE, Ye near Linzhang on the Zhang River: an official in robes stands on the riverbank before a crowd of villagers and elders; a group of shamans in fringed robes stand trembling at the water's edge before guards; in the background, labourers dig a network of irrigation canals across green fields. Clear day. No one harmed, figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
wei-takes-hexi: 409 BCE, Hexi near Hancheng: Wei troops with dagger-axes and crossbows advance across the loess plateau west of the Yellow River, chariots and foot soldiers in ordered ranks, while Qin forces retreat toward the Luo River in the distance; newly built Wei forts rise on the hills. Dusty, seen from afar, no bloodshed. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
qin-taxes-grain: 408 BCE, Yong near Fengxiang: Qin officials with bronze measuring vessels and bamboo slips sit at tables in a village square as farmers bring baskets of millet to be measured; granaries with thatched roofs, fields stretching to the Qinling hills. Golden autumn day. No legible writing. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
li-kui-reforms: c. 406 BCE, Anyi in Wei: in a hall, a minister in robes presents bundles of bamboo slips to a ruler; outside, well-ordered farmland with officials measuring fields and state granaries buying grain from farmers in a good harvest. Spring light. No legible writing, figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, ochre and green.
wei-conquers-zhongshan: c. 406 BCE, Gu near Dingzhou: a Wei army besieges a walled city on the northern plain at the foot of the Taihang mountains, siege ladders and earthworks around, banners raised; a general in armour sits before his tent, an untouched bowl in front of him. Seen from afar, no bloodshed. Late winter, grey sky. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
knife-money-of-qi: c. 400 BCE, Linzi: a bustling market street in the Qi capital, merchants in robes trade salt, fish, silk and pottery, using strings of bronze knife-shaped coins; a mint workshop nearby where craftsmen pour bronze into stone moulds; traders from the central plains bring spade-shaped coins. Bright day, many small figures. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
nie-zheng-assassination: 397 BCE, Yangzhai near Yuzhou: outside a great hall of the Han state, guards rush in disarray toward the steps while a single swordsman in dark clothing disappears into the shadows of a gate; in the street below, a veiled woman kneels among onlookers. No blood or bodies shown, figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
marquess-wu-on-the-river: c. 387 BCE, Xihe on the Yellow River: a decorated river boat sails down between towering loess cliffs and mountains; on deck, a ruler in robes gestures at the steep banks while a general in armour beside him shakes his head and points to the people in villages on the shore. Bright day, rushing brown water. Figures small. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
tian-qi: 386 BCE, Linzi: a royal envoy from the Zhou court in plain robes presents a jade token and bronze vessels to a new ruler of Qi in a grand palace hall; officials and nobles kneel in rows, banners of the Tian family. Golden morning light through tall timber columns. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
wu-qi-chu: c. 386 BCE, Ying near Jiangling: a stern general in armour reviews Chu troops on a parade ground by the lakes, soldiers with crossbows and dagger-axes in neat ranks; in the background, nobles in elaborate robes leave the capital with carts toward remote border lands. Misty air, cloud-swirl banners. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, black and red.
qin-abolishes-human-burial: 384 BCE, Yong near Fengxiang: at a Qin royal funeral, a procession carries lacquered coffins and clay and wooden figurines to a tomb, while a group of attendants who would once have been buried stand aside, freed; a duke in mourning robes stands at the tomb edge. Grey autumn day, cypress trees. Ink and light colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
qin-moves-to-yueyang: 383 BCE, Yueyang near Xi'an: a new walled Qin capital on the Wei plain, officials register households in groups of five at tables in a square, merchants set up stalls in a newly opened market, soldiers patrol the walls facing east. Bright spring day, bird's-eye view. No legible writing. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, many small figures.
death-of-wu-qi: 381 BCE, Ying near Jingzhou: in a royal funeral hall draped with black and red silk, mourners and nobles crowd around a lacquered coffin bier; a general in armour has thrown himself across the bier while nobles with bows stand at the door, arrows in flight. Seen from a distance, tense, no blood. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
end-of-jin: 376 BCE, Quwo: three nobles of Han, Zhao and Wei, each with retainers and banners, stand in a once-grand Jin palace courtyard as officials remove bronze vessels; a dethroned duke in plain robes walks out of the gate alone, seen from behind. Late autumn, falling leaves, quiet decline. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
battle-of-shimen: 364 BCE, Shimen near Yuncheng: Qin troops in close ranks with crossbows and dagger-axes advance across a dry plain while Wei chariots retreat in disarray toward distant hills; afterwards, a Zhou envoy presents embroidered robes to a duke in a field camp. Seen from afar, dust, no bodies. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
duke-xiao-seeks-talent: 361 BCE, Yueyang: officials post an edict on a gate tower at the city gate while scholars and travellers gather; on the road below, a thin man in scholar's robes walks toward the gate with a small bundle of bamboo slips under his arm. Morning light, crowded city gate. No legible writing. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
hong-canal: c. 360 BCE, Daliang (Kaifeng): workers dig a broad canal across the flat central plain, carrying earth in baskets, raising embankments with iron spades; boats laden with grain already sail along a finished stretch toward the Huai River, past villages and willow trees. Bright day, bird's-eye view. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black ground with cinnabar and ochre figures.
shen-buhai-reforms-han: c. 355 BCE, Xinzheng: in a hall of the Han court, rows of officials kneel at low tables before a ruler, each holding bamboo slip records; a minister in robes walks along the rows, comparing records and checking performance. Orderly, quiet atmosphere, lamplight. No legible writing, figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
zou-ji-advises-king-wei: c. 355 BCE, Linzi: a tall, elegant minister in fine robes stands before a large polished bronze mirror in a Qi palace hall, speaking to a king on his dais; outside the palace gate, crowds of people line up eagerly to present their criticisms to officials. Bright morning light. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
gan-shi-star-catalog: c. 350 BCE, Linzi: at night on a high earthen terrace, a Warring States astronomer in long robes stands pointing up at the sky, observing with the naked eye beside a simple bronze gnomon pole, while a second scholar kneels at a low table recording on bamboo slips by an oil lamp. The deep indigo sky is full of constellations with one bright planet. A sleeping walled city with tiled roofs lies below. No telescope, no lenses, no optical instruments, no lettering. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
xianyang-capital: c. 350 BCE, Xianyang: a new Qin capital rises on the north bank of the Wei River, rammed-earth walls and palace halls on high platforms, gate towers, workers hauling timber; officials measure land and set up county boundary markers in the surrounding villages. Wide bird's-eye view, golden afternoon. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
bian-que: c. 350 BCE, Handan: a travelling physician in plain robes sits in a modest household courtyard, his fingers on the wrist of a seated patient, an apprentice with medicine pouches and bamboo slips nearby; villagers wait at the gate. Warm afternoon light, a mulberry tree. Figures small, no recognisable faces. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
shang-yang-standard-measures: 344 BCE, Xianyang: in a Qin official workshop, craftsmen cast bronze rectangular measuring vessels with a long handle and weigh grain on balance scales with standard weights; officials compare and stamp vessels, merchants queue in a market outside. Bright day. No legible writing. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, bronze and ochre tones.
fengze-assembly: 344 BCE, Fengze near Kaifeng: a ruler in royal robes and a vermilion cap rides in an elaborate chariot with royal banners before an assembly of lesser lords bowing in ranks on a plain; tents and chariots of many states surround. Bright sky, grand display. Figures small. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
maling: 342 BCE, Maling: at dusk, a Wei army column marches into a narrow wooded valley between steep hills; hidden Qi crossbowmen line the slopes on both sides, torches about to be lit. A large tree with a patch of stripped bark stands by the road. Seen from far above, no bloodshed. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, deep greens and darkening sky.
qin-defeats-wei-hexi: 340 BCE, Hexi near Dali: a peaceful parley tent on a plain between two armies, two commanders in robes drinking wine together; outside, hidden Qin soldiers emerge from behind a hill, and in the distance the Wei army flees toward the Yellow River. Seen from afar, no bloodshed. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
shang-yang-death: 338 BCE, Xianyang: an empty chariot overturned on a road near the capital and banners of officials coming from the city; in the background, the Qin capital's walls and palace halls, and fields still divided in the orderly grid of the new laws. Grey sky, sombre mood. No body or violence shown. Ink and light colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
qin-issues-coins: 336 BCE, Xianyang: in a Qin state mint, workers pour molten bronze into clay moulds and break open finished round coins with square holes, stringing them on cords; officials count strings of coins in a hall. Fire glow, smoke rising over the tiled roofs of the capital, merchants waiting at the gate. No legible inscriptions. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
xuzhou-mutual-kings: 334 BCE, Xuzhou near Tengzhou: two rulers in royal robes and tall caps face each other on a raised terrace, exchanging bows and gifts of jade and bronze, their attendants and chariots arrayed on either side; a small Zhou banner hangs neglected to one side. Bright day, many small figures. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
chu-defeats-yue: 334 BCE, Kuaiji near Shaoxing: a Chu army with painted shields, dagger-axes and crossbows advances through the hills and rice paddies of the southeast, Yue warriors with short hair retreating toward the coast; smoke rises from a hill fortress. Seen from afar, no bloodshed. Misty subtropical landscape. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, rich black and red.
su-qin-vertical-alliance: c. 333 BCE, Handan: a persuader in fine robes and cap rides in a grand chariot procession through the Zhao capital, with six banners of six states carried by attendants and officials bowing along the road. Bright day, crowds on rooftops, palace halls behind. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
zhang-yi-horizontal: 328 BCE, Xianyang: in a Qin palace hall, a sharp-tongued strategist in robes gestures over a large painted silk map laid on the floor showing rivers and mountains, while a Qin king and ministers listen; envoys from other states wait outside. Lamplight. No legible text, figures small. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
qin-ruler-takes-king-title: 325 BCE, Xianyang: a grand ceremony in the Qin palace courtyard, a ruler in black royal robes ascends a high earthen terrace while officials and soldiers in black kneel in rows; bronze bells ring, banners fly. Clear sky, imposing palace halls. Figures small, seen from behind. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
mencius-meets-king-hui: c. 320 BCE, Daliang (Kaifeng): in a Wei palace hall, an elderly scholar in plain robes kneels on a mat before a king, gesturing earnestly; ministers sit around, bronze vessels and lacquer tables. Through the open doors, ordinary people work in the fields. Warm light. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
jixia: c. 319 BCE, Linzi: by the Ji Gate of the Qi capital, a complex of elegant halls and courtyards where scholars of many schools in robes sit in circles debating, reading bamboo slips, strolling under trees; servants bring food, gingko trees and covered walkways link the halls. Bright day. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
five-states-attack-qin: 318 BCE, Hangu Pass near Lingbao: an allied army of five states with many differently coloured banners camps before a narrow pass between steep loess cliffs; the Qin fortress gate stands closed above. Some allied camps strike their tents and depart. Dusty, seen from afar, no bloodshed. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
king-kuai-abdicates: 316 BCE, Xiadu near Yi County: in the Yan palace hall, an old king in royal robes descends from the dais and hands a jade seal to a minister bowing before him, while other nobles look on uneasily; outside, troops gather in the streets. Grey sky. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
qi-invades-yan: 314 BCE, Xiadu near Yi County: a Qi army of chariots and foot soldiers enters the open gates of the Yan capital on the northern plain; soldiers carry away bronze vessels and bells on carts, while in the surrounding villages angry Yan people gather with farm tools on the hillsides. Smoke over the city, seen from afar, no bloodshed. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
zhang-yi-deceives-chu: 313 BCE, Ying near Jingzhou: in a Chu palace hall, a Qin envoy in black robes holds up a small bamboo slip and shows a tiny gap between two fingers, while a Chu king in southern robes and tall cap rises angrily from his seat; courtiers turn in shock. Lamplight, red and black lacquered pillars. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
battle-of-danyang: 312 BCE, Danyang near Xichuan: Qin troops in dark armour with crossbows and dagger-axes push forward across a river valley in the Qinling hills while a Chu army in red retreats in disorder, banners falling. Seen from high above, dust and smoke, no bodies. Autumn forests on steep slopes. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
golden-terrace: c. 311 BCE, Xiadu near Yi County: a tall earthen terrace with a timber pavilion on top, gold ingots displayed on a lacquer table at its summit, stands by a river; scholars and travellers in robes arrive by road and chariot from many directions while a king in robes bows to an elder at the foot of the steps. Bright morning. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
battle-of-yiyang: 307 BCE, Yiyang in the hills west of Luoyang: a Qin army camps around a strong walled fortress in the Luo River valley, siege ladders and earthworks raised; the fortress gates finally open as Qin troops march in. In the courtyard, a huge bronze tripod cauldron stands. Seen from afar, no bloodshed. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
li-sao: c. 305 BCE, the marshes near Ying: a lone poet-minister in a tall cap, long sword at his waist and robes adorned with orchids, walks along a riverbank among reeds and fragrant plants, seen small from behind; swirling clouds overhead contain faint dragons and a phoenix-drawn chariot. Misty dusk. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, flowing line, black, red and gold.
zhuangzi: c. 300 BCE, Meng near Shangqiu: a thinker in loose plain robes lies dozing under a large tree in a lacquer-tree grove beside a stream, a butterfly fluttering above him and more butterflies drifting among flowers; a distant village and the plain beyond. Gentle spring afternoon, serene mood. Figures small. Ink and light colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
ying-yuan-gold: c. 300 BCE, Ying near Jingzhou: in a Chu treasury workshop, craftsmen stamp small square marks into flat gold plates and cast tiny oval bronze coins in moulds; merchants weigh gold pieces on a balance scale in a market by a lake. Bright day. No legible writing, stamps shown as abstract squares. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, gold and black.
guodian-chu-slips: c. 300 BCE, Guodian near Jingmen: inside the timber chamber of a Chu tomb, attendants place bundles of bamboo slips tied with silk cords beside lacquered vessels, a scabbard and a dragon-handled cup next to a coffin with black and red lacquer designs. Lamplight, dark earth walls. No legible writing. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings.
king-huai-detained-in-qin: 299 BCE, Wu Pass near Danfeng: a narrow mountain pass in the Qinling range with a fortress gate; a Chu king in southern robes and tall cap arrives with a small retinue in chariots, and Qin soldiers in dark armour close the gates behind him. Mountain mist, steep forested slopes. Figures small, no violence shown. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
mengchang-attacks-qin: 298 BCE, Hangu Pass near Lingbao: a single moonlit view down a narrow loess gorge, the great timber gate of the pass standing open in its rammed-earth walls, and an allied army of Qi, Han and Wei soldiers on foot and in horse-drawn chariots pouring through under many banners, torches flickering along the column, steep yellow cliffs on both sides. One continuous scene, figures small, no bloodshed. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
crisis-at-shaqiu: 295 BCE, Shaqiu near Guangzong: a palace complex on the northern plain surrounded by Zhao soldiers and cavalry in short tunics and trousers riding without stirrups; inside, an empty courtyard where birds' nests on the eaves have been disturbed, and an old man in robes stands alone at a window. Winter, bare trees. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
yique: 293 BCE, Yique near Longmen: Qin troops in dark armour advance through the narrow river gorge where the Yi River passes between two steep cliffs, while the combined Han and Wei armies break and retreat; banners fall, the river glinting below the grey cliffs. Seen from afar, dust and smoke, no bodies. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre.
