No legible text. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print illustration, fine line and light colour.
feng-menglong-sanyan: 1620, Suzhou: an editor in a scholar's robe works at a desk piled with manuscripts beside a window overlooking a canal and arched stone bridge, while outside in the street a storyteller entertains a crowd of townspeople, porters and shop clerks; tiled roofs and boats. Figures small, no legible text. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
red-pill-case: 1620, the Beijing palace at night: in a dim imperial bedchamber, a lacquered tray holds a small dish of red pills beside a tea bowl, a silk-curtained bed in shadow, eunuchs and physicians waiting anxiously outside the door with lanterns; the courtyard silent under the moon. No figures in close-up. Painted as a Ming court painting, ink and deep mineral colour on silk.
palace-removal-case: 1620, the Beijing palace: before the great Palace of Heavenly Purity, officials in red robes stand in the courtyard while a procession of palace women and eunuchs carrying chests moves out through a side gate to another palace; a boy-emperor's sedan chair waits under parasols. Figures small. Painted as a Ming court painting in ink and mineral colour on silk.
fall-of-shenyang-liaoyang: 1621, Liaoyang in Liaodong: Later Jin banner cavalry and infantry with siege ladders surround the walled city beside the Taizi River, smoke rising from the gate towers, Ming defenders on the walls, the white Liaoyang pagoda standing above the roofs; spring fields and distant hills. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted in the style of an early Qing battle handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
she-an-rebellion: 1621, Yongning in the mountains of southern Sichuan: Yi warriors in dark cloaks and turbans with spears and shields gather on a high mountain ridge above deep valleys, their fortified hilltop villages behind, a Ming walled town visible far below; clouds and terraced fields. Distant view, no gore. Painted as a Ming blue-green landscape scroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
battle-of-guangning: 1622, Guangning (Beizhen) in western Liaodong: a long Ming column of soldiers, refugees and ox-carts retreats westward across a frozen winter plain toward distant mountains, the walled town with its tall brick pagoda left behind, Later Jin banner cavalry visible on the far horizon; smoke from abandoned camps, bare trees and snow. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a late Ming ink handscroll with pale colour on silk.
sino-dutch-penghu: 1622-1624, the Penghu islands in the Taiwan Strait: a small square Dutch fort of earth and stone on a flat windswept island, Dutch East India Company ships with square sails anchored offshore, while a large fleet of Ming war junks and many soldiers land on the beach and set up camps around it; low coral-stone walls, choppy sea. Distant panorama. Painted as a seventeenth-century Dutch engraving, fine hatched line, lightly coloured.
dutch-formosa: 1624, Tayouan (Anping) in southwestern Taiwan: Dutch builders and Chinese labourers raise a square brick fort with angled bastions on a sandbar beside a lagoon, East India Company ships at anchor, Siraya villagers in loincloths watching from coconut palms on the mainland shore. Bright tropical day, figures small. Painted as a seventeenth-century Dutch topographical engraving with light watercolour, fine line.
donglin-purge: 1625, Beijing: the grim stone gate of the imperial guard prison on a cold grey morning, guards in embroidered robes leading several scholar-officials in plain robes and chains through the entrance, their families and students kneeling in the snowy street outside; crows on the wall. No violence shown, figures small and seen from behind. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print illustration, stark black line.
ningyuan: 1626, Ningyuan (Xingcheng) in winter: on the battlements of a square brick city wall, Ming gunners fire large bronze Western-style cannon, clouds of white smoke rolling over the snowy plain, where Jurchen banner troops with siege carts and ladders fall back; the sea glimpsed beyond. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a late Ming battle handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
wanggongchang-explosion: 1626, Beijing: a vast mushroom-like cloud of smoke and dust rises over the southwestern quarter of the walled city, tiled roofs flattened in a wide circle, trees stripped and debris falling, survivors in Ming clothing gathering on open streets at the edge; the palace roofs and city wall in the foreground. Distant view, no bodies shown. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print illustration with smoky ink washes.
wei-zhongxian-falls: 1627, Fucheng on the North China plain: a long baggage train of carts loaded with chests, escorted by servants, halted at a rural inn in winter dusk, lanterns glowing in the courtyard, bare poplars and a frozen road; a messenger on horseback arriving with an imperial order. Quiet, ominous mood, no figures in close-up. Painted as a late Ming ink painting with muted colour on paper.
battle-of-ningjin: 1627, the Liaoxi corridor between Ningyuan and Jinzhou: Ming fortresses with brick walls and Western-style cannon stand along a coastal plain, white smoke rising from the ramparts as Later Jin banner cavalry and infantry assault in summer heat and pull back; the sea and hills on either side. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a late Ming battle handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
shaanxi-revolts: 1628, the loess plateau of northern Shaanxi: starving farmers and ragged soldiers in faded Ming uniforms gather on a cracked, barren hillside above cave dwellings, carrying hoes, spears and banners, a dry riverbed and withered fields below under a harsh pale sky. Distant view, figures small, no violence. Painted as a late Ming ink landscape with pale earth washes on paper.
postal-stations-cut: 1629, a courier relay station in northern Shaanxi: a walled post station with empty stables and a closed gate, a few dismissed couriers in short jackets leading their horses away down a dusty loess road, an official reading an order at the doorway; dry hills and a fading afternoon. Figures small, no legible writing. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
jisi-incident: 1629, outside Beijing in winter: Later Jin banner cavalry in coloured armour camp on the plain before the great city walls and gate towers, smoke rising from villages, while Ming defenders crowd the battlements and relief troops arrive from the east; snow on the fields. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as an early Qing court-style painting in ink and colour on silk.
yuan-chonghuan: 1630, Beijing in late summer: an empty general's armour, helmet and sword rest on a wooden stand in a deserted frontier command tent, banners furled, while through the open flap the distant walls and gate towers of Beijing appear under a heavy grey sky, a silent crowd gathered far off near the city gate. Sombre mood, no violence, no figures in close-up. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print illustration in black and grey ink.
battle-of-liaoluo-bay: 1633, Liaoluo Bay off Kinmen: a large fleet of Chinese junks with batten sails and fire ships closes on several Dutch East India Company warships, flames and cannon smoke drifting across the bay, rocky granite islands and the Fujian coast behind. Fishing sampans flee toward the shore under a stormy autumn sky. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a seventeenth-century Dutch maritime engraving with light watercolour, fine line.
chongzhen-calendar: 1634, the Beijing Ancient Observatory: on a brick platform on the city wall stand large bronze armillary spheres and quadrants, a Jesuit in Chinese scholar's robes and Chinese astronomers in official dress taking measurements at dusk, a table below with star charts and calculation sheets; stars appearing in a deep blue sky. No legible text. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
fengyang-tombs-burned: 1635, Fengyang in Anhui: the imperial ancestral tomb complex with a long spirit way of stone statues and red halls, now burning, smoke and flames rising from the halls and pine groves as rebel horsemen ride away across the plain. Distant panorama, no figures in close-up, no gore. Painted as a late Ming ink painting with smoky washes and touches of red on paper.
qing-proclaimed: 1636, Mukden (Shenyang): before the Dazheng Hall, an octagonal pavilion flanked by ten small banner pavilions, ranks of Manchu, Mongol and Han officials in fur-trimmed robes and banner commanders in armour kneel in the courtyard under fluttering banners of eight colours, incense and music. Ruler a distant figure on the steps. Painted as an early Qing court painting, ink and mineral colour on silk.
qing-invasion-joseon: 1636-1637, Namhansanseong in Korea in deep winter: Qing banner armies camp in the snowy valleys around a mountain fortress whose stone walls follow the ridgeline, smoke rising from many campfires, Joseon soldiers in padded coats and broad hats watching from the walls. Pine trees bend under snow along the steep slopes. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Joseon documentary painting in ink and light colour on paper.
tiangong-kaiwu: 1637, Fenyi in Jiangxi: a panoramic scene of rural crafts in one landscape — farmers transplanting rice, women reeling silk from cocoons, smiths at an iron furnace with bellows, papermakers lifting bamboo screens from vats, salt boiled in pans; a village with tiled houses and hills. Many small figures. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print technical illustration, crisp black line with light colour.
nongzheng-quanshu: 1639, Songjiang near Shanghai: a flat Jiangnan farming landscape of canals and rice fields, farmers working chain-pump waterwheels, ploughing with water buffalo and planting sweet potatoes, a scholar's study in the foreground with books and specimens on a table; willows and boats. Figures small, no legible text. Mulberry groves line the canal banks. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print agricultural illustration with light colour.
battle-of-songjin: 1641-1642, Songshan near Jinzhou: a vast Qing army of banner troops with trenches and earthworks encircles a walled Ming town on rolling hills, Ming relief columns broken and retreating toward the coast, cavalry pursuing, smoke over the plain; the Bohai sea glimpsed beyond. Supply wagons and horses crowd the Qing rear lines. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as an early Qing battle handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
luoyang-1641: 1641, Luoyang: before the gates of a princely palace with red walls, rebel soldiers open granaries and hand out sacks of grain to long lines of hungry peasants in ragged clothes, carts piled with rice and silver; smoke from the palace roofs, the city walls and Mang hills beyond. Figures small, no gore. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print illustration, strong black line with light colour.
kaifeng-flood-1642: 1642, Kaifeng on the Yellow River: a vast muddy flood engulfs the walled city, only gate towers, the top of the Iron Pagoda and rooftops rising above the brown water, small boats rescuing survivors, army camps on distant high ground. No bodies shown. The broken dike gapes on the horizon under a leaden sky. Painted as a late Ming ink landscape with heavy brown and grey washes on paper.
battle-of-tongguan-1643: 1643, Tongguan pass where the Yellow River bends: Li Zicheng's rebel cavalry stream through the fortified pass beneath steep loess cliffs, the Ming army's banners scattered across the hills, then the column continues toward the walls of Xi'an in the distance. Dust rises from thousands of hooves in the autumn light. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a late Ming landscape handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
zhang-xianzhong-wuchang: 1643, Wuchang on the Yangtze: rebel boats and soldiers swarm across the broad river toward the walled city on Snake Hill, the Yellow Crane Tower standing above the waterfront, smoke rising from the princely palace inside the walls; grey sky and wide river. Merchant junks scatter downstream past Turtle Hill on the far bank. Distant view, no gore. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
qing-moves-capital-beijing: 1644, Beijing: a long procession of Manchu bannermen in fur-trimmed armour and officials on horseback enters the great Zhengyangmen gate, a small yellow sedan chair carried in the middle, parasols and banners of eight colours; townspeople in Ming robes kneel along the road, the Forbidden City roofs beyond. Figures small. Painted as an early Qing court painting, ink and colour on silk.
hongguang-regime: 1644, Nanjing: in the old Ming palace, officials in Ming red robes and winged caps argue in factions in a hall while a lavish palace banquet with opera performers goes on in a courtyard, the city's grand walls and Yangtze beyond. Figures small, no close-ups. Painted as a late Ming woodblock-print illustration in the Nanjing style, fine line with light colour.
banner-land-enclosure: 1644-1645, the Zhili plain near Beijing: Manchu bannermen on horseback stake out fields with ropes and boundary flags, while Han farmers in Ming-style clothes leave their villages with carts of belongings and children; flat wheat fields, poplars and mud-walled houses. Figures small, no violence. Banner flags of yellow and white flutter over the newly claimed fields in a cold spring wind. Painted as an early Qing ink painting with pale colour on paper.
yangzhou-massacre: 1645, Yangzhou: seen from a distance across the Grand Canal, the walled city lies under columns of dark smoke, broken city walls and silent streets, Qing banners flying on the gate towers, a few refugees on boats in the foreground slipping away through reeds. Aftermath only, no bodies, no gore. Painted as an early Qing ink landscape with sombre grey washes on paper.
queue-order: 1645, a street in a Jiangnan town: a barber's stall at a crossroads with a bench, basin and razor, Han men in Ming-style robes lining up while Qing soldiers with queues stand guard; nearby, townsmen argue and some turn away in protest. Tiled shops and a canal behind. Figures small, no violence. Painted as an early Qing woodblock-print illustration, black line with light colour.
li-zicheng-dies: 1645, Jiugong Mountain in southeastern Hubei: a steep forested mountain with a Daoist temple near the summit wreathed in cloud, a few weary horsemen riding along a narrow path, local villagers with farm tools on a ridge above; misty green valleys. Figures tiny, no violence. Painted as an early Qing ink landscape hanging scroll in the manner of the Orthodox School, ink and light colour on paper.
jiading-massacre: 1645, Jiading near Shanghai: seen from far off, a small walled canal town with a pagoda lies under smoke under a grey summer sky, Qing troops' boats on the canal, abandoned fields and empty villages in the foreground. Aftermath only, no bodies, no gore. Willows droop over the still canal, and the town gate stands open and empty. Painted as an early Qing ink landscape with sombre washes on paper.
li-dingguo-guilin: 1652, Guilin: Southern Ming troops with war elephants and banners advance toward the walled city among dramatic karst peaks beside the Li River, smoke rising from the gate towers; Qing defenders on the walls. Soldiers in red and blue jackets with spears and muskets march along the riverbank, bamboo rafts carrying supplies on the clear green water. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as an early Qing blue-green landscape handscroll, ink and mineral colour on silk.
fifth-dalai-lama-visit: 1652-1653, Beijing: a great procession of Tibetan monks in maroon robes and yellow hats on horseback and in palanquins enters the city, carrying parasols and banners, received by Manchu officials in court robes with queues; the newly built Yellow Temple north of the walls. The lama himself is a small distant figure in a palanquin. Painted as a Qing court painting, ink and mineral colour on silk.
zheng-chenggong-nanjing: 1659, Nanjing: a vast fleet of Zheng war junks with batten sails fills the Yangtze below the city walls, soldiers camped on the hills near Guanyinmen, then Qing cavalry sallying out from the gates and the camps in disarray; smoke over the riverside, Purple Mountain behind. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as an early Qing battle handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
great-clearance: 1661, the Fujian coast: villagers in Qing-era clothing with queues carry bundles and lead water buffalo inland along a road away from empty fishing villages, burned boats and abandoned houses by the shore, a line of boundary markers and watchtowers along the hills, Qing soldiers supervising. Figures small, no violence. Painted as an early Qing ink landscape with pale colour on paper.
kumiao-case: 1661, Suzhou: in the courtyard of the Confucian temple, a crowd of scholars in robes and queues gathers in mourning for the late emperor, kneeling with a petition, while officials and soldiers enter through the gate; ancient cypress trees and tiled halls. Figures small, no violence. Incense smoke rises from a bronze censer before the main hall. Painted as an early Qing woodblock-print illustration, black line with light colour.
yongli-killed-kunming: 1662, Kunming: a quiet walled city beside Dian Lake under grey clouds, Qing soldiers guarding a small compound, a lone sedan chair carried along an empty road by a few bearers, the Western Hills rising across the water. Sombre mood, no figures in close-up, no violence. Fishing boats lie idle along the reedy shore. Painted as an early Qing ink landscape with muted colour on paper.
huang-zongxi-mingyi: 1663, Yuyao in Zhejiang: a scholar's simple study in a hillside cottage among bamboo, an older man in a plain robe writing by lamplight at a desk scattered with books, the window open to dark hills and the first glow of dawn. Figure seen from behind, no legible writing. Painted as an early Qing literati ink painting in the manner of the Anhui School, ink and light colour on paper.
calendar-case: 1664, Beijing: the bronze instruments on the observatory platform on the city wall stand unattended under a stormy sky, while in a courtyard below officials in Qing court robes lead an elderly Jesuit in Qing official dress away in chains; star charts scattered on a table. Figures small, no violence. Painted as a Qing court-style painting in ink and colour on silk.
oboi: 1669, the Forbidden City: in a palace hall, a group of young wrestlers in short jackets and sashes grapple with a burly elderly minister in a dark court robe, officials stepping back, a youthful figure in yellow seated on a distant dais. Figures small, no blood. Painted as a Qing court painting, ink and mineral colour on silk, decorative architecture.
three-feudatories-end: 1681, Kunming: Qing armies with banners and cannon surround the walled city beside Dian Lake, siege works and camps across the plain, the gates opening as defenders surrender; the Western Hills behind, clouds overhead. Columns of banner cavalry with yellow, white, red and blue flags ride along the lakeshore, and supply carts line the roads into the plain. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a Qing court battle painting, ink and colour on silk.
taiwan-prefecture: 1684, Tainan: a new Qing prefectural yamen with tiled roofs and a gate courtyard rising in a town of brick houses, Qing officials in court robes with queues arriving from a junk at the harbour, local Han settlers and indigenous people watching; old Dutch fort ruins and palms nearby. Figures small. Painted as a Qing court-style topographical painting, ink and colour on silk.
lifting-sea-ban-1684: 1684, Guangzhou harbour on the Pearl River: a newly opened customs house with tiled roofs at the waterfront, Qing officials in robes and queues inspecting cargo from many Chinese junks with batten sails, porters carrying bales of tea and silk, sampans crowding the river; city walls and pagodas behind. Clerks with abacuses tally cargo on the quay. Painted as a Qing woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
kangxi-southern-tour: 1684, the Yellow River near its Huai confluence and then Nanjing: an imperial procession on horseback with banners and parasols inspects long earthen river dikes, officials kneeling along the embankment, labourers repairing levees, imperial boats on the river. The emperor is a small figure among the retinue. Painted in the style of the Kangxi Southern Inspection Tour scrolls, ink and colour on silk.
albazin: 1685-1686, Albazin on the Amur River: Qing troops in Manchu armour with cannon and earthworks besiege a wooden Russian stockade fort with log towers on a bluff above the wide river, boats on the water, taiga forest and low hills behind. Russian defenders in kaftans watch from the palisade. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a Qing court battle painting, ink and colour on silk.
battle-of-ulan-butung: 1690, Ulan Butung in Inner Mongolia: Galdan's Dzungar army shelters behind a long line of camels laid down and covered with felt along a marsh, while Qing banner troops with cannon and muskets fire across the grassland, white smoke drifting; hills and a red butte behind. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Qing court battle painting, ink and colour on silk.
dolon-nor-assembly: 1691, Dolon Nor on the Inner Mongolian grassland: a great encampment of imperial yellow tents and Mongol yurts on the steppe, Khalkha princes in fur-trimmed robes kneeling before a large imperial tent, horses and banners everywhere, wrestling and archery contests on the grass. Emperor a distant figure. Painted as a Qing court painting in the style of Castiglione's Mongol banquet scenes, ink and colour on silk.
jao-modo: 1696, Jao Modo by the Tuul River in Mongolia: Qing banner troops with cannon hold a hillside under a pine-dotted ridge while Dzungar cavalry charge across the valley below, smoke and dust rising, baggage carts and camels in the rear. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a Qing court battle painting in the style of the Qianlong conquest engravings, ink and colour.
peach-blossom-fan: 1699, Beijing: an elegant private stage in a garden hall, actors in late Ming costume performing a kunqu scene, a young woman holding a white folding fan spotted with red peach blossoms, musicians with flutes and clappers, an audience of officials in Qing robes and queues seated at tables; lanterns and painted screens. Painted as a Qing court painting, ink and soft colour on silk.
chengde-mountain-resort: 1703, Rehe (Chengde): a summer palace of grey-tiled halls, pavilions and lakes nestled in green mountains, with the odd hammer-shaped Sledgehammer Peak on the skyline; Mongol princes in fur-trimmed robes ride in with retinues, Qing officials with queues greet them, imperial yurts pitched in the Garden of Ten Thousand Trees, deer grazing on the lawns. Figures small. Painted as a Qing court painting in the Castiglione manner, ink and colour on silk.
yinreng-deposed: 1708, the Forbidden City: in a vast palace courtyard officials and princes in Qing court robes and queues kneel in rows on the stone pavement, while a young man in a yellow-brown robe is led away by guards through a side gate; golden roofs, autumn sky. All figures small and seen from behind or afar. Painted as a Qing court painting, ink and mineral colour on silk.
fixed-ding-quota: 1712, a rural county yamen in north China: clerks in Qing dress with queues sit at a long table copying household registers, farmers in short jackets and straw hats waiting in line at the gate; through the doorway, peaceful wheat fields and a growing village of mud-brick houses. Calm scene, no legible writing. Painted as a Qing woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
kangxi-dictionary: 1716, the Wuying Hall printing office in the Forbidden City: scholars in Qing robes with queues compare manuscript sheets of characters while craftsmen carve woodblocks, print pages and bind thick stitched volumes in blue covers stacked on tables; red columns and lattice windows. No legible text on any page. Painted as a Qing court painting, fine line and soft colour on silk.
kangxi-atlas: 1718, a mountainous Qing province: a survey team of Jesuits in Qing official dress and Chinese surveyors with queues sets up a brass quadrant and measuring chain on a hilltop, a large hand-drawn map sheet with mountains and rivers on a field table, horses and attendants waiting; folded ridges stretching to the horizon. No legible text. Painted as a Qing court painting, ink and colour on silk.
kangxi-bans-christianity: 1721, Beijing: a European-style church facade with a cross on the roof standing among grey-tiled courtyard houses, its gate closed, a few missionaries in Qing robes leaving with bundles under escort, Qing officials with queues reading an order at the gate; a winter street with passers-by. Figures small. Painted as a Qing court-style painting with Western perspective in the Castiglione manner, ink and colour on silk.
tanding-rumu: 1723, a north China village: farmers in short jackets and queues plough fields with oxen, while at the village gate a county clerk measures a field boundary with a rope and a landlord in a fine robe pays tax silver at a table; mud-brick houses and willow trees. Peaceful, figures small. Painted as a Qing woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
lobzang-danjin-revolt: 1723-1724, the Qinghai plateau near Xining: Qing banner cavalry sweep across a high grassy plain dotted with black yak-hair tents of the Khoshut Mongols, herds of horses and sheep scattering, snow mountains and Qinghai Lake in the distance. Tibetan-style monastery walls stand on a far hillside, and Qing supply camels follow the cavalry in a long line. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a Qing court battle painting, ink and colour on silk.
huohao-guigong: 1724, a provincial treasury in a Qing yamen: clerks in official dress with queues melt and recast small silver ingots into large uniform ingots in a furnace room, others weigh and record them at scales; officials in robes with rank badges inspect; locked treasury chests in rows. No legible writing. Account books lie stacked on a lacquered shelf by the door. Painted as a Qing woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
gaitu-guiliu: 1726, the mountains of Yunnan near Kunming: a Qing official in court robes with soldiers arrives at a hilltop chieftain's fortified compound, the hereditary chief in local dress handing over a seal box, Yi and Miao villagers in embroidered clothing watching; terraced fields and cloud-wrapped peaks. Figures small. Painted as a Qing tribute-album style painting of southwestern peoples, ink and colour on paper.
treaty-of-kyakhta: 1727, Kyakhta on the Siberian-Mongolian border: on a grassy plain a Qing envoy's camp of tents and a Russian log-built trading post face each other across a boundary line of wooden markers, camel caravans loaded with tea bricks and furs arriving, Russian officers in tricorn hats and Qing officials in robes meeting. Figures small. Painted as an eighteenth-century European topographical engraving with light watercolour.
amban-tibet: 1727-1728, Lhasa: the white and red Potala Palace on its hill above the town, a small Qing official residence with Chinese tiled roofs in the valley, an escort of Qing soldiers in red jackets and Tibetans in chuba robes with yaks on the road; snow peaks around. Figures small. Painted in the style of a Tibetan thangka landscape, mineral pigments, bright blue and green.
grand-council: 1729, the Forbidden City: a row of small modest board rooms beside the Gate of Heavenly Purity, where ministers in court robes and queues kneel at low tables drafting edicts by lamplight, a eunuch carrying sealed boxes toward the inner palace; golden roofs and red walls beyond. Figures small, no legible writing. Painted as a Qing court painting, fine line and colour on silk.
opium-ban-1729: 1729, a Fujian port town: Qing yamen runners with queues raid a small opium den in a back street, seizing long pipes and lamps from low couches, the smoky room lit by oil lamps, an official reading an edict at the doorway to a gathering crowd; tiled shops and a harbour behind. Figures small, no violence. Painted as a Qing woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
the-scholars-novel: 1750, Nanjing: a poor scholar's simple lodging near the Qinhuai River, a man in a worn robe writing at a desk by a window, while outside along the river examination candidates in blue robes crowd teahouses and pleasure boats, and the huge examination hall rows are visible beyond. Figures small, no legible writing. Painted as a Qing woodblock-print illustration of the novel, fine line with light colour.
canton-system: 1757 onward, Guangzhou: a row of Western-style factory buildings with verandas and flagpoles lines the Pearl River waterfront outside the city wall, foreign merchants in tricorn hats and Chinese Hong merchants in silk robes with queues inspect tea chests, while sampans, junks and East Indiamen crowd the river. Painted as a Canton export painting in gouache on paper, bright daylight.
altishahr-khojas: 1759, Kashgar: Qing banner cavalry and infantry ride across a desert plain toward the mud-brick walls of the oasis city with its domed mosque and poplar trees, local Uyghur townspeople in turbans and long coats watching from orchards; the snowy Pamir mountains on the horizon. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted in the style of the Qianlong conquest engravings of the western regions, fine copperplate line.
sino-burmese-war: 1765-1769, near Bhamo on the Irrawaddy: Qing troops in red jackets with mules struggle through tropical jungle hills and monsoon rain, while Burmese soldiers with muskets man a wooden stockade on the riverbank; war boats on the wide brown river, palm trees and golden pagoda spires in the distance. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted in the style of a Burmese temple mural, flat bright colours.
torghut-return: 1771, Ili valley: a vast column of Torghut Mongols, weary families with camels, ox-carts, horses and sheep, arrives over a mountain pass into the green Ili valley, felt yurts dismantled and packed, Qing officials waiting with supplies of grain and tents below. Epic distant panorama, small figures. Painted as a Qing court painting, ink and colour on silk, wide landscape.
second-jinchuan-campaign: 1771-1776, the Gyalrong mountains of western Sichuan: Qing soldiers with cannon climb steep snowy slopes toward tall stone watchtowers of the local chiefdoms perched on cliffs above a deep river gorge, cable bridges and smoke from siege fires. Supply porters with heavy loads climb zigzag paths, and pine forests cling to the cliffs under drifting cloud. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted in the style of the Qianlong conquest copperplate engravings, fine line, lightly coloured.
siku-quanshu: 1773-1782, Beijing: in a grand library hall, scholars in Qing robes and queues copy texts at long tables while attendants carry finished volumes in wooden boxes to tall bookcases; in a courtyard outside, a small bonfire of confiscated books burns as officials watch. Figures small, no legible text. Painted as a Qing court painting, fine line and colour on silk.
wang-lun-uprising: 1774, Linqing on the Grand Canal in Shandong: rebel sect members in white headbands and plain jackets armed with swords and spears gather outside the walls of a canal city with a tall brick pagoda, grain barges stalled on the canal, Qing troops arriving in the distance. Figures small, no gore. Painted as a Qing woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
yizhulou-case: 1778, Rugao in Jiangsu: a scholar's family garden pavilion with a carved wooden name plaque left blank, Qing officials and yamen runners entering through the gate, collecting stacks of poetry books into baskets while family members kneel in the courtyard; bamboo and a pond. Figures small, no violence. Neighbours peer over the garden wall in silence. Painted as a Qing woodblock-print illustration, black line with light colour.
lin-shuangwen-rebellion: 1787-1788, central Taiwan near Dali: Qing troops landing from junks advance through sugarcane fields and bamboo groves toward villages surrounded by bamboo palisades, rebel militia with spears on a hillside, mountains of the central range behind. Qing war junks lie at anchor off a sandy shore, and smoke drifts above a distant walled county town. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted in the style of the Qianlong Taiwan campaign copperplate engravings, fine line with light colour.
anhui-troupes-beijing: 1790, Beijing: a temporary opera stage with a curving tiled roof set up on a decorated street for an imperial birthday, actors in brilliant painted faces and embroidered costumes performing acrobatics, musicians with fiddles and gongs, crowds of townspeople with queues watching; lanterns and banners everywhere. Figures small. Painted as a Qing court painting of birthday celebrations, ink and bright colour on silk.
red-chamber: 1791, Beijing: a woodblock printing workshop producing an illustrated novel, freshly printed pages drying on lines; one illustration shows a great aristocratic garden with pavilions, a young man and young women in elegant Qing dress beside a lotus pond under falling petals. No legible text. Readers in a nearby bookshop leaf through the bound volumes. Painted as a Qing woodblock-print novel illustration, fine black line with soft colour.
sino-nepalese-war: 1792, the Himalaya between Shigatse and Nepal: Qing banner troops with Tibetan auxiliaries cross high snowy passes in long columns, horses and yaks carrying cannon, Gorkha soldiers on a ridge above terraced fields in a steep valley. Prayer flags flutter on a cairn at the pass, and glaciers gleam under a hard blue sky. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted in the style of the Qianlong conquest copperplate engravings, fine line, lightly coloured.
golden-urn: 1793, Lhasa: inside the Jokhang temple's dim hall lit by butter lamps, a gleaming golden urn on an altar draped with silk, monks in maroon robes and Qing ambans in court robes standing on either side, painted pillars and thangkas on the walls. Figures small, no close-ups. Painted in the style of a Tibetan thangka, mineral pigments with gold detail.
white-lotus: 1796-1804, the mountains on the Hubei-Sichuan-Shaanxi border: rebel bands in white headcloths move through densely forested gorges and terraced hills, while Qing troops build fortified stockade villages on hilltops and burn bridges; mist in the valleys. Refugee families with baskets and goats climb toward the walled hilltop refuges, and smoke rises from a burned river ferry below. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a Qing ink landscape scroll with light colour on paper.
heshen-falls: 1799, Beijing: a magnificent mansion compound with gardens and pavilions in winter, officials and soldiers with queues carrying out chests of silver, gold ingots, jade, furs and porcelain into the snowy courtyard, clerks listing them at tables. Figures small, no violence. Bolts of silk, clocks from Europe and coral trees are lined up on the steps, and onlookers peer through the open gate into the courtyard. Painted as a Qing court-style painting, ink and colour on silk.
eight-trigrams: 1813, the Forbidden City: in autumn, a band of sect rebels with white headbands and swords climb over a palace gate wall, while from a balustrade a young man in Qing court dress fires a long matchlock musket, guards rushing across the courtyard; golden roofs and red walls. Figures small, no gore. Painted as a Qing court painting, ink and colour on silk.
jahangir-khoja-revolt: 1826, Kashgar: horsemen from Kokand in turbans and quilted robes ride across a dusty plain toward the walled Qing garrison town, while later Qing banner cavalry pursue a small group into the snowy Tianshan foothills; poplar trees and mud-brick houses. Camels with baggage follow the horsemen through the dust. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted in the style of a Central Asian Persianate miniature, bright flat colours.
sanyuanli-incident: 1841, Sanyuanli north of Guangzhou: a large crowd of Chinese villagers with queues, farm tools, spears and banners surrounds a small column of British soldiers in red coats in a rain-soaked landscape of paddy fields and hills, muskets useless in the downpour. Village banners and gongs rise above the crowd, and a temple roof shows among bamboo groves. Distant view, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century Canton export painting in gouache on paper.
battle-of-the-bogue: 1841, the Bogue (Humen) at the mouth of the Pearl River: British steam and sailing warships bombard granite Qing forts on hillsides along the narrow channel, smoke billowing, Qing war junks retreating; green hills and wide estuary. Rowing boats packed with marines head for a rocky landing beach, and the Qing banners on the fort walls are wreathed in smoke. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century British naval engraving, fine hatched line, lightly coloured.
haiguo-tuzhi: 1842, Yangzhou: a scholar's study with a desk covered by world maps, globes and translated books, a scholar in Qing dress with a queue sketching a map of foreign coasts and steamships by lamplight; through the window, a canal city and garden. Figure small, seen from behind, no legible text. A small brass telescope rests on the windowsill. Painted as a Qing woodblock-print illustration with light colour.
battle-of-zhenjiang: 1842, Zhenjiang on the Yangtze at the Grand Canal: British troops in red coats scale the city walls while smoke rises over the town, Manchu garrison soldiers on the battlements, British steamships on the river below Jinshan hill with its pagoda. Townspeople flee by boat along the Grand Canal, and the city gate towers burn against a hot summer sky. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century British illustrated newspaper engraving.
shanghai-opened: 1843-1845, Shanghai on the Huangpu River: a muddy riverside strip with a few new two-storey Western merchant houses and warehouses, sailing ships at anchor, Chinese junks crowding the river, porters with queues carrying bales, the walled Chinese city visible upstream. Figures small. Tea chests and bales of raw silk stand stacked on the bund, a Customs junk flies a pennant, and rice paddies stretch flat beyond the settlement. Painted as a nineteenth-century Canton export painting in gouache, panoramic waterfront.
taiping-capital-nanjing: 1853, Nanjing: a great Taiping army in red and yellow headscarves with long hair and banners marches through the city gates, crowds of townspeople watching, officials of the new regime posting proclamations, the Porcelain Tower rising above the roofs. No legible writing. Taiping war boats crowd the Yangtze outside the walls, and women soldiers march in their own ranks with banners. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese woodblock print with bright colour.
xiang-army: 1853, Hengyang in Hunan: recruits in plain jackets and trousers with queues drill with spears and muskets on a riverbank parade ground, officers on horseback, flatboats being built for a river navy on the Xiang River; hills and a walled town. Figures small. Rows of tents stand in neat lines, drums beat at the drill ground, and officers in Qing robes inspect the ranks. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese woodblock print illustration with light colour.
nian-rebellion: 1853, the Huaibei plain in Anhui: bands of Nian horsemen with banners ride across a flat yellow plain past earthen-walled villages, cavalry raising dust, peasants watching from the walls, a broad sky and bare trees. Wagon trains of plunder and herds of cattle follow the horsemen, while dust clouds hang over the sorghum fields and a lone watchtower stands on an earthen wall. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese ink landscape with pale colour on paper.
taiping-northern-expedition: 1853-1855, near Tianjin in winter: a Taiping column in red headscarves is trapped in a flooded, frozen plain of villages and canals, while Mongol cavalry of the Qing ride around it. The Grand Canal lies frozen, villages are ringed with earthworks and dikes, smoke rises from burned hamlets, and the dark winter sky hangs low over thin poplar trees and ice. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century Dianshizhai Pictorial lithograph, fine line in black ink.
tianjing-incident: 1856, Nanjing: a Taiping palace compound with tall walls and ornate gate towers at night, torches moving through courtyards and smoke rising from one palace, soldiers in red headscarves running along the streets, the city silent beyond. Lanterns lie fallen in the empty streets, and the Porcelain Tower is a pale shape against the dark. Distant view, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese woodblock print with dark ink and red highlights.
panthay-rebellion: 1856-1872, Dali in Yunnan: the walled city of Dali with its Three Pagodas beneath the Cangshan mountains beside Erhai Lake, Hui soldiers in turbans and Bai villagers on the walls, a mosque and Chinese-style roofs within, Qing army camps in the distance. Figures small. Caravans of mules carrying tea and salt pass the city gate. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese landscape painting, ink and colour on paper.
treaties-tianjin: 1858, Tianjin: a Chinese temple hall used for negotiations, British and French diplomats in frock coats seated across a table from Qing officials in court robes and hats with queues, papers and inkstand on the table; foreign gunboats visible on the Hai River through the doorway. Figures small, no legible text. Interpreters stand quietly behind the chairs. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving.
aigun: 1858, Aigun on the Amur River: a wooden Russian riverboat and log buildings on one bank, a Qing walled town with gate towers on the other, Russian officers in greatcoats and Qing officials in fur-trimmed robes meeting in a tent on the shore; broad river, forests and low hills. Figures small. Cossack soldiers and Qing bannermen stand apart along the riverbank. Painted as a nineteenth-century Russian topographical watercolour.
battle-of-sanhe: 1858, Sanhe in Anhui: Taiping armies in red headscarves surround a fortified town of earthen walls among lakes and paddy fields, smoke rising from Xiang Army camps, banners on both sides. Taiping cavalry close in from the flanks over low hills, defenders' cannon smoke hangs over the earthen ramparts, and reeds and willows line the shallow lakes in the autumn haze. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese woodblock print with light colour.
zizheng-xinpian: 1859, Nanjing (Tianjing): a scholar in Taiping dress with long hair sits at a desk drafting a treatise, with drawings of a steam locomotive, a steamship and a bank building pinned beside him, a window opening onto the city walls. Figure seen from behind, no legible text. A Western book and a small globe lie on the desk. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese woodblock print with light colour.
convention-of-peking: 1860, Beijing: a stately hall of the Board of Rites where British and French envoys in uniforms and frock coats sit facing Qing princes and officials in court robes, documents on a long table, foreign troops with bayonets outside in the courtyard. Figures small, no legible text. A carriage and mounted escort wait outside the gate, and the city walls are visible beyond the roofs. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving.
xinyou-coup: 1861, Beijing: inside a palace hall a yellow silk curtain screens two seated empresses dowager, a small boy on a throne before it, officials in Qing court robes kneeling in rows; guards in the courtyard. Figures small, faces not shown. Officials in black hats with peacock feathers bow low, palace eunuchs line the walls, and through the open doors the golden roofs of the Forbidden City glint in autumn light. Painted as a Qing court painting, ink and colour on silk.
zongli-yamen: 1861, Beijing: a modest official compound with a gate courtyard and tiled roofs, a sedan chair arriving, Western diplomats in frock coats and top hats entering while Qing officials in court robes greet them at the gate; a quiet hutong lane with willow trees. Figures small. Clerks carry document boxes across the courtyard, and a translator waits at the hall door. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving.
tongwen-guan: 1862, Beijing: a classroom in a traditional courtyard building with lattice windows, young Manchu and Han students in Qing robes with queues seated at wooden desks, a Western teacher in a dark frock coat standing beside a blackboard with a globe and a few foreign books on a shelf; a winter courtyard with a bare tree outside. Figures small, no legible writing on board or books. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine line with light wash.
dungan-revolt: 1862-1873, the Wei River valley near Xi'an and the loess hills of Gansu: burned villages and broken earthen walls across a dry landscape, columns of refugees with carts and mules on dusty roads, and years later Zuo Zongtang's Qing army camps with tents and banners spreading below the loess cliffs; a mosque minaret and a Chinese temple roof stand ruined far apart. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese ink landscape with pale earth colours on paper.
fall-of-tianjing: 1864, Nanjing: a breach blown in the massive city wall near Purple Mountain, Xiang Army soldiers in plain jackets with queues and banners pouring through the smoke into the city, fires rising from the Taiping palaces inside; the Yangtze and the surrounding hills under a hot summer sky. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese woodblock print of a Qing victory, bright colour and bold line.
jiangnan-arsenal: 1865, Shanghai on the Huangpu River: a new arsenal compound of brick workshops with tall smokestacks, steam engines and lathes inside a machine hall, Chinese workers with queues casting cannon barrels and building a small steamship on a slipway, while in a separate building translators work with Western books; Chinese junks on the river. Figures small, no legible text. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine hatched line.
tianjin-massacre: 1870, Tianjin on the Hai River: seen from across the river, smoke rises from a burning Catholic church with Gothic arches and a French orphanage beside it, an angry crowd gathered on the bank in the summer heat, junks and sampans on the water below. Distant view, no bodies, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century Dianshizhai Pictorial-style lithograph, fine ink line.
educational-mission: 1872, Shanghai harbour: a group of about thirty Chinese boys in long gowns, skullcaps and braided queues, with two officials, stand on a wharf beside trunks and walk up a gangway onto a Pacific steamship with tall funnels and masts, families and porters on the quay waving; sampans on the Huangpu River. Figures small, seen from behind. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine line with light wash.
china-merchants-steam: 1872-1873, the Shanghai Bund: a new company steamship with a tall smokestack and paddle wheels moored at a wharf, Chinese crews and porters with queues loading tribute rice bags and cargo, Chinese merchants in long gowns overseeing, foreign steamers and junks along the Huangpu River. Figures small. Painted as a nineteenth-century Canton export painting in gouache on paper, bright harbour view.
japanese-taiwan-expedition: 1874, the Mudan area in Hengchun, southern Taiwan: Japanese soldiers in Western-style dark uniforms with rifles march up a steep jungle valley toward a Paiwan village of slate-stone houses, Paiwan warriors watching from forested ridges, Japanese transport ships anchored offshore in a blue bay. Palm trees and banana groves line the riverbed. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Meiji-era Japanese nishiki-e woodblock print, bold colour.
great-famine: 1876-1879, Shanxi near Taiyuan: a parched landscape of cracked fields and bare trees under a white sky, villagers in ragged padded jackets with queues waiting in a long line at a relief kitchen beside a temple where officials ladle porridge from cauldrons; empty loess villages behind. Sombre mood, no bodies, figures small. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese famine-relief woodblock illustration in black ink.
reconquest-of-xinjiang: 1876-1877, near Ürümqi in Xinjiang: a long Qing army column with modern rifles, Krupp cannon and camel supply trains crosses a stony desert plain toward a mud-walled city, the snowy Tianshan range glittering behind; poplar groves and an oasis. Supply carts and herds of horses trail behind, and banners flutter in the dry wind. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese ink and colour painting with a wide desert landscape.
battle-fuzhou: 1884, Mawei anchorage on the Min River below Fuzhou: French ironclad warships open fire on a line of small wooden Chinese steam warships at anchor, smoke and flames rising, the Fuzhou shipyard with its workshops on the bank and green hills behind. Sampans scatter toward the riverbanks. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, dramatic smoke and fine hatched line.
xinjiang-province: 1884, Dihua (Ürümqi): a new provincial yamen with Chinese tiled gate and courtyard set in a walled town, Qing officials in court robes arriving on horseback, Uyghur and Hui townspeople in turbans and caps in a bazaar street outside, camels resting; the snowy Bogda peak in the distance. Figures small. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese ink and colour painting on paper.
battle-of-zhennan-pass: 1885, Zhennan Pass on the Guangxi-Vietnam border: Qing soldiers in black turbans and padded jackets with old and new rifles charge down from a long stone wall built across a mountain pass, French troops in kepis retreating through the rugged green hills below. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese woodblock print celebrating a victory, bold colour.
beiyang-fleet: 1888, Liugong Island off Weihai: a modern naval fleet of grey ironclad battleships with twin funnels and cruisers riding at anchor in a sheltered bay, a naval base with brick buildings, wharves and coastal gun batteries on the island hills, sailors in Qing navy uniforms drilling on the pier. Distant panorama. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine maritime detail.
battle-of-yalu-1894: 1894, the Yellow Sea off Dalu Island: a naval battle between Chinese and Japanese steam warships, smoke from funnels and guns rolling over a grey sea, one cruiser listing and sinking, burning ships scattered across the horizon. Low islands lie dim on the horizon, waterspouts rise from shells striking the sea, and signal flags flutter from the masts in the afternoon light. Distant panorama, no individual figures, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving with dramatic smoke and waves.
gongche-shangshu: 1895, Beijing: in the courtyard of a provincial guild hall, hundreds of examination candidates in long gowns, skullcaps and queues gather around a table where a long petition scroll is being signed with brushes, others reading it by the gate; grey tiled roofs and a spring sky. Figures small, no legible writing. Painted as a nineteenth-century Dianshizhai Pictorial lithograph, fine ink line.
battle-of-weihaiwei: 1895, Weihaiwei in deep winter: Japanese troops have taken the snowy shore batteries and fire on Chinese warships trapped in the harbour, while torpedo boats circle the anchorage at night; Liugong Island's naval base under smoke. Ice floes drift in the black water, searchlights sweep across the bay, and snow covers the hills and the brick barracks along the shore. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Meiji-era Japanese nishiki-e woodblock print, snow and dark sea.
triple-intervention: 1895, Lüshun harbour on the Liaodong Peninsula: Japanese troops in dark uniforms march out of the fortified port to waiting transport ships, while Russian, German and French warships lie offshore; hills with forts around the narrow harbour entrance. Japanese flags are lowered over the fort walls, and Chinese fishermen and townspeople watch from small boats and the quays as transports steam out of the harbour. Distant panorama, small figures. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine hatched line.
republic-of-formosa: 1895, Taipei and northern Taiwan: a hastily raised yellow banner with a tiger emblem flies over a Qing-style yamen, while Black Flag militiamen and local volunteers in turbans with old rifles man earthworks among rice fields and bamboo, Japanese troops advancing over the hills. Rain clouds hang over the Tamsui River. Distant view, no gore, no legible text. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving.
jiaozhou-bay: 1897, Jiaozhou Bay at Qingdao: German warships anchored in a broad bay, German marines in spiked helmets landing from boats onto a beach and raising a flag over a small Qing camp while Chinese fishermen with queues watch from their boats; low green hills and a fishing village. Gulls circle over the anchored ships. Distant panorama. Painted as a nineteenth-century German illustrated newspaper engraving.
imperial-university-peking: 1898, Beijing: the gate of a converted princely mansion with red columns and grey-tiled roofs becomes a new university, students in long gowns and queues arriving with book bundles, a few officials in court robes at the gate, a courtyard with old trees. Figures small, no legible signs. Rickshaws and carts wait in the hutong lane. Painted as a nineteenth-century Dianshizhai Pictorial lithograph, fine ink line.
yan-fu-evolution: 1898, Tianjin: a translator's study in a brick house of the treaty-port city, a scholar in a long gown and queue writing at a desk beside an English book, a kerosene lamp and pot of tea; through the window, steamships on the Hai River and Western buildings. Figure seen from behind, no legible text. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese lithograph illustration with soft watercolour.
six-gentlemen-executed: 1898, Caishikou in Beijing: an autumn market crossroads lined with shops, a silent crowd of townspeople with queues gathered at a distance, Qing soldiers with banners and carts forming a cordon; grey sky and bare trees. Viewed from afar, no violence shown, no close-ups. Shutters are closed on the shops, and a few crows sit on the bare branches. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese woodblock print in sombre black and grey.
oracle-bones-identified: 1899, Beijing: a scholar-official's study where a few pieces of yellowed tortoise shell and ox bone lie on a desk beside a magnifying glass and a pharmacy's paper packets, the scholar in a gown and queue bending over them in lamplight, rubbing papers and books stacked nearby. Figure seen from behind, no legible writing. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese lithograph with soft watercolour.
library-cave-dunhuang: 1900, Dunhuang: in the Mogao cave cliffs at the edge of the desert, a Daoist caretaker in a simple robe holds a lamp at a cracked painted wall opening into a small chamber stacked to the ceiling with bundles of manuscript scrolls and silk paintings; Buddhist murals faintly visible around him, sand dunes outside. Figure small, from behind. Painted as a watercolour sketch, warm ochre tones.
southeast-mutual-protection: 1900, Shanghai: a quiet consular meeting room on the Bund with Qing officials in court robes and Western consuls in frock coats around a table, documents and tea set; through tall windows, a calm Huangpu River with steamers and junks, life going on in the streets. Figures small, no legible text. Rickshaws and carriages pass on the Bund. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving.
late-qing-reforms: 1901, Xi'an: in a provincial yamen hall used as a temporary court, officials in Qing robes and queues kneel as an edict is read aloud from a yellow scroll, a yellow-curtained throne at the back; outside, couriers ready horses to carry copies across the country, the city wall and bell tower beyond. Figures small, no legible text. Painted as a Qing court-style painting in ink and colour.
boxer-protocol: 1901, Beijing: one interior scene in a Legation Quarter hall, Qing plenipotentiaries in court robes and hats seated along one side of a long table covered with papers and inkstands, opposite rows of foreign envoys in frock coats and dress uniforms, foreign soldiers of several nations standing at the open doorway through which a sunlit courtyard is glimpsed. Figures small, seen from across the room, no legible text, a single unbroken picture. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine black line hatching.
subao-case: 1903, Shanghai International Settlement: a Mixed Court room with a Chinese magistrate in Qing robes and a British assessor seated at a raised bench, two young defendants in long gowns standing before them, Sikh policemen and lawyers in the room, spectators crowding the benches. Figures small, no legible text. Painted as an early twentieth-century Chinese lithograph illustration in the Dianshizhai style.
british-expedition-tibet: 1904, Gyantse in Tibet: a towering whitewashed fortress on a rocky hill above a monastery town and barley fields, British and Indian troops with mountain guns camped on the plain below, smoke rising from the dzong walls, Tibetan defenders on the ramparts; snowy peaks around. Mules and yaks carry supplies in long lines, and prayer flags flutter on the hillside. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour.
tongmenghui: 1905, Tokyo: a Japanese-style room with tatami mats and sliding paper doors, a large group of young Chinese students and exiles in Western suits and school uniforms, some with queues cut, sitting and standing around a low table, one speaking; lantern light, a garden outside. Figures small, seen from behind. Painted as a Meiji-era Japanese woodblock print illustration, soft colour.
constitutional-preparation: 1906, Beijing: in a palace hall, officials in Qing court robes with peacock-feathered hats stand before a yellow curtain, others in newly tailored Western suits who have returned from abroad hold books and documents; foreign travel trunks by the door. Figures small, no legible text. Bound volumes of foreign constitutions lie on a lacquered table, a European clock ticks on a stand, and courtiers whisper along the red pillars. Painted as an early twentieth-century Chinese lithograph illustration.
qiu-jin-executed: 1907, Shaoxing in Zhejiang: a single quiet view of a canal town at dawn under drizzle, whitewashed houses with black-tiled roofs lining a narrow canal, an arched stone bridge in the middle distance, a moored wooden boat, and the empty Xuanting crossroads beyond with a lone willow; mist over wet flagstones. One unified scene, no figures in close-up, no violence, mournful mood. Painted as a Republican-era watercolour sketch in soft grey ink washes.
cixi-guangxu-die: 1908, the Forbidden City in late autumn: palace courtyards hung with white mourning banners, officials in white mourning garments kneeling in rows, a tiny boy in a yellow robe carried in a sedan chair toward the Hall of Supreme Harmony; golden roofs under a grey sky. Figures small, no faces shown. Painted as a late Qing court-style painting in ink and colour.
beijing-zhangjiakou-railway: 1909, Badaling near Zhangjiakou: a steam locomotive pulling passenger coaches climbs a zigzag switchback track up a steep mountain slope, another engine pushing from behind, the Great Wall winding along the ridgeline above, engineers and workers in Western and Chinese dress watching from a station platform. Figures small. Steam and smoke curl into the clear autumn sky, and stone tunnel portals open into the mountainside. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour.
manchurian-plague: 1910-1911, Harbin in winter: a snowy street with Russian-style brick buildings, medical workers in white gowns and gauze masks escort people to isolation railway carriages, a field hospital tent and steaming sanitation carts, townspeople in fur hats keeping their distance. No bodies shown, figures small. Smoke rises from disinfection fires at the edge of town. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour in cold blue and grey.
huanghuagang-uprising: 1911, Guangzhou: a quiet hillside cemetery at Huanghuagang outside the city, a simple burial mound among trees where mourners in long gowns and Western suits lay wreaths, the walls and roofs of Guangzhou in the distance. Calm and sombre, no violence, figures small. Pine and camellia trees surround the grave, incense smoke drifts, and a stone path leads up the slope. Painted as an early twentieth-century Chinese lithograph illustration with soft watercolour.
railway-protection: 1911, Chengdu: a large crowd of townspeople, gentry in long gowns and students gathered in a street before a Qing yamen, holding incense and paper tablets, soldiers with rifles lining the gate; tiled shops and an autumn sky. Rain clouds gather low over the city walls. Distant view, no gore, no legible text. Painted as an early twentieth-century Chinese lithograph illustration in the Dianshizhai style.
mongolia-independence: 1911, Urga (Ulaanbaatar): a great Buddhist monastery with Tibetan-style temple halls and gilded roof ornaments rising among wooden houses and felt yurts, crowds of Mongol princes and monks in maroon and yellow robes gathered for an enthronement ceremony, horses and banners on the frozen plain. The ruler unseen inside. Painted in the style of a Mongol zurag painting, bright mineral colours.
roc-founded: 1912, Nanjing on New Year's Day: the former viceroy's yamen with its gate decorated with flags of five horizontal stripes, a crowd of revolutionary soldiers, officials in Western suits and citizens with queues cut gathered in the cold courtyard, a small figure on the steps addressing them. Figures small, from behind, no legible text. Painted as a Republican-era woodcut print, bold black and red.
cn-second-revolution: 1913, Nanjing in summer: Beiyang troops in grey uniforms with rifles and field guns advance toward the massive Ming city wall, smoke rising over the gate, southern soldiers on the ramparts, the Yangtze and Purple Mountain beyond. Supply wagons and pack mules follow the troops along a dusty road, telegraph poles line the way, and boats crowd the river crossing at Pukou. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Republican-era woodcut print, strong black line.
cn-national-protection-war: 1915-1916, Kunming and the mountains of Yunnan: soldiers of the National Protection Army in khaki uniforms with rifles march out through a city gate in a long column toward red-earth mountains, townspeople watching, mules carrying supplies. Figures small. The column passes an old city gate tower with sweeping eaves, banners of the army flutter overhead, and terraced fields and eucalyptus trees line the road beneath a bright high-plateau sky. Painted as a Republican-era watercolour sketch, warm earth tones.
cn-new-culture-movement: 1915, Shanghai: a small editorial office above a street of shophouses, young men in long gowns and Western suits around a table with magazine proofs, a printing press in the back room; outside, a tram and rickshaws pass and students read magazines at a newsstand. Figures small, no legible text. Painted as a Republican-era woodcut print in the style of the Lu Xun woodcut movement.
cn-warlord-era: 1916-1920s, north China: on a dusty plain outside a walled city, rival armies in grey and khaki uniforms with field guns, armoured trains and cavalry face each other along a railway line, refugees with carts moving away, the gates of Beijing in the far distance. Telegraph poles lean along the tracks. Distant panorama, no gore. Painted as a Republican-era woodcut print, bold black and white.
cn-manchu-restoration: 1917, Beijing in July: soldiers with long queues and old-style uniforms guard the Forbidden City gates, yellow dragon flags hastily hung over shops, townspeople in long gowns and caps staring from shop doorways, while far off at the city wall Republican troops in grey uniforms with rifles gather to advance and a small biplane circles overhead. Figures small, no close-ups. Pigeons wheel above the golden roofs. Painted as a Republican-era watercolour sketch, hazy summer light.
cn-cai-yuanpei-peking-university: 1917, Beijing: a single autumn view of the red-brick main building of Peking University beside an old courtyard campus, students in long gowns and Western suits walking with books along a path under yellowing trees, a few bicycles leaning against a grey courtyard wall, an elderly scholar in a long gown greeting students at the doorway. Figures small, no legible text, one continuous scene with no panels. Painted as a Republican-era watercolour sketch in soft tones.
shi-dakai-dadu-river: 1863, Anshunchang on the Dadu River in Sichuan: a swollen torrent of brown water roars through a deep gorge beneath towering mountains, a Taiping army with long hair and banners trapped on the southern bank among rocks and makeshift rafts, Qing troops and Yi warriors holding the far bank and the passes above, spring clouds over the peaks. Distant panorama, small figures, no gore. Painted as a nineteenth-century Chinese ink landscape scroll with light colour on paper.
deguang-dies: 947, Shahulin on the North China Plain near Luancheng: a long Khitan column of mounted warriors in fur-trimmed robes and felt caps halts beside a bare grove under a hazy early-summer sky; in the centre a large felt tent is pitched, attendants gather quietly outside, horses stand with heads bowed, ox-carts loaded with plunder wait along a dusty road leading north toward faint hills. No figures in close view. Painted as a Liao-period handscroll in the manner of Hu Gui's Khitan horsemen, ink and light colour on silk, muted ochres.
wuyue-holds-fuzhou: 947, Fuzhou in northern Fujian: Wuyue war junks with matting sails and oars arrive up the Min River estuary, troops in lamellar armour disembarking onto muddy banks; on the hills around the walled city, the siege camps of the Southern Tang army are breaking up, banners falling back along green valley roads; defenders on the rampart wave flags. Small figures, wide view, misty subtropical mountains, morning light. Painted as a Five Dynasties ink-and-light-colour handscroll on silk, Dong Yuan-style soft southern hills.
hezhong-three-revolts: 948, Puzhou on the Yellow River bend in southern Shanxi: a large walled city with rammed-earth ramparts and gate towers is ringed by an army camp of tents, palisades and siege ladders; soldiers in lamellar armour dig earthworks in long lines, mounted officers ride between banners, the broad muddy Yellow River and a floating bridge beyond, dry loess hills under a pale winter sky. All figures small and distant. Painted in Five Dynasties monumental landscape style, ink and light colour on silk.
chu-civil-war: 950, Changsha on the Xiang River: smoke drifts over the tiled roofs and palace halls of the Chu capital while two bodies of troops with differing banners face each other across a riverside street; townspeople flee with baskets on shoulder poles toward boats on the wide river, and the green ridge of Mount Yuelu rises across the water. Figures small, scene seen from a distance, overcast afternoon. Painted as a Five Dynasties handscroll, ink and pale colour on silk, soft southern landscape manner.
liu-chengyou-purge: 950, Bianjing (Kaifeng): a mounted army in lamellar armour with long spears and rows of banners marches along a wide earthen road across the flat Yellow River plain toward the distant walls and gate towers of the capital; supply carts and foot soldiers stretch back to the horizon, dust rising in winter light, bare willows by a canal. No faces in close view. Painted as a Five Dynasties ink-and-colour handscroll on silk, crisp line, restrained palette of ochre, grey and cinnabar.
night-revels-han-xizai: 950, Jinling (Nanjing): an evening banquet inside a Southern Tang official's residence, lit by candles, with tall painted folding screens dividing the room; guests in dark official robes and black gauze caps sit on wooden couches, a woman plays a pipa, another dances, servants carry trays of wine and fruit, low lacquer tables and a large bed with curtains. Elegant, quiet atmosphere, figures seen at middle distance. Painted as a Five Dynasties figure handscroll, fine line, rich mineral colours on silk.
northern-han-founded: 951, Taiyuan in the Fen River valley: a walled city with high gate towers stands among brown loess hills; in a palace courtyard officials in red and green robes with black caps bow in rows before a raised hall, while outside the gate Khitan envoys on horseback in fur hats wait beside camels bearing gifts. Distant mountains, crisp autumn light, figures small. Painted in Five Dynasties ink and light colour on silk, after the northern monumental landscape tradition.
liao-shizong-murdered: 951, Xiangshan near Xuanhua: a Khitan campaign encampment in a mountain valley at night, dozens of round felt tents around a large imperial yurt, campfires and tethered horses; armed riders gather in the dark beside the main tent, torches flaring, the scene tense but seen from a distance with no violence shown. Rugged hills and stars above. Painted as a Liao-dynasty handscroll in the manner of Hu Gui's steppe scenes, ink and light colour on silk, dark blue night tones.
chai-rong-accession: 954, Bianjing (Kaifeng): a grand palace hall with red columns, bracket sets and grey tiled hip roof; in the courtyard, rows of civil and military officials in purple, red and green robes with black winged caps kneel on stone paving, ceremonial guards hold banners and halberds, a small robed figure sits far away on the throne platform at the top of the steps. Morning light, solemn order. Painted in the manner of a Five Dynasties court painting, fine line and mineral colours on silk.
death-of-feng-dao: 954, Bianjing (Kaifeng): a quiet scholar-official's residence with a tiled gate and courtyard, white mourning banners hung by the doorway; officials in plain white hemp mourning robes arrive with offerings, servants burn paper beside a covered wooden coffin hall, an old pine and bare plum branches in the garden, shelves of scrolls inside the study. Grey winter light, subdued mood, small figures. Painted as a Five Dynasties ink handscroll on silk with pale washes of colour.
shizong-buddhism: 955, Kaifeng: in a government foundry yard, workers in short tunics feed bronze Buddhist statues and temple bells into glowing clay furnaces, molten metal poured into coin moulds, piles of new round square-holed coins in baskets; through a gateway, an emptied monastery hall stands with closed doors while a few monks with bundles walk away. Smoke rising, figures small and busy. Painted as a Five Dynasties ink-and-colour handscroll on silk, earthy browns and bronze tones.
kaifeng-expansion: 955, Bianjing (Kaifeng): thousands of labourers with baskets, carrying poles and wooden rammers build a new outer rammed-earth city wall across the flat plain, surveyors stretch cords for wide straight avenues, officials on horseback inspect plans, carts bring earth; inside, crowded tiled roofs of the old city and canal boats on the Bian River. Bright spring day, panoramic view. Painted as a Qingming-scroll-style handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, many tiny figures.
wang-pu-strategy: 955, Bianjing (Kaifeng): inside a palace study hall with lattice windows, a robed official in a black winged cap unrolls a large painted map of rivers and mountains on a low table before a seated ruler seen from behind; scrolls, brush stand and inkstone nearby, a few attendants stand by a screen painted with landscape. Calm daylight, figures small within the architecture. Painted in Five Dynasties court style, ink and mineral colours on silk.
zhou-takes-four-prefectures: 955, Qinzhou (Tianshui) in the Gansu uplands: a Later Zhou army in lamellar armour advances through terraced loess valleys and narrow mountain passes, supply mules and horsemen winding along a cliff road, banners on a ridge; a small walled frontier town opens its gate below with its defenders lowering their flags. Autumn colours, deep valleys, wide panoramic scale. Painted as a Five Dynasties monumental landscape on silk, ink with light ochre and green.
fall-of-shouzhou: 957, Shouzhou on the Huai River: a massive walled city surrounded by siege works, earth mounds, palisades and floating pontoon bridges over a flooded moat; the city gate stands open as a column of defenders files out carrying banners lowered, while besieging troops in lamellar armour wait in ranks. Low winter sky, reeds and wetlands all around, all figures distant. Painted as a Five Dynasties handscroll in ink and light colour on silk.
southern-tang-cedes-jiangbei: 958, Jinling (Nanjing) on the Yangtze: a Southern Tang delegation of officials in robes and black caps boards a decorated river boat at the city's waterfront, carrying lacquer boxes of tribute, rolls of silk and bundled registers; the wide Yangtze stretches north toward a hazy far shore, purple mountain hills behind the city walls. Soft spring light, subdued mood. Painted in Southern Tang style after Dong Yuan, ink and light colour on silk, soft wet riverside landscape.
equal-taxes-map: 958, the Kaifeng countryside: imperial survey officials in robes and black caps with clerks and farmers measure fields using long ropes and wooden poles, a scribe records on a scroll at a portable table, oxen and ploughs paused nearby, a village of thatched and tiled houses with willows behind; flat green fields under a wide sky. Figures small and many. Painted as a Five Dynasties genre handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
shizong-northern-campaign: 959, Wakou Pass near Xiong County: a Later Zhou army with cavalry and infantry in lamellar armour moves north across marshland and canals by boats and causeways, banners streaming; Khitan defenders withdraw from a frontier fort with earth walls, columns of riders retreating toward the horizon. Summer haze, reeds, flat northern plain. Distant figures only. Painted as a Five Dynasties ink-and-colour handscroll on silk, broad panoramic composition.
death-of-chai-rong: 959, Bianjing (Kaifeng): a palace complex draped with white mourning hangings, officials in white hemp robes kneeling in long rows in the courtyard before a great hall, a small child in plain robes led up the steps by attendants seen from behind; guards stand still with lowered banners. Overcast summer evening, sombre stillness. Painted in Five Dynasties court style, fine line and muted mineral colours on silk.
li-yun-rebellion: 960, Zezhou in the Taihang mountains of southeast Shanxi: early Song cavalry and infantry in lamellar armour march up a narrow mountain road through steep gorges, supply carts and banners stretching behind; ahead, a walled town on a hilltop with smoke rising from it. Spring greenery, rocky cliffs, figures small. Painted in early Northern Song monumental landscape style, ink and light colour on silk, after Li Cheng.
li-chongjin-rebellion: 960, Yangzhou by the Grand Canal: Song troops encamp around the walls of the city, siege towers and banners beside canals and willows; a column of smoke rises from inside the city where a residence burns, townspeople watch from boats on the canal. Autumn dusk, distant view, no figures close-up. Painted as an early Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, with soft water and city tones.
cup-of-wine: 961, Kaifeng: an evening banquet in an early Song palace hall, candles glowing, low tables laid with wine cups and dishes; a robed ruler seen from behind raises a cup while several generals in fine robes sit along both sides, attentive and still, servants carrying ewers, painted screens and red pillars framing the scene. Warm lamplight, dignified mood, figures at middle distance. Painted as a Northern Song court painting, fine line and mineral colours on silk.
song-conquers-jingnan-hunan: 963, Jiangling (Jingzhou) on the middle Yangtze: a Song army column marches peacefully through an opened city gate, local officials bowing at the roadside, then continues south along the river toward misty Hunan hills; boats crowd the riverbank, banners fly over the walls. Spring morning, broad river landscape, small figures. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
song-conquers-later-shu: 965, Chengdu basin: a Song army advances along the plank roads clinging to Sichuan cliffs and by boats up the Yangtze gorges, then reaches the walled city of Chengdu among green fields; the city gate opens and a procession of court officials comes out carrying registers in surrender. Misty mountains, sweeping view, tiny figures. Painted in Northern Song monumental landscape style, ink and blue-green colour on silk.
song-conquers-southern-han: 971, near Guangzhou: on a broad plain by the Pearl River, Song crossbowmen and cavalry in lamellar armour face a line of war elephants with howdahs; the elephants turn and flee under volleys of arrows, while the walled city with its pagodas rises beyond and junks crowd the river. Distant view, no blood, tropical banyan trees and hills. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
guangzhou-shibosi: 971, Guangzhou harbour on the Pearl River: tall Arab dhows and Chinese junks moored at wooden piers; Song customs officials in robes and black caps sit under an awning recording cargo on blank scrolls while porters carry bales of spices, ivory and incense; foreign merchants in turbans and long robes stand by. Bright subtropical sunlight, busy port. Painted as a Northern Song genre handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
palace-examination: 973, Kaifeng palace: in a vast pillared hall, rows of candidates in plain robes and caps sit at small individual desks writing with brushes on blank paper; officials patrol the aisles, a distant robed figure presides from a raised dais under a canopy, guards at the doors. Quiet concentration, morning light through lattice windows, figures small. Painted as a Northern Song court painting, ink and mineral colours on silk.
southern-tang-conquered: 975, the Yangtze at Caishi below Jinling: a long pontoon bridge of boats lashed together spans the wide river, Song troops and horses streaming across; on the far shore, the walls of Jinling lie under siege with drifting smoke and banners, Purple Mountain behind. Grey winter light, sweeping river panorama, tiny figures. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll in ink and light colour on silk.
taizu-death-candle-axe: 976, Kaifeng palace at night in winter: snow on the tiled roofs and courtyard; through a lattice window of a palace chamber, a candle throws two indistinct shadows on a paper screen, while outside guards stand at a distance in the snowfall and a lone eunuch waits by the steps. Mysterious, quiet atmosphere, no violence. Painted as a Northern Song ink painting on silk with snow-scene washes, in the manner of Fan Kuan's snow landscapes.
