yuelu-academy: 976, Changsha: at the foot of forested Mount Yuelu, a newly built academy compound of halls, lecture rooms and libraries with grey tiles and whitewashed walls; scholars in plain robes walk through a gate carrying scrolls, students read under maples in a courtyard, the Xiang River and the city across the water. Autumn colours, peaceful morning. Painted as a Northern Song landscape handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
wuyue-submits: 978, Hangzhou by West Lake: a ceremonial procession of Wuyue officials with carts of registers and tribute, led by a king in robes seen from behind, leaves the city gates toward waiting boats on the canal northward; townspeople line the willow-lined lakeshore peacefully, pagodas on the hills. Calm spring day, misty lake. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and soft colour on silk.
song-conquers-northern-han: 979, Taiyuan: a large Song army encircles the walled city in the Fen River valley, rows of tents, siege engines and earth ramps; the city gate opens as a small procession of officials comes out in surrender, while on a far ridge Liao horsemen ride away. Spring dust, loess hills, figures tiny. Painted in early Northern Song monumental landscape style, ink and light ochre on silk.
xiao-chuo-regency: 982, the Liao Supreme Capital on the steppe of Bairin: a walled city with Buddhist pagodas amid grasslands; inside a large felt-hung hall, Khitan nobles in fur-trimmed robes and Chinese-style officials in robes gather on two sides before a curtained throne where a woman regent sits far away beside a small boy, attendants with fans. Seen at middle distance, no faces. Painted as a Liao-period court painting, ink and colour on silk.
li-jiqian-revolt: 982, Dijin Marsh in the Ordos: a small band of Tangut horsemen in felt cloaks and with braided hair rides out across a windswept steppe of reeds, sand and salt lakes, followed by families with camels, sheep and tents; low sun, vast empty landscape, figures small and distant. Painted as a Liao-Song frontier handscroll in the manner of Hu Gui, ink and light colour on silk, dusty tones.
taiping-yulan: 983, Kaifeng: inside the imperial library hall, scholar-officials in robes and black caps sit at long tables copying and collating texts, tall shelves stacked with scroll cases, assistants carrying bundles of bound volumes, ink stones and brushes everywhere; sunlight through lattice windows. No legible text. Painted as a Northern Song court genre painting, fine line and soft mineral colours on silk.
yongxi-expedition-qigou: 986, Qigou Pass near Zhuozhou: on the dry plain south of Youzhou, a broken Song army retreats in disorder across a river, carts abandoned, banners down, while Khitan cavalry in fur hats sweep in from low hills; dust clouds and summer heat haze. Distant, panoramic view, no gore. Painted as a Liao-Song period handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, after the steppe horsemen manner of Hu Gui.
yang-ye-death: 986, Chenjiagu valley near Shuozhou: a narrow mountain valley in northern Shanxi where a small band of Song soldiers in armour holds a ridge with banners, surrounded far below by Khitan cavalry; the empty valley road where help never arrived stretches away. Dusk, long shadows, steep loess cliffs, all figures tiny. Painted as an early Northern Song monumental landscape, ink and light colour on silk.
wang-xiaobo-li-shun: 993, Qingcheng in western Sichuan: on terraced tea hills below forested Mount Qingcheng, crowds of tea farmers in short jackets and straw hats gather with hoes, baskets and bamboo poles, a homemade banner raised, mist in the valleys and Daoist temples above. Morning light, crowd at a distance. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll in ink and blue-green colour on silk, after Sichuan landscape tradition.
fan-kuan-travelers: 1000, Mount Hua area: a towering central granite peak rises above dense forest, a thin waterfall falling down its cliff; below, along a path by a stream, a small mule caravan with two travellers passes boulders, a temple roof hidden among the trees. Majestic, vertical composition, mist at the base of the peak. Painted in Northern Song monumental landscape style, dense raindrop texture strokes, ink and pale colour on silk.
lingzhou-falls: 1002, Lingzhou on the Yellow River in Ningxia: Tangut cavalry in felt cloaks ride through the open gate of an earth-walled frontier city, Song banners lowered, camels and supply carts following; irrigated fields and the broad Yellow River beside the city, the Helan mountains on the horizon. Dry, bright light, panoramic distance. Painted as a Song frontier handscroll, ink and ochre colour on silk.
xiao-talin-killed: 1004, Chanzhou on the Yellow River: Song soldiers man large frame-mounted crossbows behind the earthen walls of a riverside city; across the snowy plain, Khitan cavalry in fur hats pause and gather around a fallen banner as a bolt flies out from the walls. Winter, frozen river, distant view, no gore. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
jingdezhen-named: 1004, Jingdezhen in Jiangxi: a pottery town in green hills along the Chang River, smoke rising from long dragon kilns climbing the slopes; potters throw bowls on wheels, workers carry racks of pale bluish-white qingbai wares, boats loaded with crates on the river. Misty morning, busy small figures. Painted as a Northern Song genre handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
tianshu-fengshan: 1008, Mount Tai: a vast imperial procession climbs the stone stairway up the mountain, banners, parasols and palanquins winding through pines and cliffs, officials in ceremonial robes and black caps in long lines; at the summit, an altar with smoke rising from offerings. Clear autumn morning, grand scale, tiny figures. Painted as a Northern Song monumental landscape on silk, ink and blue-green colour.
champa-rice: 1012, the lower Yangtze countryside: farmers in straw hats transplant young rice seedlings in flooded paddies under a dry, pale sky, while an official with clerks distributes sacks of seed grain from carts at a village granary; water wheels and dikes, willows and thatched houses. Calm, busy rural scene, figures small. Painted as a Northern Song genre handscroll in the style of the Tilling and Weaving pictures, ink and light colour on silk.
jiaozi: 1024, Chengdu: inside a government office, clerks print sheets of paper money from carved wooden blocks with red and black ink, stacks of blank-patterned notes drying on racks, an official inspecting; merchants with bundles wait at the counter, strings of iron coins piled in the corner. No legible characters. Painted as a Northern Song genre painting, fine line and light colour on silk.
fan-gong-dike: 1024, the Jiangsu coast near Dongtai: thousands of labourers with baskets and carrying poles build a long earthen seawall across flat tidal marshland, officials on horseback supervising; on one side the grey sea and mudflats, on the other side salt pans, salt boiling sheds and green farmland. Windy overcast day, vast horizontal scale. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
bronze-acupuncture-figures: 1027, Kaifeng: in a court medical academy hall, two tall bronze teaching statues in the shape of a standing robed man, wearing a bronze cap and a short bronze wrap, their arms and chest dotted with tiny points; a physician in robes and cap teaches students holding fine needles, a book of diagrams on a table. Lattice window light, calm teaching scene, small figures. Painted as a Northern Song court genre painting, fine line and mineral colours on silk.
li-yuanhao-succeeds: 1032, Xingzhou (Yinchuan) below the Helan mountains: Tangut warriors and nobles in narrow-sleeved robes, felt hats and tonsured heads with fringe hair gather in a palace courtyard of rammed-earth buildings; banners fly, horses and camels tethered nearby, irrigated green fields beyond the walls. Figures seen at a distance. Painted in the style of a Western Xia Buddhist wall painting, earthy reds and greens on plaster.
tangut-script: 1036, Xingqing (Yinchuan): in a scriptorium hall, Tangut scholars in robes sit at low desks writing dense, complex unreadable characters on paper with brushes, wooden printing blocks and Buddhist sutra scrolls piled nearby, a monk translating from a book. Warm interior light, focused atmosphere, no legible writing. Painted in the style of a Western Xia mural from the Mogao and Yulin caves, mineral colours on plaster.
battle-of-sanchuankou: 1040, Sanchuankou near Yan'an: a deep loess valley where three rivers meet in winter; Tangut cavalry pour down from the snowy ridges onto a Song relief column strung out along the riverbank, banners falling, the Song troops encircled. Wind-blown snow and dust, distant panoramic view, no gore. Painted as a Northern Song monumental landscape handscroll on silk, ink and pale colour, after Fan Kuan.
fan-zhongyan-shaanxi: 1040, Yanzhou (Yan'an) on the northwest frontier: across bare loess ridges, Song soldiers and local militia build rammed-earth forts and watchtowers, while others drill with crossbows and spears on a flat terrace below; a scholar-general in robes and cap, seen from behind among a few officers, surveys the deep gullies from a hilltop. Autumn wind, vast yellow hills, small figures. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and ochre colour on silk.
haoshuichuan: 1041, Haoshuichuan in the Liupan mountains: a narrow valley where a Song army marches into an ambush; flights of pigeons burst from boxes set on the road as Tangut cavalry charge down from both slopes. Distant view, dust and banners, no gore, steep green-brown hills. Painted as a Northern Song landscape handscroll on silk, ink and light colour, small figures.
battle-of-dingchuan: 1042, Dingchuan Fort near Guyuan: a small square earth-walled Song fort stands on a dry plateau, encircled by vast rings of Tangut cavalry in felt cloaks with banners; the water channel leading into the fort has been cut, smoke rises from inside the walls, and the defenders' flags droop. Autumn grassland, distant Liupan mountains, all figures tiny, no gore. Painted in Western Xia cave-mural style, earthy ochre, red and green mineral colours on plaster.
liao-extra-tribute: 1042, Kaifeng: in a palace reception hall, Song officials in robes and black caps face Khitan envoys in fur-trimmed robes and felt hats across a long table; outside in the courtyard, rolls of silk and chests of silver are stacked for delivery. Formal, tense atmosphere, figures at middle distance. Painted as a Northern Song court painting, fine line and mineral colours on silk.
qingli-reforms: 1043, Kaifeng: in a government office hall, scholar-officials in robes and black winged caps confer around tables stacked with personnel registers and memorials, a senior minister seen from behind, clerks bringing documents; through the doorway, a courtyard with officials waiting. Daylight, quiet seriousness. Painted as a Northern Song court genre painting, ink and light colour on silk, no legible writing.
wujing-zongyao: 1044, Kaifeng: in a workshop of the military arsenal, artisans in short tunics grind charcoal, sulphur and saltpetre in mortars, pack fire-arrows and gunpowder pots into baskets; a scholar-official at a table compiles an illustrated book of weapons and a small iron fish-shaped compass floats in a bowl of water. Warm light, small figures. Painted as a Northern Song genre handscroll, fine line, ink and light colour on silk.
qingli-peace: 1044, Xingqing (Yinchuan): a Song envoy delegation in robes and black caps arrives with ox-carts carrying bolts of silk, chests of silver and bricks of tea at the gate of a Tangut palace below the Helan mountains; Tangut nobles in felt hats and fur robes receive them. Clear autumn light, distant view. Painted in Western Xia mural style, ochre, red and green mineral colours.
yueyang-tower-record: 1046, Yueyang Tower on Dongting Lake: a newly restored three-storey timber tower with sweeping upturned eaves rises above the city walls of Yuezhou, overlooking a vast lake dotted with sailing boats, reed islands and the distant isle of Junshan in mist; a few scholars in robes stand on the balcony gazing across the water, fishermen haul nets below. Clear spring evening, golden light. Painted as a Northern Song landscape handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
old-drunkard-pavilion: 1046, the hills southwest of Chuzhou: a small open pavilion with a tiled roof stands in a wooded mountain valley beside a clear spring; a gathering of scholars in robes sits with wine cups and a jar, villagers carrying loads and children walk along the path, servants warm wine over a brazier. Pines, maples, a tumbling stream and grey rocks, late afternoon light, relaxed mood, small figures. Painted in Northern Song landscape style, ink and light colour on silk.
yuanhao-assassinated: 1048, Xingqing (Yinchuan) under the Helan mountains: night over a Western Xia palace compound of rammed-earth walls and tiled halls; torches flare in a courtyard as Tangut guards in felt hats run toward a hall entrance, attendants scatter along a corridor, everything seen from far above with no violence shown. Dark mountains and stars behind, banners stirring in the wind. Painted in the style of a Western Xia cave wall painting, earthy reds and greens on plaster, dark tones.
shanghu-yellow-river: 1048, Shanghu near Puyang on the North China Plain: the swollen brown Yellow River pours through a wide breach in a broken earthen dike, spreading floodwater across fields and villages; thatched roofs and treetops stand out of the water, peasants in short jackets escape on rafts and small boats with bundles and oxen, officials on the remaining dike top look on. Grey rain clouds, vast flat horizon, figures small. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and pale wash on silk.
nong-zhigao-rebellion: 1052, Yongzhou (Nanning) on the Yong River in Guangxi: Zhuang warriors in dark indigo jackets and turbans, carrying shields, crossbows and spears, march through green karst hills toward a walled river city flying unfamiliar banners; boats on the river, rice terraces and banana trees, mist around the limestone peaks. All figures small, distant view, no gore. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll in ink and blue-green colour on silk.
kunlun-pass: 1053, Kunlun Pass near Binyang in Guangxi: at night, a long column of Song cavalry and infantry in lamellar armour, banners furled, threads silently over a narrow mountain pass between steep karst peaks under rain and a dim moon; far behind, the lanterns of a festival camp still glow in the valley. Dark blue tones, tiny figures, no fighting shown. Painted as a Northern Song night landscape, ink and pale colour on silk.
sn-1054: 1054, Kaifeng: before dawn, on a raised stone observation terrace of the imperial astronomical bureau, a few astronomers in robes and black caps stand by a bronze armillary sphere and gnomon, gazing up at an unusually brilliant new star shining near the horns of Taurus in a pale sky; the tiled roofs of the capital below. Quiet, wondering mood, small figures. Painted as a Northern Song ink and light colour painting on silk.
yingxian-pagoda: 1056, Yingxian in northern Shanxi: a towering octagonal wooden pagoda of five visible storeys with deep bracketed eaves is under construction in a temple compound; carpenters on timber scaffolding hoist beams with ropes and pulleys, others cut wood in the courtyard, Khitan and Han workmen and monks below. Flat plain and distant mountains, clear autumn light. Painted as a Liao-period Buddhist temple painting, ink and mineral colours on silk.
su-brothers-jinshi: 1057, Kaifeng: in a palace courtyard after the examination results, a group of young successful candidates in new green robes and black caps with flowers pinned to them ride out on horses through a gate, crowds of townspeople watching along the street, a senior examiner in purple robes seen from behind at the hall steps. Spring blossoms, festive daylight, small figures. Painted as a Northern Song court genre painting, ink and colour on silk.
wang-anshi-memorial: 1058, Kaifeng: in a modest official's study, a scholar in a plain robe and black cap, seen from behind, writes a long memorial by lamplight at a desk heaped with paper rolls, brushes and an inkstone; through the open window, the dark roofs of the capital and a single bare tree. Quiet night, warm lamplight, no legible text. Painted as a Northern Song figure painting, fine line, ink and light colour on silk.
new-book-of-tang: 1060, Kaifeng: in a historiography office of the Song court, scholar-officials in robes and caps sit at long tables collating old Tang records, piles of scrolls and bound volumes, clerks carrying bundles, a senior scholar seen from behind reviewing a finished set of volumes in cloth wrappers. Soft daylight through lattice windows, focused calm. Painted as a Northern Song genre painting, ink and light colour on silk, no legible writing.
bao-zheng-death: 1062, Kaifeng: outside the Kaifeng prefectural yamen, with its tiled gate, drum and stone lions, crowds of townspeople in plain clothes gather in mourning, white cloth hung from the gate, officials in white robes carrying offerings inside; the busy city street beyond falls quiet. Overcast day, figures small, respectful mood. Painted as a Northern Song genre handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
baojia-system: 1070, a village on the Kaifeng plain in winter: peasants in padded jackets drill with spears and bows in a threshing yard under the eye of a local headman, while others register households before a clerk at a table outside a temple gate; thatched houses, bare willows, stacks of straw, oxen tethered. Pale winter light, many small figures. Painted as a Northern Song genre handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
zhou-dunyi-taiji: 1070, Lianxi below Mount Lu near Jiujiang: a scholar's simple thatched study beside a stream lined with lotus pond, an elderly scholar in plain robe seen from behind contemplates a scroll with a circular cosmological diagram of black and white rings; students sit on the veranda, misty peaks of Mount Lu behind. Summer, quiet. Painted as a Northern Song landscape, ink and light colour on silk, no legible text.
state-trade-law: 1072, Kaifeng: in the courtyard of a government trade bureau, clerks weigh bales of goods on large steelyard scales, merchants in robes bargain with officials at counters, carts loaded with grain, salt and cloth come and go; nearby, surveyors measure a field outside the city wall with ropes. Busy daylight scene, many small figures. Painted as a Qingming-scroll-style handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
xihe-campaign: 1072, the Tao River valley near Lintao: a Song army column in lamellar armour advances along the river through high grassland valleys, Tibetan herders with yaks and black tents withdrawing toward the mountains, a new rammed-earth fort being built on a terrace; snow peaks behind. Wide, clear sky, figures small. Painted as a Northern Song landscape handscroll, ink and blue-green colour on silk.
guo-xi-early-spring: 1072, Kaifeng palace: in an imperial painting studio, a court painter in robe and cap, seen from behind, works on a tall silk hanging scroll of a misty early-spring mountain landscape with twisting crab-claw trees, assistants grinding ink and holding brushes, other finished scrolls hanging on the wall. Soft spring light. Rendered in Northern Song court painting style, ink and light colour on silk.
ly-song-war: 1075-1077, the Như Nguyệt River in northern Đại Việt: Song troops in lamellar armour with banners camp on the north bank among rice fields and bamboo, while on the south bank Đại Việt soldiers in short tunics hold a long bamboo stockade fortified line; small war boats on the river, low green hills, morning mist. Distant figures, no gore. Painted as a Song-period handscroll in ink and light colour on silk.
lingshan-border-talks: 1075, the mountains near Daizhou in northern Shanxi: Song and Khitan envoys in their distinct robes and fur hats meet in a felt tent on a high ridge, maps and archive scrolls spread on a table, horses tethered outside; a watershed ridgeline with border markers runs into the distance. Windy autumn, figures small. Painted as a Northern Song landscape handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
zhang-zai-guanxue: 1077, Hengqu village near Meixian under the Qinling mountains: a modest rural academy of tiled halls among fields, students in plain robes bowing at a mourning hall hung with white cloth, a scholar's books and desk visible inside; misty Qinling peaks behind, winter wheat fields. Sombre, quiet scene, small figures. Painted as a Northern Song landscape, ink and pale colour on silk.
crow-terrace-case: 1079, Kaifeng: outside the Censorate offices, nicknamed the Crow Terrace for the many crows roosting in its old cypress trees, armed guards escort a robed scholar-official, seen from behind, through a heavy red-lacquered gate; officials in black caps watch from a covered corridor, and a clerk follows carrying bundles of confiscated poem manuscripts. Autumn dusk, dark birds circling the trees, tense quiet. Painted as a Northern Song figure painting, ink and light colour on silk.
cheng-brothers-luoxue: 1080, Luoyang: in a courtyard lecture hall surrounded by peonies and old pines, two scholar-teachers in plain robes and caps, seen at a distance, sit on mats while many students in robes listen in rows, books and brushes before them; the tiled roofs of Luoyang and the Mang hills behind. Spring light, calm learning. Painted as a Northern Song genre painting, ink and light colour on silk.
yuanfeng-reform: 1080, Kaifeng: in the palace complex, a long row of government office halls with tiled roofs, red pillars and gates, officials in robes of purple, red and green bustling between buildings carrying documents, a hall being re-signed with blank plaques; ministers confer in a courtyard. Clear day, orderly scene, small figures. Painted as a Northern Song architectural painting, fine ruled line, ink and colour on silk.
five-route-xia-campaign: 1081, Lingzhou on the Yellow River in Ningxia: in winter, Song siege camps surround an earth-walled city on the plain, while torrents of water released from breached Yellow River dikes flood the Song encampments; soldiers struggle through icy water, supply carts stranded, Helan mountains in the distance. Grey sky, panoramic view, no gore. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and pale colour on silk.
red-cliff-odes: 1082, the Red Cliff near Huangzhou: on a calm moonlit autumn night, a small boat drifts on the broad Yangtze beneath towering reddish cliffs, a few robed scholars sitting in it with wine cups, one playing a bamboo flute; reeds along the shore, the full moon over the river, wide misty water. Painted as a Southern Song-style ink landscape on silk, Ma Yuan-like composition, sparse and poetic.
battle-of-yongle: 1082, Yongle fortress near Mizhi on the loess plateau: a newly built rammed-earth fort on a bare hilltop is encircled by a sea of Tangut cavalry in felt cloaks; the stream below has been seized, the defenders on the walls look thirsty and few, smoke rising, autumn rains approaching. Panoramic distant view, deep gullies, no gore. Painted as a Northern Song landscape handscroll, ink and ochre on silk.
yuanyou-restoration: 1086, Kaifeng palace: in a great hall, a curtained screen behind which a regent empress sits, with a small boy emperor on the throne in front, seen from afar; an elderly minister in purple robes with officials in rows bow at the steps, scrolls of edicts being carried out. Formal morning, red pillars and gold. Painted as a Northern Song court painting, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
wang-anshi-death: 1086, Jiangning (Nanjing): a simple retirement residence at the foot of Zhongshan, a quiet house with a tiled gate among pines, white mourning banners hanging at the entrance; a few scholars and servants in plain robes arrive with offerings, an old donkey that once carried its owner along the hill path stands tethered by the wall. Early summer, grey sky, bamboo and pond, sombre mood. Painted as a Northern Song landscape, ink and light colour on silk.
quanzhou-shibosi: 1087, Quanzhou harbour in Fujian: large ocean-going Chinese junks with multiple matting sails and Arab dhows anchor in a broad estuary; customs officials in robes inspect cargo at wooden wharves, merchants in turbans and Southeast Asian sailors with sarongs unload spices, incense and ivory; a stone pagoda and a mosque minaret rise in the town behind. Bright day. Painted as a Song-period genre handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
dream-pool-essays: 1088, Runzhou (Zhenjiang): in a garden retreat called the Dream Brook, an elderly scholar in plain robe, seen from behind, writes at a desk surrounded by curiosities: a magnetic needle on a thread, fossil shells, clay movable type pieces, star charts; a stream flows past bamboo and rocks outside. Peaceful afternoon, no legible text. Painted as a Northern Song genre painting, ink and light colour on silk.
su-song-clock: 1088, Kaifeng: a tall three-storey wooden astronomical clock tower about 12 metres high with a bronze armillary sphere on its roof platform; through open panels, a large water-driven wheel, gearing and small time-jack figures are visible; officials and craftsmen in robes stand around it in a palace courtyard. Clear daylight. Painted as a Northern Song technical illustration in ink and light colour on silk.
shaoshu-restoration: 1094, the southern road out of Kaifeng: several exiled officials in plain robes with small bundles ride donkeys and walk under escort along a long road toward distant southern mountains, family members following with carts, willows by the road; behind them the walls of the capital. Autumn, melancholy mood, figures small. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
qingtang-campaign: 1099, Qingtang (Xining) in the Huangshui valley: Song soldiers in lamellar armour enter a walled Tibetan city with flat-roofed houses and a Buddhist temple, Tibetan nobles in fur-trimmed robes and monks in red standing at the gate; high grassland plateau and snow mountains around. Clear blue sky, distant view. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and mineral colours on silk.
su-shi-death: 1101, Changzhou on the Grand Canal: a canal boat moored at a quiet waterside town of white walls and grey tiles; mourners in white gather on the bank around a small house, scrolls of calligraphy and a bamboo hat left on a table inside; willows and a stone bridge. Summer evening, sad and calm. Painted as a Southern Song-style ink landscape on silk, light colour.
yuanyou-stele: 1102, Kaifeng: before a palace gate, stone masons carve a tall stone stele on a tortoise base with dense unreadable lines of names, officials in robes watching, others walking away in silence; a large inscribed stele already standing beside the gate. Grey day, ominous mood, no legible text. Painted as a Northern Song court genre painting, ink and light colour on silk.
yingzao-fashi: 1103, Kaifeng: in a timber yard, carpenters measure and cut standardized beams and bracket sets according to a large printed architectural manual held open by a robed official; a half-built palace hall frame with complex dougong brackets rises behind, workers hoisting beams. Bright day, many small figures. Painted as a Northern Song architectural ruled-line painting, ink and light colour on silk, no legible text.
painting-academy: 1104, Kaifeng palace: in a pavilion beside a garden of rocks and flowering trees, young academy painters in robes and caps sit at desks painting birds, flowers and landscapes on silk, a robed examiner walks among them, a peacock and cranes in the garden as models. Spring light, refined atmosphere. Painted in the Huizong academy style, fine detailed line and delicate colour on silk.
flower-rock-network: 1105, Suzhou on the Grand Canal: labourers with ropes and wooden rollers haul a huge, hollowed, eroded Taihu limestone rock onto a large barge, while officials supervise and townspeople watch resentfully; canal convoys loaded with rocks and potted trees wait in line, white-walled houses and arched bridges along the water. Overcast day, many small figures. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
qingming-scroll: 1110, Kaifeng: a bustling scene along the Bian River on the Qingming festival day, a great arched timber Rainbow Bridge crowded with pedestrians and stalls, cargo boats with masts lowered passing beneath, shops, inns, carts and donkeys along the banks, hundreds of tiny figures in daily clothing. Spring sunlight, lively mood. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, fine line, ink and light colour on silk.
battle-of-ningjiang: 1114, Ningjiang near Songyuan in Manchuria: on a snowy plain beside a frozen river, a small band of Jurchen horsemen in fur coats and caps, with braided hair, charges toward an earth-walled Liao fort with banners; the Liao garrison scatters. Winter, cold blue sky, distant view, no gore. Painted in the style of a Jin-dynasty hunting handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
battle-of-hubudagang: 1115, Hubudagang in Manchuria: a vast Liao army with countless banners and tents fills a snowy plain, while a much smaller force of Jurchen cavalry in fur coats sweeps down from a ridge, the Liao lines breaking and fleeing; winter sun, frozen marshes and forests. Panoramic, small figures, no gore. Painted as a Jin-period steppe handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
zhu-yu-compass: 1119, the sea off Guangzhou: a large Song ocean-going junk with tall matting sails under heavy grey clouds; on deck, sailors in short jackets gather around a bowl of water in which a magnetized needle floats, a navigator watching it while the helmsman steers; rough waves, distant islands hidden in mist. Painted as a Song-period handscroll, ink and pale wash on silk.
fang-la: 1120, the hills of Qingxi in western Zhejiang: a crowd of peasants and lacquer-tree workers in short jackets and straw hats gathers with hoes, bamboo spears and red headbands in a misty mountain valley, a homemade banner raised; terraced fields and lacquer trees around. Morning light, crowd at a distance. Painted as a Northern Song landscape handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
alliance-at-sea: 1120, Dengzhou (Penglai) on the Shandong coast: a Song envoy ship with matting sails leaves the harbour below a cliffside pavilion, heading across the grey Bohai Sea; on deck officials in robes and caps with boxes of gifts stand at the rail, sailors raising the sails. Windy morning, wide seascape. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
jin-takes-supreme-capital: 1120, the Liao Supreme Capital on the steppe: Jurchen cavalry in fur coats and helmets pour through the gates of a walled city with pagodas and halls, Liao defenders withdrawing, smoke rising above the walls; open grassland under a big summer sky, herds of horses beyond. Distant panoramic view, no gore. Painted as a Jin-period handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
song-jiang-surrenders: 1121, Haizhou (Lianyungang) on the Shandong-Jiangsu coast: Song government troops in armour surround a small band of outlaws on a beach, their seized boats burning in the harbour; the outlaws lay down weapons and bow; a walled coastal town and hills behind. Grey sea, distant view, no gore. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
song-fails-at-yanjing: 1122, before Yanjing (Beijing): a Song army in lamellar armour retreats southward in disorder across the dry northern plain, abandoning supply carts, tents and fallen banners along the road, while Khitan horsemen in fur hats pursue from the direction of the great city walls; the Western Hills rise on the horizon. Autumn dust clouds, low sun, distant panoramic view, all figures tiny, no gore. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
song-buys-yanjing: 1123, Yanjing (Beijing): long lines of Jurchen carts and captives on foot leave the city walls northward, carrying away goods and people, while a Song delegation in robes rides in through an empty gate into silent deserted streets; the Western Hills behind. Early summer, desolate mood, small figures. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and pale colour on silk.
yelu-dashi-goes-west: 1124, Kedun on the Mongolian steppe: a column of Khitan horsemen in fur robes with families, ox-carts and herds of horses rides westward across a vast grassland, a small walled garrison town behind; distant mountains and an enormous sky. Late summer, golden grass, tiny figures. Painted as a Liao-period steppe handscroll in the manner of Hu Gui, ink and light colour on silk.
xia-submits-to-jin: 1124, Xingqing (Yinchuan): inside a large felt tent, Tangut envoys in felt hats and long robes present gifts of horses, camels and bolts of cloth before a Jurchen general and officials in fur-trimmed robes who sit at the far end; outside, banners of both sides, the Helan mountains behind and irrigated fields of the Ningxia plain around. Distant view, formal mood. Painted in Western Xia cave-mural style, ochre, red and green mineral colours on plaster.
huizong-abdicates: 1125, Kaifeng: in winter, a palace hall where officials in robes kneel before a young man in imperial robes being seated on the throne, while at a side gate an older figure in robes, seen from behind, leaves with attendants toward boats and carts loaded with belongings; snow on the roofs. Hurried, tense mood. Painted as a Northern Song court painting, fine line and mineral colours on silk.
liao-falls: 1125, the snowy hills near Ying County in northern Shanxi: a small party of Khitan horsemen in fur robes is surrounded by Jurchen cavalry in a winter valley, banners lowered; the tall wooden Yingxian pagoda visible far away on the plain. Grey sky, cold, figures tiny, no gore. Painted as a Jin-period handscroll in ink and light colour on silk.
first-siege-kaifeng: 1126, Kaifeng: Song defenders in armour line the great brick-faced walls and gate towers with crossbows and catapults, while Jurchen cavalry and siege towers encamp on the frozen plain outside; carts of silver and silk wait at a gate for ransom. Winter, smoke on the horizon, distant view, no gore. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and pale colour on silk.
chen-dong-petition: 1126, Kaifeng in winter: tens of thousands of townspeople and Imperial University students in scholar robes and caps crowd the broad square before a palace gate, many kneeling and holding up petition scrolls, a great drum standing beside the gate; guards stand motionless on the gate tower above, snow on the roofs. The crowd is seen from a high distance, no faces close. Painted as a Northern Song genre handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
gaozong-enthroned: 1127, Yingtianfu (Shangqiu): a hurried enthronement on a simple raised earthen altar outside a walled city, a robed prince seen from behind ascending the steps while civil officials in robes and generals in lamellar armour bow below; banners flutter, a small army camp of tents and horses spreads around, smoke from cooking fires. Early summer, sense of urgency and improvisation. Painted in early Southern Song court style, ink and light colour on silk.
zong-ze-death: 1128, Kaifeng: on the city wall overlooking the Yellow River in the north, an old general in armour, seen from behind, lies ill on a couch by a window while officers gather around him; beyond the battlements, the broad river under storm clouds and distant enemy camps. Summer evening, sad mood. Painted as a Southern Song figure painting, ink and light colour on silk.
miao-liu-mutiny: 1129, Hangzhou: armed troops in lamellar armour surround a palace hall, an infant in imperial robes carried by attendants toward the throne, officials kneeling uncertainly in the stone courtyard; far outside the city, a relieving army with banners marches along the lakeside road. Spring, West Lake and hilltop pagodas in the background, tense mood, small figures. Painted as a Southern Song court painting, ink and light colour on silk.
gaozong-flees-to-sea: 1130, the Zhejiang coast near Mingzhou (Ningbo): a fleet of Song junks with matting sails and painted sterns flees across a winter sea toward rocky islands, while on the shore behind, Jurchen cavalry in fur coats arrive at the empty beach and halt at the waterline. Grey sky, crashing waves, distant figures, no gore. Painted as a Southern Song landscape with Ma Yuan-style rhythmic water lines, ink and pale colour on silk.
zhong-xiang-yang-yao: 1130, Dongting Lake near Changde: large multi-deck paddle-wheel warships driven by treadmills churn across the vast lake, homemade rebel banners flying from their masts, among reed islands and stilt-house fishing villages; peasants in straw hats and short jackets row small boats out to join them. Misty spring morning, wide lake view, small figures. Painted as a Southern Song landscape in the manner of Xia Gui, ink and light colour on silk.
huangtiandang: 1130, Huangtiandang on the Yangtze near Nanjing: large Song warships with tall sterns and iron-hooked grappling chains block a stretch of the river, while a Jin fleet of smaller boats is trapped in a dead-end marsh channel among tall reeds; war drums on the decks, banners flying. Spring river, distant view, no gore. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
liu-yu-qi: 1130, Daming in Hebei: a hurried ceremony in a walled city where Jurchen envoys in fur robes present a set of imperial robes and a seal box to a Han official in robes, seen from behind, before rows of officials; Jurchen guards stand by. Formal, cold mood, figures small. Painted as a Jin-period court painting, ink and light colour on silk.
battle-of-fuping: 1130, Fuping on the Shaanxi plain: a huge Song army arrayed in long ranks behind marshland, banners in rows and camps behind; Jurchen cavalry in fur coats cross the marsh on bundles of brushwood and charge, and the Song lines begin to break and flee toward the loess hills. Autumn, dust, panoramic distant view, all figures tiny, no gore. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
qin-hui-returns: 1130, Yuezhou (Shaoxing): a small boat arrives at a stone canal landing, an official in robes and his wife, seen from behind, step ashore carrying few belongings, while court officials in black caps wait on the steps to receive them; white-walled houses, arched stone bridges, willows and black-awning boats. Winter mist, quiet canal town. Painted as a Southern Song genre painting, ink and light colour on silk.
battle-of-heshangyuan: 1131, Heshangyuan near Baoji in the Qinling mountains: Song soldiers on high ridges behind wooden palisades shoot massed crossbows down at Jin cavalry pressing up a narrow valley; the Jin columns turn back in confusion, banners falling. Autumn, steep forested mountains and drifting mist, distant view, all figures tiny, no gore. Painted as a Southern Song landscape, ink and light colour on silk.
yue-fei-xiangyang: 1134, Xiangyang on the Han River: a Song army with banners, cavalry and infantry crosses the Han River on boats and a pontoon bridge toward a large walled city, while the Qi defenders flee out of the far gate along a road into the hills; green spring hills, clear sky, river boats. Distant view, no gore. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
battle-of-xianren-pass: 1134, Xianren Pass in the Qinling mountains: a fortified mountain pass with stone walls and gate towers perched on steep cliffs, Song defenders on the ramparts with crossbows, while Jin armies with siege ladders and banners crowd the narrow valley below; dense forests, rushing rivers and mist. Distant view, no gore. Painted as a Southern Song landscape, ink and blue-green colour on silk.
li-qingzhao-jinshi: 1134, Jinhua in Zhejiang: a woman scholar in a plain robe, seen from behind, writes at a desk in a modest room with a few surviving bronzes, rubbings and books around her; through the window, an autumn courtyard with a plane tree and falling leaves. Quiet, melancholy, no legible text. Painted as a Southern Song figure painting, fine line and light colour on silk.
huaixi-mutiny: 1137, Luzhou (Hefei): a long column of Song soldiers with banners, carts and horses marches north out of a walled city across the flat Huai plain toward the border of Qi, while anxious officials watch from the city wall; empty camps and tents left behind. Autumn, grey sky, distant view, no gore. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
battle-of-shunchang: 1140, Shunchang (Fuyang) on the Huai plain in midsummer: from the gates of a small earth-walled city, Song foot soldiers with long axes and short spears sally out at noon against heavily armoured Jurchen cavalry, whose horses stand exhausted in the blazing heat beside a river; shimmering haze, dust, wilted fields, banners hanging limp. Distant panoramic view, all figures small, no gore. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll in ink and light colour on silk, warm ochre tones.
yancheng: 1140, Yancheng near Luohe in Henan: on an open plain of summer wheat fields, Song infantry in lamellar armour with long-handled axes and banners advance in close formation against charging Jurchen heavy cavalry; behind the Song lines, a messenger on horseback gallops in from the south carrying a sealed order. Dust clouds, low hills, distant view, all figures tiny, no gore. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
treaty-of-shaoxing: 1141, Lin'an (Hangzhou): in a palace hall above West Lake, Song officials in robes and black caps bow before Jurchen envoys in fur-trimmed robes who stand at the centre holding a sealed document case; servants carry in lacquer chests of silver and bolts of silk, the hills and pagodas of Hangzhou visible through open doors. Winter light, formal, subdued mood, figures at middle distance. Painted as a Southern Song court painting, fine line and mineral colours on silk.
generals-disarmed: 1141, Lin'an (Hangzhou): three generals, seen from behind, now dressed in civil officials' purple robes and black caps instead of armour, walk slowly into a palace council hall, while outside the gate their armour, banners and military seals are carried away on lacquer trays by court officials; guards in neat rows. Spring, red pillars and grey tiles, solemn mood. Painted as a Southern Song court painting, ink and light colour on silk.
wanyan-liang-coup: 1149, Huining near Harbin: the Jin palace compound at night, timber halls with tiled roofs within rammed-earth walls, snow on the ground; armed Jurchen nobles with braided hair and fur coats hurry through a torch-lit courtyard toward the main hall, guards standing aside at the gate, all seen from far above with no violence shown. Cold blue moonlight, orange torches. Painted as a Jin-dynasty handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
jin-zhongdu: 1153, Zhongdu (Beijing): a long procession of the Jin court, with Jurchen nobles in fur-trimmed robes, Han officials in robes, carts, camels and banners, enters the gates of a newly rebuilt walled capital with palace halls and glazed roof tiles; the Western Hills rise behind. Spring day, festive and grand, many small figures. Painted as a Jin-dynasty handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, in the manner of northern court painting.
qin-hui-death: 1155, Lin'an (Hangzhou): a grand ministerial mansion with tiled gate towers and garden pavilions, white mourning cloth hung over its entrance; officials in white robes come and go, while across the street ordinary townspeople glance from their shopfronts; West Lake and misty hills beyond. Late autumn, grey and still. Painted as a Southern Song genre painting, ink and light colour on silk, in the manner of Li Song's urban scenes.
huizi: 1160, Lin'an (Hangzhou): inside a government printing workshop, workers ink large bronze printing plates and press sheets of mulberry-bark paper money with patterned designs and red seal colours, sheets drying on racks, officials counting stacks; outside, merchants exchange notes at a busy market street. No legible characters. Painted as a Southern Song genre painting, fine line and light colour on silk.
battle-of-tangdao: 1161, Tangdao off the Shandong coast near Qingdao: a small fleet of Song warships under sail closes on a much larger Jin fleet anchored in a bay; Song archers shoot fire arrows and toss gunpowder bombs, the Jin ships' oiled-cloth sails catching fire, smoke billowing over the grey sea, rocky headlands behind. Distant, panoramic, no gore. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
shizong-of-jin: 1161, Liaoyang in Manchuria: in front of a walled city with a tall brick pagoda, Jurchen nobles in fur robes and Han officials in robes gather in a courtyard and kneel before a raised dais where a robed figure, seen from behind, receives their homage; banners and horses fill the square. Autumn, clear northern sky. Painted as a Jin-dynasty court painting, ink and light colour on silk.
xiaozong-rehabilitates-yue-fei: 1162, Lin'an (Hangzhou): by the shore of West Lake beneath Qixia Hill, a solemn reburial ceremony at a new tomb with stone figures and a memorial hall; officials in robes bow, incense smoke drifts, honour guards in armour stand along the spirit path, boats on the misty lake. Early spring, willows budding, figures small. Painted as a Southern Song landscape in the Ma Yuan manner, ink and light colour on silk.
fuli: 1163, Fuli near Suzhou in northern Anhui: a Song army camp on the Huai plain at night in disarray, tents abandoned and supply carts overturned, soldiers streaming south across fields while Jin cavalry campfires glow on the horizon; a full moon behind clouds. Distant view, no gore, sombre mood. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and pale wash on silk.
treaty-of-longxing: 1165, Lin'an (Hangzhou): Song envoys in robes and caps depart from the city's northern gate with a modest train of carts carrying silk and silver, while Jin envoys in fur hats ride alongside; peaceful farmland and canals stretch north. Spring, calm mood, distant view. Willow-lined canals and farmhouses border the road, a few farmers pause at their ploughs to watch the envoys pass. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
quanzhen-founded: 1167, Ninghai (Muping) on the Shandong coast: a Daoist master in a plain patched robe and topknot, seen from a distance, sits in a simple hermitage hut on a hillside overlooking the sea, while seven disciples in robes sit before him; pines, rocks and clouds around. Calm autumn morning. Painted as a Jin-period Daoist painting, ink and light colour on silk.
fan-chengda-mission: 1170, the road to Zhongdu (Beijing): a small Song embassy of officials in robes on horseback, with servants and carts, travels north across the plain, passing ruined villages and an old palace site of Kaifeng, local people in Jurchen-style clothes watching; Zhongdu's walls appear on the horizon. Autumn, melancholy mood. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
lu-you-shu-journey: 1170, the Three Gorges near Kuizhou (Fengjie): a small wooden river boat is hauled upstream by trackers with ropes along a narrow cliff path, a scholar-official in robes seen from behind standing on deck, towering limestone cliffs and swirling rapids, the gate of Qutang Gorge ahead. Misty autumn, monkeys on the rocks. Painted as a Southern Song landscape, Xia Gui-style ink and pale wash on silk.
zhu-xi-granaries: 1171, Wufu village near Jianning in northern Fujian: villagers in short jackets carry sacks of grain into a newly built tiled community granary, while a scholar in a plain robe and clerks at a table record loans; green hills, rice paddies and bamboo groves around. Autumn harvest, warm light, small figures. Painted as a Southern Song genre painting, ink and light colour on silk.
goose-lake: 1175, Goose Lake Temple near Yanshan in Jiangxi: in a Buddhist temple hall set among misty green mountains, several scholars in plain robes and caps sit on mats facing each other in debate, students listening around them; a lake and pines outside. Early summer, calm intellectual atmosphere, figures small. Painted as a Southern Song figure painting in ink and light colour on silk.
white-deer-grotto-revival: 1179, White Deer Grotto at the foot of Mount Lu: a rebuilt academy of tiled halls and courtyards in a wooded valley beside a stream, a stone grotto nearby; students in plain robes bow before a teacher in a lecture hall, others read under pines, a white deer grazing near the gate. Mist on the peaks, peaceful autumn. Painted as a Southern Song landscape, ink and light colour on silk.
changbian-completed: 1183, Lin'an (Hangzhou): an elderly scholar in robes, seen from behind, presents a huge set of bound volumes wrapped in silk cases, carried in on many lacquer trays by attendants, to court officials in a palace hall; shelves of books and red pillars around. Calm daylight, solemn mood, no legible text. Painted as a Southern Song court painting, fine line and mineral colours on silk.
four-books: 1190, Zhangzhou in southern Fujian: in a printing workshop, craftsmen carve wooden blocks and print pages for bound books, stacks of new volumes tied with string, a scholar in plain robe seen from behind inspecting a printed sheet; banana trees and a courtyard outside. Warm light, no legible text. Painted as a Southern Song genre painting, ink and light colour on silk.
yellow-river-captures-huai: 1194, Yangwu near Yuanyang in Henan: the muddy Yellow River bursts through a broken dike and floods across the plain toward the southeast, swallowing villages and fields; peasants in short jackets escape on rafts with livestock, and in the distance the floodwaters meet a wide river. Grey storm sky, vast scale, small figures, no corpses. Painted as a Jin-period landscape handscroll, ink and pale wash on silk.
shaoxi-abdication: 1194, Lin'an (Hangzhou): in a palace courtyard draped with white mourning cloth for a funeral, officials in white robes gather before a coffin hall, while a young prince in robes, seen from behind, is led up steps by ministers to a hall; an empty throne seat waits. Summer, tense solemn mood. Painted as a Southern Song court painting, ink and light colour on silk.
qingyuan-ban: 1196, Lin'an (Hangzhou): outside a city academy, government clerks in robes nail closure notices of blank paper on the gate while students in plain robes leave quietly carrying bundles of books; officials watch from horseback. Autumn, falling leaves, subdued mood, no legible text. A stone gate with empty lecture halls behind it, scattered pages blowing across the courtyard paving. Painted as a Southern Song genre painting, ink and light colour on silk.
zhu-xi-death: 1200, Kaoting near Jianyang in northern Fujian: a modest academy hall among green hills and bamboo, white mourning banners at the gate; a few students and scholars in plain white robes arrive quietly for the funeral, a coffin draped in cloth in the hall, books on shelves. Spring rain, misty hills, sombre mood. Painted as a Southern Song landscape, ink and light colour on silk.
ma-xia-painting: 1200, Lin'an (Hangzhou): a tiny scholar under a twisting pine stands on a rocky outcrop in the lower corner, gazing across a vast misty river into empty space, a faint far shore and moon in the upper distance; a small boat drifts in the mist. Asymmetrical composition with most of the picture empty. Painted in Southern Song academy style, Ma Yuan 'one-corner' composition, ink and pale wash on silk.
xin-qiji-beigu: 1205, Jingkou (Zhenjiang): a pavilion atop Beigu Hill overlooking the broad Yangtze, a veteran in robes, seen from behind, stands at the railing gazing north across the river toward distant hills; boats on the water, autumn clouds, wind in the pines. Below the hill, the walls and rooftops of Jingkou and moored war junks line the riverbank. Painted as a Southern Song landscape, Xia Gui-style ink and pale wash on silk, contemplative mood.
kaixi: 1206, the Huai River frontier: a Song army in lamellar armour crosses the Huai River on boats and pontoon bridges, banners flying; on the far bank, Jin fortifications and cavalry wait. Summer clouds, flat plain, distant view, no gore. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, with the court city of Lin'an implied far behind by misty pagodas.
han-tuozhou-killed: 1207, Lin'an (Hangzhou): at dawn, on a quiet lane beside the palace walls of Hangzhou, a minister's carriage is halted by armed palace guards, officials watching from a gateway; mist over West Lake, willows, all seen from a distance with no violence shown. Winter, cold atmosphere. Lanterns still glow faintly along the lane, and frost covers the roof tiles. Painted as a Southern Song genre painting, ink and pale colour on silk.
jiading-peace: 1208, Lin'an (Hangzhou): a Song embassy leaves the city by its northern gate, officials in robes on horseback with carts loaded with silver and bolts of silk and a small sealed lacquer box, heading north; townspeople watch, the walls and hills of Hangzhou behind. Autumn, sombre mood. Willows and canal boats line the road out of the city. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
battle-of-yehuling: 1211, Yehuling (Badger Mouth Pass) near Zhangjiakou: Mongol cavalry in fur hats and deels charge in waves down from the steppe plateau through a mountain pass, while a large Jin army with banners and infantry breaks and flees down the slopes; rocky ridges, dust, autumn. Distant panoramic view, no gore. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll in the manner of Liu Guandao's steppe horsemen, ink and colour on silk.
jin-moves-to-kaifeng: 1214, the road from Zhongdu to Kaifeng: a long Jin court procession with carts, camels, palanquins and officials in robes travels south across the North China Plain, carrying chests and archives, while far behind, the walls of Zhongdu stand under a hazy sky. Summer, dust, small figures. Mounted Jurchen guards in fur caps ride alongside the column, and peasants watch from the roadside fields. Painted as a Jin-period handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
red-coat-army: 1214, Weizhou (Weifang) in Shandong: crowds of peasants wearing red jackets, armed with spears, hoes and bows, gather on a hillside above a village, homemade banners raised, horses and carts; wheat fields and low hills around. Spring, crowd seen from a distance. Smoke from cooking fires drifts above the crowd, and a few riders on shaggy horses scout the road ahead. Painted as a Jin-period handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, red accents.
zhongdu-falls: 1215, Zhongdu (Beijing): columns of black smoke rise over the walled city and palace roofs as Mongol cavalry in fur hats ride through an opened gate; refugees stream out along the roads, the Western Hills in the distance. Early summer, hazy sky, distant view, no gore. Abandoned carts and scattered goods lie along the roads leading away from the city. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
mongol-khwarazm-campaign: 1219-1221, Otrar on the Syr Darya: a vast Mongol army with horse archers, siege catapults and banners encamps around a mud-brick walled Central Asian city with domed buildings; smoke rises from the citadel, the river and desert steppe beyond. Distant panoramic view, no gore. Rows of felt tents and tethered horses fill the foreground. Painted as a Persian miniature in the Ilkhanid Jami al-Tawarikh manner, flat colours, gold sky.
qiu-chuji-meets-genghis: 1222, Parwan in the Hindu Kush: in a large white felt tent in a mountain valley camp, an elderly Daoist master in plain robe sits facing a Mongol ruler surrounded by attendants, all seen from a distance through the tent's opening; snow peaks, horses and many yurts around. Calm, respectful mood. Painted as a Yuan-period handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
lizong-enthroned: 1224, Lin'an (Hangzhou): in a palace hall at dusk, a young man in imperial robes, seen from behind, is led to the throne by a powerful minister while officials kneel in rows, an empty place where another prince was expected; white mourning cloth hangs from the eaves. Tense, solemn mood. Painted as a Southern Song court painting, ink and light colour on silk.
zhao-rugua: 1225, Quanzhou: a trade official in robes sits at a desk in a harbour office writing in a book, while foreign merchants in turbans, sarongs and robes describe their homelands, displaying goods such as ivory, frankincense, pepper and coral; ocean junks and dhows visible through the window. Bright day, no legible text. Painted as a Southern Song genre painting, ink and colour on silk.
western-xia-falls: 1227, Zhongxing (Yinchuan): Mongol cavalry encircle the earthen walls of the Tangut capital beneath the Helan mountains, smoke rising from the city, Buddhist pagodas visible; Tangut envoys emerge from a gate carrying gifts in surrender. Summer heat, distant view, no gore. Irrigation canals and green fields of the Ningxia plain lie empty around the walls. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and colour on silk, with Western Xia mural ochres.
genghis-death: 1227, the Liupan Mountains in Ningxia: in a summer encampment of white felt yurts in a high green valley, a large tent is surrounded by silent guards; a closed covered cart drawn by oxen prepares to leave north at dusk, riders lined up in a long column. No portrait, solemn mood. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll in the manner of Liu Guandao, ink and colour on silk.
ogedei-enthroned: 1229, the Kherlen River in Mongolia: a vast kurultai assembly on the grassy steppe, hundreds of white felt yurts and a great ceremonial tent, Mongol nobles in deels and fur hats kneeling in rows, horses and banners of yak tails; a figure seen from afar raised on a felt carpet. Summer sky, river bend. Painted as a Persian miniature in Ilkhanid style, gold sky, bright colours.
mongols-invade-korea: 1231, Kaegyong (Kaesong): Mongol cavalry in fur hats ride across autumn hills toward the walled Goryeo capital with its palace halls and Buddhist pagodas; later, boats crowded with court officials and families cross the strait toward Ganghwa Island. Distant panoramic view, no gore. Wooden Goryeo temple halls with curved eaves are visible among autumn maples, and the sea glitters toward the island. Painted in Goryeo Buddhist painting style, mineral colours and gold on silk.
battle-of-sanfengshan: 1232, Sanfengshan near Yuzhou in Henan: in a heavy snowstorm, a frozen Jin army huddles in a valley among three hills while Mongol cavalry in fur hats encircle them from the ridges; snow-laden banners, overturned carts. Distant view, white and grey tones, no gore. Snow-covered pines on the slopes, a few horses stand still in the drifts, and grey clouds hang low over the three peaks. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and pale colour on silk.
thunder-crash-bombs: 1232, Kaifeng: on the great city walls, Jin defenders lower iron-cased gunpowder bombs on chains toward Mongol siege shelters below, bright flashes and smoke bursting, others thrust fire lances from the battlements; the Mongol siege camp spreads across the plain. Night, dramatic light, distant view, no gore. Mongol wooden siege shelters covered with hides stand at the foot of the wall. Painted as a Jin-period handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
song-mongol-alliance: 1233, Xiangyang on the Han River: a Song army column with carts of grain and banners marches out from a walled city along a riverside road, a Mongol envoy on horseback with fur hat accompanying the officers; boats loaded with supplies on the river. Autumn day, distant view. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
duanping: 1234, Luoyang: Song troops in lamellar armour march into the ruined city, crumbling walls, overgrown palace foundations and empty streets, while far off on the hills, Mongol cavalry gather; a few starving soldiers forage in the fields. Summer haze, desolate atmosphere, no gore. Weeds grow between broken roof tiles, and a stone stele stands alone in the empty palace grounds. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and pale colour on silk.
karakorum-built: 1235, Karakorum on the Orkhon valley steppe: a newly walled city with a palace hall of Chinese-style tiled roofs, workshops and markets, surrounded by hundreds of yurts; artisans from many lands build walls, ox-carts arrive with timber, horses graze. Summer, vast sky. Merchants with camels from the west arrive at the gate, and a silver fountain tree stands in the palace courtyard. Painted as a Persian miniature in the Ilkhanid manner, bright colours and gold.
mongols-sack-chengdu: 1236, Chengdu: from far off across the Chengdu plain, columns of smoke rise over the walled city while Mongol cavalry ride through rice fields toward the gates; refugees flee along roads toward mountains. Autumn, grey sky, distant view, no gore. Abandoned bamboo groves and farmhouses line the roads, and the river glints under smoke. Painted as a Southern Song landscape handscroll, ink and pale wash on silk, sombre tones.
meng-gong-xiangyang: 1239, Xiangyang and Fancheng on the Han River: Song troops raise banners over the twin walled cities facing each other across the river, workers rebuilding walls and moats, war boats on the river; green hills around. Spring, distant view. Labourers carry baskets of earth and stone, soldiers drill on the riverbank, and a pontoon bridge links the two cities across the water. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
yu-jie-mountain-forts: 1243, near Chongqing: a fortified mountain city perched on a steep flat-topped hill above the confluence of rivers, stone walls following the cliff edges, soldiers and farmers building ramparts, terraced fields inside; misty Sichuan mountains around. Civilians carry baskets of stone up winding steps, banners fly on the gate towers, and boats below on the river bring supplies of grain and timber. Painted as a Southern Song landscape, ink and blue-green colour on silk.
qin-jiushao: 1247, Huzhou: a scholar in robes sits at a desk in a study overlooking a lake, arranging red and black counting rods on a board, a scroll with blank grids beside him, assistants calculating with rods. Peaceful afternoon, no legible text. Bamboo and a garden rock outside the open window, a teapot on a stand, and stacks of bound volumes nearby. Painted as a Southern Song genre painting, ink and light colour on silk.
song-ci: 1247, Hunan: in a courtyard of a provincial yamen, a judge in robes and cap, seen from behind, consults an open handbook while assistants prepare vinegar, wine and steaming braziers used in inquests; clerks record, onlookers wait at the gate. No bodies shown, calm, investigative atmosphere. Bamboo screens and a stone courtyard. Painted as a Southern Song genre painting, ink and light colour on silk.
li-ye-ceyuan: 1248, Fenglong Mountain near Yuanshi in Hebei: a retired scholar in robes sits in a mountain retreat study with circle diagrams and counting rods spread on a table, students around him; pines and rocky hills outside the window. Calm autumn day, no legible text. A small stream passes the study, and a servant brings tea on a tray. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty scholar's landscape, ink and light colour on paper.
dali-conquest: 1253, the Jinsha River in Yunnan: Mongol soldiers cross the swift river on rafts made of inflated animal hides, horses swimming alongside, steep gorges and snowy mountains behind; beyond, the Dali basin with Erhai Lake and three white pagodas. Clear autumn, distant view. Mongol horsemen gather on the shore, and local fishermen watch from the far bank. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
kaiping-founded: 1256, Kaiping on the steppe of Inner Mongolia: builders lay out a square walled city on grassland near a river, with an inner palace of tiled halls, earthen walls rising, surveyors with ropes, carts of timber, and Mongol yurts nearby. Summer, wide sky, small figures. A Han scholar-architect in robes, seen from behind, studies the layout with Mongol officers. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
first-mongol-vietnam: 1258, Thăng Long (Hanoi): Mongol cavalry ride into a riverside city of wooden houses and temples in the Red River delta; soon after, Trần troops with spears and boats counterattack along the river. Misty paddy fields, bamboo groves, distant view, no gore. Thatched stilt houses, water buffalo in the fields and small river boats crowd the scene. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
diaoyu: 1259, Diaoyu Fortress at Hechuan: a fortified mountain city on a steep cliff above the junction of three rivers, Song defenders on the ramparts, while the Mongol camps fill the valley below; summer storm clouds gather. Distant view, no gore. Steep stone steps climb to the gate, rivers swirl around the base of the cliff, and terraced fields cover the summit plateau inside the walls. Painted as a Southern Song landscape, ink and blue-green colour on silk.
siege-of-ezhou: 1259, Ezhou (Wuchang) on the Yangtze: Mongol troops encircle the walled city across the river, siege engines on the bank, Song war boats on the water; a messenger rides into the Mongol camp. Autumn, wide river panorama, distant view, no gore. Hills of Wuchang rise behind the walls, and river junks carry Song reinforcements. Painted as a Southern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
fire-lance-shouchun: 1259, Shouchun (Shouxian): on a city wall, Song soldiers test a long bamboo tube weapon, a flash and smoke bursting from its mouth as a projectile flies; others watch, gunpowder pots stacked nearby. Daylight, Huai plain beyond. Officers in lamellar armour observe from a gate tower, and craftsmen inspect bundles of bamboo tubes and coils of fuse on the parapet. Painted as a Southern Song genre painting, ink and light colour on silk.
kublai-khan-1260: 1260, Kaiping (Shangdu) on the steppe: a kurultai assembly with hundreds of yurts around a walled palace, Mongol nobles in deels and fur hats kneeling, banners and horses; a ruler, seen from afar, raised before a great tent. Summer sky. Han officials in robes stand together with Mongol princes, and herds of horses graze on the grassland. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll in the manner of Liu Guandao, ink and colour on silk.
toluid-civil-war: 1260-1264, the Orkhon valley near Karakorum: two great Mongol cavalry armies with yak-tail standards face each other across a wide grassland, while far to the south a long line of empty grain carts stands idle on the road from China; the walled city of Karakorum with its tiled palace roof and ring of yurts lies behind. Autumn grass, enormous sky, figures tiny, no gore. Painted as a Persian miniature in the Ilkhanid Jami al-Tawarikh manner, flat bright colours, gold sky.
hao-jing-detained: 1260s, Zhenzhou (Yizheng) on the north bank of the Yangtze: a scholarly Mongol envoy in plain Han robes, seen from behind, sits reading in the courtyard of a guarded government lodge, walls high around him, a single wild goose flying overhead; guards in Song armour at the gate, the wide river and sails beyond the wall. Autumn, quiet, many years implied by an old tree. Painted as a Southern Song figure painting, ink and light colour on silk.
li-tan-rebellion: 1262, Jinan in Shandong: a large Mongol and Han army encircles the walled city with ditches and palisades, the Daming Lake and springs visible inside the walls, smoke over the city; Mount Qianfo rises to the south. Summer haze, distant panoramic view, banners in rings around the city, all figures small, no gore. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, after the northern landscape tradition.
public-fields-law: 1263, the lower Yangtze countryside near Lin'an: government surveyors in robes measure rice paddies with ropes and poles, while unhappy landowners in fine gowns argue with clerks at a table under a willow, and tenant farmers stand watching; canals, stone bridges, white-walled farmhouses and distant hills. Overcast spring, many small figures. Painted as a Southern Song genre handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
dadu-construction: 1267, northeast of the old Jin capital: thousands of workers build the rammed-earth walls and laid-out grid of a vast new city on the plain, surveyors with cords mark straight avenues, a lake with an island and palace terraces taking shape; Mongol overseers on horseback and Han architects in robes consult plans. Spring, Western Hills behind, panoramic view, tiny figures. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty ruled-line architectural painting, ink and light colour on silk.
siege-of-xiangyang-begins: 1268, Xiangyang and Fancheng on the Han River: a ring of newly built Mongol earthen forts and palisades encircles the twin walled cities, while on the river, shipwrights build rows of new warships and sailors drill with oars; the Song cities stand defiant with banners on their walls. Autumn, green hills, distant panoramic view, no gore. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
phagspa-script: 1269, Dadu (Beijing): in a palace hall, a Tibetan lama in red-and-yellow robes, seen from a distance, presents a scroll of square-shaped unreadable letters to the court, Mongol nobles in deels and Han officials in robes standing on both sides, scribes copying the new script at low tables. Incense smoke, Tibetan thangkas and Chinese screens, no legible writing. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty court painting, ink and mineral colours on silk.
dadu-named-capital: 1272, Dadu (Khanbaliq): a panoramic view of the new imperial capital, square walls with gate towers, broad straight avenues, the palace with white marble terraces beside the Taiye Lake, the drum tower and markets crowded with camels, carts and merchants from many lands. Clear spring morning, many tiny figures. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and colour on silk, in fine ruled-line architectural style.
bunei-invasion: 1274, Hakata Bay in northern Kyushu: Yuan and Goryeo warships anchored in the bay, troops landed on the beach with banners and drums, while Japanese mounted samurai in ō-yoroi armour with bows ride along the shore and pine-covered dunes; storm clouds gather over the sea. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the style of a Kamakura-period emakimono handscroll like the Mongol Invasion Scrolls, ink and colour on paper.
battle-of-dingjiazhou: 1275, Dingjiazhou on the Yangtze near Tongling: a huge Song fleet of warships with matting sails breaks and scatters downriver, banners falling, while Yuan troops on both banks fire catapults and Yuan boats advance; smoke drifts over the wide river and reed islands. Spring, grey sky, distant panoramic view, no gore. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
jia-sidao-killed: 1275, the road south to Zhangzhou in Fujian: a disgraced former minister in plain robe, seen from behind, rides a sedan chair under the escort of a few soldiers through hilly country, arriving at the gate of a small mountain temple amid pines and bamboo; the escort officer walks ahead. Autumn, gloomy dusk, no violence. Painted as a Southern Song landscape, ink and pale colour on silk.
battle-of-jiaoshan: 1275, Jiaoshan island in the Yangtze near Zhenjiang: a great line of Song warships chained together by iron links fills the river beside a wooded island with a temple; Yuan boats shoot fire arrows and the chained ships burn, smoke billowing across the water. Summer, distant view, no gore. Yuan soldiers watch from the riverbank hills. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
linan-falls: 1276, Lin'an (Hangzhou): Yuan cavalry and officers ride in orderly columns through the city gate beside West Lake, while Song officials in robes kneel on the roadside presenting seals and registers; a palanquin with the young emperor and court ladies is led away north by escorts. Early spring, misty lake and pagodas, no gore. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
duanzong-enthroned: 1276, Fuzhou: in a modest hall in the coastal city, ministers and generals in robes and armour kneel before a small boy in imperial robes, seen from far away on a makeshift throne; loyal soldiers fill the courtyard, ships in the Min River harbour behind. Early summer, sense of urgency. Painted as a Southern Song court painting, ink and light colour on silk.
pu-shougeng-defects: 1276, Quanzhou harbour: a great fleet of ocean-going junks lies anchored in the bay, and on the wharf a merchant official in rich robes and turban, seen from a distance, hands over registers to Yuan officers on horseback; the city gate is closed against a Song fleet waiting offshore. Overcast day, distant figures, no violence shown. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
quanzhou-shibosi-yuan: 1277, Quanzhou (Zaitun): a vast bustling harbour filled with large four-masted junks, Arab dhows and Indian ships; merchants of many lands in turbans, robes and sarongs bargain on wharves piled with porcelain crates and silk bales, a mosque minaret, Buddhist twin stone pagodas and Hindu temple roofs in the city. Bright sun. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty genre handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
gaocheng-observatory: 1279, Gaocheng near Dengfeng below Mount Song: a tall brick gnomon tower with a long stone scale running north along the ground, astronomers in robes measuring the noon shadow with a sighting device; temples and wooded hills of Mount Song behind. Clear winter-solstice noon, small figures. A clerk notes readings at a small table, and an assistant adjusts a pinhole shadow-definer on the stone scale. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty landscape, ink and light colour on silk.
shoushi-calendar: 1280, Dadu (Beijing): on the terrace of the imperial observatory, astronomers in robes operate a large bronze simplified armillary instrument and a gnomon, assistants recording measurements on blank sheets, Mongol officials watching; the palace roofs and walls below, clear night sky with stars. No legible text. A water clock and bronze star globe stand nearby on the terrace. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty court painting, ink and light colour on silk.
yuan-zaju: 1280, Dadu (Beijing): a crowded wooden theatre stage in a city pleasure quarter, actors in colourful costumes and painted faces perform a scene with musicians playing drums, clappers and flutes at the side; Mongol, Han and Central Asian spectators fill the benches and balconies. Lantern light, lively atmosphere. Painted in the style of the Yuan-dynasty Zaju mural of Guangsheng Temple, Shanxi, mineral colours on plaster.
sea-grain-transport: 1282, Liujiagang near Taicang at the Yangtze mouth: a fleet of flat-bottomed sea junks with matting sails loads sacks of tax grain at the harbour, porters carrying sacks up gangplanks, officials checking cargo, the fleet setting out into the open sea under a spring wind. Wide estuary, many small figures. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
ahmad-assassinated: 1282, Dadu (Beijing) at night: torches flare outside a palace gate in the Yuan capital, armed men in Han and Mongol dress gathering in confusion, horses rearing, guards running along the walls; the scene is seen from a distance, with no violence shown. Spring night, dark blue sky. Lanterns sway on the gate tower. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and pale colour on silk.
wen-tianxiang: 1283, Dadu (Beijing): in a bare prison courtyard of the Yuan capital in winter, a lone Song scholar-official in plain robes and cap, seen from behind, stands facing south and bows deeply; guards wait by the gate, snow on the roof tiles, a single plum tree. Solemn, dignified mood, no violence. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty figure painting, ink and pale colour on paper.
champa-campaign: 1283, Vijaya near Quy Nhơn in Champa: Yuan war junks land troops on a tropical beach below brick Cham temple towers; the Cham king's forces withdraw into jungle hills with elephants, while Yuan soldiers occupy a deserted wooden palace. Palm trees, hot sun, distant view, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Cham temple relief combined with Yuan handscroll ink and colour.
second-vietnam-war: 1285, the Red River delta near Thăng Long: Yuan cavalry and infantry march through empty, abandoned villages and burned fields, while Đại Việt soldiers in short tunics with spears gather in boats on the river and in bamboo groves for a counterattack. Hot season, misty paddies, distant view, no gore. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
branch-secretariats: 1286, a provincial capital of the Yuan: a new government compound with tiled gates and halls, Mongol and Han officials in robes arriving on horseback, clerks carrying registers, messengers of the postal relay riding out along roads to distant towns. Clear day, orderly busy scene, small figures. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty architectural genre painting, ink and light colour on silk.
nayan-rebellion: 1287, the Liao River plain near Tongliao: an elderly Mongol emperor, seen from afar, rides atop a wooden pavilion carried by four elephants at the centre of a great army, while two vast cavalry forces meet on the grassland; banners and dust. Summer, distant view, no gore. Painted as a Persian miniature in the Ilkhanid Jami al-Tawarikh manner, flat bright colours.
zhiyuan-chao: 1287, Dadu (Beijing): in a government treasury office, clerks print large grey-paper banknotes with patterned borders and red seal marks from bronze plates, stacks of notes bundled on tables, merchants exchanging old notes at a counter; Mongol officials watch. No legible text. Strings of copper coins and silver ingots are piled in a corner, and a guard stands at the treasury door. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty genre painting, ink and light colour on silk.
battle-of-bach-dang-1288: 1288, the Bạch Đằng River estuary: at low tide, rows of iron-tipped wooden stakes emerge from the riverbed and trap a Yuan fleet of large junks, while small Đại Việt boats attack from hidden creeks among mangroves and limestone hills. Grey sky, distant view, no gore. The Yuan junks list and run aground on the stakes as the tide falls, their sails slack. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and colour on silk.
huitong-canal: 1289, Linqing in western Shandong: thousands of labourers dig a new canal channel across the flat plain, building stone locks and sluice gates; grain barges wait to enter, officials on horseback supervising. Autumn, willows and villages, panoramic view, small figures. Workers carry earth up ramps in baskets on poles, stonemasons cut blocks for the lock walls, and tents for the labourers line the bank. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
guan-hanqing-dou-e: 1290, Dadu (Beijing): a theatre stage where an actress in white robes performs a tragic scene as paper snowflakes fall in midsummer, actors as officials in robes on one side, musicians playing; spectators watching from benches. Lantern light, dramatic mood. Painted wooden backdrops, hanging curtains and a raised timber platform frame the stage, with a few props such as a stool and a table. Painted in the style of the Yuan-dynasty Guangsheng Temple drama mural, mineral colours on plaster.
