eg-tanis-and-thebes: c. 1069 BCE, Tanis in the delta: a temple city of reused granite obelisks and statues among marshes, a king's court in linen, and on the right half of the scene a distant Theban temple of Amun with priests in leopard skins, the two halves separated by the long Nile. Painted in the manner of a Third Intermediate Period papyrus illustration, fine black outlines.
eg-carthage-founded: c. 814 BCE, Carthage: Phoenician ships with curved prows and square sails anchored in a sheltered bay, settlers in long robes unloading jars and bales on the shore, a woman of rank in a fine robe seen from behind directing workers who mark out the line of a city wall with an oxhide strip, hills behind. Painted in the manner of a Phoenician ivory carving and painted pottery, warm ivory, red and ochre.
eg-piye-conquest: c. 727 BCE, Memphis: a Kushite army with archers and horses in Nubian dress and Egyptian-style kilts storms the white walls of Memphis from boats moored alongside, the city's temples and pyramids beyond, river crowded with ships. No gore. Palm groves line the riverbanks, and townspeople watch from the rooftops as Kushite standards are raised over the gate. Painted in the style of a Late Period Egyptian relief, figures in profile, flat earth colours.
eg-assyrian-conquest: 671 BCE, Memphis: Assyrian soldiers in conical helmets and scale armour with shields and spears march into a captured Egyptian city, a column of chariots, captives and booty of statues and gold carried out of temple gates, palms and the Nile. No gore. Scribes tally the plunder on the riverbank. Rendered in the style of an Assyrian palace relief from Nineveh, carved stone, figures in registers.
eg-psamtik-i: c. 664 BCE, Sais in the western delta: a pharaoh's court with Egyptian officials in linen and Greek mercenaries in bronze helmets and round shields standing in ranks, Greek trading ships moored at the river quay, a new temple pylon behind. Bales of goods and jars of oil are stacked on the quay. Painted in the style of a Late Period Egyptian painting combined with Greek black-figure vase motifs, flat colour.
eg-cambyses-conquest: 525 BCE, Pelusium in the eastern delta: Persian infantry with wicker shields and long spears, archers in pleated robes and soft caps advance across the marsh-fringed plain toward an Egyptian fortress, Egyptian troops with bows on the walls, dust rising. No gore. Persian cavalry wait on the flanks, and reed beds frame the scene. Rendered in the style of an Achaemenid relief from Persepolis, processional rows of soldiers in profile.
eg-hanno-the-navigator: c. 500 BCE, the Atlantic coast of West Africa: a fleet of Carthaginian galleys with oars and square sails sails past a green coast with mountains and a large river mouth, fires burning on the hillsides at night, settlers and sailors on deck. Painted in the manner of a Punic and Greek vase painting of ships, flat black, red and cream.
eg-nectanebo-ii: 343 BCE, the Nile delta near Pelusium: one continuous riverside scene. In the middle distance Persian troops in long robes and soft caps with tall spears march through the open gate of a mud-brick Egyptian fortress beside reed marshes. In the foreground on the river, an Egyptian king in a blue crown sits in a small papyrus boat with a few attendants, rowing away upstream, palms and a temple pylon on the far bank. No gore. A single unified picture, no panels, registers or dividing lines. Painted in the manner of a Late Period Egyptian papyrus illustration, flat colour and black outlines.
eg-alexander-conquers-egypt: 332 BCE, Memphis: a young Macedonian king in a cuirass and cloak seen from behind is received by Egyptian priests in white linen and leopard skins before a temple pylon, Macedonian cavalry and phalanx soldiers with long spears behind him, crowds watching, palms and the Nile. Incense smoke rises before the temple door. Painted as a Hellenistic mosaic with small stone tesserae, warm ochres and whites.
eg-alexandria-founded: 331 BCE, the Mediterranean coast of Egypt: surveyors and architects in Greek chitons mark out a grid of streets on a sandy strip between the sea and a lake, using barley meal sprinkled on the ground, flocks of birds pecking at it, ships in a harbour and an island offshore. Painted as a Hellenistic mosaic, small tesserae, pale blue sea and sandy ochres.
eg-library-of-alexandria: c. 283 BCE, Alexandria: a colonnaded hall of the Mouseion with shelves of papyrus rolls in pigeonholes, scholars in Greek himations reading and copying at tables, one drawing geometric figures on a wax tablet, a garden courtyard with a fountain outside and the harbour in the distance. Painted in the style of a Hellenistic Roman fresco, soft ochre, red and green.
eg-eratosthenes: c. 240 BCE, Alexandria: a scholar in a Greek himation stands in a sunlit paved courtyard of the Museum, beside a tall granite obelisk and a vertical bronze rod casting a short noon shadow on the flagstones, measuring the shadow's angle with a simple bronze instrument. Assistants hold wax tablets and a measuring cord; colonnades, palm trees and the distant harbour with the Pharos lighthouse lie beyond under a bright sky. One single continuous scene, no inset, no frame, no lettering. Painted in the style of a Hellenistic Roman fresco, warm light and earth colours.
eg-battle-of-zama: 202 BCE, Zama in Tunisia: on a dusty plain, Roman legionaries in bronze Montefortino helmets with crests, mail shirts and tall curved oval scutum shields open lanes in their ranks as Carthaginian war elephants charge through, Roman and Numidian cavalry sweeping round the flanks, olive trees and distant hills, seen from a distance, no gore. The Romans carry no round shields; trumpeters blow long straight tubae. Painted in the manner of a Roman mosaic, small coloured tesserae, warm earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-masinissa-numidia: c. 202 BCE, Cirta in Numidia: a fortified city on a rock plateau above a deep gorge, a Berber king on horseback with a beard and a diadem riding with light Numidian cavalry, horses without saddles, herds and wheat fields around the plateau. Village women carry water jars along the gorge path. Painted in the manner of a Roman mosaic of North Africa, warm ochres and greens.
eg-rosetta-stone-decree: 196 BCE, Memphis: inside a temple courtyard, a stone carver chisels a dark granite slab divided into three bands of fine script rendered as an illegible texture, priests in white linen and shaven heads standing around, a statue of a Ptolemaic king nearby, lotus columns behind. Painted in the style of a Ptolemaic Egyptian temple relief, flat colour and fine outlines.
eg-destruction-of-carthage: 146 BCE, Carthage: smoke and flames rise over a great harbour city with a circular naval harbour and tall houses on the Byrsa hill, Roman legionaries in bronze helmets on the walls, Roman ships in the bay, fleeing citizens far away. No gore. Siege towers stand against the broken walls, and the empty market lies covered in ash. Painted in the manner of a Roman fresco, smoky reds and dark ochres.
eg-jugurthine-war: c. 108 BCE, Numidia: Roman legionaries in mail with oval shields climb a rocky desert slope toward a Numidian stronghold on a high crag, Numidian horsemen fighting from the hilltop, and in the foreground Roman officers in a camp counting chests of silver. Pack mules wait at the foot of the slope under a hot sky. Painted in the manner of a Roman mosaic, warm ochres, reds and dark outlines.
eg-cleopatra-death: 30 BCE, Alexandria: Roman warships and legionaries arriving in the great harbour beneath the tall lighthouse of Pharos, the royal palace on the shore with its columned halls and a closed mausoleum building, Egyptian courtiers in mourning, a small cobra symbol carved on a pillar. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco from Pompeii, deep red and black with soft modelling.
eg-ptolemy-almagest: c. 150 CE, Alexandria: an astronomer in a Greek himation sits writing in a study with an armillary sphere of bronze rings and star charts, scrolls on shelves, a window opening onto the night sky over the harbour with the lighthouse lit. An oil lamp burns beside a bronze astrolabe, and a sundial stands in the courtyard. Painted in the style of a Roman-Egyptian fresco, warm ochres and a dark blue sky.
eg-septimius-severus: c. 203 CE, Leptis Magna on the Libyan coast: a new marble four-way triumphal arch and colonnaded forum with Corinthian columns rising beside the sea, Roman citizens in togas, workers on scaffolding, ships in a rebuilt harbour. Carved friezes of a triumphal procession decorate the arch, merchants unload amphorae on the quay, and a theatre with stone seats faces the turquoise sea. Painted as a Roman North African mosaic, rich ochres and blues.
eg-arian-controversy: c. 318 CE, Alexandria: inside a basilica church with columns and lamps, a group of bearded Christian clergy in long robes debate fiercely around a table with scrolls, the bishop seated at the head, crowds of laypeople listening from the aisles. Light falls through high windows onto the mosaic floor. Painted in the style of a Late Antique Coptic fresco, bold outlines and flat earth colours.
eg-augustine-of-hippo: c. 396 CE, Hippo Regius on the Algerian coast: a bishop in a simple robe sits writing at a desk in a whitewashed room with scrolls and codices, a window onto a basilica courtyard and the Mediterranean, olive trees on the hills. A lamp flickers on the desk, and a few clergy wait at the door. Painted in the manner of a Late Antique North African mosaic, small tesserae, soft colours.
eg-hypatia: c. 415 CE, Alexandria: a quiet scholar's lecture room with an astrolabe, a geometry diagram on a board and scrolls, an empty chair at the front, and outside the window a distant agitated crowd moving along a colonnaded street toward a church, a sombre late afternoon light. No violence depicted. Painted in the style of a Late Antique fresco, muted earth tones.
eg-vandals-take-carthage: 439 CE, Carthage: Vandal warriors with long hair, cloaks and spears pour through a gate in the great walls of a Roman city, citizens in tunics watching from colonnaded streets, Roman grain ships at anchor in the harbour being seized. No gore. Smoke rises from a single burning villa. Painted in the manner of a Late Roman North African mosaic, ochres, reds and blues.
eg-vandalic-war: 533 CE, Ad Decimum near Carthage: Byzantine cataphract cavalry in mail and plumed helmets charge across a dusty plain, Vandal horsemen scattering, the walls of Carthage on the horizon, dust rising, seen from far away. No gore. Byzantine infantry with round shields follow in close ranks, a general's banner flies above them, and olive groves line the road. Painted in the style of a Byzantine mosaic, gold background and coloured stone tesserae.
eg-muslim-conquest-egypt: 641 CE, the Babylon fortress at Old Cairo: Arab horsemen of Amr ibn al-As in mail shirts, simple turbans and cloaks with lances camp beside the Nile before a Roman fortress with round towers, Byzantine soldiers on the walls, Coptic churches and palm groves beyond, sailing boats on the river. Only light rope-pulled traction mangonels hauled by teams of men stand before the gates: no counterweight trebuchets with weight boxes, which came five centuries later. Painted in the style of an early Islamic manuscript painting, flat colours and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-kairouan-founded: 670 CE, Kairouan on the Tunisian plain: Arab soldiers and builders lay out a new garrison town in a flat scrubland, mud-brick walls and a first simple mosque with a courtyard and a square minaret rising, camels and tents around, olive trees. Workers dig a large cistern for water, and the hot sun beats down. Painted in the manner of an Islamic manuscript painting, warm ochres and soft blues.
eg-tariq-crosses: 711 CE, the Strait of Gibraltar: ships with lateen sails crowded with Berber and Arab soldiers cross the narrow strait from Tangier, the great limestone Rock of Gibraltar rising ahead, horses on deck, the African coast with mountains behind. Gulls circle above the waves, a small boat carries a commander ahead of the fleet, and morning mist clings to the rock's slopes. Painted in the style of an Andalusian Islamic manuscript painting, flat colour and gold.
eg-al-qarawiyyin: 859 CE, Fez: a mosque of whitewashed walls and green-tiled roofs being built in the narrow medina, a woman of means in a veil seen from behind with craftsmen, and students in robes sitting in a courtyard with a fountain around a teacher, books on low stands. Painted in the manner of a Moroccan and Andalusian Islamic manuscript painting, rich greens and gold.
eg-fatimid-caliphate-founded: 909 CE, Raqqada near Kairouan: Kutama Berber horsemen in white robes with banners ride into a palace city of domed buildings and gardens, a leader in robes received by crowds, palm trees and the Tunisian plain. Drummers and flag bearers lead the procession, while townspeople in turbans crowd the gates and rooftops, and a golden parasol is held over the rider. Painted in the style of an Islamic manuscript painting, flat colours and gold.
eg-fatimid-conquest-cairo: 969 CE, the Nile near Fustat: Fatimid soldiers and builders lay out the walls and gates of a new royal city in the desert, marking lines with ropes and stakes, camels carrying bricks, the Nile and the pyramids in the distance at dawn. Astrologers watch the sky for the auspicious hour. Painted in the manner of a Fatimid lustreware and manuscript painting, gold and ochre.
eg-saladin-ayyubid: 1171 CE, Cairo: a Friday prayer in a great mosque with a columned courtyard and wooden pulpit, a large crowd of worshippers seen from behind in turbans and robes, soldiers in mail at the doors, minarets of Cairo around. No religious figures depicted. Sunlight falls on carpets and hanging lamps, and the voice of a preacher seems to fill the hall. Painted in the style of an Islamic manuscript painting, gold and lapis blue.
eg-battle-of-mansurah: 1250, Mansurah in the Nile delta: Mamluk cavalry in turbans and mail with curved swords fight among narrow streets and canals against French knights in surcoats with crosses, crusader banners falling, palm trees, seen from a distance. No gore. Crowds of townspeople watch from rooftops, and broken lances litter the street while the river glints beyond the houses. Painted in the manner of a Mamluk manuscript painting, flat colours and gold.
eg-ibn-khaldun-muqaddimah: 1377, Qal'at Ibn Salama in western Algeria: a scholar in a turban and robe sits writing in a whitewashed room in a castle on a rocky hill, books and manuscripts around, a window over a wide valley with Berber tents and herds. Ink pots and reed pens lie on a low table, and a lamp burns at dusk. Painted in the manner of a Maghrebi manuscript painting, warm ochres and greens.
eg-battle-of-ridaniya: 1517, Ridaniya outside Cairo: Ottoman Janissaries with muskets and tall white caps and cannons fire across a dusty plain at Mamluk cavalry in mail and turbans, smoke rising, the minarets and citadel of Cairo in the distance. No gore. Banners of both armies fly above the dust, Ottoman cavalry wait in the wings, and camels carry supplies at the rear of the lines. Painted in the style of an Ottoman miniature, flat colours and gold.
eg-french-campaign-egypt: 1798, Embabeh near Cairo: French infantry squares in blue coats and bicorne hats fire on charging Mamluk horsemen in brilliant robes and turbans, smoke drifting, the Giza pyramids on the horizon. No gore. Palm trees line the Nile behind the battle, villagers watch from mud-brick houses at a distance, and French officers on horseback direct the fire inside the squares. Painted as a late eighteenth-century European history painting, oil on canvas, warm desert light.
eg-muhammad-ali-rise: 1805, Cairo: the citadel above the city with domes and minarets, a new governor in Ottoman dress and a turban seen small from behind on a terrace overlooking soldiers drilling in European style, a cotton field and a factory chimney below. Mosque domes catch the evening light over the city. Painted in the style of an early nineteenth-century watercolour by a European traveller, soft light.
eg-french-invasion-algeria: 1830, Sidi Fredj near Algiers: French troops in blue coats and red trousers land from rowing boats on a sandy beach, warships with sails in the bay, a small white tower on a peninsula, Algerian horsemen watching from the hills. Cannon are being hauled through the sand, smoke rises from a warship's guns, and supply crates pile up on the shore under a bright June sky. Painted as a nineteenth-century French history painting, oil on canvas.
eg-suez-canal-opens: 1869, Port Said: a procession of steamships with flags and smoking funnels enters the new canal, crowds watching from the banks and pavilions, sailing ships and boats in the harbour, desert stretching beyond. A long sandy embankment edges the straight channel, Egyptian dignitaries and European guests fill a decorated grandstand, and fireworks are prepared for the evening celebration. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine lines and many small figures.
eg-british-occupation: 1882, Tel el-Kebir in the eastern Egyptian desert: British infantry in red and khaki uniforms advance at dawn across sand toward earthwork entrenchments defended by Egyptian soldiers in tarbushes, smoke from cannon, a railway and canal nearby. No gore. The pale light of sunrise spreads over the dunes, bayonets glint in long lines, and cavalry and artillery follow behind the advancing infantry across the sand. Rendered as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving.
eg-el-alamein: 1942, El Alamein in the Western Desert: a night artillery barrage lights the horizon, columns of tanks and trucks moving forward across flat sand, infantry in khaki shorts and helmets, minefields marked with tape. No gore. Searchlights sweep the sky, dust trails rise behind the vehicles, and the dark outline of a ridge stands on the horizon. Painted as a 1940s war artist's watercolour, sand tones and orange flashes.
eg-revolution-1952: 1952, Cairo: tanks and army trucks halted in a broad city square at dawn, soldiers in khaki uniforms and caps standing beside them, a crowd of Cairenes in tarbooshes, galabiyas and summer suits gathering to watch. Belle Epoque apartment buildings with iron balconies line the square, people leaning from the balconies; tram cars and horse carts wait behind the tanks. Soft summer morning light and dust in the air. One single continuous street scene, no inset, no frame, no signs or lettering. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour.
eg-algerian-war: 1954, the Aures mountains in Algeria: a rugged, rocky landscape of steep ridges and Berber villages of stone houses, small groups of fighters in djellabas with rifles moving along a path at dusk, a French army post on a distant ridge. No violence shown. Olive trees and terraced fields cling to the slopes. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, earthy browns and greys.
eg-suez-crisis: 1956, Port Said: the canal entrance seen from the waterfront, dark smoke rising over the harbour, the hulls of ships sunk in the channel to block it, and paratroopers drifting down in the far distance. Egyptian civilians and a few soldiers watch from a quay lined with arcaded colonial buildings; fishing boats sit idle at the quay. A long stone breakwater runs out into the grey water with an empty stone pedestal at its end. No gore, no statues of torch-bearing figures, no lettering. Painted as a muted 1950s documentary watercolour, grey and blue tones.
eg-tunisian-revolution: 2010, Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia: a dusty provincial town street with whitewashed buildings, an abandoned wooden fruit cart in the foreground near a government building, and further along the road a crowd gathering at a distance under an overcast December sky. No figures in close-up. Shop shutters are half closed, and a scrawny palm leans over the road. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, pale ochre and grey.
eu-stonehenge: c. 3000 BCE, Salisbury Plain, Wiltshire: Neolithic farmers in hide and woven wool garments dig a great circular ditch with red-deer antler picks, piling white chalk into a bank, while others carry baskets of earth; a ring of wooden posts marks the centre, cattle graze on the rolling green downland, and a low winter sun sets on the horizon. Painted in the manner of a modern archaeological reconstruction in watercolour, inspired by the earth tones of Neolithic chalk and grooved-ware pottery, soft light.
eu-troy-founded: c. 3000 BCE, the hill of Hisarlik near the Dardanelles: a small fortified settlement of mud-brick and stone houses with a thick stone wall and a gate on a low hill above a marshy plain, villagers in wool tunics carrying jars, fishing boats on a bay, the narrow strait and the hills of Thrace beyond. Painted in the style of an Early Bronze Age Aegean pottery painting, simple dark brown figures on a pale clay ground.
eu-bell-beaker: c. 2800 BCE, Zambujal, Portugal: a hilltop fortified settlement with round stone towers above a river valley, a potter shaping a tall bell-shaped cup decorated with bands of comb-impressed patterns, an archer with a stone wrist guard testing a bow, a smith casting a copper dagger over a small fire, pine trees and the distant Atlantic. Painted as a muted archaeological watercolour reconstruction, warm reddish earth and pale stone.
eu-knossos-palace: c. 1900 BCE, Knossos in Crete: a sprawling palace of many storeys around a great central court, red-painted downward-tapering wooden columns, light wells and painted walls, people in colourful flounced skirts and kilts carrying storage jars to magazines, horns of consecration on the roofline, olive groves and Mount Ida in the distance. Painted in the style of a Minoan fresco, vivid reds, blues and ochres, lively flowing figures.
eu-thera-eruption: c. 1600 BCE, Akrotiri on Thera: a towering column of grey and black ash rises from the volcano in the centre of the island, lightning flickering in the cloud, ash falling over the multi-storey stone houses of a harbour town, its people in boats rowing away across a darkened sea, empty streets with storage jars. No bodies. Painted in the style of the Akrotiri wall paintings, swallows and lilies in a frieze, ochres and blues.
eu-mask-of-agamemnon: c. 1550 BCE, Mycenae in the Argolid: in a circle of upright stone slabs on a rocky hillside, mourners in woollen robes lower a ruler wrapped in cloth into a deep shaft grave, a beaten gold mask over his face, bronze swords with inlaid daggers, gold cups and amber beads laid beside him, hills and olive trees behind. Painted in the style of a Mycenaean fresco, flat colour and bold outlines.
eu-mycenaeans-take-knossos: c. 1450 BCE, Knossos in Crete: Mycenaean warriors in boar's-tusk helmets and figure-of-eight shields arrive at the partly burned palace, scribes in a store room counting goods on small clay tablets of linear script rendered as indistinct marks, Minoan servants carrying jars, smoke-stained columns and a quiet central court. Painted in the style of a late Minoan-Mycenaean fresco, ochres, reds and blues.
eu-lion-gate: c. 1250 BCE, Mycenae: a massive gateway of enormous stone blocks with a huge lintel and above it a triangular relief of two standing lions facing a column, Cyclopean walls winding around the rocky citadel, a chariot drawn by two horses entering, soldiers in boar's-tusk helmets on the walls, olive trees and mountains behind. Painted in the style of a Mycenaean fresco, flat colours, bold outlines.
eu-trojan-war: c. 1200 BCE, the plain before Troy: high stone walls and towers of a citadel on a hill above a plain by the sea, a large camp of Greek ships drawn up on the beach, warriors in bronze armour, crested helmets and round shields in the distance, and a great wooden horse standing before the walls. Painted in the style of a Greek black-figure vase painting, black figures on an orange clay ground.
eu-dorian-invasion: c. 1100 BCE, Laconia: a long column of migrants in simple wool tunics and cloaks with herds of sheep and goats, ox carts and spears moving down a mountain pass into the fertile Eurotas valley, a ruined Mycenaean palace on a hill, the Taygetus mountains rising behind. Painted in the style of a Greek Geometric vase painting, black silhouettes in bands on pale clay.
eu-first-olympics: 776 BCE, Olympia in Elis: a footrace of young athletes on a simple earthen track in a green valley beside a sacred grove of olive and plane trees, spectators on the grassy slopes, an altar of Zeus with smoke rising, the river Alpheios flowing nearby. Painted in the style of a Greek black-figure vase painting, running figures in profile on an orange ground.
eu-syracuse-founded: 734 BCE, Syracuse in Sicily: Greek colonists in tunics land from wooden ships with square sails onto the island of Ortygia, carrying amphorae, tools and a sacred fire, men marking out plots, local Sicel people watching from the hills, the bright sea and sheltered harbour. Painted in the style of a Corinthian vase painting, animal friezes and figures in black and purple on cream.
eu-solon: c. 594 BCE, Athens: a bearded lawgiver in a himation addresses citizens in the open Agora, poor farmers with hoes listening, men on the hillside pulling up wooden boundary markers of mortgaged land, a rotating wooden law board standing nearby. Behind rises the rocky Acropolis with only a small archaic temple and rough walls: no Parthenon or other classical marble temples, which were built over a century later. Merchants and sailors gather round. Painted in the style of an Attic black-figure vase painting, figures in profile on orange clay. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-cleisthenes: 508 BCE, Athens: citizens in himations gather on the Pnyx hill, some scratching names on broken pottery sherds for ostracism, others dropping pebbles into clay urns, a herald on a simple stone speaker's platform. Behind them the rocky Acropolis carries only the old archaic Temple of Athena and modest early shrines: no Parthenon, no Erechtheion, no Propylaia, which did not yet exist. Grey olive trees on the slopes, mud-brick houses below. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting, orange figures on black. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-marathon: 490 BCE, the plain of Marathon in Attica: Athenian hoplites in bronze crested helmets, greaves and round shields run in a dense line toward Persian soldiers in trousers and soft caps near the beach, Persian ships at anchor in the bay, marshes and mountains around. No gore. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting, dynamic figures in profile.
eu-thermopylae: 480 BCE, Thermopylae: a narrow pass between steep mountain cliffs and the sea, a small line of Greek hoplites with red cloaks and bronze shields standing shoulder to shoulder at a rebuilt stone wall, a vast Persian army stretching far away along the coast road. No gore. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting, orange figures on black.
eu-salamis: 480 BCE, the strait of Salamis: Greek triremes with bronze rams and three banks of oars ram larger Persian ships in narrow waters, the island of Salamis on one side and the mountains of Attica on the other, a royal throne on a hillside watching. No gore. Painted in the style of a Greek black-figure vase painting, ships in a frieze on orange clay.
eu-parthenon: c. 447 BCE, the Acropolis of Athens: a marble Doric temple under construction, workers on wooden scaffolding carving the frieze, oxen hauling marble drums up a ramp, a sculptor overseeing statues in a workshop, the city and the sea below. Painters apply bright colours to the finished metopes, and citizens climb the hill to watch the work. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting, warm orange figures on black.
eu-peloponnesian-war: 431 BCE, Attica: Spartan hoplites in red cloaks and bronze helmets ravage olive groves and wheat fields outside Athens, smoke rising from farmhouses, Athenians watching from the Long Walls that run to the port of Piraeus with triremes in the harbour. No gore. Crowds of rural refugees shelter in makeshift huts between the walls, and the harbour bristles with masts. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting.
eu-socrates: 399 BCE, Athens: a simple stone prison cell lit by a small window, an old bearded man in a himation seated on a bed surrounded by grieving friends and students, a cup on a low stool, lamplight and evening shadows, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of an Attic red-figure vase painting, orange figures on a black ground.
eu-alexander-campaign: 334 BCE, the Granicus river: Macedonian cavalry with spears charge across a shallow river and up a steep bank against Persian horsemen, a young king with a white plumed helmet small in the centre, dust and water spray. No gore. Persian archers stand on the far bank, the plain stretching beyond to distant hills, and banners flutter in the wind. Painted in the style of the Alexander Mosaic from Pompeii, small stone tesserae, earth tones.
eu-first-punic-war: 241 BCE, the Aegates Islands off Sicily: Roman war galleys with corvus boarding bridges and bronze rams engage Carthaginian ships laden with supplies in a choppy sea, rocky islands on the horizon. No gore. Sails are lowered for battle, oars churn the water white, marines with shields crowd the decks, and gulls wheel above the masts under a windy spring sky. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco, dark blue sea and red-brown ships.
eu-hannibal-alps: 218 BCE, the western Alps: a long column of soldiers, horses, mules and African war elephants struggling along a narrow snowy mountain path, steep cliffs and glaciers above, Gallic tribesmen watching from rocky ridges. Soldiers in cloaks lead pack animals by the bridle, an elephant's driver urges it forward, and snow swirls in a cold wind over the pass. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco, cool whites and greys, figures small against vast mountains.
eu-cannae: 216 BCE, Cannae in Apulia: a dusty summer plain by the Aufidus river, a huge Roman army in dense ranks being slowly enclosed by Carthaginian, Spanish and Gallic infantry and Numidian cavalry, seen from far above. No gore. Dust rises from thousands of feet, the river glints on one side of the field, cavalry clash on the wings, and low hills frame the horizon under a hot sky. Painted in the style of a Roman mosaic, small tesserae, warm earth colours.
eu-pydna: 168 BCE, Pydna in Macedonia: Roman legionaries with oval shields and short swords press into gaps in the Macedonian phalanx, its long pikes tilting, the slopes of Mount Olympus in the background, a river and dust. No gore. Elephants stand at the edge of the field, cavalry wait in reserve, and the evening sun lights the dust above the struggling lines. Painted in the style of a Hellenistic relief, figures in profile, marble texture.
eu-third-punic-war: 146 BCE, Carthage, Tunisia: Roman soldiers and engineers pull down the walls of a captured harbour city, smoke rising from the Byrsa hill, the circular naval harbour empty, a plough being drawn symbolically across the scorched ground. No gore. Roman officers watch from horseback, the bay is crowded with Roman ships, and wisps of smoke drift across the empty streets toward the sea. Painted in the manner of a Roman fresco, smoky reds and dark ochres.
eu-gallic-wars: 52 BCE, Alesia in Burgundy: Roman legionaries build a double ring of wooden palisades, ditches and towers around a hilltop Gallic town, Gallic warriors with long hair and shields on the walls above, the green Burgundian hills around. Siege engines stand ready behind the earthworks, a relieving Gallic army gathers on a distant ridge, and Roman soldiers dig trenches under an overcast autumn sky. Painted in the style of a Roman relief, carved stone figures, a long horizontal frieze.
eu-rubicon: 49 BCE, the Rubicon in northern Italy: a Roman general on horseback seen from behind crosses a small river at a ford, followed by a legion with eagle standards and shields, a dawn mist over poplars and fields. Soldiers splash through the shallow water, horses tossing their heads, and a stone milestone stands by the road on the far bank. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco, soft greens and ochres.
eu-caesar-assassinated: 44 BCE, Rome: the portico of the Theatre of Pompey, a group of senators in white togas crowding around one man at the far end of a columned hall, seen from a distance, a toga fallen on the floor, a statue on a pedestal. No gore. Daggers glint faintly in the crowd. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco from Pompeii, deep red and ochre with soft modelling.
eu-augustus: 27 BCE, Rome: senators in white togas assemble in the Senate House, presenting an oak-leaf crown and a golden shield to a man in a toga seen from behind, the Forum outside with temples. Lictors with rods stand at the doors, citizens crowd the steps outside, and laurel trees frame the entrance under a bright sky. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco, warm red and ochre, figures in a frieze.
eu-crisis-third-century: 235 CE, Moguntiacum on the Rhine: a Roman legionary camp of wooden and stone buildings by a wide river, soldiers in mail with oval shields gathered in an angry crowd around a commander's tent, smoke rising on the far bank, grey sky. No gore. Merchants close their shops near the gate, and a few coins lie scattered on the ground. Painted in the style of a Late Roman mosaic, dark tones.
eu-tetrarchy: 293 CE, Nicomedia in Bithynia: four emperors in purple cloaks and military dress stand together embracing on a palace terrace, guards in mail around, the Gulf of Izmit and hills behind. Ships sail on the gulf, and clerks with scrolls wait in the colonnade behind the emperors. Painted in the style of the Porphyry Tetrarchs sculpture rendered as a Late Roman mosaic, stiff stylised figures, purple and red.
eu-milvian-bridge: 312 CE, the Milvian Bridge near Rome: an army with shields painted with a Chi-Rho symbol crosses the Tiber on a stone bridge, the river crowded with boats and a wooden pontoon collapsing, Roman soldiers on horseback, a sign of light in the sky. No gore. Banners and trumpets crowd the riverbank. Painted in the style of a Late Roman mosaic, small coloured tesserae, warm earth tones.
eu-constantinople: 330 CE, Constantinople on the Bosporus: a new city of colonnaded streets, a large forum with a porphyry column and a statue on top, a hippodrome, a palace overlooking the sea, crowds at a dedication ceremony, ships in the Golden Horn. Priests and officials process with incense, and new marble statues line the avenue. Painted in the style of a Byzantine mosaic, gold background and coloured tesserae.
eu-adrianople: 378 CE, Adrianople in Thrace: Gothic cavalry charge from the hills onto a Roman army on a dusty plain in summer heat, a circle of Gothic wagons, burning fields, Roman legionaries in mail with shields. No gore. Smoke from burning grass drifts over the field, Gothic infantry press forward from behind the wagons, and Roman standards lean and waver in the dust. Painted in the style of a Late Roman mosaic, earth colours.
eu-division-of-empire: 395 CE, Milan: in a single wide palace hall, two young emperors, Arcadius and Honorius, in purple robes and pearl diadems stand side by side at the centre on a raised marble step, seen at a distance. Courtiers in embroidered Late Roman tunics and cloaks and generals in scale armour gather on either side, turning toward one or the other brother. Tall columns and arched windows let light fall onto a patterned marble floor. One continuous scene, no panels, seams or frames, no lettering or maps with writing. Painted in the style of a Late Roman mosaic, gold and earth tones.
eu-sack-of-rome-410: 410 CE, Rome: Visigothic warriors with long hair and cloaks enter the city through the Salarian Gate at night, carrying away treasure, smoke rising over the temples and basilicas, citizens fleeing into churches. No gore. Torches light the narrow streets, carts are piled with silver vessels and fine cloth, the Colosseum looms dark in the background, and frightened families gather on the steps of a basilica. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript, flat colours.
eu-catalaunian-plains: 451 CE, the Catalaunian Plains in Champagne: Roman and Visigothic armies with shields and banners meet Hunnic horse archers on a vast flat plain, dust rising, a wagon camp in the distance. No gore. Roman standards and Visigothic banners rise above the infantry, Hunnic riders draw bows at full gallop, a low ridge rises at the centre of the field, and a red sunset glows over the plain. Painted in the style of an illuminated manuscript, flat colours and gold.
eu-sack-of-rome-455: 455 CE, Rome: Vandal ships at the mouth of the Tiber being loaded with statues, gold vessels and treasure from the city, Vandal warriors carrying bronze tiles stripped from a temple roof, the city on its hills behind. No gore. Citizens watch quietly from the city walls, a bishop in robes stands at a gate, and warriors wheel carts of loot along a paved Roman road toward the river. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript.
eu-476-fall-of-western-roman-empire: 476 CE, Ravenna: a boy emperor in purple robes seen from behind hands over his diadem and robes to a Germanic general with long hair and a fur cloak, in a palace hall with mosaics on the walls, soldiers in mail around. Courtiers lower their eyes, and a lamp burns before an empty throne. Painted in the style of a Byzantine mosaic from Ravenna, gold ground.
eu-496-baptism-of-clovis: 496 CE, Reims: a Frankish king with long hair kneels in a baptismal font in a stone church, a bishop pouring water from a vessel, Frankish warriors in cloaks watching, candles and incense. The scene is seen from the back of the nave, with the figures small, coloured light falling from high windows, monks singing, and a dove descending above the font. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript, gold leaf and bright pigments.
eu-732-battle-of-tours: 732, between Tours and Poitiers: Frankish infantry in a dense shield wall with axes and spears stand on a wooded rise while Umayyad cavalry in mail and turbans charge from the plain, banners flying. No gore. Autumn leaves blow across the field, Frankish nobles on horseback wait behind the infantry, and the Roman road to Tours runs in the distance past forests and small fields. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript, flat colours.
eu-793-lindisfarne-raid: 793, Lindisfarne off the Northumbrian coast: Viking longships with square sails beached on the sand of a small island, Norse raiders with axes carrying chests from a stone monastery, monks fleeing across the tidal flats, grey sea. No gore. Seabirds wheel over the dunes, and a stone cross stands on the shore. Painted in the style of an insular illuminated manuscript like the Lindisfarne Gospels.
eu-800-charlemagne-crowned: 800, Rome: in the basilica of Old St Peter's on Christmas Day, a tall king in a cloak kneels at the altar while a pope places a crown on his head, clergy and Frankish nobles around, mosaics and candlelight. The figures are seen small from the back of the crowded basilica, lamps hanging from the beams. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript, gold leaf and lapis.
eu-843-treaty-of-verdun: 843, Verdun: Lothair, Louis the German and Charles the Bald, three Carolingian kings in simple gold circlet crowns and long tunics with cloaks, sit at a table with a large parchment, bishops in early medieval vestments and Frankish nobles standing around, clerks with quills copying. Through a round Romanesque arch the old Roman stone walls of Verdun and the river Meuse are visible, horses waiting. Plain cloth pennants and crosses only: no heraldic coats of arms, no fleur-de-lis or English lions, no Gothic spires. Painted as a Carolingian illuminated manuscript, gold and purple. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-sarazm: Around 3000 BCE, Sarazm in the green Zeravshan valley: a cluster of mud-brick houses with flat roofs and courtyards on a terrace above the river, poplar trees and snowy mountains behind; villagers in simple woven wool tunics weigh lumps of blue turquoise and greenish copper ore beside a small clay furnace, while a trader unloads leather bundles from a pack donkey. Afternoon light, dusty fields. Painted in an ochre, umber and turquoise palette inspired by ancient Central Asian painted pottery and rock art. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-karasuk: Around 1500 BCE, the Minusinsk Basin of southern Siberia: a grassy steppe valley beside the Yenisei with low birch-bark and felt huts, cattle and sheep grazing; a bronze-smith in a fur-trimmed leather tunic kneels by a small charcoal fire, pouring molten bronze into a stone mould, finished curved bronze knives with animal-head handles laid out on a hide beside him, a few herders watching. Clear morning light. Rendered in the spirit of steppe bronze-age art, rock-carving outlines and warm earthen palette like Scythian-style animal ornament. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-yaz: Around 1500 BCE, Yaz-Depe in the Margiana oasis: a raised mud-brick citadel on a high platform overlooks green irrigated fields cut by straight canals, farmers in plain wool robes digging a channel with wooden hoes, tamarisk bushes and desert sand at the edges of the oasis, a small fire altar smoking on the citadel wall. Low evening sun, long shadows. Painted in a muted earthen palette in the manner of ancient Central Asian wall painting, flat colour and dark outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-li-bai: 701 CE, Suyab in the Chu valley: a Tang garrison town with rammed-earth walls and a gate tower, Sogdian merchants' houses and a caravanserai outside, Bactrian camels resting; in a courtyard, a small family group in Tang round-collared robes and Sogdian caftans gathers by a doorway at dawn, a newborn swaddled in silk held by a woman seen from behind, the snow-capped Tian Shan behind the town. Painted in the style of a Sogdian mural from Panjakent mixed with Tang mineral colours, lapis blue and ochre. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-muqanna: Around 776 CE, the mountains near Kesh in Sogdiana: a fortified hilltop castle of mud brick on a rocky crag, its walls lined with Sogdian villagers and Turkic warriors in white garments, banners fluttering; far below in the valley, a column of Abbasid soldiers in black with lances and round shields approaches along a stream between orchards. Seen from a distance at dusk, no fighting shown up close. Painted as a Persian miniature, bright mineral colours, gold sky, stylised rocks. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-kutadgu-bilig: 1069, Kashgar: inside a Kara-Khanid palace hall with carved wooden pillars and woven carpets, a scholar in a turban and long caftan, seen from behind and small in the scene, kneels before an enthroned Turkic ruler in fur-trimmed robes and offers a bound manuscript; courtiers and guards line the walls, a window shows the oasis city's domes and poplars. Warm lamplight. Painted in the style of a Persian-Turkic miniature, rich blues, reds and gold, flat perspective, decorative borders without writing. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-kalyan: Bukhara in 1127, a period miniature-style painting: Kara-Khanid builders on wooden scaffolding finish the top of the tall round Kalyan Minaret. It is made of plain tan baked brick laid in decorative bands, with a single narrow band of turquoise glaze near the top. Around it stand low flat-roofed mud-brick houses and an old brick mosque with plain brick arches and wooden columns. There are no blue-tiled domes, no tiled portals and no later Timurid or Shaybanid buildings. Merchants in robes and turbans lead camels through a dusty market below. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-western-liao: 1132, Balasagun in the Chu valley: a Khitan encampment of large felt yurts and banners on the plain outside a walled Central Asian city with mud-brick walls; Khitan horsemen with shaved crowns and side-locks, in round-collared robes, ride in through the gate escorting a prince on a white horse, local Turkic townsfolk watching from the walls, the snowy Tian Shan behind. Painted in the style of a Liao-Yuan handscroll of steppe riders, ink and light colour on silk, fine brushwork. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-yasawi: 1166, Yasi on the Kazakh steppe: in a simple mud-brick courtyard beside a small domed khanqah, an elderly Sufi in a plain wool cloak and tall felt cap, seen from behind, recites to a seated circle of Turkic nomads in sheepskin coats and felt hats; horses tethered nearby, yurts and open steppe stretching to the horizon at sunset. Quiet devotional mood. Painted in the manner of a Timurid Persian miniature, delicate figures, lapis and gold palette, flat decorative ground. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-bibi-khanym: 1399, Samarkand: the vast Bibi-Khanym Mosque under construction, its great portal and turquoise-tiled dome rising behind wooden scaffolding; hundreds of craftsmen in turbans and caftans carry bricks and glazed tiles, and a line of Indian elephants hauls marble blocks across the dusty courtyard, poplars and city walls beyond. Bright midday sun. Painted as a Timurid Persian miniature in the style of Bihzad's workshop, crowded small figures, rich blues and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-marv-1510: 1510, the plain outside Merv: a great battle seen from a distance, Safavid horsemen in red-tipped turbans (the Qizilbash) charging with lances and curved swords against Uzbek cavalry under horsetail standards, clouds of dust rising, the walls of Merv and mud-brick towers on the horizon, a river glinting. No close-up violence. Painted as a Safavid Persian miniature, vivid reds, blues and gold, stylised hills, many small figures in ordered ranks. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-khiva: 1511, Khwarezm: Uzbek horsemen in quilted caftans and fur hats ride across flat irrigated land toward the mud-brick walls of a desert oasis town, canals and mulberry trees lining the road, townsfolk opening the gates; behind them the sandy Kyzylkum desert under a hazy sky. Calm late afternoon. Painted in the style of a Shaybanid Bukhara-school miniature, clear outlines, ochre, green and lapis colours, gold sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-sher-dor: 1619, the Registan square in Samarkand: the newly finished Sher-Dor Madrasa with its huge portal decorated in glazed tile mosaics of striped tigers chasing deer beneath a rising sun with a face, twin fluted turquoise domes on either side; opposite stands the older madrasa of Ulugh Beg, while merchants, students in turbans and camels cross the open square. Bright morning light. Painted as an Uzbek-Persian miniature, intense blues, ochres and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-zhety-zhargy: 1680, the steppe near Turkestan: a large gathering of Kazakh clan elders in fur-trimmed robes and tall felt hats seated in a wide circle on carpets before a great white yurt, a khan seated at the head, small in the scene, with elders speaking and a scribe beside him; horses tethered, flocks and the domed shrine of Turkestan on the horizon. Golden evening light. Painted in the style of a late Persian-Central Asian miniature, warm earth tones and soft blues. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-kokand: 1709, the Ferghana valley: a small walled town of mud-brick with a modest fortress gate amid orchards, cotton and mulberry fields, mountains around the valley; Uzbek tribal horsemen in striped quilted robes and turbans gather outside the gate with banners while townspeople greet them, carts and donkeys on the road. Spring morning light. Painted as a Central Asian miniature in the Bukhara school manner, flat bright colours, gold sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-manghit: 1785, Bukhara: the massive sloping mud-brick walls of the Ark citadel with its gate between two towers, a crowd of townspeople, mullahs in white turbans and soldiers in striped caftans gathered on the square below as a procession of court officials enters; the Kalyan Minaret and blue domes rise over the city. Clear afternoon light. Painted in the style of a late Bukhara miniature, detailed small figures, ochre, turquoise and lapis tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-kenesary: 1837, the open Kazakh steppe: a large band of Kazakh horsemen in quilted chapan coats and fox-fur hats, carrying lances, muskets and banners, gathers on a ridge; in the distance a small Russian wooden fort with a palisade and a watchtower stands by a river, smoke rising from its chimneys. Vast grass, wide sky, autumn colours. Painted as a nineteenth-century documentary watercolour of the steppe, soft washes, fine pen detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-verny: 1854, at the foot of the Zailiysky Alatau: Russian soldiers in white tunics and peaked caps and Cossacks build a small earthen and timber fort, raising log walls and a wooden gate; carts of timber, tents and grazing horses around, apple orchards and Kazakh yurts nearby, snowy Tian Shan peaks behind. Bright summer day. Painted as a mid-nineteenth-century Russian topographical watercolour, clear light, fine detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-turkestan-gg: 1867, Tashkent: a Russian administrative compound with a whitewashed building, columned porch and the imperial eagle flag on its roof, set beside the flat mud-brick houses, poplars and canals of the old city; Russian officers in white tunics stand with local notables in turbans and striped robes on the steps, carts and camels in the dusty street. Afternoon light. Painted as a nineteenth-century Russian documentary oil sketch, warm dusty palette. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-bukhara-protectorate: 1868, Samarkand: Russian infantry in white tunics and kepi caps march in column across the Registan square past the great tiled madrasas, a few Russian officers on horseback, townspeople in turbans and robes watching from the edges and from shop fronts; a faint haze of dust, the turquoise domes above. No fighting shown. Painted in the style of a nineteenth-century Russian history painting, realistic oil, bright Central Asian sun. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-transcaspian-railway: 1888, Samarkand: a small steam locomotive with a tall funnel pulls wooden carriages into a new single-storey railway station on the edge of the city, Russian railwaymen in caps beside it, local Uzbek men in turbans and striped robes and a line of camels watching; bales of cotton stacked on the platform, the blue domes of Samarkand on the horizon. Clear afternoon. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated-newspaper engraving, fine cross-hatched lines, lightly tinted. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-abai: 1890, the steppe near Semey: inside a Kazakh felt yurt with its wooden lattice walls, embroidered hangings and a low table, an older Kazakh man in a dark robe and skullcap, seen from behind and small, writes by lamplight in a notebook, a dombra lute hanging on the wall; through the open door, horses grazing on the evening steppe. Quiet, reflective mood. Painted as a late-nineteenth-century watercolour, warm lamplight, soft washes. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-jadids: 1905, Samarkand: a new-method school room in a mud-brick building with wooden desks and a blackboard, boys in skullcaps and striped robes sitting on benches with slates and printed primers, a teacher in a turban and European-style jacket standing by a globe; through the window, the domes of the city. Morning light streams in. Painted as an early-twentieth-century documentary watercolour, gentle tones, fine pencil drawing. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-alash: 1917, Semey: in a modest hall with wooden floors and tall windows, a crowded congress of Kazakh delegates in a mix of European suits and traditional robes with fur hats sit on benches, a speaker at the front seen from behind; snow outside the windows, the onion dome of a church and the Irtysh river beyond. Dim winter light. Rendered as a Soviet-era-style woodcut print, bold black lines, muted ochre and grey tints. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-basmachi: Around 1918, the Ferghana valley: a band of Uzbek and Kyrgyz horsemen in quilted chapan robes and turbans, carrying old rifles, rides along a mountain path above a green valley of orchards and poplar-lined villages, snow peaks behind; seen from a distance, dust trailing. Grim but calm mood. Painted as an early-twentieth-century documentary watercolour, earthy greens and browns. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-kokand-autonomy: February 1918, Kokand: seen from a distance across snowy fields, columns of dark smoke rise over the flat roofs and domes of the old city, a few figures on horseback and on foot hurrying along the road away from the town; leafless poplars and a grey winter sky. No close-up violence. Rendered as a stark Russian Civil War-era woodcut print, black and white with a smoky grey tone. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-bukhara-1920: 1920, Bukhara: seen from a distance, Red Army soldiers in long greatcoats and pointed budenovka caps advance across open ground toward the great sloping walls of the Ark citadel, smoke rising over the city and the Kalyan Minaret standing above; an old biplane circles overhead. No close-up violence. Painted as an early Soviet documentary watercolour sketch, dusty ochres and greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-hujum: 1927, Tashkent: a large crowd of Uzbek women gathered on an open square on a spring day, some throwing dark horsehair veils and long robes onto a bonfire on a platform, others watching uncertainly; men in skullcaps standing at the edges, red banners without writing, flat-roofed buildings and poplars around. Seen from a distance, tense and serious mood. Rendered as a 1920s woodcut print, bold lines, black with muted red. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-koreans: Autumn 1937, a bare steppe near Ushtobe: a long freight train of wooden boxcars halted on a lonely track, Korean families in padded coats climbing down with bundles, pots and small children onto the dry grass, a few mud-brick huts and dugouts in the distance, a grey sky over the empty plain. Somber, quiet mood. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, browns and greys, soft washes. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-rds1: 29 August 1949, the Semipalatinsk test site: a tall steel tower stands alone on a flat empty steppe, seen from very far away as a bright flash and a rising mushroom cloud glow on the horizon at dawn; in the foreground a low concrete observation bunker and a few distant Kazakh yurts and horses on the grass. Eerie, quiet light. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, dusty yellows and greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-virgin-lands: 1954, the northern Kazakh steppe: a long line of tractors pulling ploughs turns the endless grassland into dark furrows under a huge sky, young settlers in work clothes and caps standing beside a row of canvas tents and a wooden barracks, a water truck nearby. Bright spring morning, wind in the grass. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, broad earth tones, not propaganda. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-sputnik: October 1957, Baikonur on the flat Kazakh steppe at night: an R-7 rocket lifts off from its launch pad in a bright plume of flame and smoke, the steel support arms falling back, floodlights and low concrete buildings around, a few engineers in coats watching from far away; dark sky with stars. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, deep blues and orange glow. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-gagarin: 12 April 1961, Baikonur: the white Vostok rocket stands on the launch pad on the flat spring steppe at dawn, wrapped in service towers, vapour drifting from its sides; a tiny figure in an orange spacesuit and white helmet, seen from behind, walks toward the lift with a small group of technicians. Clear pale sky. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft greys, white and orange. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-jeltoqsan: December 1986, Almaty: a wide snowy central square in front of a large modernist administrative building, a crowd of young people in winter coats and hats gathered quietly at a distance, lines of police vehicles parked along the edge, the snow-covered mountains above the city in grey winter light. Calm, sombre mood, seen from far away. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, cool greys and blues. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-alma-ata-protocol: December 1991, Alma-Ata: a long conference table in a plain modern hall with tall curtained windows, small flags on the table without emblems legible, delegates in dark suits seen from behind and at a distance, papers and microphones before them; outside the windows, snow and the mountains above the city. Formal, quiet mood. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, neutral tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-tajik-civil-war: 1992, the outskirts of Dushanbe: seen from a hillside, a quiet valley of poplars and flat-roofed houses with a thin column of smoke rising in the distance, families with bundles and a donkey cart walking along a dusty road toward the mountains, an abandoned truck beside the road. Sombre autumn light. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft browns and greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-astana: 1997, Akmola on the northern Kazakh steppe: a modest Soviet-era town of low apartment blocks beside the Ishim river, with construction cranes and the steel frames of new government buildings rising on the open grassland across the water, trucks moving earth; wide sky with clouds. Bright summer day. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, open washes, pale greens and blues. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-andijan-2005: May 2005, Andijan: a broad city square with a fountain and Soviet-era administrative buildings, seen from far above, a large crowd gathered at a distance and a line of military trucks parked along a side street; poplars and the Ferghana mountains faint beyond. Tense, quiet atmosphere, no violence shown. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, greys and dusty greens. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-tulip: March 2005, Bishkek: a large crowd of protesters in spring coats, some holding pink and yellow flags without writing, gathered at a distance in a wide square before a large white government building, snowy mountains behind the city and bare trees just budding. Seen from far away, no individual faces. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, soft colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-silk-road-economic-belt: 2013, Astana: the exterior of a modern university campus on the steppe, glass and stone buildings around a broad plaza, students walking; beyond the city an old caravan route is suggested by a long freight train of containers crossing the open grassland toward the horizon. No people shown in detail. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, cool clear light, neutral tone. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-mirziyoyev: Around 2017, Tashkent: a bustling street near the Chorsu bazaar with its large blue dome, shoppers and traders at stalls of melons, bread and spices, small currency exchange kiosks and a bus passing; new construction cranes on the skyline. Ordinary people at a distance, no recognisable faces. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, warm everyday colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ca-kazakh-unrest-2022: January 2022, Almaty: a snowy city square seen from far away at dusk, with a large administrative building, a scattering of people in winter coats at a distance and military trucks parked along the avenue, faint smoke in the cold air and the snowy mountains above the city. Quiet, tense mood, no violence shown. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, cold blues and greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-khasekhemwy: Around 2690 BCE, Hierakonpolis in Upper Egypt: a great mud-brick enclosure with niched walls on the edge of the desert above the Nile, priests in white linen kilts carrying offerings toward a shrine, a standard topped with a falcon and another with the Seth animal raised side by side; palm groves and the river beyond. Bright sun. Painted in the style of an Egyptian tomb painting, flat colours, profile figures on an ochre ground. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-great-sphinx: Around 2500 BCE, Giza: workers in linen kilts with copper chisels and wooden mallets carve a vast lion with a royal head out of the yellow limestone bedrock, wooden scaffolds against its flank, overseers watching; the pyramid of Khafre rises behind under construction, sledges of stone and ramps nearby. Bright desert sun. Painted in the style of an Egyptian tomb painting, flat ochre and blue, profile figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-rhind-papyrus: Around 1560 BCE, Thebes: a scribe in a white linen kilt sits cross-legged on a mat in a shaded courtyard, a papyrus roll spread across his lap, writing with a reed pen from a palette of red and black ink, simple geometric drawings of triangles and grain measures on the sheet; columns, palm trees and a sunlit garden pool beyond. Painted in the style of an Egyptian papyrus illustration, flat colours, fine black outline. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-cyrene-founded: Around 631 BCE, the coast of Cyrenaica: Greek colonists in chitons and cloaks climb from small oared ships beached on the shore up a green limestone plateau, carrying amphorae and tools, a spring flowing from the rocks above; a few marking out the first walls of a new city, the blue Mediterranean behind. Painted in the style of Greek black-figure vase painting, black silhouettes on terracotta orange. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-antony-monasticism: Around 270 CE, the Eastern Desert of Egypt: an aged hermit in a coarse brown tunic and cloak, small in the scene, sits at the mouth of a cave in a rocky mountain, a basket of palm leaves at his side, a spring and a few date palms below; vast barren cliffs and golden desert all around. Quiet dawn light. Painted in the style of a Coptic Christian icon or wall painting, flat colours, simple forms. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-last-hieroglyph: 394 CE, Philae on the Nile near Aswan: the temple of Isis with its great pylon gateway and carved columns on its island, a lone priest in white linen carving small figures into the stone of a gateway by lamplight, palms and granite rocks along the river, a felucca drifting past at dusk. Quiet, elegiac mood. Painted in the manner of a Roman-era Egyptian tomb painting, faded ochres and blues. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-chalcedon-coptic-schism: 451 CE, Chalcedon on the Bosporus: a great basilica church interior with marble columns and an apse mosaic, rows of bishops in white and gold vestments seated on benches, imperial officials in silk at the front, a Gospel book on a central throne; across the water through an open door, the walls of Constantinople. Painted in the style of a Byzantine mosaic, gold ground and coloured tesserae. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-fustat-founded: 641 CE, beside the Nile: an Arab army camp of tents grows into a settlement of mud-brick houses, a simple mosque of palm trunks and mud walls with a palm-frond roof at its centre where men gather to pray; the Roman fortress of Babylon and the river behind, camels and date palms. Clear morning light. Painted in the style of an early Islamic manuscript illustration, flat colours, gold accents. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-berber-revolt: 740 CE, the hills behind Tangier: a great gathering of Berber tribesmen in hooded woollen burnouses and turbans, with spears, round leather shields and horses, assembles on a rocky slope under plain banners; below, the small walled port town of Tangier and the Strait with the coast of Spain faint across the water. Seen from a distance, windy daylight. Painted in the style of a medieval Islamic manuscript illustration, flat colours, ochre hills, gold accents. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-idrisid-dynasty: 788 CE, Volubilis in Morocco: among the ruined Roman columns and arches of the old city on a green plain, Berber tribal chiefs in wool burnouses gather around a newly arrived Arab nobleman in a white turban and cloak, small in the scene, seen from behind, pledging allegiance with raised hands; olive groves and the Zerhoun hills behind. Spring light. Painted in the style of a Maghrebi Islamic manuscript illustration, flat colours, fine outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-tulunid-dynasty: Around 876 CE, al-Qata'i near Fustat: the great Mosque of Ibn Tulun under construction, a vast courtyard ringed by arcades of brick piers with pointed arches, a minaret with an outer spiral stair rising at one side; workers carry bricks and stucco, a governor's escort of Turkish soldiers in caftans passes, the Nile and Fustat beyond. Golden afternoon light. Painted as an Abbasid-era Islamic manuscript illustration, ochre and lapis palette. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-ikhshidid-dynasty: Around 940 CE, Fustat on the Nile: a riverside palace with arched windows and gardens of palms, an audience courtyard where an official in a black Abbasid robe receives ministers and Nubian guards; boats with lateen sails crowd the river below and the walls of the old Roman fortress stand nearby. Warm evening light. Painted in the style of an early Islamic manuscript painting, flat bright colours, gold sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-al-azhar: 972 CE, the new Fatimid city of Cairo: the freshly built al-Azhar Mosque, a courtyard surrounded by arcades of keel-shaped arches on marble columns, carved stucco decoration, worshippers in white robes and turbans gathering for Friday prayer, scholars seated with students in the shade of the prayer hall. Clear morning light. Painted in the style of a medieval Islamic manuscript illustration, fine line, ochre, lapis and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-ibn-al-haytham-optics: Around 1011, Cairo: a dark room in a stone house where a single beam of sunlight passes through a small hole in a shutter and casts an inverted image of the street outside on the opposite wall; a scholar in a turban and robe, small and seen from behind, sits on a carpet beside lamps, lenses and manuscripts, observing. Dim, dramatic light. Painted in the style of a medieval Islamic scientific manuscript illustration, warm tones, gold accents. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-banu-hilal: 1057, the plains of Ifriqiya near Kairouan: a long column of Arab Bedouin tribes on the move, camels laden with black goat-hair tents, families, flocks of sheep and riders with long spears, crossing dry grassland; in the distance smoke rises over the walls and minaret of Kairouan. No close-up violence. Painted in the style of a medieval Arabic manuscript illustration of the Maqamat, flat colours, gold sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-marrakesh-founded: 1070, the plain of Marrakesh: Almoravid Saharan Berbers with veiled faces in indigo litham and robes set up a camp of tents and begin building mud walls and a modest fortress on the flat red plain, camels and date palms around, the snowy High Atlas on the horizon. Bright clear day. Painted in the style of a Maghrebi Islamic manuscript illustration, red ochre, indigo and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-almohads-take-marrakesh: 1147, Marrakesh: seen from a distance, the red rammed-earth walls of the city surrounded by Almohad troops with white banners, tents and siege ladders, horsemen in turbans and Berber footsoldiers ringing the walls, smoke rising inside the city, palm groves and the snow-capped Atlas mountains behind. No close-up violence. Painted in the style of a medieval Islamic manuscript illustration, flat colours, stylised hills. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-hafsid-dynasty: Around 1229, Tunis: the kasbah citadel on a hill above the white-walled medina, the minaret of the Zaytuna mosque rising among flat roofs, a ruler's procession with white banners and drummers entering the citadel gate, courtiers in turbans and soldiers in mail lining the way; the lagoon and sea beyond. Bright Mediterranean light. Painted in the style of a medieval Andalusi-Maghrebi manuscript illustration, flat colours and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-mansa-musa-cairo: Cairo in 1324, a period miniature-style painting: Mansa Musa of Mali in rich robes under a gold parasol rides into Cairo, followed by a long caravan of camels carrying gold and by attendants with gold staffs. The skyline is Mamluk: tiered stone minarets with balconies, ribbed or carved stone domes, the Ibn Tulun mosque and the medieval Citadel of Saladin with plain walls. There are no Ottoman pencil minarets and no Muhammad Ali Mosque. Crowds of Cairenes in turbans watch. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-ibn-battuta: 1325, Tangier: a young traveller in a white turban and travelling cloak, seen from behind, rides a donkey out through the town gate onto a dusty road leading east, a small bundle of belongings and a waterskin tied to the saddle; whitewashed houses and minaret behind him, the blue Strait of Gibraltar to one side. Bright morning light. Painted in the style of a Maqamat manuscript illustration of al-Wasiti, flat colours, gold background. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-black-death-cairo: 1348, Cairo: a nearly empty street of tall stone houses with wooden mashrabiya windows, closed shop shutters, a few mourners in dark robes walking slowly behind a covered bier toward a cemetery of domed tombs, the Citadel faint in the haze. Silent, sombre mood, no bodies shown. Painted in the style of a Mamluk-era manuscript illustration, muted ochres and greys, gold sky dimmed. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-ceuta-captured: 1415, Ceuta: a Portuguese fleet of carracks and galleys with square sails painted with crosses anchored in the bay, boats ferrying armoured knights ashore, the walled Moroccan port town on its narrow peninsula with mosque towers, smoke rising over the walls, Mount Hacho behind. Seen from a distance, no close-up violence. Painted in the style of a fifteenth-century illuminated manuscript, bright colours, gold details. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-regency-of-algiers: 1529, Algiers: Ottoman corsair galleys with oars and lateen sails surround the small Spanish fort of the Peñón on its rocky islet in the harbour, cannon smoke drifting, the whitewashed town climbing the hillside behind with its kasbah and minarets. Seen from a distance across the bay. Painted in the style of an Ottoman miniature in the manner of Matrakçı Nasuh, bird's-eye view, bright flat colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-conquest-of-tunis-1535: 1535, the bay of Tunis: a great Habsburg fleet of galleys and carracks with striped sails lies offshore, Spanish and German troops with pikes and arquebuses land on the beach beneath the fortress of La Goulette, smoke rising from cannon, the white city of Tunis across the lagoon. Seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century Flemish tapestry cartoon, rich colour, panoramic bird's-eye view. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-battle-of-alcacer-quibir: 1578, the plain near Ksar el-Kebir: seen from a hilltop, a Portuguese army in steel armour and morions with pikes and banners is surrounded by masses of Moroccan horsemen and musketeers in turbans and white robes, dust and smoke clouds over the dry fields, a river winding nearby. No close-up violence. Painted in the style of a late sixteenth-century European battle engraving, hand-coloured, panoramic. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-alaouite-dynasty: Fez in 1666, a period painting: Moulay al-Rashid's horsemen in white burnouses with long muskets and green and red banners ride into Fez through an old Marinid city gate of plain ochre stone with a horseshoe arch and battlements. There is no blue-tiled gate, because the Bab Bou Jeloud did not yet exist. Behind the gate stand the green-tiled roofs of the Qarawiyyin and square Maghrebi minarets above white and ochre houses, and townspeople in djellabas line the walls. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-rosetta-stone-found: 1799, near Rashid in the Nile delta: French soldiers in blue coats and bicorne hats digging foundations for a fort pause around a large dark granite slab partly covered by rubble, an officer and a scholar in civilian dress kneeling to look closely, palm trees and the old mud-brick fort walls nearby. Bright hazy sun. Painted as an early-nineteenth-century engraving, hand-coloured, fine cross-hatching. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-muhammad-ali-reforms: Cairo around 1820, an early 19th-century oil painting: a new state cotton mill of stone with tall brick chimneys by a Nile canal, where workers carry bales of cotton. Conscript soldiers of Muhammad Ali's new army march past in European-style short jackets and red tarbushes with muskets. Behind them rises the medieval Citadel with its Mamluk walls and older minarets, but without the large Ottoman domed Muhammad Ali Mosque, which had not yet been built. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-champollion: 1822, Paris: a small scholar's study in a tall apartment, books and papers piled everywhere, plaster casts and engraved copies of Egyptian inscriptions pinned to the walls, a young man in a dark coat, seen from behind, leaning over a table covered in drawings of hieroglyphs and a large print of a stone tablet; candlelight and Paris rooftops through the window. Painted as an early-nineteenth-century French interior oil painting, warm intimate light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-abd-al-qadir: 1832, the plain of Eghris near Mascara: a great gathering of Algerian tribal horsemen in white burnouses with long muskets and green banners stands before a tent beneath a large tree, a young leader in a white cloak, small and seen from behind, receiving their pledge; the town of Mascara and hills behind. Bright midday light. Painted as a nineteenth-century French documentary oil painting, warm desert tones, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-urabi-revolt: September 1881, Abdeen Palace square in Cairo: ranks of Egyptian soldiers in white uniforms and red tarbushes drawn up in the broad square before the long European-style palace façade, an officer on horseback, small, facing the palace, a crowd of onlookers behind; palms and gas lamps. Bright midday sun. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated-newspaper engraving, fine lines, light hand-colouring. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-treaty-of-bardo: May 1881, Bardo palace near Tunis: French troops in blue coats and red trousers stand in the courtyard of an ornate Tunisian palace with horseshoe arches and tiled walls, while in an open hall beyond French officers in kepis and the Bey's courtiers in tall red chechia caps sit at a table with papers. Seen from a distance. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated-newspaper engraving, cross-hatched, lightly coloured. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-italo-turkish-war: 1911, the coast at Tripoli: Italian warships with grey hulls and smoke stacks anchored offshore, soldiers in grey-green uniforms landing by boat on the beach before the white walls and minarets of the old city, and a small early monoplane flying over the palm oasis beyond. Seen from a distance, hazy daylight. Painted as an early-twentieth-century illustrated-magazine colour lithograph, flat bright tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-treaty-of-fez: 1912, Fez: in a palace courtyard with green-tiled roofs, carved cedar wood and a fountain, French officials in dark suits and uniforms sit at a table with documents opposite Moroccan court dignitaries in white djellabas and turbans; French soldiers in blue stand at the gate, the medina's rooftops and minarets beyond. Seen from a distance. Painted as an early-twentieth-century documentary watercolour, soft warm light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-egyptian-revolution-1919: March 1919, Cairo: a great crowd of Egyptian men in tarbushes and galabiyas and women in black veils march together down a broad street lined with European-style buildings, carrying green flags showing a crescent and a cross, students and clerics side by side; British soldiers in khaki watching from a distance. Painted as a 1920s Egyptian lithograph illustration, bold forms, warm palette. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-rif-war: 1921, the Rif mountains near Annual: seen from a high ridge, Berber fighters in brown djellabas with rifles take cover among rocks and pines above a valley where a long column of Spanish soldiers in khaki and dust-covered supply mules is strung out along a winding road toward a hilltop outpost. No close-up violence. Painted as a 1920s documentary watercolour, dry ochres and dark greens. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-egyptian-independence: 1922, Cairo: a festive view along the Nile corniche with crowds of Egyptians in tarbushes and suits, green flags with a crescent and stars hung from balconies of European-style buildings, a horse-drawn royal carriage with an escort of cavalry passing in the distance, feluccas on the river. Bright spring day. Painted as a 1920s Egyptian lithograph illustration, soft greens and creams. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-tutankhamun-tomb: November 1922, the Valley of the Kings: by candlelight, a small group of archaeologists in 1920s suits, seen from behind, peer through an opening in a sealed doorway at the bottom of rock-cut steps into a dark chamber glinting with gilded couches, statues of guardians, chariots and boxes; Egyptian workmen with lamps behind them. Painted as a 1920s illustrated-magazine watercolour, golden light against deep shadow. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eg-muslim-brotherhood: 1928, Ismailia on the Suez Canal: a modest café and a small mosque in a quiet street of low houses with balconies, a group of young Egyptian men in tarbushes and plain suits sitting together listening to a teacher, seen from behind; a canal ship with funnels visible over the rooftops. Evening light. Painted as a 1920s documentary watercolour, warm muted tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
