Painted as an Italian Renaissance oil painting, soft sfumato light, warm earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1513-the-prince: 1513, near Florence: in the evening, a lean man in a long dark red gown, seen from behind, writes at a wooden desk in the study of a stone farmhouse, a pile of classical books open beside him, a candle, a window looking out over vineyards and olive groves toward the distant dome of Florence Cathedral. Painted in the style of an Italian High Renaissance oil painting, warm chiaroscuro, deep reds and browns. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1519-magellan-expedition: 1519, Sanlúcar de Barrameda: at the mouth of the Guadalquivir river, five carracks and naos with square sails painted with crosses set out to sea under a morning sky, sailors climbing the rigging, small boats ferrying supplies, townspeople and friars watching from the sandy shore with whitewashed houses and a castle on the hill. Painted as a sixteenth-century Spanish oil painting or a Flemish marine picture, fine rigging detail, golden light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1524-german-peasants-war: 1524, Thuringia near Mühlhausen: a large band of German peasants in smocks, hose and floppy caps march across a hilly field carrying scythes, flails, pikes and a banner with a laced peasant shoe, a preacher among them; a walled town with steep roofs and church towers in the valley behind, and a lord's castle on a hill. Seen from a distance. Rendered as a German Renaissance woodcut in the manner of Dürer's circle, black line with light hand colouring. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1526-battle-of-mohacs: 1526, Mohacs: seen from a low hill at a great distance, a huge Ottoman army with Janissaries in tall white caps, rows of cannon, crescent standards and cavalry spreads across a marshy plain by the Danube, facing a much smaller Hungarian army of armoured knights in a line under red-and-white banners; artillery smoke drifting over the field. On the horizon only a small Hungarian town with a Gothic church tower and timber houses, no minarets and no mosque domes. No blood. Painted in the style of an Ottoman miniature from the Suleymanname, bright flat colours, gold sky, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1536-calvin-geneva: 1536, Geneva: in the plain stone interior of Saint Pierre cathedral, its walls whitewashed and stripped of images, a thin bearded preacher in a black gown and cap speaks from a high pulpit to a large congregation of townspeople in sober dark clothes, a printed book on the lectern; through the windows Lake Geneva and the Alps. Seen from the back. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century Swiss or Netherlandish oil painting, muted blacks and greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1543-de-revolutionibus: 1543, Nuremberg: in a printer's workshop with timber beams, journeymen in aprons work a wooden screw press, sheets with circular diagrams of the planets around a central sun hung up to dry, a printer inspecting a fresh page, cases of metal type, an armillary sphere on a shelf; through the window the steep roofs of Nuremberg. No telescopes. Rendered as a German Renaissance woodcut with light hand colouring, crisp black line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1547-ivan-the-terrible: 1547, Moscow: inside the Dormition Cathedral of the Kremlin, walls covered with gold-ground frescoes and icons, a metropolitan in a jewelled mitre places a fur-trimmed cap crown on a young man in gold brocade robes, boyars in tall fur hats and long caftans standing in rows, candles and incense smoke. Seen from far off, figures small. Painted in the style of a Russian illuminated chronicle miniature, gold, cinnabar and green. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1555-peace-of-augsburg: 1555, Augsburg: in a large oak-lined town hall chamber, princes and envoys of the Imperial Diet in fur-trimmed gowns, slashed doublets and flat caps sit along long tables, Catholic bishops on one side and Lutheran princes on the other, a clerk reading from a sealed document; through tall windows the gabled houses and onion domes of Augsburg. Painted in the style of a German Renaissance oil painting, precise detail, rich blacks and reds. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1568-eighty-years-war: 1568, Heiligerlee in Groningen: on flat marshy farmland under a vast cloudy Dutch sky, a rebel army of Dutch foot soldiers with pikes and arquebuses and orange sashes advances toward lines of Spanish tercios in morion helmets, a small monastery and windmill nearby, smoke drifting from musket fire. Seen from a distance. No blood. Painted in the style of a Dutch seventeenth-century battle landscape, oil on oak, browns and greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1571-battle-of-lepanto: 1571, the Gulf of Patras: seen from far above the sea, hundreds of oared galleys with lateen sails and banners crowd the water in long crescent formations, the Holy League fleet with large galleasses meeting the Ottoman fleet, puffs of cannon smoke, mountains of western Greece on the horizon under a bright sky. No blood. Painted as a Venetian Renaissance oil painting in the manner of Veronese, rich blues and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1588-spanish-armada: 1588, off Gravelines on the Flemish coast: at night, burning fireships drift on the wind toward a crescent of tall Spanish galleons at anchor, which cut their cables and scatter, English warships with striped sails waiting in the darkness, orange light on stormy sea and low clouds. Painted in the style of a late sixteenth-century Netherlandish marine oil painting, dark greens and fiery orange, detailed rigging. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1598-edict-of-nantes: 1598, Nantes: in the great hall of the castle of the Dukes of Brittany, a French king in a black doublet with a white ruff, seen small from across the room, sits at a table signing a document, flanked by Catholic and Protestant noblemen in ruffs and cloaks, a bishop and a Huguenot minister in black; the Loire visible through the windows. Painted as a late sixteenth-century French oil painting, sober blacks, whites and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1600-hamlet: 1600, London's Bankside: the round timber-framed Globe theatre open to the sky, its thatched roof and white walls, crowds of standing groundlings in doublets and caps around the stage and gentlefolk in the galleries, actors in Elizabethan costume on the stage, one holding a skull, a flag flying from the roof; the Thames and city spires behind. Painted in the manner of an Elizabethan oil painting or detailed engraving with hand colour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1602-dutch-east-india-company: 1602, Amsterdam: on a busy quay along a canal lined with brick houses with stepped gables, merchants in black clothes and white ruffs crowd around an open trading house, sacks of pepper and crates of nutmeg and cloves unloaded from tall three-masted East Indiamen in the harbour, barrels and small boats, the red-brick tower of the Oude Kerk behind. Painted in the style of a Dutch Golden Age oil painting, clear light, silvery skies. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1605-don-quixote: 1605, Madrid: in a printer's shop near a narrow sunny street of whitewashed houses, journeymen work a wooden press, freshly printed books stacked on a counter, a few customers in Spanish doublets and capes browsing, one opening a book whose woodcut frontispiece shows a thin knight on a bony horse beside a squire on a donkey and windmills. Painted in the style of a Spanish Golden Age oil painting, warm browns, dramatic light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1610-sidereus-nuncius: 1610, Padua: on the roof terrace of a house at night, a bearded scholar in a long dark gown, seen from behind, looks through a long slender leather-covered refracting telescope on a wooden stand toward a bright Jupiter and a crescent Moon over the red tile roofs and domes of Padua, a sheet of paper with sketched dots and a candle lantern beside him. Painted as an early seventeenth-century Italian oil painting, deep blue night, candlelight. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1642-english-civil-war: 1642, Edgehill in Warwickshire: seen from the top of a steep wooded ridge, two armies draw up on the green fields below in the autumn afternoon, regiments of pikemen and musketeers in buff coats and helmets with coloured banners, cavalry on the wings, cannon smoke drifting; hedges and a village church in the distance. No blood. Painted in the style of a seventeenth-century English or Dutch battle painting, oil, soft greens and browns. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1649-execution-of-charles-i: 1649, Whitehall in London: seen from a distance on a cold January day, a great crowd in dark cloaks and tall hats fills the street before the stone Banqueting House, soldiers with pikes holding them back, a black-draped wooden scaffold built against the building's windows with small figures standing on it; snow-grey sky, smoke from chimneys. Rendered as a seventeenth-century Dutch engraving of a public event, fine line, sober tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1682-palace-of-versailles: 1682, Versailles: a long procession of gilded coaches pulled by horses and courtiers in wigs, lace and silk coats arrives along a broad avenue at the vast stone palace with its marble courtyard and gilt railings, formal gardens, fountains and canals stretching away behind; bright summer light. Seen from a high point, figures small. Painted in the style of a seventeenth-century French oil vista painting of royal palaces, crisp perspective, soft blues and golds. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1683-battle-of-vienna: 1683, the Kahlenberg above Vienna: from the wooded heights, a great charge of Polish winged hussars with tall feathered frames on their backs and lances sweeps down the slopes toward a vast Ottoman siege camp of tents and trenches ringing the walled city with the spire of Saint Stephen's cathedral, cannon smoke drifting over the Danube plain. No blood. Painted as a seventeenth-century Baroque battle painting, oil, golden smoky light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1687-principia: 1687, London: in a London print shop, a printer in a leather apron shows a thick freshly bound volume to a group of gentlemen in long wigs and coats from the Royal Society, open pages with geometric diagrams of orbits and curves, a wooden press and type cases behind, an apple on a windowsill, Wren-era church spires visible outside. Painted in the style of a late seventeenth-century Dutch genre interior, oil, warm window light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1688-glorious-revolution: 1688, the English coast at Torbay: a large Dutch fleet of tall warships with orange flags anchored in a wide bay, boats rowing soldiers in red and blue coats and broad hats ashore, local townspeople greeting them, green hills and a fishing village behind; calm November light. Painted as a Dutch Golden Age marine oil painting in the manner of the Van de Veldes, silvery sky, fine rigging. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1689-bill-of-rights: 1689, Westminster: in the Banqueting House with its painted ceiling, members of the Lords and Commons in wigs and dark coats stand before a seated king and queen in robes and crowns, seen from across the hall, while a clerk reads from a long parchment scroll; candles and tall windows, soft winter light. Painted as a late seventeenth-century English oil history painting, sober reds, blacks and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1698-petrine-reforms: 1698, Moscow: in a courtyard of the Kremlin before onion-domed churches, a very tall young ruler in Western coat and tricorne stands among boyars in long caftans and tall fur hats while a servant with shears trims the long beard of one of them, others watching uneasily; Western-dressed officers nearby, snow on the ground. Figures small. Rendered as a Russian lubok popular print, bold outlines and bright hand colouring. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1700-great-northern-war: 1709, Poltava: seen from a distant hill, Russian infantry in green coats and tricornes in long lines with redoubts and cannon face blue-coated Swedish troops on an open Ukrainian steppe, white cannon smoke rolling across the field, the town and its church domes on the river bluff behind; summer morning. No blood. Painted in the style of an eighteenth-century Russian battle painting or mosaic, oil, soft greens and blues. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1751-encyclopedie: 1751, Paris: in a busy print shop on a narrow Paris street, printers in aprons work wooden presses, stacks of large folio volumes and loose engraved plates of machines, tools and crafts on a table, two men in wigs and coats discussing a page by the window, apprentices hanging sheets to dry. Painted in the style of an eighteenth-century French genre painting in the manner of Chardin, soft light, warm browns. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1756-seven-years-war: 1757, Rossbach in Saxony: seen from a hill, Prussian cavalry in white and blue sweep across rolling autumn fields toward columns of French and imperial troops in white and blue coats, lines of Prussian infantry in dark blue firing, white powder smoke over the hills and a village church tower. No blood. Painted as an eighteenth-century military oil painting, soft greys and greens, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1762-social-contract: 1762, Amsterdam: in a bookseller's shop on a canal, a printer hands newly bound small volumes to customers in tricornes and frock coats, stacks of books, a wooden press behind, a canal with barges and narrow gabled houses outside the leaded windows; soft grey daylight. Painted in the style of an eighteenth-century Dutch genre painting, oil, cool light and warm interiors. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1765-spinning-jenny: 1765, Stanhill in Lancashire: inside a stone cottage with a low beamed ceiling, a weaver in a waistcoat and shirtsleeves turns the wheel of a wooden spinning frame with a row of eight spindles drawing thread, his wife carding wool and children watching by the hearth, baskets of cotton, a window on green hills. Painted in the style of an eighteenth-century English genre painting, oil, warm firelight and browns. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1769-watt-steam-engine: 1769, Glasgow: in a workshop with brick walls, an instrument maker in a waistcoat and an apprentice adjust a brass model steam engine with a cylinder, a separate condenser vessel, pipes and a beam, tools, drawings and a forge glow behind; through a window the masts of ships on the Clyde. Painted as an eighteenth-century English oil painting in the manner of Joseph Wright of Derby, dramatic lamplight and shadow. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1772-partitions-of-poland: 1772, a royal council chamber: three monarchs' envoys in eighteenth-century court dress, powdered wigs and sashes stand around a large table covered with a map of a kingdom, each pointing to a different part of it, while a distant figure in Polish noble dress with a fur-trimmed kontusz stands helplessly by the window; gilded rococo interior. Rendered as an eighteenth-century allegorical engraving, fine line and hand colour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1776-wealth-of-nations: 1776, London: inside a pin workshop, ten workers in shirts and aprons sit along a bench each doing one step, drawing wire, cutting, pointing, putting on heads, while a gentleman in a frock coat and wig takes notes and a merchant inspects papers of finished pins; through the window a London street of brick houses and shop signs without lettering. Painted as an eighteenth-century English genre painting, oil, warm light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1780-josephinism: 1780s, a Bohemian village near Vienna: a man in a plain grey military coat, seen from a distance, guides a wooden plough pulled by oxen in a field while peasants in smocks and head-scarves and a village priest watch, thatched farmhouses, a baroque church with an onion spire and rolling fields behind under a high summer sky. Painted as an eighteenth-century Austrian oil genre painting, soft greens and golds. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1781-critique-of-pure-reason: 1781, Königsberg: a small slender man in a grey coat and tricorne, seen from behind, takes his regular afternoon walk along a tree-lined avenue past the brick cathedral and gabled houses by the Pregel river, a servant following with an umbrella, townspeople setting their watches; cool northern autumn light. Painted as an eighteenth-century German topographical watercolour, delicate washes and fine pen line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
eu-1789-declaration-of-the-rights-of-man: 1789, Versailles: in a large temporary assembly hall with columns and a skylight, hundreds of deputies in black coats, clergy in cassocks and nobles in lace and plumed hats crowd the benches, a president standing at a raised desk, a speaker reading from a sheet, public galleries packed with spectators. Seen from high up, figures small. Painted in the style of a French revolutionary-era oil painting by David's circle, cool light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.

eu-2024-ai-act: 2024, Brussels: the great semicircular hemicycle of a modern parliament chamber with curved rows of blue seats and desks with small screens, hundreds of anonymous lawmakers raising their hands in a vote, large wall screens glowing with abstract blue charts, interpreters' glass booths along the top. ir-tepe-yahya-tablets: c. 2900 BCE, Tepe Yahya in Kerman: on a dusty mound settlement of mud-brick houses in a dry valley ringed by bare mountains, a scribe in a wool wrap sits in a doorway pressing marks into a small rectangular clay tablet with a reed stylus, baskets of grain, clay sealings and pottery jars around him, a donkey loaded with bundles of soft stone vessels nearby. Painted in the manner of ancient Near Eastern painted pottery and wall painting, ochre, black and cream. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-lapis-lazuli-trade: c. 2600 BCE, Sar-i Sang in Badakhshan: in a steep rocky mountain gorge, miners in rough wool garments break deep blue stone flecked with gold from the cliff using fire-setting and stone hammers, others pack the blue blocks into baskets on donkeys for a caravan setting off down the valley along a river; snow peaks above. No riding. Painted in the style of an ancient Mesopotamian shell-and-lapis inlay like the Standard of Ur, blue, red and white. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-marlik: c. 1200 BCE, Marlik in the Alborz foothills of Gilan: on a green hilltop above river valleys and forests, people in woollen robes lower a richly decorated gold beaker embossed with winged bulls into a stone-lined tomb, along with silver bowls, bronze weapons and clay animal figurines, mourners and priests standing around under a misty sky. Painted in the style of an ancient Iranian embossed goldwork relief, gold and deep green tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-nebuchadnezzar-i-susa: c. 1110 BCE, Susa in Khuzestan: Babylonian soldiers with bows, spears and two-wheeled horse chariots stand before the mud-brick walls and ziggurat-topped citadel of the Elamite city, smoke rising from inside, while priests carry out a large gold-covered statue of a god on a litter toward a waiting cart; flat plains and a river. Seen from afar. Rendered in the style of a Mesopotamian carved stone relief, warm limestone tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-hasanlu: c. 800 BCE, Hasanlu in West Azerbaijan: seen from the plain at a distance at dusk, a fortified hilltop citadel with mud-brick walls and towers burns, a great column of smoke rising, attacking soldiers in pointed helmets with spears and chariots gathered below, the lake and mountains beyond. No bodies. Painted in the style of an Assyrian and Urartian palace relief, carved stone with faint traces of colour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-darius-reforms: c. 518 BCE, Susa: in the columned hall of the Achaemenid palace, tribute bearers of many nations in different dress, Medes in rounded caps, Bactrians with camels, Lydians with vessels, line up before a royal treasury where officials in long pleated robes weigh gold coins on bronze balance scales, glazed brick walls with winged bulls and archers behind. Rendered in the style of an Achaemenid relief from Persepolis, carved grey stone with traces of colour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-kings-peace: 387 BCE, Sardis in Anatolia: in the courtyard of the Persian satrap's palace below a rocky acropolis, Greek envoys in himations and sandals stand before a Persian satrap in a long robe and soft tiara seated on a chair, a royal official holding up a sealed document, Persian guards with spears; the Lydian plain and the Pactolus river beyond. Rendered as a Greek red-figure vase painting, black ground, terracotta figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-kandahar-edict: c. 260 BCE, Kandahar: on a bare rocky outcrop above a dry river valley, stonecutters in simple wrapped cloths finish carving long lines of small weathered marks into a smoothed boulder face, a Greek-dressed official and an Indian official in turban and dhoti watching, merchants with camels passing on the road below; hazy sun over brown mountains. No legible writing. Painted in the style of an ancient Indian Ajanta-type mural, warm ochres and earthy reds. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-an-shigao: 148 CE, Luoyang: outside the gate of a Han-dynasty monastery courtyard with tiled roofs and a wooden tower, a foreign monk in a saffron-brown robe, with a small group of Han scholars in long robes and black caps, sits on mats at low tables with bamboo slips and scrolls, translating; ox-carts and city walls behind. Rendered in the style of a Han-dynasty tomb mural, flowing ink outline with red, ochre and black on plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-mani: c. 240 CE, Ctesiphon by the Tigris: in a market square of the Sasanian capital with vaulted mud-brick buildings and palm trees, a preacher in a white robe, seen small from behind, speaks to a gathering crowd of merchants, Persians in long tunics and trousers, Christians and travellers, a disciple holding a painted book with bright pictures; the river and boats behind. Rendered in the style of a Manichaean illuminated manuscript fragment from Turfan, bright blue, red and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-mazdak: c. 494 CE, Ctesiphon: before the vast brick arch of a Sasanian palace hall, a crowd of poor farmers and townspeople in tunics and caps open the doors of a noble's granary and carry out sacks of grain, a preacher in white robes standing on steps addressing them, nobles in rich robes watching from a balcony; dusty afternoon light. Rendered in the style of a Sasanian silver plate engraving, gilt silver tones, stylised figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-gondishapur: c. 550 CE, Gondishapur in Khuzestan: in a courtyard of a Sasanian academy with brick arches and a garden, physicians and scholars in robes and caps, Persians, Syriac Christian monks and an Indian scholar, examine herbs, read from codices and scrolls, a teacher instructs students beside a patient; an infirmary hall behind and date palms. Painted in the manner of a Persian miniature, flat bright colours, gold and lapis blue. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-bamiyan-buddhas: c. 570 CE, Bamiyan: in a wide green valley with poplar trees below a long pale sandstone cliff riddled with cave openings, two colossal standing robed figures are being carved in deep niches, wooden scaffolds and ladders against them, workers with chisels and plaster, monks in robes walking below, a caravan of camels on the valley road and snowy Hindu Kush peaks. Painted in the style of a Central Asian Buddhist cave mural, ochre, lapis and malachite. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-persian-area-command: 661 CE, Zaranj in Sistan: at the mud-brick gate of a desert town among dunes and reed marshes, Tang envoys in red round-collared robes and black futou caps, with an escort of horsemen, present a sealed scroll of appointment to a Persian prince in a pearl-studded crown and long Sasanian robe and his followers. Figures small. Painted in the manner of a Tang-dynasty court painting, mineral blues, greens and vermilion on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-kalila-and-dimna: c. 750 CE, Basra: in a scholar's house with a shaded courtyard and palm trees by a canal, a Persian man in a long robe and turban sits on a carpet among Middle Persian and Arabic manuscripts, writing, while an open book beside him shows painted pictures of a lion, a bull and two jackals; a servant brings a cup of sherbet. Painted in the style of a medieval Arabic manuscript illustration of Kalila wa Dimna, flat bright colours, gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-imam-reza-shrine: early ninth century, Sanabad near Tus in Khorasan: in a village of mud-brick houses and orchards on a broad plain under mountains, a modest domed brick tomb stands in a walled garden, pilgrims in turbans and long robes arriving on foot and with camels, some kneeling in prayer in the courtyard, lamps at the doorway at dusk. No sacred figure shown. Painted in the style of a Persian miniature, lapis blue, turquoise and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-mahmud-somnath: 1026 CE, Ghazni: a returning army of Ghaznavid horsemen in mail and turbans with banners, and long camel trains heavily laden with chests of treasure, wind along a dusty road toward the walled mountain city of Ghazni with its brick minarets and citadel, crowds watching from the walls, bare brown mountains around. Seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Persian miniature, gold sky, flat bright colours, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-al-biruni-india: c. 1030 CE, Ghazni: in a courtyard of a palace with brick arches, a scholar in a turban and long robe sits on a carpet with Sanskrit palm-leaf manuscripts and Arabic books around him, an Indian pandit in a dhoti and shawl explaining a text, an astrolabe and a brass sundial beside them, mountains beyond the walls. Painted in the style of a Persian manuscript miniature, flat colours, lapis blue and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-jalali-calendar: 1079 CE, Isfahan: on the flat roof of a Seljuk observatory with brick walls and a large curved quadrant arc built into masonry, astronomers in turbans and robes take sightings of the stars with brass astrolabes and armillary spheres at night, one writing tables by lamplight; the domes and brick minarets of Isfahan below under a starry sky. No telescopes. Painted in the style of a Persian miniature, deep blue night, gold stars. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-alamut: 1090 CE, Alamut in the Alborz mountains: a stone fortress built along the top of a sheer rocky crag above a green river valley, its walls, towers and gates reached by a narrow winding path, men in plain robes and turbans climbing with supplies on mules, terraced fields and snow peaks around under dramatic clouds. Painted in the style of a Persian miniature landscape, swirling rocks in pink and lilac, gold sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-minaret-of-jam: c. 1190 CE, Jam in Ghor: in a narrow rugged mountain valley where two rivers meet, a slender tapering brick minaret about sixty-five metres tall rises from the riverbank, its surface covered in intricate geometric brick patterns and bands of turquoise glazed decoration with no legible script, masons on wooden scaffolding at the top, a small settlement and bare cliffs around. Painted as a Persian miniature, ochre and turquoise, gold sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-gulistan: 1258 CE, Shiraz: in a walled Persian garden full of blooming roses, cypress trees and a water channel with a small pool, an elderly poet in a white turban and robe sits on a carpet under a pavilion writing in a book, a few listeners sitting nearby, nightingales in the trees, the city's domes and mountains beyond. Painted as a Persian miniature in the Shiraz school, rich blues, greens and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-chen-cheng-herat: 1414, Herat: in the garden palace of the Timurid ruler, a delegation of Ming envoys in round-collared official robes and black gauze caps presents silk bolts and porcelain to a seated Timurid shah in a turban under a canopy, surrounded by courtiers in long coats, musicians and cypress trees; tiled domes behind. Figures small. Painted in the style of a Timurid Persian miniature from the Herat school, lapis blue, gold and turquoise. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-goharshad-mosque: 1418, Mashhad: in a vast courtyard of a newly built mosque, four tall arched iwans faced with dazzling blue, turquoise and yellow tilework, a great turquoise dome beside the tomb shrine, tile-makers and masons on scaffolding finishing the patterns, worshippers in turbans crossing the courtyard. No legible inscriptions. Painted as a Timurid Persian miniature, turquoise, lapis and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-uzun-hasan: 1467, eastern Anatolia near Tabriz: seen from a hill, a victorious army of Turkmen horsemen in turbans and mail with long lances and horsetail standards rides across a wide snowy plain, the tents of a defeated camp scattered behind them, mountains under a pale winter sky. No blood. Painted as a Turkmen-style Persian miniature of the Tabriz school, bold colours and swirling landscape. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-babur-kabul: 1504, Kabul: a small army of Timurid horsemen in turbans and quilted coats with bows rides through a mountain pass toward the walled city of Kabul and its hilltop citadel, orchards and gardens along the river below, snow-capped peaks around and autumn trees. Figures small. Painted as a Mughal miniature from the Baburnama, bright greens, ochres and gold, fine detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-mulla-sadra: c. 1630, Shiraz: in the arched courtyard of a Safavid religious school with blue tiled walls, a pool and orange trees, students in turbans and long robes sit in a circle on carpets around a teacher, books open on wooden stands, scholars debating in the arcades; afternoon light. Teacher seen small and from behind. Painted as a Safavid Persian miniature in the Isfahan style, soft pastels, gold and lapis. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-durrani-empire: 1747, near Kandahar: in an open field before a domed shrine, a gathering of Pashtun tribal chiefs in large turbans, long shirts and embroidered waistcoats sit in a circle on carpets, one young warrior standing as an elder places a sheaf of wheat in his turban; horses, rifles and tents nearby, bare brown hills under a clear sky. Figures small. Painted as an eighteenth-century Persian or Mughal miniature, ochre and green. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-battle-of-krtsanisi: 1795, Tbilisi: seen from a hill across the Kura river, the old town of balconied houses, churches with conical domes and the hilltop Narikala fortress lies under smoke rising from fires, Qajar horsemen in tall black lambskin hats massed on the riverbank, the Caucasus mountains behind. No bodies. Painted in the style of a Qajar-period Persian painting, rich reds and browns, flat stylised landscape. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-first-anglo-afghan-war: 1839, Kabul: a long column of British and Indian troops in red coats and shakos, with camels, elephants hauling cannon and baggage carts, marches into the valley toward the walled city and the Bala Hissar citadel on its hill, Afghan onlookers in turbans and cloaks on the slopes, snow-capped mountains around. Painted as a mid-nineteenth-century lithograph in the style of James Atkinson's Afghan sketches, soft watercolour tints. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-bab: 1844, Shiraz: on a May night, the modest brick house of a merchant in a narrow lane of the old city, an oil lamp glowing in an upper window with carved wooden latticework, one traveller in a turban and cloak at the doorway, the domes and cypress trees of Shiraz under a starry sky. No faces shown, no religious figure depicted. Painted in the style of a Qajar-period Persian watercolour, deep blues and warm lamplight. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-amir-kabir: 1851, Tehran: in the new brick courtyard of the Dar ul-Funun college with arched arcades, Iranian students in long coats and tall black lambskin hats gather around European-style instructors with globes, maps and laboratory instruments, a rifle drill being practised at the far side, the Alborz mountains above the city. Figures small. Painted in the style of a Qajar-era Persian painting or lithograph, soft colours and fine line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-anglo-russian-convention: 1907, Saint Petersburg: in a gilded room of the Foreign Ministry with tall windows over the Neva, two diplomats in frock coats sit at a polished table signing documents, a large map of Persia and Afghanistan spread out with two shaded zones, officials standing behind, chandelier light. Figures small. Rendered as an early twentieth-century illustrated newspaper engraving with light watercolour tint. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-afghan-independence: 1919, Kabul: on a sunny summer day a festive crowd in turbans, karakul caps and long coats fills a broad open square before a European-style palace, and troops in khaki with rifles parade. Over them flies the Afghan flag of that time: a plain black field with a small white central emblem of a mosque framed by a wreath, NOT a red or green striped tricolour. Mountains rise beyond the city's mud-brick houses. Figures small. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour, warm ochres and blues. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-trans-iranian-railway: 1930s, Mazandaran in the Alborz mountains: a high stone arch railway bridge is built across a deep forested gorge, labourers in felt caps and engineers in hats on wooden scaffolding, a small steam locomotive with a few wagons waiting at the tunnel mouth on the mountainside, mist in the green valley below. Painted as a 1930s documentary watercolour, greens, greys and warm stone. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-kashf-e-hijab: 1936, Tehran: a broad tree-lined avenue of the modernising capital with new European-style buildings, horse-drawn carriages and a few cars, passers-by including men in suits and Pahlavi caps and women in long coats and hats, an older woman in a dark chador walking at the side of the street. Figures small and calm. Painted as a 1930s documentary watercolour, soft ochres and greens. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-tehran-conference: 1943, Tehran: the garden of the Soviet embassy compound on a late-November afternoon, a colonnaded neoclassical building among plane trees, staff cars parked on the gravel and soldiers of three Allied armies standing guard; on the portico three elderly statesmen in overcoats and a military greatcoat sit in a row, seen small from a distance, surrounded by aides, officers and press photographers with cameras on tripods. Muted documentary watercolour in wartime greys and khaki, light pencil underdrawing. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-oil-nationalisation: 1951, Abadan on the Shatt al-Arab: the vast oil refinery stretches along the riverbank under hard summer sun, with distillation towers, storage tanks and flare stacks, and idle tankers anchored in the brown river. Iranian workers and clerks in shirtsleeves gather at the refinery gates while officials in suits raise the Pahlavi-era green, white and red tricolour with a golden Lion and Sun emblem in the white band (not the later Islamic Republic emblem) over the administration building, and crowds watch from the dusty road. Mid-twentieth-century documentary gouache illustration, ochres and steel greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-saur-revolution: 1978, Kabul: a spring morning over the city seen from a hillside, flat-roofed mud-brick houses and the walls of the Arg palace below the bare Asmai mountain, a few tanks parked across a wide avenue and a thin column of smoke rising over the palace compound; townspeople in turbans, pakol caps and long shirts watch quietly from rooftops far away. Restrained documentary watercolour, pale dusty palette, loose brushwork, small distant figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-soviet-afghan-war: 1979, outside Kabul: a long column of Soviet armoured personnel carriers and canvas-covered trucks winds along a dusty mountain road through a barren valley in winter, snow on the Hindu Kush peaks; on a ridge far off, a small group of Afghan villagers and fighters in shawls and turbans watch beside a mud-walled fortified farmstead and leafless poplars. Muted documentary gouache illustration, cold blues and dusty browns, everything seen from a great distance. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-hostage-crisis: 1979, Tehran: the long brick wall and iron gates of the United States embassy compound on a November day, a large crowd of students and onlookers in winter coats and headscarves filling the street, banners with no legible writing, bare plane trees along the pavement and the low chancery building visible behind the wall; seen from across the avenue at a distance, no faces in close-up. Neutral documentary watercolour, grey winter light, restrained palette. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-taliban-kabul-1996: 1996, Kabul: a war-damaged city in autumn seen from a hilltop, roofless buildings and broken walls along the Kabul River with brown mountains behind; a line of pickup trucks carrying armed men in black and white turbans drives along an empty avenue, while a few residents in shawls and blue burqas watch from doorways far away. Muted documentary watercolour, dusty beige and grey tones, quiet and distant, no faces visible. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-war-in-afghanistan: 2001, north of Kabul: the Shomali plain in late autumn, an empty road between mud-walled villages and bare poplars, distant plumes of smoke on the horizon from air strikes; a convoy of four-wheel-drive vehicles waits by the roadside with Afghan fighters in pakol caps and a few foreign soldiers in desert fatigues, snow-capped mountains behind. Documentary gouache illustration, muted earth tones and pale sky, all figures small and seen from a distance. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-green-movement: 2009, Tehran: a vast silent crowd fills a broad avenue leading toward Azadi Square on a June afternoon, many thousands of marchers in everyday clothes, many wearing green scarves and wristbands and holding up green ribbons, the white arched monument tower rising at the far end and the Alborz mountains hazy beyond; seen from high above at a great distance, no individual faces. Neutral documentary watercolour, soft summer light, touches of green in a grey city. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-jcpoa: 2015, Vienna: a high-ceilinged hall of a nineteenth-century palace on the old city ramparts on a July evening, crystal chandeliers and tall windows; delegations in dark suits sit around a long negotiating table with rows of national flags behind them, microphones, folders and water glasses on the table, interpreters along the walls, the whole room seen from the back at a distance with no recognisable faces. Neutral documentary gouache illustration, warm lamplight and cream walls. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-fall-of-kabul-2021: 2021, Kabul: the city's airport in August heat, a large crowd of civilians with bundles, suitcases and children waiting along the perimeter fence and the airport road, a grey military transport plane standing on the runway, dust haze over the city and brown mountains behind; seen from a distance, no faces visible. Neutral documentary watercolour, pale ochre and grey palette, quiet and restrained. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
ir-twelve-day-war: 2025, near Qom: the arid mountains around the Fordow site at dawn, a bare rocky ridge with tunnel entrances and a fenced compound of low buildings at its foot, thin columns of dust and smoke rising from the hillside, an empty desert road winding below; no people visible, the scene viewed from far away across the plain. Restrained documentary watercolour, pale sand and grey-violet dawn tones, calm and spare. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-flame-pottery: c. 3000 BCE, Shinano River valley, Niigata: a Middle Jomon settlement of thatched pit dwellings among autumn chestnut and beech woods. Outside a hut, potters in plant-fibre clothing shape wet grey-brown CLAY by hand into tall jars with dramatic flame-like rims of looping clay crests and handles; the vessels are solid earthenware with cord-marked and incised clay surfaces, clearly pottery and NOT woven baskets or wicker. Finished unfired jars dry on mats, others blackened and reddened from an open firing pit of glowing wood, the river and wooded mountains behind. Soft archaeological watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-kamegaoka-dogu: c. 1000 BCE, Kamegaoka on the Tsugaru plain, Aomori: a final Jōmon village of thatched pit dwellings beside a reedy marsh in late summer; craftspeople in woven bark-fibre garments sit on mats painting bowls and combs with red and black lacquer, while one shapes a small clay figurine with huge goggle-like eyes and an ornately patterned, clothed body, fine pots nearby, the cone of Mount Iwaki on the horizon. Earth-toned archaeological watercolour reconstruction with ink line and red lacquer accents. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-suiko-shotoku: 593, Asuka in the Nara basin: a palace of timber halls with cypress-bark roofs beside the newly built Asuka-dera temple with grey tiled roofs and a tall pagoda in continental style; courtiers in long robes and caps form ranks in the gravel courtyard, the empress a small seated figure under a canopy far in the background, monks in brown and grey robes arriving with sutra boxes, green hills beyond. Painted in the style of an early Yamato-e handscroll, mineral pigments, fine ink line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-twelve-cap-ranks: 603, Oharida Palace in Asuka: a gravel courtyard before a timber hall with a bark-shingle roof, courtiers lined up in rows wearing long robes and stiff silk caps in graded colours of purple, blue, red, yellow, white and black, each row a different hue; an official on the hall steps hands a cap to a kneeling man, attendants holding fans, pines and low green hills behind. Painted in the style of an early Yamato-e handscroll, bright mineral colours on paper, fine ink outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-tang-missions: 630, Naniwa harbour on Osaka Bay: two large wooden sailing ships with mat sails and painted hulls wait at a timber wharf, envoys in court robes and caps, Buddhist monks and young students boarding with chests and bundles of scrolls; officials and families watch from the shore beside a thatched warehouse, the calm bay shining in morning light with distant islands. Painted as a Yamato-e emakimono handscroll, mineral blues and greens, fine ink line, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-name-nippon: 702, Fujiwara-kyō in the Nara basin: Japan's first grid-planned capital, its great audience hall with grey tiled roof and vermilion pillars facing a broad gravel courtyard; at sunrise an envoy party in Tang-style court robes and black caps bows before setting out for China, the red disc of the rising sun lifting over the eastern hills behind the palace, banners on tall poles, ranked courtiers watching. Tang-influenced Nara court painting, mineral pigments on hemp, gold and vermilion accents. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-wado-kaichin: 708, Chichibu in the mountains of Musashi: miners in hemp clothing carry baskets of native copper from a hillside outcrop down to a riverside workshop under cedar forest; smiths pour molten copper from crucibles into stone moulds, and rows of round bronze coins with square holes cool on straw mats, an official in court robe and cap supervising with a scribe. Painted in the style of a Nara-period illustrated sutra scroll, ink and light colour, earthy reds and greens. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-kojiki: 712, Heijō-kyō: inside a timber hall of the new Nara capital, a scholar-official in court robe and cap kneels at a low desk brushing columns of unreadable characters onto a long paper scroll by lamplight, while an elderly court reciter beside him speaks from memory; scroll boxes, an inkstone and brushes around them, sliding doors open onto a gravel court and a tiled gate. Painted as a Yamato-e handscroll, soft mineral colours, fine ink line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-nihon-shoki: 720, Heijō-kyō: in the palace's great audience hall with vermilion pillars and grey tiled roof, a prince in court robes leads a line of officials carrying lacquered boxes of scrolls toward the throne, which is hidden behind a hanging curtain; ranks of courtiers in robes of different colours kneel on mats, spring sunlight falling on the gravel courtyard outside. Tang-influenced Nara court painting style, mineral blues, greens and vermilion on hemp, fine line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-konden-einen: 743, the Nara basin near Heijō-kyō: farmers in hemp tunics clear new fields at the forest edge, felling trees, digging out stumps and cutting irrigation channels, an ox pulling a plough through freshly opened rice paddies; a provincial official and a scribe mark the boundaries with ropes and wooden stakes while a noble's steward looks on, the capital's pagodas small on the horizon. Painted in the style of a Nara-period handscroll, ink and light colour on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-manyoshu: 759, Heijō-kyō: a poetry gathering in a noble's garden on a spring evening, courtiers in long robes seated on mats under blossoming plum trees beside a pond, one reciting from a slip of paper while others hold brushes; beyond the earthen garden wall, a frontier guard with a bow and village women carrying baskets pass along the road, scrolls piled on a low table. Painted as a Yamato-e handscroll, soft mineral colours, plum-pink and green. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-enryaku-ji: 788, Mount Hiei above Lake Biwa: on a forested ridge, a young monk in grey robes and a few labourers raise a small thatched timber hall in a clearing among tall cryptomeria trees; a single oil lamp burns before a carved Buddhist image inside, mist drifting through the trunks and the broad lake shining far below in evening light. Painted in the manner of a Heian-period temple-founding handscroll, ink and soft colour on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-kana: c. 900, Heian-kyō: in a room of a shinden-style mansion, noblewomen in layered silk robes with long flowing hair sit behind folding screens writing flowing cursive letters on decorated paper, the script reduced to abstract unreadable strokes, brushes, inkstones and lacquer letter boxes beside them; a garden with a pond and red maples seen through raised bamboo blinds on an autumn afternoon. Yamato-e handscroll style like the Tale of Genji scrolls, flat mineral colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-pillow-book: c. 1000, the Heian-kyō imperial palace: a lady-in-waiting in many-layered silk robes kneels by a raised bamboo blind at dawn, a stack of paper on a low lacquered writing box beside her, gazing out at a snowy garden and pale mountains; other court ladies talk in the background behind curtains of state, a brazier glowing. Painted in Yamato-e style with the roofless bird's-eye view of interiors, flat mineral colours and fine ink line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-honen: 1175, Yoshimizu in the eastern hills of Kyoto: a simple thatched hermitage among pines, an elderly monk in black robes seated on the veranda while a varied crowd gathers in the yard, farmers, merchants, women, warriors and beggars with palms joined and prayer beads in hand, reciting together; the roofs of the capital spread below in hazy afternoon light. Kamakura-period illustrated biography handscroll style, ink and colour on paper, lively small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-shugo-jito: 1185, Kamakura: the warrior government's headquarters, plain timber halls with thatched roofs behind a wooden palisade near the sea; armoured warriors in eboshi caps dismount at the gate, while on the veranda retainers kneel in rows receiving documents of appointment from a seated lord seen from behind, horses tethered under pines, the wooded hills of Kamakura beyond. Kamakura-period emakimono style, ink and colour on paper, energetic line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-eisai-zen: 1191, Hakata Bay on the Kyushu coast: a Song Chinese junk with battened sails anchored offshore, a monk in black robes stepping ashore with sutra boxes and a small earthenware pot of tea seedlings; nearby carpenters raise the timber gate and hall of a new temple in Song style, merchants and onlookers gathered on the sandy beach. Kamakura-period emakimono style, ink and light colour on paper, sea in pale blue washes. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-hojo-shikken: 1203, Kamakura: in a plain wooden hall of the shogunate, an elderly warrior in dark hitatare and eboshi sits beside a raised dais where a young shogun is seated behind a half-lowered bamboo blind, rows of vassals kneeling on straw mats, bows and armour on racks along the wall; a pine-covered hillside and the sea seen through open shutters. Kamakura-period emakimono style, ink and colour on paper, all faces small. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-goseibai-shikimoku: 1232, Kamakura: a council hall of the shogunate, a dozen councillors in hitatare and eboshi caps seated in a ring on straw mats around a clerk who unrolls a long law scroll, other clerks copying it at low desks for distribution to the provinces; retainers wait outside with saddled horses and lacquered document boxes, summer light on the cryptomeria. Kamakura-period emakimono style, ink and light colour, no legible writing. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-heike-monogatari: c. 1240, Heian-kyō: in a temple courtyard at dusk, a blind monk in dark robes with a shaven head plays a biwa lute with a large plectrum, chanting to a crowd of townspeople, warriors and children seated on mats; lanterns lit, a temple bell tower behind, a few cherry petals drifting through the air. Kamakura-period emakimono style, ink and muted colour on paper, warm lantern glow. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-genko-war: 1331, Mount Kasagi near Kyoto: a fortified temple on a steep wooded mountain, wooden palisades and standing shields along the cliff paths, defenders in armour with longbows on the ridge; far below, the banners of a besieging shogunate army spread along the Kizu River valley, campfire smoke rising into autumn mist. Kamakura-period battle handscroll style, ink and colour on paper, all figures small and distant. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-kenmu: 1333, Heian-kyō: the imperial palace grounds, a crowd of warriors in armour and hitatare waiting restlessly at the gate with petitions, while inside courtiers in black court robes and tall lacquered caps confer in a vermilion-pillared hall; the emperor is seen only as a shadowy figure behind a lowered blind, autumn maples in the courtyard. Late Kamakura emakimono style, ink and colour on paper, fine line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-nanbokucho: 1336, Yoshino in the mountains of Nara: a small mountain palace among temple halls on a steep forested ridge, wild cherry trees in pale blossom; a procession of courtiers, ladies in travelling cloaks and a few armoured warriors climbs the winding path carrying lacquered chests and wrapped boxes of the sacred regalia, mist filling the valleys below. Nanboku-chō-period emakimono style, ink and soft colour on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-kinkaku-ji: 1397, Kitayama in northwest Kyoto: a three-storey pavilion with upper floors covered in gold leaf stands at the edge of a mirror-like pond, its reflection in the water, pine-covered islets and rocks around it, wooded hills behind; small figures of courtiers and monks stroll on the path and a boat glides across the pond in early autumn. Muromachi-period ink and light colour hanging scroll style, gold accents. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-zeami: c. 1400, Heian-kyō: an outdoor Noh performance on a roofed cypress stage, a masked actor in a brocade robe moving slowly with a fan, musicians with flute and drums kneeling at the rear and a chorus at the side, a pine tree beside the stage; samurai lords and courtiers watch from a raised gallery in the evening light. Muromachi-period ink and colour painting on paper, restrained gold and indigo. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-ryukyu-unified: 1429, Shuri on Okinawa: a hilltop castle with curving limestone walls overlooking the harbour of Naha, its red-lacquered main hall blending Chinese and Japanese styles; below, Chinese junks and Ryukyuan trading ships at anchor, porters carrying bales of silk, ceramics and sappanwood up from the quays, officials in Ming-style robes and head-wraps gathered in the courtyard. Ryukyuan court painting with Ming influence, bright vermilion and turquoise sea. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-ginkaku-ji: 1482, Higashiyama in eastern Kyoto: a modest two-storey wooden pavilion with dark unpainted timbers and a bronze phoenix on the roof stands beside a pond garden at the foot of wooded hills; in a small study room nearby a host in plain robes prepares tea, a monochrome ink landscape scroll hanging in the alcove, moonlight over the pond and mossy stones. Muromachi ink painting in the manner of Sesshū, grey washes with faint colour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-kaga-ikki: 1488, Kaga province near present Kanazawa: Takao Castle on a wooded hill above the Sai River plain, surrounded by thousands of farmers, monks and local warriors armed with bamboo spears, hoes and long bows, their plain banners streaming; rice fields stretch toward the Sea of Japan, smoke rising from the castle gate, all figures small. Late Muromachi illustrated temple-history handscroll style, ink and colour on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-iwami-ginzan: 1526, Iwami Ginzan in the hills of Ōda, Shimane: a narrow wooded valley with mine adits cut into the slopes, miners in short work jackets carrying baskets of ore down plank paths, smelting huts with clay furnaces sending up smoke as workers refine silver, merchants weighing ingots on scales; small boats wait in a cove beyond the hills. Late Muromachi genre painting, ink and light colour on paper, many small busy figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-nobunaga-kyoto: 1568, Kyoto: a long column of warriors in lacquered armour with spears, tall plain banners and matchlock guns enters the capital along a broad street past townhouses and temple roofs in autumn; townspeople watch from doorways, a palanquin under escort in the middle of the column, the Higashiyama hills behind. Painted in the style of Momoyama gold-ground genre painting, gold-leaf clouds drifting across one continuous view, bright mineral colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-nagasaki-port: 1571, Nagasaki: a deep sheltered bay among green hills where a large Portuguese carrack with a high stern castle and square sails lies at anchor, small boats ferrying goods ashore; on the newly laid-out harbour streets Portuguese merchants in ruffs and baggy breeches, Jesuit priests in black and Japanese porters and samurai mingle among bales of silk, a small wooden church on the cape. Nanban-style painting, gold ground and bright mineral colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-fall-muromachi: 1573, Kyoto: the moated residence of the shogun surrounded by Oda troops with spears, matchlocks and plain banners; a small procession of retainers and a palanquin leaves through the gate under escort and heads out along the road past the burned outskirts of the upper city, townsfolk watching from a distance, summer haze over the hills. Momoyama-period genre painting, ink and colour on paper with gold-leaf clouds, small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-taiko-kenchi: 1582, the plain near Osaka: survey officials in kataginu vests and straw hats stretch measuring cords and bamboo poles across rice paddies, a clerk noting figures in a ledger on a folding stool, village headmen in plain kimonos bowing as they point out field boundaries, farmers with sickles at the paddy edge; ripe golden rice, thatched villages and distant hills. Momoyama genre painting, ink and light colour on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-sword-hunt: 1588, a village near Osaka: farmers in plain hemp kimonos and straw hats bring swords, spears and old matchlocks into a temple courtyard, piling them on straw mats before seated samurai officials in kataginu vests; clerks record each weapon, ox carts are loaded with bundles of blades, a temple hall roof behind and rice paddies beyond. Momoyama-period genre painting, ink and light colour on paper, small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-rikyu: 1591, Kyoto: a tiny thatched tea house in a mossy garden in early spring rain, a stepping-stone path leading to its low crawl-in entrance; inside, a bare alcove with a hanging scroll and a single camellia in a bamboo vase, an iron kettle on a sunken hearth and an empty host's mat; a few samurai stand waiting in the outer garden under umbrellas. Muted Momoyama ink painting in quiet wabi taste, grey washes and moss green. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-buke-shohatto: 1615, Fushimi Castle, Kyoto: a great reception hall with gilded sliding doors painted with pines, rows of daimyo in formal robes and lacquered caps kneeling in strict order on tatami, an official on the dais reading aloud from a long scroll, swords laid beside the lords; through the open doors, the castle keep and stone walls in summer light. Early Edo Kanō-school painting, gold leaf and malachite green, all figures small. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-kyoho-reforms: c. 1720, Edo: on reclaimed marshland beside the Sumida River, with the white walls of Edo Castle in the distance, labourers dig drainage canals and lay out new rice fields; a group of samurai officials in kamishimo inspects the work, one holding an open Dutch book of botanical engravings, a clerk with an abacus checking accounts. Edo-period ukiyo-e woodblock print, flat colours, crisp outlines, wide sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-kanagawa-convention: 1854, Yokohama on Edo Bay: black-hulled American steam frigates with paddle wheels and smoking funnels anchored offshore; on the beach stands a temporary wooden treaty house hung with plain striped curtains, American sailors and marines in blue uniforms lined up with a band facing samurai officials in kamishimo and guards with pikes, crowds of villagers watching from behind fences. Contemporary Japanese kawaraban woodblock print, bright flat colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-harris-treaty: 1858, Edo Bay off Kanagawa: the cabin of an American steam frigate at anchor, two Japanese commissioners in formal robes and lacquered caps seated across a table from an American envoy in a dark frock coat, interpreters standing by, documents and inkwells on the table, an oil lamp swaying; through the stern windows, the green hills of Kanagawa and small fishing boats. Late Edo nishiki-e woodblock print, crisp outlines and bright colour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-satcho-alliance: 1866, Kyoto: a quiet winter night in the inner room of a samurai residence, a small group of samurai in dark haori jackets with topknots and two swords laid at their sides kneel facing one another across tatami by the light of a paper lantern, a pot of tea and a folded letter between them; through a half-open sliding door, snow falls on a small garden and a stone lantern. Late Edo nishiki-e woodblock print, deep indigo and lamp-lit ochre. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-meiji-restoration: 1868, Tokyo: a long imperial procession crosses a bridge toward the moats and stone walls of the former Edo Castle, a gilded palanquin in the centre carried by bearers, courtiers in court robes and caps, samurai with swords and a few soldiers with Western rifles and kepis marching alongside; crowds of townspeople kneel along the riverbank in autumn sunlight. Meiji-era nishiki-e woodblock print, vivid aniline reds and blues, crisp line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-charter-oath: 1868, the Kyoto Imperial Palace: inside the cypress-wood Shishinden hall, court nobles in black robes and tall caps and daimyo in formal dress kneel in rows on matting before a Shinto altar with sakaki branches, offerings and white paper streamers; a young emperor sits far in the background behind a lowered blind, while an official reads from a scroll; spring light through the open doors. Meiji-era nishiki-e woodblock print, soft colours, all faces small. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-iwakura-mission: 1871, Yokohama harbour: a large American side-wheel steamship with tall masts and a smoking funnel waits in the bay, small boats rowing out to it; on the quay a party of Japanese envoys, some in court robes and topknots, others in new Western frock coats and top hats, and a group of young students board while crowds and officials watch beside brick warehouses, December sky. Meiji-era Yokohama-e woodblock print, bright colours, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-land-tax-reform: 1873, a farming village near Tokyo: government surveyors in Western-style jackets and caps measure a rice field with chains and poles, a clerk writing assessments at a small table under a tree, village headmen in kimono and farmers in straw raincoats looking on; thatched farmhouses, a newly built telegraph line on wooden poles and distant hills under a pale sky. Meiji-era nishiki-e woodblock print, flat colours and crisp outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-ryukyu-disposition: 1879, Shuri on Okinawa: the red-lacquered main hall of Shuri Castle above its curving limestone walls, Japanese soldiers in dark Western uniforms and police lined up in the courtyard, Ryukyuan court officials in broad robes and flat hats standing silent in a group, a palanquin waiting at the gate; palm trees and the sea far below under a heavy grey sky. Meiji-era nishiki-e woodblock print, muted colours, all figures small. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-freedom-rights: 1881, Tokyo: a crowded public speech meeting in a large wooden hall, a speaker in a Western suit gestures from a low platform before an audience of hundreds, men in kimono and haori, some in bowler hats, students and a few women; uniformed police officers sit at a side table ready to halt the meeting, paper lanterns overhead. Meiji-era nishiki-e woodblock print, lively crowd, bright colours with dark uniforms. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-anglo-japanese-alliance: 1902, London: a quiet official room in the Foreign Office with tall windows overlooking St James's Park in winter, a British statesman in a frock coat and a Japanese diplomat in a dark morning coat seated at a mahogany table, documents and an inkstand between them, clerks standing by; grey London light and a coal fire. Edwardian illustrated newspaper engraving, fine cross-hatching, sober tones, figures seen from a middle distance. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-russo-japanese-war: 1904, Port Arthur on the Liaodong Peninsula: the fortified harbour seen from the bare hills above, Russian battleships at anchor among plumes of smoke, Japanese infantry in dark blue winter uniforms dug in along trenches and siege guns on the slopes, a Chinese village of grey-roofed houses in the valley below; winter sky, everything small and distant. Meiji-era war nishiki-e woodblock print, dramatic sky, restrained red. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-taisho-crisis: 1913, Tokyo: a winter day in front of the wooden parliament building in Hibiya, a huge crowd of men in bowler hats, students in caps and workers in short coats filling the street, some waving plain banners, mounted police holding the edges; a newspaper office in the background, a tram stopped in the road, smoke from a distant fire. Taishō-period newspaper illustration, ink and wash, many small figures, no legible signs. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-tsingtao: 1914, Qingdao on the Shandong coast: German forts and red-roofed colonial buildings on the hills above the bay, a German church spire, Japanese siege artillery on the surrounding ridges firing in the autumn haze, a Japanese seaplane overhead and warships on the grey sea, Chinese fishing junks drawn up on a distant beach. Early twentieth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine line with sepia wash, everything seen from a distance. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-twenty-one-demands: 1915, Beijing: inside a Chinese government hall with lacquered pillars, carved screens and electric lamps, a Japanese envoy in a dark morning coat hands a thick bound document across a table to Chinese officials in Western suits and long gowns, aides and interpreters standing in a semicircle; through the window, the tiled roofs and grey walls of the capital under a cold sky. Republican-era woodcut print, strong black lines, sombre mood. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-rice-riots: 1918, Uozu on the Toyama coast: a summer evening at the fishing harbour, a crowd of fishermen's wives in work kimono, aprons and headscarves gathered at a rice merchant's warehouse to stop sacks being loaded onto a steamship, police in white summer uniforms standing by; wooden houses, beached fishing boats and the snowy Tateyama mountains across the bay. Taishō-period watercolour sketch, soft dusk light, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-washington-naval: 1922, Washington, D.C.: inside the Memorial Continental Hall, a neoclassical auditorium with white columns, delegations of Britain, the United States, Japan, France and Italy seated around a long U-shaped table covered in green baize, papers and inkwells, press and spectators in the galleries; winter light through tall windows, all figures small and seen from the gallery. Early 1920s illustrated magazine lithograph, muted greens and creams. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-kanto-earthquake: 1923, Tokyo: the aftermath of the great earthquake seen from the hills above, a vast flattened district of burned wooden houses with only brick chimneys and a few concrete buildings standing, smoke drifting from smouldering ruins under an orange-grey sky; survivors with bundles and handcarts trek along a cracked road, a tram line twisted, the Sumida River beyond. Taishō-period watercolour sketch, ash greys and rust, distant small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-peace-preservation: 1925, Tokyo: a street outside a ward office where men of all classes, office clerks in suits and bowler hats, workers in short coats and farmers in kimono, queue to register as voters; across the street a pair of uniformed police in dark coats and sabres watch from a corner beside a newspaper stand, a tram and electric poles behind. Taishō-period watercolour illustration with ink line, quiet muted colours, no legible signs. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-manchukuo: 1932, Changchun in Northeast China: a cold March day at a modest government compound by the railway, Japanese Kwantung Army officers in khaki greatcoats and Chinese officials in long gowns and Western suits standing in ranks in front of a plain brick building, a slim figure in a dark Western suit far away on the steps, soldiers holding back a small watching crowd; bare trees and a steam train. Republican-era woodcut print, stark black and white. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-february-26: 1936, Tokyo: deep snow in the government quarter at dawn, soldiers in khaki greatcoats and steel helmets with rifles holding a snow-covered street barricade in front of a stone government building, a machine gun behind sandbags, footprints in the snow, the dark silhouette of the Diet building rising in the distance through falling snow; no casualties shown. Shōwa-era watercolour illustration, cold blue-grey and white palette. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-marco-polo-bridge: 1937, Lugou Bridge southwest of Beijing: a long grey stone bridge of eleven arches with rows of small carved stone lions on its balustrades crosses the shallow Yongding River on a July night, the walled town of Wanping nearby; Chinese soldiers in grey uniforms hold positions on the bridge while tiny flashes of rifle fire show far off in the dark fields. Republican-era woodcut print in the Lu Xun woodcut movement style, black and white with moonlight. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-nanjing-massacre: 1937, Nanjing: a December view of the massive grey Ming city wall and a great arched gate under a dark winter sky, columns of black smoke rising from burning districts within the city, the gate empty and silent, a few small refugees with bundles walking away along a frozen road; no bodies shown, only the scarred wall and smoke. Republican-era woodcut print in the Lu Xun woodcut movement style, black and white, sombre and restrained. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-tripartite-pact: 1940, Berlin: a September day in the vast marble hall of the Reich Chancellery, uniformed officers and diplomats in dark suits stand in rows around a long table where three men sit signing documents, photographers and newsreel cameras on tripods along the wall, tall windows with heavy curtains; everyone seen from the far end of the hall, small and anonymous, no symbols or flags shown. Neutral 1940s illustrated news lithograph, grey and sepia tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-midway: 1942, the open Pacific near Midway Atoll: a Japanese aircraft carrier with a wooden flight deck burning on the horizon under a June sky, a column of black smoke rising, escorting destroyers circling and American dive bombers small overhead, white spray from near misses on the deep blue sea; everything seen from a great distance. Mid-twentieth-century documentary watercolour, ocean blues and smoke greys, no visible casualties. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-surrender: 1945, Tokyo Bay: the deck of the battleship USS Missouri on 2 September, rows of Allied officers in khaki and white uniforms and sailors crowding the turrets and rails, a small group of Japanese delegates in formal morning coats and top hats and army uniforms standing before a green-covered table with documents, the grey fleet anchored across the bay and Mount Fuji faint in the haze. Documentary watercolour, overcast greys, all figures small. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-okinawa: 1945, Okinawa: a view from the sea toward the green coral island under an overcast spring sky, hundreds of American landing ships and grey warships offshore, smoke rising from the ridges inland and the ruined stone walls of Shuri castle on the distant heights, civilians in plain clothes seen tiny on a beach road; no casualties shown, everything distant. Restrained documentary watercolour, muted greens and smoke greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-tokyo-trial: 1946, Ichigaya, Tokyo: the converted auditorium of the former army ministry, the Tokyo war-crimes tribunal in session. A raised bench of judges in black robes beneath a row of Allied flags: United States, Britain, the Republic of China (red field, blue canton with a white sun; NOT the red five-star flag of the People's Republic, which did not yet exist), Soviet Union, France, the Netherlands, Australia. Defendants in suits sit in a dock with translation headphones, white-helmeted military police behind, lawyers at tables, a press gallery under film lights. Muted documentary watercolour, no recognisable faces, all writing illegible. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-astro-boy: 1963, Tokyo: an evening in a small family living room of a wooden house, parents and three children in casual clothes kneeling on tatami around a low table, gathered in front of a boxy black-and-white television set on legs, its screen glowing with an indistinct cartoon figure flying among stars; rice bowls on the table and a sliding door open to the narrow lane outside. Gentle Shōwa-era watercolour illustration, warm lamplight. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-shinkansen: 1964, near Tokyo: a sleek white and blue bullet train with a rounded nose speeds along an elevated track across a plain of rice paddies on an autumn morning, small farmhouses and power lines below, the snow-capped cone of Mount Fuji rising in the distance under a clear sky, a few farmers looking up from the fields. Muted documentary gouache illustration, clear blues and autumn golds, crisp shapes. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-china-normalization: 1972, Beijing: the Great Hall of the People in September, a vast reception hall with high ceilings, chandeliers and red carpet, two delegations of Chinese and Japanese officials in dark suits and Mao suits seated at a long table with documents and small paired national flags, photographers crowding behind a rope; everyone seen from the far end of the hall, small and anonymous. Muted documentary gouache illustration, restrained warm palette. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-peace-friendship-treaty: 1978, Beijing: a signing ceremony in a large hall of the Great Hall of the People in August, two diplomats in dark suits seated at a long green-covered table signing leather-bound treaty folders, rows of Chinese and Japanese officials standing behind them, small national flags on the table and press photographers in front; seen from a distance, no recognisable faces. Muted documentary watercolour, soft greens and creams. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-kyoto-protocol: 1997, Kyoto: the modernist Kyoto International Conference Hall with its sloping trapezoid concrete forms beside a pond and wooded hills on a December evening; inside a vast plenary hall, rows of delegates from many nations at long desks with microphones and translation headphones, a podium far in front, seen from the back of the hall, nobody recognisable. Neutral documentary gouache illustration, cool blues and warm hall lights. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-tokyo-olympics-2020: 2021, Tokyo: the new Japan National Stadium at night, its wooden-louvred eaves and green planted terraces lit, the bowl of empty multicoloured seats almost entirely without spectators, tiny athletes running on the red track far below under bright floodlights, a few officials in masks at the trackside; the city skyline glowing beyond. Neutral documentary watercolour, quiet night palette, no recognisable people. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
jp-slim-moon: 2024, the surface of the Moon: a small boxy Japanese lunar lander with gold foil and solar cells rests tilted on its nose on the grey slope of a crater, rocks and fine dust around it, a tiny wheeled rover nearby, the black sky above with the blue Earth hanging low on the horizon; no people present. Precise documentary gouache illustration, stark lunar greys and deep black, soft Earthlight. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-dangun-legend: Legendary age, near Pyongyang: a mythic mountain landscape with a great sandalwood tree on a summit wrapped in clouds, a bear and a tiger sitting at the mouth of a cave below with bundles of mugwort and garlic, a heavenly figure in flowing robes descending with attendants of wind, rain and cloud; pine ridges and a river valley stretching away. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, ochre, red and black on plaster, flowing cloud motifs. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-samhan: c. 100 BCE, near Iksan in southwestern Korea: a walled village of thatched round and rectangular houses within an earthen rampart and wooden palisade, tall wooden poles topped with carved birds at the gate, farmers in white hemp clothing tending rice paddies, a bronze-bell ritual with a shaman by a sacred grove, low hills behind. Painted in the manner of an early Korean mural, earthy ochres and ink line on plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-gaya-founded: 42 CE, Gimhae on the south coast of Korea: on the round summit of Gujibong hill, a gathering of village chiefs in hemp robes with feathered caps and their people singing and dancing around a sacred spot, a golden box wrapped in red cloth descending on a purple cord from the clouds; the river delta, thatched villages and the sea spread below. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo-era tomb mural, ochre and red on plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-byeonhan-iron: c. 200 CE, Gimhae on the Nakdong River delta: smiths at a riverside settlement pump bellows at clay furnaces and hammer red-hot iron into flat axe-shaped ingots stacked in bundles; traders load them into wooden boats bound for the commanderies and for Wa ships with rowers at the shore, thatched houses on the hill behind. Painted in the manner of an early Korean tomb mural, ochre, red and charcoal on plaster, lively figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-goi-reform: 260, Wiryeseong near the Han River (present Seoul): a palace compound of timber halls with thatched and early tiled roofs within packed-earth walls; officials stand in ranks in the courtyard wearing robes in colours of purple, crimson and blue with silver flower ornaments on their caps, a king seated far back in the hall with attendants, the river and hills beyond.
