Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, mineral reds and ochres on plaster, fine line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-buddhism-goguryeo: 372, Gungnae on the Yalu River (present Ji'an): a monk in robes arrives at the stone-walled capital with an envoy party from Former Qin, attendants carrying a gilt-bronze Buddha image and lacquered boxes of scriptures; Goguryeo nobles in spotted robes and feathered caps receive them at the palace gate, stepped stone tombs and pine-covered mountains around the city. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, ochre, red and green on plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-beopheung-code: 520, Gyeongju: in a palace courtyard of the Silla capital, officials stand in rows by rank wearing robes of purple, scarlet, blue and yellow with ornamented caps, while a minister reads from a long scroll before a king seated on a raised platform under a canopy; great earth burial mounds rise beyond the palace walls in spring light. Painted in the manner of a Three Kingdoms-period Korean mural, mineral colours and ink on plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-muryeong: 523, Gongju: a royal funeral procession of Baekje courtiers in robes and gold-ornamented caps carries a lacquered wooden coffin toward an arched brick tomb chamber built into a hillside, its bricks moulded with lotus patterns in Southern Dynasties style, a stone guardian beast placed at the entrance; mourners with banners, the Geum River and wooded hills behind. Painted in the manner of a Baekje-era mural, soft ochre, red and green on plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-ichadon: 527, Gyeongju: a palace courtyard of the Silla capital where courtiers and townspeople in robes gather in awe as white flowers rain down from the sky and the earth trembles, a young court official standing calm in plain white robes before the king's pavilion; behind them a forest grove where a temple is planned, earth burial mounds beyond. Painted in the style of a Goryeo Buddhist painting, gold line on dark silk, soft red and green, serene mood. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-sabi: 538, Sabi (present Buyeo): a new capital rising on the bend of the Baengma River below Busosan hill, palace halls with grey tiled roofs and a five-storey stone pagoda under construction, workers hauling timber; at the riverbank a boat carrying monks in robes and envoys with sutra boxes and Buddha images sets off toward the sea for Japan. Painted in the manner of a Three Kingdoms-period Korean mural, soft mineral colours on plaster, gentle hills. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-daegaya: 562, Goryeong: the hills of the Daegaya capital crowned with rows of great burial mounds, an earthen fortress on the ridge, Silla soldiers in iron lamellar armour with spears and shields, mounted officers with stirrups at their head, entering through the gate as Gaya defenders lay down arms; thatched houses and smoke in the valley below. Painted in the manner of a Three Kingdoms-period Korean tomb mural, ochre, red and black on plaster, small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-hwarang: 576, near Gyeongju: a band of aristocratic Silla youths in bright silk robes with flowers in their caps ride and practise archery in a wooded mountain valley, others sit on rocks by a stream listening to a monk in grey robes, a few play flutes, pines and blossoming trees on the slopes, Namsan mountain behind. Painted in the style of a Three Kingdoms-period Korean mural, mineral colours with fine ink line, lively figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-cheomseongdae: 633, Gyeongju: a bottle-shaped stone tower of curved granite courses with a square window halfway up and a square frame at its top stands on a plain beside the palace, at night under a sky full of stars and a crescent moon; a court astronomer in robes climbs a ladder to the window while officials with lamps and a scribe wait below, earth burial mounds in the background. Painted in the manner of a Goryeo-era Buddhist painting, deep blue night with gold stars. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-yeon-gaesomun: 642, Pyongyang: the walled Goguryeo capital at night seen from across the Taedong River, torches moving along the ramparts and around the palace gate, a column of armoured soldiers with spears massed in the outer court under a commander on horseback, smoke rising faintly over the palace halls; no violence shown, everything distant and dark. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, ochre and black on plaster with flickering red torchlight. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-silla-tang-alliance: 648, Chang'an: the Tang palace hall with vermilion pillars and green-glazed tiles, a Silla envoy in a Silla court robe with attendants bowing low on the stone terrace before the emperor seated on a dais far in the background among officials in Tang robes and black futou caps; gifts of silk and gold set on mats, the grand courtyard with guards in armour. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-silla-surrenders: 935, Gyeongju: a long procession of carriages, oxcarts and officials in robes leaving the Silla capital along a road through autumn fields toward the north, the king travelling in a curtained carriage, townspeople weeping by the roadside; behind them the palace roofs, the stone pagodas and great burial mounds of a thousand-year capital under a pale autumn sky. Painted in the style of Goryeo Buddhist painting, muted gold, red and green on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-myocheong: 1135, Pyongyang: the walled city on the Taedong River besieged in winter, Goryeo government troops in lamellar armour camped in tents on the snowy plain with banners and siege ladders, rebels watching from the battlements, smoke from cooking fires and the frozen river in the foreground; all figures small and distant. Painted in the manner of a Goryeo-period painting, ink and muted colour on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-metal-type: 1234, Ganghwa Island: a royal printing workshop in a timber hall of the island refuge capital, artisans casting small bronze characters in sand moulds over a charcoal furnace, others setting the tiny metal types into a frame, inking it and pressing sheets of mulberry paper, freshly printed pages drying on lines, the type too small to read; through the open doors, the walled island and the sea. Painted in the style of a Goryeo-period painting, ink and soft colour on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-samguk-yusa: 1281, Ingaksa temple in the hills of Gunwi: an elderly monk in grey robes sits at a low desk in a timber temple hall with a tiled roof, surrounded by piles of old bound books and scrolls gathered from across the land, a young monk grinding ink beside him; through the open lattice doors, a stone pagoda, autumn maples and a valley with a stream. Painted in the style of a Goryeo Buddhist painting, fine gold line and soft red and green on silk, no legible writing. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-gongmin: 1356, Gaegyeong (present Kaesong): the Goryeo royal palace on the slopes of Songaksan, courtiers in Goryeo robes with Korean topknots and black caps replacing Mongol braids and dress, gathered in the stone courtyard, soldiers in lamellar armour marching out through the gate with banners toward the north, a king seated far back in the hall; pine-covered mountain behind. Goryeo-period painting, ink and mineral colour on silk, fine line, small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-cotton: 1363, Sancheong in the hills of southern Korea: a scholar-official in a Goryeo robe and black cap kneels with his father-in-law in a small walled garden beside a thatched farmhouse, planting a few precious cotton seeds in a carefully dug row; villagers watch over the fence, white cotton bolls on a single surviving plant, terraced fields and blue mountains behind. Painted in the style of Joseon-era genre painting in the manner of Kim Hong-do, light ink and colour on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-gwajeon: 1391, Gaegyeong (present Kaesong): a stone-paved square before a government office of the Goryeo capital where officials in robes and black caps throw bundles of old land registers onto a large bonfire, the flames and smoke rising high for days, clerks carrying more ledgers out from a storehouse, a crowd of townspeople and soldiers watching; Songaksan mountain behind. Joseon-era documentary painting in uigwe style, ink and colour on paper, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-kangnido: 1402, Hanyang (present Seoul): inside a scholarly office of the new Joseon capital, officials in robes and black gat hats kneel around a huge silk map spread across the floor, painting coastlines and rivers of Asia, Europe and Africa in blue and ochre with Korea drawn large, Chinese and Islamic source maps beside them, place names reduced to unreadable dots; Bugaksan mountain through the open doors. Joseon-period painting, ink and mineral colour on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-cheugugi: 1441, Gyeongbokgung palace in Hanyang: in a stone-paved courtyard after summer rain, an official in a red robe and black cap kneels beside a bronze cylinder rain gauge on a carved granite pedestal, measuring the water with a ruler while a scribe records it; other officials hold umbrellas, the palace halls with curved tiled roofs and Bugaksan mountain misty behind. Joseon court documentary painting in uigwe style, fine ink and soft mineral colour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-yi-hwang: 1568, Dosan near Andong: a small Confucian study hall of plain wood with a tiled roof beside the Nakdong River, an elderly scholar in a white robe and black gat hat sits on the wooden floor painting neat diagrams on large sheets of paper, a pupil grinding ink, lotus pond and plum trees in the garden, misty hills and river beyond. Joseon literati painting, ink and light colour on paper, quiet and spare, the diagrams abstract circles and lines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-daedong: 1608, near Hanyang: a riverside granary on the Han River where farmers in white hemp clothes and straw hats unload sacks of rice from ox carts and boats, officials in robes and black gat hats at a table weighing the sacks on scales and recording them, storehouses with tiled roofs, sailing barges at the wharf and mountains behind. Joseon genre painting in the manner of Kim Hong-do, lively ink line with light colour on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-donguibogam: 1613, Hanyang: a royal medical office of the Joseon court, physicians in robes and black caps grinding herbs in stone mortars and weighing roots on small scales, shelves of small wooden drawers and dried plants hanging from beams, while craftsmen in the next room print the thick volumes from carved wooden blocks and stack the bound books; a courtyard with medicinal plants outside. Joseon genre painting in the manner of Kim Hong-do, ink and light colour on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-sangpyeong: 1678, a market town near Hanyang: a busy open-air market of thatched stalls, merchants and farmers in white clothes and gat hats paying with strings of round copper coins with square holes for rice, cloth, salt and pottery, a peddler with a back-frame, a money-changer counting coins on a straw mat; hills and a pavilion behind. Joseon genre painting in the manner of Kim Hong-do, lively brushwork, light colour on paper, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-hong-gyeong-nae: 1811, Jeongju in North Pyongan: the stone-walled town on a winter plain, besieged by government troops in Joseon military uniforms with spears, matchlocks and banners camped around it, peasants and merchants in white padded clothes defending the battlements; snow on the fields, smoke from fires, everything seen from a distant hill. Joseon documentary painting in uigwe style, ink and muted colour on paper, small figures, no casualties shown. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-donghak: 1860, near Gyeongju: on a hillside in spring, a scholar in white robes and black gat hat sits under a pine tree beside a modest thatched pavilion, villagers, farmers and women in white hanbok gathering around him, some bowing, a bowl of clear water set on a low table; the Gyeongju valley and old burial mounds in the hazy distance. Joseon genre painting, soft ink line and light colour on paper, calm mood. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-daewongun: 1865, Hanyang: the rebuilding of Gyeongbokgung palace, thousands of labourers in white clothes hauling great timber beams and stones on ropes and wooden rollers, carpenters raising the frame of the vast throne hall, officials in robes and black gat hats supervising from a platform, banners of the work gangs fluttering, Bugaksan mountain behind. Joseon court documentary painting in uigwe style, fine ink and colour on paper, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-byeongin: 1866, Ganghwa Island: French steam warships with masts and funnels anchored in the narrow strait, boats landing marines in dark uniforms below a mountain fortress; on the ramparts of Jeongjok mountain fortress Korean tiger hunters and soldiers in Joseon uniforms with matchlocks wait behind stone walls in autumn, smoke drifting over the hills, all figures small. Joseon documentary painting, ink and colour on paper, or nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving style. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-imo: 1882, Hanyang: a summer street of the Joseon capital where crowds of soldiers in faded uniforms and townspeople in white clothes surge toward a walled government compound, smoke rising beyond its tiled roofs; in the background Qing soldiers in tunics with banners arrive through the city gate, everything seen from a distant hill. Nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine cross-hatching, no casualties shown. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-gapsin: 1884, Hanyang: a December night in the palace district, the new post office building lit by a fire on its roof, guards and courtiers in robes rushing through a palace gate, Qing soldiers in padded tunics and Japanese legation troops in dark uniforms facing each other across a snowy courtyard, lanterns and torches casting light; all figures small, no casualties shown. Dianshizhai Pictorial lithograph style, fine line, dense composition. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-gabo: 1894, Hanyang: a government courtyard where officials, some in traditional robes and gat hats and others in new Western-style uniforms, read a proclamation to a crowd of commoners in white clothes, former slaves and craftsmen listening, a clerk burning old status registers in a brazier; Japanese soldiers stand at the gate, the palace roofs behind. Nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine line with sepia tone, no legible writing. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-independence-club: 1896, Hanyang: a busy street near the West Gate where a newsboy hands out sheets of a new newspaper to townspeople in white hanbok and black gat hats, scholars and merchants reading the pages, a small printing shop with a hand press visible through an open door; the old Yeongeunmun gate in the distance, telegraph poles. Late nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine cross-hatching, the newspaper text unreadable. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-debt-movement: 1907, Daegu: a crowded courtyard of a public hall, men in white hanbok and gat hats laying down tobacco pipes and pouches in a heap, women in long skirts donating silver rings and hairpins into a wooden box, schoolboys bringing coins, a clerk recording gifts at a table; tiled-roof houses and the hills of Daegu behind. Early twentieth-century documentary watercolour sketch, soft daylight, no legible writing. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-an-jung-geun: 1909, Harbin: the railway station platform on an October morning, a Russian steam train with a special carriage standing at the platform, Russian soldiers in long grey greatcoats lined up in an honour guard, officials in frock coats and top hats and a crowd of onlookers in winter coats, brick station buildings and bare trees; everything seen from far along the platform, no violence shown. Early twentieth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, sepia tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-land-survey: 1912, a Korean village near Seoul: Japanese colonial surveyors in dark uniforms and peaked caps set up a theodolite on a tripod among rice paddies, assistants with measuring poles and chains, while Korean farmers in white clothes and straw hats watch uneasily from the field banks; thatched houses, a village shrine tree and bare hills. Early twentieth-century documentary watercolour, soft muted colours, small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-provisional-government: 1919, Shanghai French Concession: a narrow lane of grey brick shikumen terraced houses with carved stone gateways, a small group of Korean men in dark Western suits and long gowns gathered in a plain upstairs room around a table with papers and an oil lamp, the window open onto plane trees and lane rooftops; spring evening light. 1930s Shanghai lithograph illustration style, muted browns and greys, quiet mood. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-yun-bong-gil: 1932, Hongkou Park, Shanghai: a large crowd of Japanese military officers in uniform and civilians in formal clothes on an April morning around a decorated reviewing stand under trees, soldiers in ranks on the lawn; a puff of smoke rising over the platform as the crowd turns, everything seen from far across the park, no casualties shown. Republican-era woodcut print in the Lu Xun woodcut movement style, black and white. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-soshi-kaimei: 1940, Seoul: inside a colonial government office, a queue of Korean men and women in white hanbok and dark Western clothes waiting before a long wooden counter where Japanese clerks in uniforms record registration forms, the forms unreadable, bare plastered walls and ceiling fans; through the window, a schoolyard where children stand in rows before a teacher. Late 1930s lithograph illustration, muted greys and browns. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-liberation-army: 1940, Chongqing: a terraced hillside city above the Yangtze in autumn fog, a small courtyard of a brick building where a few dozen Korean volunteers in khaki uniforms and caps stand in ranks before officers in Western suits and uniforms, Chinese soldiers and townspeople watching at the gate; wooden stilted houses and the river below. Republican-era woodcut print, strong black lines with a single ochre tone. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-rok-founded: 1948, Seoul: a hot August day in front of the domed granite colonial capitol building, a large crowd of men in white shirts and hanbok and women in long skirts gathered in the plaza with many Korean flags, dignitaries on a distant stage, American soldiers and Korean police lining the street, Bugaksan mountain behind. Muted documentary watercolour, summer haze, all figures small, no portraits. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-dprk-founded: 1948, Pyongyang: a September day on the bank of the Taedong River, a plain public square before a modest government building, a crowd of citizens in white clothes and workers in caps standing in orderly rows with flags, a distant stage, the river and low hills beyond; everything seen from far away, no portraits. Neutral muted documentary watercolour, soft greys and greens. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-jeju-uprising: 1948, Jeju Island: the broad green slopes of Hallasan volcano under a heavy grey sky, villages of thatched stone houses with black basalt walls scattered across the foothills, thin plumes of smoke rising from distant villages, oreum cones and the sea beyond; no people visible, a quiet mourning landscape. Restrained documentary watercolour, muted greens, greys and black volcanic stone. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-incheon: 1950, Incheon harbour: grey landing ships and warships crowd the channel at high tide in September, landing craft heading for a sea wall where marines climb ladders, smoke rising over the harbour island and waterfront buildings, mud flats exposed in the distance, aircraft overhead; everything seen from far out at sea, no casualties shown. Mid-twentieth-century documentary watercolour, smoke greys and sea blues. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-china-rok: 1992, Beijing: a guest-house hall at the Diaoyutai state compound in August, two diplomats in dark suits seated at a long table signing documents in leather folders, small Chinese and South Korean flags on the table, officials standing behind and photographers in front; seen from the back of the room at a distance, no recognisable faces. Neutral documentary watercolour, soft creams and greens. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-parasite: 2020, Los Angeles: the Hollywood theatre complex on a February night, a long red carpet lined with photographers and floodlights, the warm-lit facade and palm trees against a dark blue sky, small anonymous guests in evening dress walking far away; a giant golden statuette shape glows at the theatre entrance. Neutral documentary gouache illustration, night blues and golds, no recognisable people. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
kr-nuri: 2022, Naro Space Center on the southern coast near Goheung: a white three-stage rocket lifts off from its launch pad on a June afternoon on a column of bright flame and white smoke, the umbilical tower beside it, green forested hills and the blue sea with small islands around, a few spectators far away on a beach. Documentary gouache illustration, clear blues and greens, crisp shapes, no text or flags readable. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-three-sisters: c. 2500 BCE, the Valley of Oaxaca: a small field of early maize with climbing bean vines twining up the stalks and broad squash leaves covering the ground, villagers in woven fibre clothing tending the plants with digging sticks, a woman grinding maize on a stone metate beside a pole-and-thatch hut, dry hills and cacti around. Painted in the style of a Mixtec codex, flat bright colours on a pale deerskin ground with bold black outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-first-pottery: c. 2300 BCE, the Tehuacán Valley in Puebla: a small settlement of pole-and-thatch huts among columnar cacti, a woman shaping simple round-bottomed clay bowls while another tends an open firing pit with smoke rising, finished brownish vessels on a mat beside stone grinding tools and baskets, mountains in the dry season light. Painted in the style of a Mixtec codex, flat earth colours with bold black outlines on a pale ground. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-san-jose-mogote: c. 1500 BCE, San José Mogote in the Valley of Oaxaca: a growing village of wattle-and-daub houses on a rise above maize fields, a lime-plastered public building on a low platform at its centre, craftsmen working magnetite mirrors and shell ornaments in courtyards, villagers carrying water jars; the green valley and mountains around. Painted in the style of a Mixtec codex, flat bright colours on a pale ground with bold black outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-tlatilco: c. 1400 BCE, Tlatilco on the shore of Lake Texcoco: a farming village of thatched houses among maize fields beside the reedy lake, a family placing small painted pottery figurines and polished bowls with offerings into a grave pit beside a house, mourners standing quietly around in woven garments, canoes on the water and volcanoes on the horizon. Painted in the style of an Aztec codex, flat bright colours on a pale ground with black outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-cuello: c. 1200 BCE, Cuello in northern Belize: a small early Maya farming village in lowland forest, oval thatched houses raised on low plastered platforms around a courtyard, people in cotton cloth grinding maize and carrying simple red pottery jars, a garden of maize and cacao trees at the edge of the tall jungle. Painted in the style of a Maya mural like Bonampak, warm red, ochre and Maya blue on a plaster ground, flowing outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-chalcatzingo: c. 800 BCE, Chalcatzingo in Morelos: two great rocky hills rising from a dry valley, on the cliff face a large carved relief of a seated figure inside a cave-like mouth with scrolls of rain clouds, carvers on a wooden scaffold chiselling the stone with hammerstones, villagers below carrying offerings; terraced maize fields and a village of thatched houses. Painted in the manner of Olmec-era cave painting, earthy reds and ochres on stone. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-nakbe: c. 800 BCE, Nakbe in the Mirador Basin of Petén: hundreds of workers in cotton loincloths and tunics carry limestone blocks and baskets of rubble up a huge rising platform in the tropical forest, a plastered temple taking shape on top, others burning limestone to make plaster, the green forest canopy stretching to the horizon. Painted in the style of a Maya mural, warm reds, ochres and Maya blue on plaster, flowing black outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-maya-script: c. 300 BCE, San Bartolo in Petén: inside a small room of a pyramid temple lit by torchlight, a Maya painter in a cotton wrap applies colour to a wall mural of the maize god among flowering plants, with a short column of glyphs drawn as abstract unreadable shapes, pots of red, yellow and blue paint and brushes at his feet, an assistant holding the torch. Painted in the style of the San Bartolo murals, Maya red, yellow and blue on cream plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-joya-de-ceren: c. 600, Joya de Cerén in the Zapotitán valley: a small Maya farming village of adobe and thatch houses, maize and agave gardens and storehouses with pots and tools, its inhabitants hurrying away along a path, as a great dark cloud of volcanic ash rises from a vent nearby and grey ash begins to fall over the fields in the evening light. Painted in the style of a Maya mural, ochres and greys with Maya blue sky, flowing outlines, small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-uxmal: c. 900, Uxmal in the Puuc hills of Yucatán: the steep oval Pyramid of the Magician rising above a plaza, beside a long palace with stone mosaic facades of lattice patterns, stepped frets and rain-god masks with curling noses; Maya nobles in feathered headdresses and cotton capes cross the plaza, low scrub forest around under a hot blue sky. Painted in the style of a Maya mural like Bonampak, red, ochre and Maya blue, crisp black outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-dresden-codex: c. 1200, the Yucatán Peninsula: inside a cool masonry room of a Maya town, a scribe in a cotton mantle kneels on a mat painting a long screen-folded bark-paper book coated in white lime, figures of gods and rows of dots and bars drawn as abstract unreadable shapes, shell pots of red and black paint beside him, an astronomer pointing out of the doorway to Venus bright in the dawn sky. Painted in the style of a Maya codex, flat red, black and blue on a cream ground. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-paquime: c. 1200, Paquimé in Chihuahua: a sprawling town of multi-storey adobe buildings with T-shaped doorways in a desert valley, traders arriving on foot with loads of copper bells and marine shells, scarlet macaws kept in adobe pens with round stone-ringed openings, a ball court and water channels, mountains under a wide sky. Painted in the style of Mesoamerican codex art, flat earth reds, macaw scarlet and turquoise with bold black outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-kiche-kingdom: c. 1400, Q'umarkaj in the Guatemalan highlands: a fortified city on a plateau ringed by deep ravines, white plastered temples on stepped pyramids, a ball court and palaces around a plaza, K'iche' lords in feathered headdresses and jaguar-skin capes holding a council, pine-covered mountains and drifting cloud. Painted in the style of a highland Maya codex, flat bright red, green and blue with black outlines on a pale ground. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-aztec-sun-stone: 1502, Tenochtitlan: in a sculptors' yard near the great temple precinct, Aztec stone carvers in white cotton mantles work with stone chisels on a huge flat basalt disc lying on the ground, its concentric rings of calendar symbols and a central face emerging, others painting it red and ochre; the twin-shrine pyramid and canals of the island city behind under a clear sky. Painted in the style of an Aztec codex, flat bright colours with bold black outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-guadalupe: 1531, Tepeyac hill north of Mexico City: a December dawn on the rocky dry slope, an Indigenous man in a coarse cactus-fibre cloak gathers an armful of red Castilian roses blooming impossibly among cacti and frost, a soft golden light glowing over the hilltop; the lake and the Spanish town on the old Aztec causeway far below. Painted in the manner of a sixteenth-century colonial Mexican oil painting, warm gold and rose tones, small distant figure. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-viceroyalty: 1535, Mexico City: the great central plaza of the new Spanish city built over the ruins of Tenochtitlan, a viceroy's procession of mounted Spanish nobles in plumed hats, armoured guards with halberds and friars in brown habits entering before a stone palace, crowds of Nahua people in white mantles watching, canals and the volcanoes on the horizon. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century colonial Mexican manuscript illustration, ink and watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-printing-press: 1539, Mexico City: a small whitewashed workshop off a colonial street, a printer in a dark doublet pulling the lever of a wooden screw press while an assistant inks the type with leather balls, an Indigenous apprentice in a white mantle hanging freshly printed sheets to dry on lines, a Franciscan friar examining a bound book, the text unreadable; sunlight through an arched doorway. Colonial-era woodcut illustration style, black line with light watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-zacatecas-silver: 1546, Zacatecas: a rugged mountain called La Bufa above a dry ravine, Spanish prospectors in doublets and helmets and Indigenous workers with baskets and picks at the entrance of a mine shaft, ore being crushed by mules turning a stone mill, rough adobe huts and smoke from a smelting furnace, cacti on the hillsides under a vast sky. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century colonial Mexican manuscript, ink and watercolour, small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-landa-mani: 1562, Maní in Yucatán: the stone-walled courtyard of a Franciscan friary with a whitewashed church facade, a great bonfire burning in the plaza where friars in grey-brown habits throw folded bark-paper books and carved painted figures into the flames, Spanish soldiers in helmets standing guard, Maya townspeople in white cotton watching in grief from a distance; smoke rising into a pale sky above the flat scrub forest. Sixteenth-century colonial manuscript illustration style, ink and watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-sor-juana: 1691, Mexico City: a nun's cell in the convent of San Jerónimo, a tall room lined with shelves of leather-bound books, globes, a lute and scientific instruments, a nun in a white habit and black veil seated at a writing desk by a window with quill and inkwell, seen from behind, letters on the desk unreadable; through the window, the tiled domes of the city. Colonial Mexican oil painting in the late Baroque manner, warm browns and soft light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-nojpeten: 1697, Lake Petén Itzá: the small island city of Nojpetén crowded with white plastered temples and thatched houses rising from the blue lake, a Spanish oared galley with armed soldiers in helmets and breastplates approaching across the water, Itza canoes scattering, thick tropical forest on the shores and morning mist; all figures small, no casualties shown. Colonial-era manuscript illustration, ink and watercolour with deep greens and lake blue. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-bourbon-reforms: c. 1767, Mexico City: inside the royal customs house with stone arches around a courtyard, royal officials in powdered wigs, tricorne hats and embroidered coats inspect bales and barrels arriving on mule trains, clerks at desks weighing silver bars and counting coins into chests marked with royal arms, merchants in capes arguing, Indigenous porters unloading tobacco. Colonial Mexican oil painting in casta-painting style, fine detail, warm earth colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-central-america-independence: 1821, Guatemala City: a September morning in the main plaza before the arcaded Palace of the Captains General, a crowd of townspeople, Creole gentlemen in tailcoats and cocked hats and Indigenous people in woven clothing gathered while church bells ring from the cathedral, officials appearing on the palace balcony, rockets bursting in the sky and the volcano Agua on the horizon. Early nineteenth-century Latin American engraving with hand colouring. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-federal-republic-ca: 1823, Guatemala City: a meeting hall in a colonial building with whitewashed walls and dark wooden beams, delegates of five provinces in tailcoats and high collars seated around a long table with papers, quills and candles, a blue-and-white striped banner without emblems on the wall, onlookers crowding the doorway; through the arched window, the volcanoes. Early nineteenth-century Latin American engraving, fine line with soft watercolour wash. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-caste-war: 1847, near Valladolid in Yucatán: Maya peasant fighters in white cotton clothes and straw hats, armed with machetes and old muskets, advance through dense low scrub forest toward a colonial town whose church towers rise above a stone wall, smoke rising from burning haciendas and henequen fields in the distance; all figures small, no casualties shown. Nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine cross-hatching. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-guadalupe-hidalgo: 1848, Villa de Guadalupe north of Mexico City: a February day in a quiet room of the colonial church precinct, Mexican commissioners in dark frock coats and an American envoy seated at a table signing papers by candlelight, a plain whitewashed wall and a map of Mexico rolled on the table; through the window, the domed basilica and dry hills of Tepeyac. Nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine line with sepia tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-walker-nicaragua: 1856, Granada on Lake Nicaragua: the colonial town of pastel adobe houses, red-tiled roofs and a cathedral beside the great lake, American filibusters in red flannel shirts and slouch hats with rifles occupying the plaza while Nicaraguan townspeople watch from arcades; the volcano Mombacho rising behind and steamships on the lake. Nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine cross-hatching, warm tropical light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-la-reforma: 1857, Mexico City: the hall of the National Palace where elected deputies in black frock coats and cravats stand around a long table to swear to the new constitution, a bound document on a velvet cushion, spectators crowding the galleries, a Mexican tricolour flag hanging from a pillar; tall windows onto the Zócalo and the cathedral towers. Nineteenth-century Mexican lithograph, fine line and soft grey tones, figures small. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-reform-war: c. 1860, central Mexico: a dusty plain under a dramatic sky, Liberal infantry in blue uniforms and kepis with muskets advancing across the field and Conservative troops with artillery holding a stone hacienda wall, smoke from cannon drifting across maguey fields, a church dome and mountains on the horizon; everything seen from a distant hill, no casualties shown. Nineteenth-century Mexican lithograph, fine line with sepia wash. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-second-empire: 1864, Chapultepec Castle in Mexico City: an imperial couple arrives at the hilltop palace in an open gilded carriage, Austrian and French officers in plumed helmets and Mexican lancers escorting them up the winding road between old cypress trees, a crowd of townspeople watching, the valley of Mexico and the snowy volcanoes spread beyond. Mid-nineteenth-century European history painting in oil, cool silvery light, small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-united-fruit: c. 1900, Puerto Limón on the Caribbean coast of Costa Rica: a long wooden pier where Afro-Caribbean labourers in shirtsleeves carry great green banana stems on their shoulders from a steam train into the hold of a white steamship, endless banana plantations behind the railway, palm trees and tin-roofed warehouses under a hot sky. Early twentieth-century documentary watercolour, lush greens and harbour blues, small busy figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-panama-independence: 1903, Panama City: a November day in the plaza of the old walled town by the Pacific, a crowd of townspeople in white suits and straw hats cheering before the cathedral with its pearl-shell towers, a new red, white and blue quartered flag raised on a balcony, an American gunboat anchored in the bay behind the sea wall. Early twentieth-century illustrated magazine engraving, fine line with light colour wash. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-decena-tragica: 1913, Mexico City: a February view over the downtown rooftops toward the old Ciudadela armoury, plumes of artillery smoke rising over the avenues, a shell-damaged clock tower, overturned streetcars and empty streets, a few civilians in hats hurrying past a barricade of sandbags; everything seen from a distant rooftop, no casualties shown. Early twentieth-century documentary watercolour sketch, smoky greys and ochres. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-panama-canal: 1914, the Panama Canal: a steamship passes through the vast concrete Miraflores locks, its massive steel lock gates open, electric towing locomotives on rails along the walls pulling it, workers in white shirts and hats watching from the lock edge, green tropical hills and the wide cut stretching away under a bright sky. Early twentieth-century documentary watercolour, clean greens and blues, engineering detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-muralism: 1922, Mexico City: inside the arcaded courtyard of a colonial public building, painters in overalls on tall wooden scaffolds paint a vast fresco on the wall showing Indigenous farmers, workers and maize fields in earthy colours, assistants grinding pigments and spreading fresh plaster, students and passers-by watching from the arcades. Painted as a 1920s documentary watercolour sketch, warm earth tones, artists seen from behind. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-cristero-war: 1927, Jalisco: dry hills of agave and oak under a vast sky, a band of rancheros and farmers in wide sombreros and white clothes with rifles and bandoliers riding horses along a mountain trail, a whitewashed village church with closed doors in the valley below, federal troops in khaki camped far away; all figures small. Mexican 1920s woodcut print style, bold black lines on cream paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-sandino: 1928, Las Segovias in northern Nicaragua: steep forested mountains in rain and mist, a band of guerrillas in broad-brimmed hats with rifles and machetes moving along a muddy jungle trail with pack mules, an American biplane flying low over the far valley; small thatched huts on a clearing. Republican-era style woodcut print, strong black and white with dense jungle textures, all figures small. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-pnr-founded: 1929, Querétaro: a March day at the Teatro de la República, a nineteenth-century theatre with gilded boxes, the stalls filled with delegates in dark suits and hats from all over Mexico, a long table of party leaders on the stage beneath a Mexican tricolour, journalists in the boxes; seen from the back of the theatre, all figures small. 1920s Mexican woodcut print, bold black line with a single red accent. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-cardenas-land-reform: c. 1936, the Laguna region of northern Mexico: a gathering of peasants in white clothes and straw sombreros in a cotton field, a government agrarian official handing over bundled land titles beside a truck, surveyors with a theodolite marking plots, families with children and ox ploughs, irrigation canals and dry mountains beyond. Mexican 1930s woodcut print in the style of the Taller de Gráfica Popular, bold black and white. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-bracero-program: 1943, Ciudad Juárez on the Rio Grande: a long line of young Mexican farm workers in straw hats, work shirts and carrying small bundles waits at a reception centre beside a railway yard, officials checking papers at wooden tables, a steam train waiting to take them north, the dusty desert mountains and the river bridge in the distance. 1940s documentary watercolour, sun-bleached ochres and blue sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-green-revolution: c. 1945, the Yaqui Valley near Ciudad Obregón in Sonora: a flat irrigated plain of experimental wheat plots under a hard blue sky, researchers in khaki shirts and hats crouching among rows of short-stemmed golden wheat, tagging stalks and carrying seed envelopes, Mexican farm workers with hoes, irrigation ditches and desert mountains on the horizon. Mid-twentieth-century documentary watercolour, golden wheat and sky blue. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-costa-rica-army: 1948, San José, Costa Rica: the courtyard of the old Bellavista military barracks, a crenellated fortress-like building, where a crowd of townspeople and schoolchildren in white shirts watch officials symbolically break a piece of the wall with a sledgehammer, soldiers handing over rifles stacked on a table; green hills around the city under a December sky. Muted documentary watercolour, gentle greens and creams, all figures small. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-guatemala-coup: 1954, Guatemala City: a June day over the city of low colonial houses and the green stone National Palace, a single old propeller aircraft flying low overhead with smoke rising from a distant fuel depot, quiet streets with a few people looking up, volcanoes on the horizon; everything seen from a hill, no casualties shown. Mid-twentieth-century documentary watercolour, muted greens and greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-guatemalan-civil-war: c. 1960s, the western highlands of Guatemala: a quiet Maya village of adobe houses with tiled roofs on a steep green mountainside in mist, women in handwoven huipils carrying water jars along a path, a white colonial church, and on the road far below a small line of army trucks; volcanoes and pine forest. Restrained documentary watercolour, soft muted greens and blues, all figures small and distant. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-tlatelolco-massacre: 1968, Tlatelolco in Mexico City: the Plaza de las Tres Culturas at dusk, the ruined Aztec pyramid platforms, the colonial stone church of Santiago and the modern apartment blocks around the square, a large crowd of students in the plaza seen from far away, soldiers' trucks parked on a distant avenue; no violence shown, a quiet sombre evening. Neutral muted documentary watercolour, grey-violet dusk tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-sandinista-revolution: 1979, Managua: a July day in the main plaza beside the ruined earthquake-damaged old cathedral on the shore of Lake Managua, a huge crowd of young people waving red-and-black and blue-and-white flags, fighters in olive fatigues sitting on the roofs of trucks, the volcano Momotombo on the far side of the lake; everything seen from a distance, no recognisable faces. Muted documentary gouache illustration, bright tropical light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-salvadoran-civil-war: c. 1980s, the mountains of northern El Salvador: green volcanic hills and coffee groves under a cloudy sky, a small village of adobe houses with tile roofs beside a dirt road, a column of soldiers walking far off on a ridge and a helicopter small in the sky, villagers carrying bundles along a path; no violence shown. Restrained documentary watercolour, muted greens and greys, all figures small. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-mexico-earthquake-1985: 1985, Mexico City: a September morning in the centre after the earthquake, a collapsed concrete apartment block with pancaked floors among standing buildings, dust in the air, a long human chain of volunteers in everyday clothes and helmets passing buckets of rubble from hand to hand, rescue workers with dogs and cranes; no casualties shown, all figures small. Muted documentary watercolour, dusty greys and pale sunlight. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-octavio-paz-nobel: 1990, Mexico City: a quiet book-lined study in a city apartment, shelves crowded with books in many languages, a writing desk with a typewriter, stacks of manuscripts and a pre-Columbian clay figure, a window opening onto the leafy Paseo de la Reforma at dusk; no people present. Muted documentary gouache illustration, warm lamp light and deep browns, still-life calm. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-nafta: 1994, the border crossing at Nuevo Laredo on the Rio Grande: long lines of articulated freight trucks with containers queue across a wide bridge toward customs booths, factories and warehouses on both banks, railway freight wagons on a parallel bridge, a January sky; no recognisable people, drivers seen small in cabs. Neutral documentary gouache illustration, steel greys and desert ochres. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-fox-elected: 2000, Mexico City: a July Sunday at a neighbourhood polling station set up in a school courtyard, citizens of all ages queuing with identity cards, a voter in a curtained cardboard booth, transparent ballot boxes on a table watched by officials and observers; jacaranda trees and colourful houses beyond the gate. Neutral documentary watercolour, warm daylight, no recognisable faces and no legible writing. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
mx-drug-war: c. 2007, Michoacán: a winding mountain road through avocado orchards and pine-covered hills, a convoy of military trucks and armoured pickups with soldiers in camouflage and helmets passing a small roadside town with pastel houses, farmers watching from the roadside; a hazy sky, everything seen from a distant hilltop, no violence shown. Restrained documentary watercolour, muted greens and dusty browns. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-ebla-tablets: c. 2400 BCE, Ebla in northern Syria: a palace archive room of mud-brick walls where scribes in fringed woollen kilts sit sorting thousands of small clay tablets onto wooden shelves along the walls, others writing on fresh tablets with reed styluses, porters carrying baskets of tablets in, the cuneiform marks too small to read; a courtyard of the palace with traders and bales of wool beyond. Painted in the style of an early Syrian shell-and-lapis inlay frieze like those from Ebla's palace, bright figures on dark ground. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-urukagina-reforms: c. 2350 BCE, Girsu in the state of Lagash: a temple courtyard of mud brick with reed-bundle doorposts, a ruler in a fleece kaunakes skirt standing before a crowd of farmers, fishermen, widows and orphans, officials and priests in shaven heads stepping back from tax tables, a clay cone being inscribed; date palms and irrigation canals behind. Painted in the style of a Sumerian shell-inlay frieze like the Standard of Ur, figures in rows on deep lapis blue. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-code-of-ur-nammu: c. 2100 BCE, Ur: a mud-brick courtyard of the royal palace, a scribe in a fringed robe reading aloud from a large clay tablet to a gathering of citizens, merchants and farmers, a judge seated on a stool with officials weighing silver rings on a balance scale as fines, a ziggurat rising in the background over date palms. Painted in the manner of a Sumerian shell-inlay frieze on lapis blue ground, figures in profile, the writing abstract. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-ziggurat-of-ur: c. 2090 BCE, Ur: the great stepped ziggurat of baked and mud brick rising in three terraces under construction above the flat river plain, long triple stairways converging at the front, hundreds of workers carrying bricks and bitumen baskets up ramps, a small shrine on the summit, date palms, reed houses and the Euphrates beyond. Painted in the style of a Sumerian shell-and-lapis inlay frieze, figures in profile against deep blue. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-babylonian-mathematics: c. 1800 BCE, Larsa in southern Mesopotamia: a scribal school in a mud-brick house, student scribes in woollen robes sitting on benches pressing wedge marks into clay tablets with reed styluses, a teacher holding up a tablet ruled in neat columns, baskets of clay and a water jar, tablets drying in the sunny courtyard, the marks abstract and unreadable. Painted in the style of an Old Babylonian terracotta plaque relief, warm clay colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-mitanni: c. 1500 BCE, northern Syria near the Khabur River: a parade of light two-wheeled war chariots with spoked wheels, each pulled by a pair of horses and carrying a charioteer and an archer in scale armour, sweeping across a grassy plain before a walled mud-brick city with towers, grooms leading spare horses on foot, distant hills. Painted in the style of a Mitanni cylinder-seal design enlarged as a wall painting, ochre and blue on cream plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-ugaritic-alphabet: c. 1400 BCE, Ugarit on the Syrian coast: a scribe's room in a stone house of the port city, scribes in fringed tunics pressing small wedge signs into clay tablets with styluses, a tablet showing a short row of thirty abstract signs, a pottery lamp and storage jars; through the doorway, the harbour with merchant ships, cedar logs and bales on the quay. Painted in the manner of a Late Bronze Age Levantine ivory carving coloured as a wall painting, ochres and blues. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-phoenician-trade: c. 1000 BCE, Tyre on its island off the Lebanese coast: a busy harbour beneath stone walls, Phoenician merchant ships with curved prows and horse-head figureheads loading cedar logs, glass vessels and bolts of purple-dyed cloth, dyers working vats of murex shells on the shore, sailors in conical caps and tunics, the mountains of Lebanon behind. Painted in the style of an Assyrian palace relief coloured with ochre and blue, figures in profile. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-solomons-temple: c. 957 BCE, Jerusalem: on a hilltop above terraced olive groves, a rectangular stone temple with a tall porch flanked by two great bronze pillars stands within a walled courtyard, a large bronze basin resting on bronze oxen nearby, priests in white linen robes and worshippers in wool tunics bringing offerings, cedar beams being lifted by labourers; the hills of Judah around. Painted in the style of an ancient Near Eastern ivory relief rendered in warm ochres. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-israel-judah-split: c. 930 BCE, Shechem between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim: a great assembly of tribesmen in woollen robes and headcloths gathered in a valley before the town's stone walls and gate, elders arguing, a young king with attendants turning away toward a waiting chariot, sheep grazing on the terraced slopes; all figures small. Painted in the style of an ancient Near Eastern relief carving, coloured in ochre, olive and blue. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-urartu: c. 860 BCE, Tushpa on the shore of Lake Van: a massive fortress of cut stone on a long rocky ridge above the deep blue lake, Urartian soldiers in crested bronze helmets with round shields on the walls, workers digging an irrigation canal through orchards and vineyards below, snow-capped mountains around. Painted in the style of an Urartian bronze relief or Assyrian palace relief, warm bronze and lapis tones, figures in profile. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-marib-dam: c. 750 BCE, Marib in the Yemeni highlands: Sabaean workers in wrapped kilts haul dressed limestone blocks to raise a long earthen-and-stone dam across a wide wadi between rocky mountains, sluice gates of fitted masonry at each end, irrigation channels running out to green fields and date palms of the oasis; a camel caravan loaded with bundles of frankincense passes on the plain below. Rendered in the manner of South Arabian alabaster relief carving with soft ochre and sand tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-nabopolassar: 626 BCE, Babylon: before a mudbrick temple gate on the Euphrates, a Chaldean leader in a fringed robe and tall cylindrical crown stands small among priests and bearded nobles as he is acclaimed king; spearmen in long tunics line the processional way, Assyrian standards lie abandoned on the ground, palm groves and the stepped ziggurat rise behind under a hazy afternoon sky. Rendered as a Mesopotamian palace relief in carved gypsum, with faint traces of red and blue pigment. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-battle-of-carchemish: 605 BCE, Carchemish on the upper Euphrates: seen from a distant hillside, Babylonian chariots with spoked wheels and ranks of archers and spearmen press across a dusty plain toward a walled citadel mound by the river, while Egyptian troops in linen kilts and striped headcloths fall back toward the water; dust and smoke drift above the walls, no gore. Rendered as an Assyrian-style palace relief in carved stone, crowded friezes of small figures, warm limestone tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-lydian-coinage: c. 600 BCE, Sardis in Lydia: in a workshop beneath the acropolis a craftsman sets a small pale-gold electrum lump on an anvil and strikes a punch with a hammer, a lion-head die mark appearing; nearby a scale weighs identical bean-shaped coins, baskets of them on a wooden table, the gold-bearing Pactolus stream and columned houses glimpsed through the doorway in morning light. Painted in the style of an East Greek black-figure vase painting, black figures on orange clay with incised detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-fall-of-lydia: 547 BCE, Sardis: from a distance, Persian infantry in soft felt caps and long trousers with wicker shields, and a line of baggage camels, gather below the steep citadel rock of Sardis, its walls and gate thronged with defenders; smoke rises over the lower town, the hills of western Anatolia behind under a pale autumn sky. Rendered in the manner of an Achaemenid stone relief from Persepolis, rows of profile figures, carved grey limestone. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-return-to-zion: 538 BCE: a long column of Judean families in plain woollen robes and head-coverings travels on foot with donkeys loaded with bundles, carts and a few camels along a dusty road through the Judean hills toward the ruined walls of Jerusalem on a ridge at dawn; elders walk at the front, children ride on packs, olive trees on the terraced slopes. Painted in the style of an ancient Near Eastern wall painting, flat earth colours, simple outlined figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-second-temple: 516 BCE, Jerusalem: on the hilltop a modest new stone temple with a plain columned porch stands within a walled court, priests in white linen robes and turbans carry vessels toward a large horned stone altar where smoke rises, a crowd of men and women in woollen mantles gathered around; the half-rebuilt city and terraced hills beyond in clear morning light. Painted in the manner of an ancient synagogue wall painting like those at Dura-Europos, flat ochre and red tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-seleucid-empire: 312 BCE, Babylon: Macedonian soldiers in bronze helmets and linen cuirasses, long sarissa pikes upright, march through the blue-glazed brick Ishtar Gate into the city, a small mounted general at their head on a horse without stirrups; Babylonian townspeople in fringed robes watch from the walls, palms and the ziggurat behind. Painted in the style of a Hellenistic fresco, as at Macedonian tombs, soft earth colours and blue. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-petra-nabataeans: c. 150 BCE, Petra: a camel caravan laden with sacks of frankincense and myrrh winds out of the narrow rose-red Siq gorge into a sandstone valley where Nabataean masons on wooden scaffolding carve a tall columned tomb facade into the cliff; merchants in robes and headcloths, water channels cut along the rock, late afternoon sun on the pink stone. Painted as a Hellenistic wall painting in Nabataean style with vine-scroll ornament, warm reds and ochres. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-paul-missions: c. 47 CE, Antioch on the Orontes: in the colonnaded main street of a Roman city, a small group of travellers in tunics and cloaks with staffs and leather bags walks toward the city gate, seen from behind, while a few people wave farewell; shops, porticoes, Mount Silpius above and the river bridge beyond in early morning light. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco from Pompeii, soft earth tones and architectural perspective. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-bar-kokhba-revolt: 132-135 CE, Betar in the Judean hills: seen from far away, a Roman legion camp with neat tents and a siege wall rings a terraced hilltop fortress, legionaries in segmented armour and red cloaks advancing up the slope with siege ramps, smoke drifting from the hill town; olive trees and rocky hills under a dusky sky, no gore. Rendered in the manner of a Roman triumphal-column relief, as on Trajan's Column, carved marble, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-council-of-chalcedon: 451 CE, Chalcedon on the Bosphorus: inside the basilica of Saint Euphemia, hundreds of bishops in white and dark vestments sit on long benches facing a raised dais where imperial officials in jewelled cloaks preside, an open gospel book on a throne at the centre; columns, marble floor and high windows letting in daylight, the city of Constantinople across the water through the door. Painted in the style of an early Byzantine mosaic, gold ground, tesserae texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-babylonian-talmud: c. 500 CE, Pumbedita in Mesopotamia: in a mudbrick academy hall by the Euphrates, rows of bearded rabbis in long robes and head coverings sit on mats around low tables, debating over unrolled scrolls, students listening at the back; oil lamps, palm-trunk beams, a canal and date palms through the doorway. Painted in the style of a Sasanian-era wall painting with flat colours and simple outlines, in the manner of Dura-Europos murals. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-battle-of-badr: 624 CE, Badr near the Red Sea coast of Arabia: seen from a great distance, a small Arab force of camels and men on foot with swords and round leather shields drawn up beside desert wells faces a much larger army on the sandy plain below dunes and dark volcanic hills; dust rising, banners, early morning light, no figure shown in detail or identifiable. Painted in the style of a Persian miniature, with an empty landscape-dominated view, gold sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-abu-bakr-caliph: 632 CE, Medina: in a palm-shaded courtyard of a simple mudbrick and palm-trunk hall, a crowd of Arab men in plain robes and turbans gathers and clasps hands with an elder seen from behind, giving their pledge; date palms, mud walls, camels tethered outside under a bright sky. No sacred figure depicted. Painted in the style of an Ottoman miniature, flat colours, gold accents, small figures in a wide view. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-basra-kufa-founded: 636 CE, Basra in southern Iraq: Arab soldiers and their families lay out a new garrison town beside a canal near the Shatt al-Arab, building houses of reed bundles and mudbrick in neat quarters around an open prayer space, camels and tents nearby, reed boats on the water, date palms and flat marshland under a hot sky. Painted as a medieval Arabic manuscript illustration in the style of the Maqamat of al-Hariri, bright flat colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-uthman-quran: c. 650 CE, Medina: in a sunlit mudbrick room roofed with palm trunks and reed matting, scribes in simple 7th-century Arabian robes and plain wrapped turbans sit cross-legged copying a sacred text in bold angular script onto large parchment sheets, finished parchment codices stacked on a low stand, messengers with camels waiting at the doorway. Through the doorway only low flat-roofed mudbrick houses and date palms; no domes, no minarets, no later Ottoman buildings. The script is not legible. Painted in a flat early Islamic manuscript style with muted colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-abd-al-malik-reforms: c. 696 CE, Damascus: in a mint workshop behind the Umayyad palace, craftsmen in tunics and turbans strike small gold dinars with dies on anvils, trays of gleaming coins bearing only script-like patterns, no images; scribes at a nearby table write registers on papyrus, columns of a Roman-era colonnade and the city behind in daylight. Writing shown as illegible marks. Painted in the style of an Umayyad mosaic, gold and green glass tesserae. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-umayyad-mosque: 715 CE, Damascus: the courtyard of the new Great Mosque, with a vast marble-paved court and arcades whose walls glitter with green and gold glass mosaics of trees, rivers and palaces; worshippers in robes and turbans cross the court, the domed treasury on columns, the prayer hall facade with tall arched windows, the old Roman temple enclosure walls around it in bright midday sun. Painted in the style of the Umayyad mosaics themselves, gold ground and green landscape. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-harun-al-rashid: c. 786 CE, Baghdad: a broad view of the Round City on the Tigris at sunset, with its green-domed palace at the centre, concentric brick walls and gates, boats on the river and markets crowded with merchants, scholars and camels; inside an open palace pavilion small figures of courtiers, musicians and a caliph seen from afar sit on carpets beneath lamps. Painted in the style of a Persian miniature, rich lapis, gold and rose. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-al-khwarizmi-algebra: c. 820 CE, Baghdad: in the House of Wisdom, a scholar in a turban and robe, seen from the side at a distance, writes geometric squares and diagrams on paper at a low desk, surrounded by shelves of manuscripts, an astrolabe and a brass armillary sphere; other scholars read by lamp-light, arched windows onto palms and the Tigris. Writing and numerals shown as illegible marks. Painted in the style of a thirteenth-century Baghdad school manuscript illustration. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-samarra-capital: 836 CE, Samarra on the Tigris: a new palace city of baked brick and stucco spreads along the riverbank, with vast courtyards, a long ceremonial staircase down to the water, polo grounds and barracks; Turkish soldiers in caftans and fur-trimmed caps on horseback ride past in formation while builders finish walls, in pale morning light. Painted as an Abbasid wall painting like the Samarra palace frescoes, warm reds, blacks and ochres. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-zanj-rebellion: 869 CE, the salt marshes of southern Iraq near Basra: in a flat white landscape of salt crust and reed beds, groups of African labourers who have thrown down their shovels gather with spears and reed banners around a leader on a mound, palm-frond huts and canals around them, reed boats on the water, smoke rising far off from an estate. Painted in the style of a medieval Arabic manuscript illustration from the Maqamat of al-Hariri, bright flat colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-tughril-baghdad: 1055, Baghdad: a column of Seljuk Turkish horsemen in long caftans, fur caps and composite bows on their backs ride with tall banners through a brick city gate into Baghdad, crowds of townspeople in turbans watching from roofs and balconies; minarets and domes along the Tigris, river boats, afternoon light. Painted in the style of a Seljuk-era Persian miniature on minai pottery, bright figures on a cream ground. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-sultanate-of-rum: c. 1077-1100, central Anatolia near Konya: Turkmen herders with felt yurts, flocks of sheep and horses move across a wide high plateau toward a walled town with Byzantine churches and a new mosque, Seljuk horsemen with banners riding alongside; snowy mountains on the horizon, steppe grass in spring light. Painted in the style of a Seljuk-period Persian miniature, flat colours, round faces and gold sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-saladin-retakes-jerusalem: 1187, Jerusalem: Saladin's army in mail coats and turbans with yellow banners encamps outside the walls while the gates stand open and long lines of Frankish townspeople in medieval dress walk out carrying bundles, paying ransom to officials at tables, the Dome of the Rock gleaming above the walls in afternoon sun. No violence, figures small. Painted in the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript of the Crusades, gold ground and bright colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-rumi-konya: c. 1244, Konya: in a whitewashed courtyard of a Seljuk madrasa with carved stone portal and turquoise-tiled dome, dervishes in tall felt hats and long white robes turn in a circling dance while musicians play reed flutes and frame drums, scholars in turbans watching from an arcade; seen at a distance, soft evening light. Painted in the style of an Ottoman miniature, such as illustrations of the lives of Sufi saints. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-osman-founds-ottomans: c. 1299, Söğüt in northwest Anatolia: a band of Turkish horsemen in caftans and white felt caps, with bows and lances, gathers at dawn beside a small stone village with tents of their tribe, then looks out over a green valley toward a Byzantine hill fortress with a domed church; pines, rolling hills, mist. Painted in the style of a sixteenth-century Ottoman miniature in the Hünername manner, flat colours and gold sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-timur-baghdad: 1401, Baghdad: seen from a distant riverbank, the city burns in thick black smoke above its broken brick walls and domes along the Tigris, while ranks of Timurid horsemen with banners and tents fill the plain in the foreground; no bodies or gore, the destruction shown only through smoke and ruin. Painted in the style of a Timurid Persian miniature from Herat, with rocky horizon and gold sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-suleiman-takes-baghdad: 1534, Baghdad: a grand Ottoman army with janissaries in tall white felt caps, sipahi horsemen and long trains of camels with cannons enters Baghdad through a gate as townspeople watch; tents with red and gold canopies on the plain, domes and minarets along the Tigris in sunlight, the sultan a small figure on a white horse under a parasol. Painted in the style of a Süleymanname Ottoman miniature, bright colours and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-fakhr-al-din: c. 1600, Deir al-Qamar on Mount Lebanon: a stone palace with arched windows and courtyards stands on a terraced mountainside of mulberry trees and silk farms; Druze men in black robes and white turbans gather in the square, an emir small among them, while mules carry silk bales down to a harbour where a Tuscan galley waits far off. Painted in the style of an Ottoman miniature mixed with an Italian Renaissance landscape view. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-mocha-coffee: c. 1600, Mocha on the Red Sea coast of Yemen: whitewashed tower houses with carved wooden window screens and minarets line the sandy shore, camels unload sacks of coffee beans brought down from the highland terraces, merchants in turbans weigh the beans on great scales while Indian and Arab dhows ride at anchor in a calm turquoise sea. Painted in the style of an Ottoman-era Persian miniature, with bright colours and gold sky. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-emirate-of-diriyah: 1744, Diriyah in Najd, Arabia: mudbrick houses and towers of the oasis town rise above the palm groves of Wadi Hanifa; in an open courtyard two groups of Arab men in long robes and headcloths clasp hands to seal a pact, a preacher and a chief seen small from behind, camels and men with swords waiting at the gate in the golden late afternoon. Painted as an eighteenth-century Ottoman provincial miniature, flat earth colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-siege-of-acre-1799: 1799, Acre on the Palestinian coast: seen from the sea, the stone walls and towers of Acre stand firm under drifting cannon smoke as French infantry in blue coats and bicorne hats entrench on the sandy plain outside, British warships with full sails firing from the bay, Ottoman defenders in turbans on the ramparts; mosque domes behind, bright morning. Painted in the style of an early nineteenth-century oil history painting of naval battles. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-lebanon-1860: 1860, Mount Lebanon: seen from far away, smoke rises from a burnt village of stone houses on a terraced mountainside of cedars and mulberry groves, refugees in local dress with mules and bundles walk down a mountain road toward the coast, where a French warship lies at anchor; no violence shown up close. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine black lines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-nahda: c. 1870, Beirut: in a printing house with tall arched windows onto the harbour, men in fezzes and frock coats set metal type at cases, a hand press prints newspaper sheets of Arabic script, a scholar at a desk piled with dictionary manuscripts and books; the sea and red-tiled roofs of the town outside in morning light. All writing illegible. Painted as a nineteenth-century watercolour with fine pen line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-ottoman-constitution-1876: 1876, Istanbul: on a broad square before an Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus, crowds of men in red fezzes and frock coats, soldiers in blue uniforms and religious scholars in turbans gather as an official on a platform reads from a scroll, minarets of great mosques and steamers on the water behind; a winter day. All writing illegible. Rendered as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine lines and crowded figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-first-aliyah: 1882, Rishon LeZion in Ottoman Palestine: a handful of Jewish settlers from Russia in caps, waistcoats and long skirts dig a well and plant vines in a dry sandy plain, with canvas tents, a mule cart and a few stone houses under construction, Arab villagers with camels passing on a track; low hills and a pale hot sky. Painted as a nineteenth-century documentary watercolour, sandy ochres and soft greens. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-battle-of-riyadh-1902: 1902, Riyadh in Najd: at night under a starry sky a small band of Arab men in robes and headcloths with rifles and swords creeps toward the mudbrick walls and tall round towers of the Masmak fortress, palm trees silhouetted, lamplight from a few windows, camels left behind among the palms; figures small and seen from behind. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour, deep blues and earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-hejaz-railway: 1908, near Medina: a steam locomotive with a long train of passenger coaches crowded with pilgrims in white garments puffs along a single track across a stark desert of black lava fields and dunes toward palm groves and a stone station building; Ottoman officials in fezzes and soldiers watch, camels resting beside the line, bright morning sun. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-armenian-genocide: 1915, the Syrian desert near Deir ez-Zor: seen from far away, a long thin column of deported Armenian families on foot, women, children and elderly men in worn clothes carrying bundles, stretches across an empty sandy plain toward the Euphrates under a harsh sun, a few mounted gendarmes at the edges; no bodies or violence shown, only the vast desert and the distance. Painted as a sombre early twentieth-century watercolour, muted ochre and grey. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-sykes-picot: 1916, London: in a quiet oak-lined government office lit by a green-shaded lamp, two diplomats in dark suits, seen from behind, lean over a large map of the Middle East spread on a table, coloured pencils and dividers beside it, regions shaded in two colours but no legible text; rain on tall windows overlooking Whitehall. Painted as an early twentieth-century lithograph illustration, muted tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-balfour-declaration: November 1917, London, the Foreign Office in Whitehall: a dim Edwardian study with tall windows on a grey day, bookshelves and a large leather-topped desk. Seen close on the desk only: a typed letter on cream paper, an inkwell, a fountain pen, a blotter and an envelope, with a map of the Eastern Mediterranean on the wall behind. No person shown, no faces or figures at all, only a single elderly gloved hand at the edge of the desk resting on the envelope. All writing illegible. Early twentieth-century watercolour, muted greys and browns. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-turkish-war-of-independence: c. 1921, near Ankara: on the high Anatolian steppe, Turkish nationalist soldiers in khaki uniforms and kalpak caps march with rifles beside ox-carts loaded with ammunition crates, village women in headscarves carrying shells on their backs, the hilltop citadel of Ankara and its small town of houses behind; grey autumn sky. Painted as a 1920s documentary watercolour, muted khaki and brown. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-battle-of-maysalun: 1920, Maysalun pass in the Anti-Lebanon mountains: seen from a ridge, a small force of Syrian soldiers and volunteers in mixed uniforms and keffiyehs with rifles faces columns of French troops with artillery and a few tanks advancing up a dusty valley road, smoke drifting over the rocky hillside; no gore, figures small, bright July sun. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-treaty-of-lausanne: 1923, Lausanne, Switzerland: a long view of a grand hotel conference hall with crystal chandeliers and tall windows onto Lake Geneva and the Alps, delegates in dark suits and a few in fezzes seated around a long green-covered table with papers, small figures at a distance, a summer afternoon. All writing illegible. Painted as a 1920s documentary watercolour, cool greens and blues. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-abolition-of-caliphate: 1924, Ankara: inside the plain stone-walled hall of the Grand National Assembly, rows of deputies in dark suits and kalpak caps sit at wooden desks raising their hands in a vote, a speaker at the rostrum seen small from behind, tall windows letting in a cold March light. All writing illegible. Painted as a 1920s documentary watercolour, muted browns and greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-turkish-alphabet: 1928, a town square in Turkey: in a public park, men in new brimmed hats and suits and women in coats stand before a large blackboard on an easel where a teacher points to rows of large chalk letters that are clearly ordinary Latin capitals, like a simple ABC chart, not runes or invented symbols; others write in notebooks at outdoor tables. Plane trees in autumn colour, a domed mosque with one minaret behind, a red Turkish flag. Painted as a 1920s Republican-era documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-saudi-arabia-founded: 1932, Riyadh: a walled mudbrick town with round watchtowers and palm groves; in a sandy square before the palace, crowds of Arab tribesmen in robes and headcloths with rifles and camels gather beneath green banners to pledge loyalty, a ruler seen small from afar among his retinue; a clear blue autumn sky. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour, warm ochres and greens. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-iraq-independence: 1932, Baghdad: along the Tigris riverbank, crowds in suits, fezzes and sidaras and robed tribal elders gather beneath palm trees and new government buildings with flags (no legible emblems) as a band of soldiers in khaki parades; river boats and a steel bridge, an October afternoon. Painted as a 1930s documentary watercolour, warm sunlight and blues. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
me-palestine-arab-revolt: 1936, Nablus: the stone-arched market streets of an old hill town lie quiet with shuttered shops during a general strike, a few men in keffiyehs and suit jackets talking in a doorway, British soldiers in khaki shorts and pith helmets patrolling at a distance beside an armoured car; olive-covered mountains of Gerizim and Ebal rise behind in summer light. Painted as a 1930s documentary watercolour, muted stone tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
