Late afternoon sun. Painted in the manner of an Ajanta cave mural, rhythmic massed figures, ochre, green and lapis blue. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-sigiriya: c. 477 CE, Sigiriya in Sri Lanka: a huge sheer granite rock rises 180 metres from the jungle, its summit crowned with palace terraces, a staircase passing through a giant brick lion gateway on its flank; below, symmetrical water gardens, pools and fountains, and workers carrying bricks up wooden ladders. Clear tropical light, mist over the forest. Painted in the soft ochre and green style of the Sigiriya rock frescoes, delicate brushwork. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-brahmagupta: 628 CE, Bhinmal in Rajasthan: on the flat rooftop of a sandstone house at night, an astronomer in a white dhoti sits with pupils around oil lamps, using a large wooden armillary ring and a gnomon, counting with pebbles on a wooden board, a dot marking an empty place; the desert town and starry sky around them, a crescent moon. Signs tiny and illegible. Painted in the style of a Rajasthani miniature painting, deep blue night, flat bright colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-wang-xuance: 648 CE, Tirhut on the north Indian plain: seen from a distance, a small Tang envoy party in round-collared robes and black futou caps rides at the head of a column of Tibetan soldiers in leather armour and Nepali troops with spears and shields, advancing across rice fields towards a walled town; the Himalayan foothills on the horizon, dust under a pale sky. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues, greens and ochre. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-gopala-pala: c. 750 CE, Gauda in Bengal: on a green riverside plain, an assembly of local chiefs in dhotis and turbans gathers under a large pavilion, raising their hands in acclamation as a new king, seen small and from behind, is seated on a cushioned throne; war elephants and boats on the river, palm trees and a Buddhist monastery with a stupa in the background. Monsoon-washed daylight. Painted in the style of a Pala-era palm-leaf manuscript illumination, red ground, bright figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-adi-shankara: c. 788 CE, Sringeri in Karnataka: on the bank of the Tunga river amid forested Western Ghats hills, a young ascetic teacher in saffron robes with a staff, seen from behind, sits with a group of disciples in a simple riverside hermitage of stone and thatch, a small shrine and stone steps leading to the water. Misty morning light. Painted in the style of a Kerala temple mural, warm yellows, reds and greens, bold outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-rajendra-ganges: c. 1019 CE, Gangaikonda Cholapuram in Tamil Nadu: a vast Chola army returns to a new capital under construction, war elephants and foot soldiers marching through a stone gateway, porters carrying sealed pots of Ganges water; behind them masons raise the towering granite vimana of a great temple with scaffolding of bamboo, and a vast irrigation tank shines beside it. Bright afternoon. Painted in the style of a Chola-period temple fresco, red, ochre and green, flowing figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-khajuraho: c. 1030 CE, Khajuraho in Madhya Pradesh: a group of sandstone temples with clustered rising spires stands on high platforms beside a lake, sculptors on bamboo scaffolding carving rows of dancers, musicians, warriors and elephants in friezes on the walls; pilgrims and a royal party walking among them. Golden morning light, palm trees and fields. Seen from a distance so the carvings read as rich texture. Painted as a Rajput-style miniature, clear bright colours, fine detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-ramanuja: c. 1100 CE, Srirangam in Tamil Nadu: on a river island between branches of the Kaveri, a great temple complex with concentric walls and carved gateways; inside a courtyard a teacher in saffron, seen from behind, leads devotees in song, with lamps, flower garlands and temple musicians playing drums and pipes; coconut palms and the river beyond. Warm evening light. Painted in the style of a south Indian temple mural, vivid reds, ochres and greens. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-rajatarangini: 1148 CE, Srinagar in Kashmir: in a wooden-roofed house beside a lake, a scholar in a woollen robe sits at a low desk by a lattice window writing on birch-bark leaves, bundles of old records and inscriptions on copper plates stacked around him; outside, the Jhelum river with boats, stone temples and snow mountains around the valley, autumn chinar trees. Script tiny and illegible. Painted in the style of a Kashmiri Pahari miniature, delicate lines and cool colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-bhaskara-ii: c. 1150 CE, Ujjain: at an astronomical school, a scholar in a white dhoti sits on a terrace teaching a group of students and a young girl, holding a palm-leaf manuscript, while a large water clock bowl floats in a basin and a gnomon casts its shadow on a marked stone floor; temple spires and the city in the background, clear daylight. Numerals tiny and illegible. Painted as a Rajasthani miniature painting, flat bright colours, decorative. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-parakramabahu: c. 1153 CE, Polonnaruwa in Sri Lanka: a vast man-made reservoir stretching to the horizon behind a long earthen embankment, labourers with baskets building the bund and stone sluices; on the shore stand royal palaces, a round brick stupa and a white-plastered image house, monks walking under palms. Clear tropical daylight and reflections in the water. Painted in the style of a Sri Lankan temple mural, red ground, flat colours, bold outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-konark: c. 1250 CE, Konark on the Odisha coast: a colossal sandstone temple shaped as a chariot with twenty-four huge carved stone wheels and seven rearing stone horses at its front, its tall tower still under construction with bamboo scaffolding; masons and labourers haul blocks by rope up ramps, the sea and casuarina trees behind, sunrise behind the structure. Painted in the style of an Odisha pattachitra cloth painting, bold outlines, red, yellow and black. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-token-currency: c. 1330, Delhi: in a busy market street of the Sultanate capital, merchants in turbans and long tunics weigh piles of copper and brass coins on scales and argue, while in a back courtyard workers hammer out coins in a crude workshop; mosque domes and the stone walls of a fortified city behind, dust and bustle in the afternoon light. Coin markings tiny and illegible. Painted in the style of an early Indo-Persian manuscript painting, bright flat colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-bahmani: 1347, Gulbarga in the Deccan: a new stone fortress with massive bastions on a rocky plain, and inside it a great mosque with many domes and arched halls under construction; nobles in turbans and long coats gather before a pavilion as a new sultan, small and far off, holds court, cavalry with lances and banners without lettering outside the walls. Hot dry afternoon light. Painted in the style of a Deccani miniature painting, gold, lilac and deep green. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-zheng-he-calicut: 1405, Calicut on the Malabar coast: a fleet of huge Ming treasure ships with multiple masts and red battened junk sails anchored offshore, smaller boats rowing to a palm-fringed beach where Chinese envoys in Ming robes and black gauze hats exchange porcelain and silk with Kerala merchants in white wraps; tiled-roof warehouses and coconut palms, warm daylight. Painted as a Ming woodblock-print illustration with light colour, fine lines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-kabir: c. 1450, Varanasi: a weaver in a simple white cloth and cap sits at a pit loom in an open-fronted house by the Ganges, singing while he weaves, a small group of listeners, both Hindu and Muslim townspeople, seated on the steps around him; the river ghats, temple spires and a mosque dome behind, boats on the water. Soft evening light. Painted in the style of a Mughal-era Rajput miniature, warm colours, fine brushwork. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-vasco-da-gama: 1498, Kappad near Calicut: three Portuguese carracks and caravels with white sails marked with red crosses lie at anchor off a palm-lined beach; a boat of European sailors in doublets and caps lands on the sand, met by curious Malabar fishermen and local officials in white cloth under parasols. Monsoon clouds, green coast, bright light. Painted in the style of a Portuguese sixteenth-century illuminated navigation chart illustration and Indian miniature colours, vivid and detailed. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-guru-nanak: c. 1499, Sultanpur Lodhi in the Punjab: on the bank of the small Bein river at dawn, a group of villagers, both Hindu and Muslim, sits on the grass around a teacher in a simple robe and turban, seen small and from behind, with a companion playing a rebab; mustard fields, a village with mud-brick houses and a small mosque, mist rising from the water. Painted in the style of a Punjabi janamsakhi manuscript painting, flat bright colours, simple forms. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-krishnadevaraya: c. 1509, Hampi in Karnataka: a magnificent city among giant granite boulders on the Tungabhadra river; a grand royal procession of decorated elephants, cavalry and musicians passes along a colonnaded bazaar street to a stone temple with a tall gopuram, poets and courtiers following a ruler seen small under a parasol. Bright afternoon sun. Painted in the style of a Vijayanagara temple ceiling mural, ochre, red and black, bold outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-portuguese-goa: 1510, Goa on the Mandovi river: seen from a distance, Portuguese carracks with crossed sails fire cannon towards a walled riverside town with Indo-Islamic domed gateways, smoke drifting over the walls, armoured soldiers with pikes and arquebuses coming ashore in boats; palm groves and green hills beyond under a hazy sky. No wounded shown. Painted as a sixteenth-century Portuguese oil history painting, warm earth tones and detailed ships. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-ramcharitmanas: 1574, Varanasi: in a small room open onto the stone steps of a Ganges ghat, an elderly poet-saint in white with a sandalwood mark sits on a mat writing on paper sheets, while below on the ghat pilgrims carry brass water pots and a group listens to a recitation; temples, boats and early morning mist over the river. Writing tiny and illegible. Painted in the style of a Mughal sub-imperial miniature, soft colours and fine detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-adi-granth: 1604, Amritsar in the Punjab: a modest brick temple with a small dome stands in the middle of a square sacred pool, reached by a causeway; a procession of Sikh devotees in turbans and simple robes carries a large bound book wrapped in cloth on a cushion beneath a canopy across the causeway, musicians with rebab and drums following, crowds on the brick terraces around the water. Early morning light. Painted in the style of a Punjab Pahari miniature, soft colours, fine detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-surat-factory: 1612, Surat on the Tapti river in Gujarat: a busy Mughal port with whitewashed merchant houses, a stone castle and mosque minarets; English merchants in doublets, ruffs and tall hats unload broadcloth from small boats at a riverside warehouse, watched by Mughal customs officials in turbans and long jamas weighing goods; tall English ships at anchor at the river mouth. Hazy afternoon light. Painted in the style of a Mughal miniature painting, fine detail and soft bright colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-fort-st-george: 1639, the Coromandel coast at Madraspatnam: on a flat sandy shore lined with palms, Indian labourers and masons build the low square walls and corner bastions of a small European fort, English traders in broad hats and coats directing them; masula surf boats carry goods through the breakers from a ship at anchor, fishing villages nearby. Bright tropical light and blue sea. Painted as a seventeenth-century Dutch-style topographical oil painting, clear detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-khalsa: 1699, Anandpur Sahib in the Punjab foothills: during the spring Baisakhi festival, a vast crowd of Sikhs in turbans and simple robes gathers on a hillside below a tented pavilion; at its front a small group of five men in saffron stand before the Guru, seen small from behind, who stirs an iron bowl with a double-edged sword. Green Shivalik hills, clear spring daylight. Painted in the style of a Pahari miniature painting, flat bright colours, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-third-panipat: 1761, the plain of Panipat north of Delhi: seen from a great distance on a winter morning, two huge armies face each other across a dusty plain, Afghan cavalry with lances and camel-mounted swivel guns on one side and Maratha horsemen with saffron banners and war elephants on the other, clouds of dust and gunsmoke drifting across. No wounded shown. Painted in the style of an eighteenth-century Mughal battle miniature, crowded rhythmic figures, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-bengal-famine-1770: 1770, the countryside near Murshidabad in Bengal: dry, cracked rice fields under a harsh pale sky, withered palms, and thin villagers in worn cotton waiting quietly with empty baskets and pots outside a revenue office where a Company official in a coat and tricorn hat sits with clerks counting coins; abandoned huts in the distance. No bodies shown. Painted as a sombre Company-school watercolour on paper, muted ochres and greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-regulating-act: 1773, Calcutta on the Hooghly river: the riverfront of the Company town with the brick walls of old Fort William, colonnaded white houses and tall-masted East Indiamen at anchor; on the steps of a government building, British officials in powdered wigs and frock coats and Bengali clerks in white gather as a new Governor-General arrives by barge under a parasol, small and seen from behind. Warm afternoon haze. Painted as a Company-school watercolour in the manner of Thomas Daniell, soft tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-asiatic-society: 1784, Calcutta: in a high-ceilinged colonial room with tall shuttered windows and a ceiling punkah fan, a small group of British scholars in frock coats and Bengali pandits in white dhotis sit around a long table covered with palm-leaf manuscripts, Greek and Latin books and Sanskrit texts, discussing; a servant pulls the fan cord. Script illegible. Warm lamp light. Painted as an eighteenth-century Company-school watercolour with fine detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-permanent-settlement: 1793, rural Bengal: a zamindar in a fine white jama and turban sits on a carpeted veranda of his country house with clerks writing in ledgers and a British collector in a coat beside him, while farmers bring sacks of rice and coins to pay rent; rice fields, palms and a river with boats behind. Clear dry-season light. Script illegible. Painted as a Company-school watercolour on paper, gentle earth colours, fine detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-ranjit-singh: 1799, Lahore: at dawn, Sikh horsemen in turbans with matchlocks, swords and banners without lettering ride through a great Mughal city gate in red sandstone, the domes and minarets of the Badshahi Mosque and the walls of the Lahore Fort rising beyond, townspeople watching from rooftops; a young leader rides small among them. Morning haze. Painted in the style of a Pahari miniature of the Sikh court, bright colours, fine detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-sugauli: 1816, Sugauli on the Bihar plain: inside a British military camp of white canvas tents, Nepali envoys in traditional robes and caps and British officers in red coats and bicorne hats sit at a table under a shady awning as documents are exchanged; sepoys stand in a row, and the foothills and distant snow peaks of the Himalaya on the northern horizon. Clear winter light. Painted as a Company-school watercolour, delicate tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-brahmo-samaj: 1828, Calcutta: in a plain hall with tall arched windows and no images or idols, a congregation of Bengali men in white dhotis and shawls sits on mats listening to a reader at a simple wooden lectern; outside, palm trees, a busy lane with palanquins and colonial houses. Soft morning light through the shutters. Figures small, no close faces. Painted as an early nineteenth-century Company-school watercolour in muted colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-sati-abolished: 1829, Calcutta: on the steps of a riverside ghat on the Hooghly, a British official in a dark coat and a Bengali crier in white read aloud a proclamation to a gathered crowd of townspeople, women in white saris among them listening; boats on the river, temples and colonial buildings along the bank, a calm morning. Paper text illegible. Painted as an early nineteenth-century Company-school watercolour, soft greens and ochres. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-first-railway: 1853, Bombay: a small steam locomotive with a tall chimney pulls a line of wooden passenger carriages out of a simple station at Bori Bunder, crowds of Indians in turbans and saris and British officials in top hats watching from the platform, flags without emblems flying; green hills and palms beyond, puffs of white steam in the sunshine. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper wood engraving with light colour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-crown-rule: 1858, Allahabad: at the fort beside the meeting of the Ganges and Yamuna rivers, a British official in a dark uniform stands on a dais reading a proclamation to rows of troops in red coats, Indian princes in jewelled turbans and a large crowd of townspeople in white; a gun salute's smoke rising beside the walls, flags fluttering. Evening light. Paper text illegible. Rendered as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine cross-hatching. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-partition-of-bengal: 1905, Calcutta: in a riverside square, a large crowd of Bengali men in dhotis and shawls and women in saris gathers around a bonfire of imported British cloth bales, while others carry home handwoven cotton; trams, colonial buildings and a temple spire behind, smoke rising in the evening sky. Seen from a distance. Painted as an early twentieth-century Bengal School watercolour wash, soft muted tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-muslim-league: 1906, Dhaka: in the garden of a nineteenth-century nawab's palace with a pink domed roof on the bank of the Buriganga river, a gathering of Muslim gentlemen in sherwanis, caps and turbans sits on chairs under a large canopy listening to a speaker; boats on the river, palms and flowering trees around. Clear winter afternoon. Figures small. Painted as a period watercolour in the Bengal School manner, soft washes. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-tagore-nobel: 1913, Santiniketan in rural Bengal: an open-air school where groups of children in white sit on the ground under great mango and sal trees with their teachers, an elderly bearded poet in a long robe walking along the red earth path, seen small from behind; simple thatched and brick buildings, rice fields beyond. Gentle golden light. Painted as a Bengal School watercolour, soft hazy washes in the manner of Abanindranath Tagore. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-non-cooperation: 1920, Calcutta: a great crowd of Indians in white homespun khadi caps and dhotis and women in saris fills a city square for a public meeting; spinning wheels are set out in front, and a pile of foreign cloth smoulders at one side, students leaving a colonial college building. Seen from above at a distance, no faces in close-up. Painted as a 1920s Indian watercolour illustration, muted earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-raman-effect: 1928, Calcutta: in a modest laboratory of the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science, a scientist in a turban and a dark coat, seen from behind, works with an assistant at a wooden bench where a beam of sunlight passes through a lens into a glass flask of clear liquid, a brass spectroscope and photographic plates beside them; tall windows, shelves of bottles. Painted as a 1920s documentary watercolour, warm subdued tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-poona-pact: 1932, Pune: in the courtyard of Yerwada prison, a frail man wrapped in a white shawl lies on a cot under a mango tree, surrounded by a small group of political leaders in caps, suits and dhotis sitting in chairs and signing papers on a low table; stone prison walls and a barred gate behind. Figures small, seen from a distance. Painted as a 1930s watercolour sketch, muted tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-goi-act-1935: 1937, a provincial town in north India: voters in turbans, caps and saris queue in a long line outside a polling station set up in a colonial school building, election officials at a table under a veranda, bullock carts and bicycles in the dusty street; bright winter sunshine and neem trees. Paper text illegible. Painted as a 1930s documentary watercolour sketch in soft earth colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-lahore-resolution: A 1940s watercolour of the All-India Muslim League session at Minto Park, Lahore, in March 1940, with the walls of the Mughal Lahore Fort behind. A large decorated shamiana tent over a stage where leaders in sherwanis and caps address a vast seated crowd in white caps, turbans and Jinnah caps. The flags are the All-India Muslim League flag: a plain green field with a white crescent and star and no white vertical stripe, so not the later Pakistan national flag. Microphones on stands. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-bengal-famine-1943: 1943, Calcutta: a long line of thin villagers in worn saris and dhotis waits quietly with metal bowls at a relief kitchen under a tarpaulin on a city pavement, volunteers ladling rice gruel from large pots; colonial buildings, a tram and a grey monsoon sky behind. No bodies shown. Drawn in the manner of Zainul Abedin's famine sketches, brush and black ink on paper, sombre and restrained. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-simla-agreement: 1972, Shimla in the Himalayan foothills: a large colonial-era Tudor-style government house with gabled roofs stands on a forested ridge of deodar cedars, mist rising from the valleys; official cars and a small group of delegates in suits and saris are seen far off on the gravel driveway, flags without emblems on poles. Calm summer evening. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, soft greens and greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-bhopal: 1984, Bhopal: in the cold grey dawn, a pesticide factory with storage tanks, pipes and a tall chimney stands on the edge of a city of low houses, a pale haze lying over the empty streets and slums around it; ambulances and a few people with cloths over their faces seen far off. No bodies shown. Painted as a muted, sorrowful documentary watercolour in grey and ochre washes. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-babri-masjid: 1992, Ayodhya on the Sarayu river in north India: a calm distant landscape at dusk, with a three-domed sixteenth-century Mughal-style mosque of plastered stone on a low mound among the town's temples, houses and trees, boats on the river and the evening sky turning violet; no people in the foreground. Quiet and reflective. Painted as a neutral documentary watercolour, soft muted washes. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-kargil: 1999, Kargil in Ladakh: a vast landscape of jagged snow-dusted Himalayan ridges and barren brown slopes under a hard blue sky, a line of small soldiers in winter gear with packs climbing a steep rocky spur, artillery smoke rising from a distant peak; a military supply road winding along the valley floor. No wounded shown. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, cool blues and browns. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sa-mumbai-attacks: 2008, Mumbai: a calm night view of the harbour front, where crowds of people stand quietly holding lit candles on the waterfront promenade beside a colonial stone gateway arch and a grand domed hotel, police barriers at the edge; boats on the dark water, city lights reflected. Seen from a distance, no faces. A mood of mourning. Painted as a neutral documentary gouache illustration, deep blues and warm candle light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-phung-nguyen-culture: c. 2000 BCE, Lâm Thao in the Red River valley of northern Vietnam: a Neolithic village of stilt houses with thatched roofs beside green rice paddies, villagers in bark-cloth wraps polishing stone axes and shaping pottery with incised patterns, others harvesting rice with knives; low forested hills and the broad river behind, misty morning light. Painted in an earthy palette inspired by prehistoric Southeast Asian pottery designs, terracotta and black, with a soft watercolour finish. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-khok-phanom-di: c. 2000 BCE, Khok Phanom Di near the Gulf of Thailand: a coastal mound settlement by mangroves and an estuary, women potters shaping and burnishing fine black and red pots with anvils and paddles, men fishing from dugout canoes, shell heaps and rice plots nearby; palm and mangrove trees, warm afternoon light. Painted in an earthy prehistoric palette of red ochre and black, like the incised pottery of the site, with soft washes. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-van-lang: c. 700 BCE, Phong Châu in northern Vietnam: a village of tall stilt houses with saddle-shaped boat-like roofs among rice paddies; a festival where warriors in feathered headdresses beat large bronze drums, and long dugout boats with feathered rowers race on the river; hills and mist behind. Rendered in the style of the incised scenes on Đông Sơn bronze drums, stylised figures, bronze-green and black. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-funan-rise: c. 100 CE, the Mekong delta near Angkor Borei: a moated town of timber and thatched stilt houses beside canals, with wooden sailing ships with outrigger and Indian-style hulls moored at a river port; merchants in sarongs and Indian traders in white cloth exchanging beads, gold rings and spices, rice fields stretching to the horizon. Humid golden light. Painted in the style of an Angkor-inspired bas-relief, warm sandstone tones, lively crowded figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-champa-founded: c. 192 CE, Trà Kiệu in central Vietnam: on a coastal plain between green mountains and the sea, a crowd of local warriors with spears and bronze daggers gathers at a wooden stockade town, lowering a Han-style garrison banner without lettering and raising their own; a small Han fortified post seen in the distance. Mist on the hills, clear morning light. Painted in the style of a Cham sandstone relief, warm reddish stone, stylised figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-kutai-inscriptions: c. 400 CE, Muara Kaman on the Mahakam river in Borneo: in a jungle clearing by a broad river, priests in white cloth stand beside a row of tall rough stone pillars carved with tiny illegible lines of letters, while villagers lead cattle and bring gifts in a great sacrificial gift-giving ceremony; longhouses on stilts and dense rainforest behind. Humid morning mist. Painted in the style of a Javanese temple bas-relief, warm stone tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-dvaravati: c. 600 CE, Nakhon Pathom in central Thailand: a moated Mon town with a large brick stupa at its centre, monks in ochre robes walking in procession around it carrying alms bowls, a carved stone Wheel of the Law on a tall pillar, townspeople in sarongs offering flowers; rice fields and palm trees around. Soft morning light. Painted in the style of a Thai temple mural, gentle colours, fine outlines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-isanapura: c. 616 CE, Sambor Prei Kuk in Cambodia: a forest city of red-brick tower temples, square and octagonal, with carved sandstone door frames and lintels, standing in walled enclosures among tall trees; a royal procession with parasols and elephants approaching a temple, Brahmin priests waiting at the steps. Dappled sunlight through the forest. Rendered in the style of a Khmer sandstone bas-relief, warm stone tones and detailed figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-annan-protectorate: 679, Tống Bình on the Red River: a walled Tang administrative town with gate towers and tiled-roof halls; Tang officials in round-collared robes and black caps receive local chiefs in Vietnamese dress who bow before a yamen hall, soldiers with spears at the gate; rice fields, the broad river and boats behind. Clear daylight. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, mineral blues, greens and red, fine line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-mataram-canggal: 732, Canggal in Central Java: on a hill below a volcano, Brahmin priests and a royal party gather around a newly raised stone with a carved lingam shrine, a small Hindu temple of andesite stone being built behind; villagers bring offerings of rice and flowers, rice terraces stepping down the slopes. Clear morning light, mist on the volcano. Rendered in the style of a Central Javanese temple bas-relief, grey volcanic stone texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-laguna-copperplate: c. 900 CE, Lumban by Laguna de Bay in Luzon: in a stilt house of bamboo and thatch on the lakeshore, a scribe incises tiny illegible letters onto a thin copper plate, while a local chief and a family sit on woven mats beside him, witnessing a debt release; outrigger canoes on the lake, coconut palms and hills behind. Soft afternoon light. Painted as a warm watercolour inspired by Southeast Asian textile and bas-relief motifs. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-butuan-song: 1001, Butuan on the Agusan river in Mindanao: large wooden balangay boats with planked hulls and outriggers are loaded with tribute goods, tortoiseshell, camphor and woven cloth, while chiefs in gold ornaments and envoys in wrapped cloth prepare to depart; stilt houses and palms line the riverbank, green mountains behind. Morning light. Painted in the style of a Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, fine detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-zhou-daguan: 1296, Angkor in Cambodia: a Chinese envoy in Yuan dress with a small retinue, seen from behind, watches a royal procession pass along a causeway towards the great sandstone towers of Angkor, with parasols, elephants with gilded howdahs and palace women carrying candles; moats, palm trees and wooden houses around. Warm morning light. Painted in the style of an Angkor bas-relief, warm sandstone tones, dense detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-ho-dynasty: 1400, Tây Đô in Thanh Hóa: a massive citadel of huge cut stone blocks with arched gateways rises on a plain between mountains; Vietnamese court officials in robes and caps gather at the gate, clerks handing out sheets of paper money to merchants, soldiers with spears along the walls. Clear daylight, green hills and rice fields around. Painted as a Vietnamese traditional silk painting, soft colours and fine line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-trailok-reform: c. 1455, Ayutthaya in Thailand: inside a royal audience hall with tiered red-and-gold roofs, rows of court officials in sompot cloth and tall caps kneel in strict ranks before an elevated throne, civil officials on one side and military on the other; scribes with palm-leaf records, river barges and white stupas visible through the doors. Golden morning light. Painted in the style of a Thai temple mural, rich reds and golds, flat figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-demak: c. 1475, Demak on the north coast of Java: a large timber mosque with a three-tiered roof supported by tall wooden pillars stands in a town square, Javanese townspeople in batik sarongs and headcloths gathering at its gate; trading ships with lateen sails in the harbour nearby, palm trees and a distant volcano. Late afternoon light. Painted in the style of a Javanese wayang beber scroll painting, flat bright colours, decorative figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-hong-duc-code: 1483, Thăng Long: in a hall of the Lê imperial palace, court officials in blue and red robes and winged caps kneel in rows as a scholar reads from a large book of laws; outside in a courtyard, village elders and women in áo tứ thân listen to a magistrate announcing rules; tiled roofs and old trees. Text illegible. Painted as a Vietnamese traditional silk painting, soft colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-mac-dang-dung: 1527, Thăng Long: seen from a distance, armoured soldiers with spears and banners without lettering occupy the courtyard of the imperial palace, a general's procession entering through the main gate as officials in court robes bow at the side; tiled roofs, lotus ponds and the Red River beyond, overcast sky. Painted as a Vietnamese traditional silk painting, ink and soft colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-manila-founded: 1571, Manila Bay at the mouth of the Pasig river: Spanish galleons at anchor, soldiers in morion helmets and breastplates landing from boats on the shore, where a burnt-out native palisade settlement stands beside new wooden stockades and a cross being raised; Filipino villagers in tunics watching from outrigger boats, palms and distant mountains. Painted as a sixteenth-century Spanish colonial oil painting, warm earth colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-trinh-nguyen-war: 1627, near Đồng Hới in central Vietnam: seen from a hilltop, a long earthen defensive wall with wooden watchtowers stretches from the mountains to the sea, Nguyễn soldiers with matchlocks and spears manning it while a Trịnh army with war elephants and banners without lettering gathers across a river plain; smoke from cannon drifting. No wounded shown. Painted as a Vietnamese traditional silk painting, ink and soft colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-quoc-ngu: 1651, Rome: in a printing workshop with a wooden screw press, a Jesuit priest in a black cassock, seen from behind, examines freshly printed sheets with a printer in an apron, cases of metal type on slanted shelves, a stack of bound books on a table; through the window, terracotta roofs and the dome of a Baroque church. Letters tiny and illegible. Painted as a seventeenth-century Dutch-style genre oil painting, warm light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-konbaung: 1752, Shwebo in upper Burma: villagers and soldiers in longyi and headcloths, armed with spears, swords and matchlocks, gather on the dry plain before a stockaded village with a wooden gate and gilded pagoda spires; a leader on a horse addresses them under a white umbrella, seen small from behind, war elephants waiting nearby. Clear dry-season light, palms and distant hills. Painted in the style of a Burmese Konbaung-era temple mural, flat warm colours, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-fall-of-ayutthaya: 1767, Ayutthaya in Siam: seen from across the Chao Phraya river at a distance, the island city's brick walls and tall prang towers rise under a sky darkened by drifting smoke, Burmese troops with spears and banners without lettering camped on the far bank, boats of refugees moving down the river. No bodies shown. Painted in the style of a Thai temple mural, muted reds and golds on a dark ground, small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-tay-son: 1771, the hills of Tây Sơn in Bình Định: a gathering of peasants in brown tunics and conical hats, armed with bamboo spears, machetes and a few matchlocks, assembles in a mountain clearing before three leaders seen from behind; red banners without lettering, thatched huts and terraced fields below, forested mountains in morning mist. Painted as a Vietnamese Đông Hồ woodblock print, bold outlines and warm natural pigments. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-chakri-bangkok: 1782, Bangkok on the east bank of the Chao Phraya: workers build a new walled royal city, raising white crenellated walls and the first palace halls with multi-tiered roofs, while barges and royal boats crowd the river; Siamese nobles in sompot cloth supervise, and across the river lie the temples of the old capital at Thonburi. Bright morning light. Painted in the style of a Thai Rattanakosin temple mural, gold, red and deep green. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-ngoc-hoi-dong-da: 1789, the outskirts of Thăng Long at the Lunar New Year: seen from a distance at dawn, a Tây Sơn army with war elephants and soldiers carrying straw-covered wooden shields advances across misty rice fields towards burning earthwork forts, Qing troops in round hats and tunics retreating towards a river; peach blossom trees in the foreground. No wounded shown. Painted as a Vietnamese traditional silk painting, ink and soft colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-nguyen-dynasty: 1802, Huế on the Perfume River: a new imperial citadel with brick walls and a moat is under construction, workers hauling stone and timber; at a great ceremony before a palace hall with yellow-tiled roofs, mandarins in embroidered robes and winged hats bow in rows to a throne, the ruler small in the distance. Green hills and river boats beyond, clear sky. Painted as a Vietnamese court painting on silk, fine line and gentle colour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-tambora: 1815, the island of Sumbawa: seen from far out at sea, a giant volcano erupts with a towering column of ash and fire into a dark sky, glowing flows running down its flanks to the coast, and a small wooden trading ship with square sails turning away on a choppy sea; the shore villages of stilt houses are hidden in ash haze. Painted as an early nineteenth-century oil seascape in the manner of a marine painter, dramatic but distant. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-singapore-founded: 1819, Singapore at the mouth of the Singapore River: a small fishing settlement of Malay stilt houses and thatched huts under palm trees, a British East India ship at anchor, and boats rowing ashore with officers in tailcoats and top hats who meet Malay chiefs in sarongs and headcloths on the beach; jungle-covered hills behind. Calm morning light. Painted as an early nineteenth-century topographical watercolour, soft greens and blues. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-tale-of-kieu: c. 1820, Huế: in a quiet pavilion by a lotus pond, a scholar-poet in a dark robe and turban, seen from behind, writes with a brush on paper at a low table by lamp light, a pot of tea and bundles of paper beside him; willows, tiled roofs and the moon reflected on the pond. Characters tiny and illegible. Painted as a Vietnamese traditional silk painting, soft greys, greens and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-cultivation-system: c. 1830, a village in central Java: Javanese farmers in sarongs and headcloths carry baskets of coffee beans and cut sugar cane under the watch of a Dutch overseer in a white suit and a local village head, a sugar mill with a chimney and sheds behind; terraced fields replaced by cane, a volcano on the horizon. Hot hazy light. Painted as a nineteenth-century Dutch colonial watercolour, muted tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-bowring-treaty: 1855, Bangkok: in a royal audience hall with golden pillars and tiered roofs, Siamese nobles in brocade jackets kneel in rows while British envoys in dark frock coats and naval uniforms stand at a table with papers; outside on the river a British steamer and many Chinese junks and Thai boats. Paper text illegible. Painted in the style of a Thai temple mural of the Rattanakosin era, gold and red tones, small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-cochinchina-campaign: 1858, the bay of Đà Nẵng: seen from a hilltop, French and Spanish steam-and-sail warships fire towards earthen coastal forts, white smoke drifting over the water, landing boats of soldiers in blue uniforms and kepis heading to the beach; Vietnamese soldiers with spears and matchlocks behind the ramparts, green mountains around the bay. No wounded shown. Rendered as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving with light tint. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-cambodia-protectorate: 1863, Oudong in Cambodia: on a hill crowned with white stupas, a wooden royal palace with tiered roofs stands among palms; Khmer court officials in sampot and white jackets kneel as a French naval officer in a dark uniform and a few sailors present papers to a king seated under a tiered parasol, small in the distance. Bright dry-season light. Painted as a nineteenth-century French travel watercolour, delicate detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-aceh-war: 1873, Banda Aceh: seen from the sea at a distance, Dutch steam warships stand off a coast of palm groves, landing boats of soldiers in dark uniforms heading to the beach, while Acehnese fighters with swords and muskets gather around a large mosque with a tiered roof and a stockade; smoke drifting in the humid air. No wounded shown. Rendered as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine cross-hatching. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-rubber-malaya: 1877, Kuala Kangsar in Perak: in a botanical garden by the Perak river, a British officer in a white suit and pith helmet watches Malay gardeners in sarongs plant young rubber seedlings in neat rows; a Malay palace with tiled roofs, palms and jungle-covered hills behind, and a small boat on the river. Soft tropical morning light. Painted as a nineteenth-century botanical-style watercolour, fresh greens and fine detail. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-krakatoa: 1883, the Sunda Strait: seen from far away on a Javanese beach with palm trees, the volcanic island of Krakatoa explodes, a vast dark column of ash rising into the sky, lightning in the cloud, and a great wave approaching the coast; small fishing boats and a steamer in the distance. Painted as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper colour lithograph, dramatic but distant, no people close up. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-third-anglo-burmese-war: 1885, Mandalay: British troops in red and khaki uniforms with pith helmets march along a broad road towards the square walled palace city with its moat, crenellated red walls and tall tiered gilded spires; Burmese townspeople in longyi watch from the side, a steamboat on the Irrawaddy, Mandalay Hill with pagodas behind. Clear dry-season light. Rendered as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving with light watercolour tint. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-philippine-american-war: 1899, the outskirts of Manila: seen from a distance, American infantry in campaign hats and blue shirts advance across rice paddies towards a line of Filipino trenches defended by soldiers in straw hats with Mauser rifles, puffs of rifle smoke, a stone church bell tower and bamboo huts behind. No wounded shown. Rendered as a period illustrated newspaper engraving, fine lines and sepia tint. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-vietnamese-communist-party: 1930, Kowloon in Hong Kong: in a small, dim upstairs room of a tenement, a few men in Western jackets and some in Vietnamese tunics sit around a table covered with papers under a single lamp, a window showing a busy street with rickshaws, shop awnings and the harbour with junks. Figures seen from behind and in shadow. Paper text illegible. Rendered as a 1930s woodcut print, bold black and white with muted tone. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-siamese-revolution-1932: 1932, Bangkok: at dawn, troops in khaki uniforms with rifles stand calmly in formation on the Royal Plaza before a domed white marble throne hall, a few officers in white uniforms reading papers aloud to a small crowd; armoured car and trees in the background, no fighting. Paper text illegible. Painted as a 1930s documentary watercolour sketch, muted tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-drv-founded: 1945, Ba Đình Square in Hanoi: a vast crowd of men and women in white shirts and áo dài, conical hats and tunics fills a broad square under a sunny sky, red flags with a yellow star waving, a small wooden platform in the distance with a slender figure speaking, seen far off; trees and French colonial buildings around. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, neutral, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-first-indochina-war: c. 1946, northern Vietnam: seen from a distance, a column of Việt Minh fighters in pith-style helmets and simple uniforms carry rifles and supplies along a muddy mountain trail through limestone peaks and jungle, porters with bicycles loaded with rice sacks; smoke rising from a distant French outpost in the valley. No wounded shown. Rendered as a woodcut print in black and earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-philippines-independence: 4 July 1946, Manila: a large crowd in white shirts and dresses gathers on a park by Manila Bay before a grandstand, a flag of the Philippines being raised on a tall pole while the American flag is lowered, soldiers in formation and a band playing; war-damaged colonial buildings and palm trees in the background, bright tropical sunshine. Small figures. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-burma-independence: 4 January 1948, Rangoon at dawn: an independence ceremony on the lawn of a colonial government building. Officials and soldiers in Burmese dress, gaung baung headwear and longyi, stand at attention as the 1948 flag of the Union of Burma is raised: a red field with a blue upper-left canton bearing one large white star surrounded by five small white stars. It is NOT the modern yellow-green-red tricolour. A Union Jack is lowered on a second pole. The golden Shwedagon Pagoda gleams on its hill in the distance and crowds watch from afar. Muted documentary watercolour, soft golden light. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-bandung-conference: 1955, Bandung in West Java: delegates from many Asian and African countries in suits, robes, saris and turbans walk along a tree-lined street from a hotel to an Art Deco conference building, crowds of local people watching and waving from the pavement, rows of flags without detail; volcanic hills behind. Small figures, no recognisable faces. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-vietnam-war: c. 1965, the Mekong delta: seen from a distance, American helicopters fly low over flat green rice paddies and a village of thatched houses, smoke rising on the horizon, while a farmer in a conical hat guides a water buffalo along a dyke; palms and a winding river. No wounded shown. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, quiet greens and greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-malaya-independence: 1957, Kuala Lumpur: a new open-air stadium packed with crowds in songkok caps, baju Melayu, Chinese and Indian dress, under a morning sky; on the field soldiers in white stand in formation as a flag is raised, a small figure at a microphone seen far off with an arm raised. Small figures, no close faces. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour illustration. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-malaysia-formed: 1963, Kuala Lumpur: a public celebration on a broad green padang before a Moorish-style colonial building with copper domes and a clock tower, crowds of Malay, Chinese, Indian and Bornean people in their dress, flags fluttering, a ceremonial band in white uniforms; palms and clear morning sky. Small figures. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration, soft colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-thirtieth-september: 1965, Jakarta: a quiet, tense city street at dawn with military trucks and soldiers in green uniforms standing guard at a distance before a colonial government building; empty pavements, palm trees and a grey sky, a single becak cyclist passing. Calm, neutral and restrained, no violence shown. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour in greys and pale greens. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-may-13-incident: 1969, Kuala Lumpur: an empty city street of shophouses with closed shutters during a curfew, a single army truck and a few soldiers at a crossroads in the distance, the sky grey; palm trees and the domes of a mosque beyond. Quiet and restrained, no violence shown. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour in grey and ochre washes. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-khmer-rouge: 1975, Cambodia: on a long dusty road out of an emptied city, a column of displaced families in black and plain clothes walks with bundles on their heads and carts, seen from far behind, towards flat rice fields under a hazy sky; sugar palms dotting the plain. No violence or bodies shown. Painted as a sombre muted documentary watercolour in grey, ochre and pale green. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-lao-pdr: December 1975, Vientiane on the Mekong: a quiet street scene with a large crowd gathered at a distance before a modernist government building. On every flagpole flies the flag of the new Lao People's Democratic Republic: horizontal red, blue and red bands with a white disc in the centre. Beside them hang plain red party banners. There are no Vietnamese flags and no yellow stars. Monks in saffron robes walk past a golden stupa, with bicycles and a few old trucks on the road and the wide Mekong beyond. Neutral and calm. Muted documentary watercolour, soft warm tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-8888-uprising: 1988, Yangon: seen from far above, a broad avenue filled with distant crowds of people in longyi, students and monks walking in a large gathering towards a golden pagoda on a hill, umbrellas against the August monsoon rain; colonial buildings and trees. No individuals recognisable, no violence shown. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, grey and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-indian-ocean-tsunami: 2004, Banda Aceh: in the calm after the tsunami, a wide flattened coastal plain covered with debris and sand, only a white mosque with domes still standing amid the waste, a few rescue workers and soldiers walking far off, palm trees bent and the sea now quiet under a pale sky. No bodies shown. Painted as a sorrowful muted documentary watercolour in grey, ochre and pale blue. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
sea-nusantara: 2022, East Kalimantan in Borneo: a vast construction site cleared in rolling green hills and forest, cranes, earthmovers and the concrete frames of new government buildings rising, roads under construction cutting through the landscape; workers in helmets small in the distance, rainforest and clouds beyond. Painted as a neutral documentary watercolour illustration, fresh greens and earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-lothagam-north-pillar: c. 3000 BCE, near Lake Turkana in Kenya: on a dry ridge above the blue lake, a group of cattle herders in leather cloaks and bead ornaments raise rough basalt stone pillars around a large circular platform cemetery, herds of long-horned cattle grazing below; volcanic hills, acacia trees and a hot hazy sky. Painted in the earthy palette of East African rock art, red ochre, white and black, simple stylised figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-pearl-millet: c. 2500 BCE, the Tilemsi valley in the Sahel: farmers in leather and woven grass garments harvest tall pearl millet stalks with stone-bladed sickles, women grinding grain on flat stones and storing it in clay pots beside round huts; cattle grazing on dry grassland and a dusty sky beyond. Painted in the style of Saharan rock art, ochre and white on a sandstone ground, stylised figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-dhar-tichitt: c. 2000 BCE, Dhar Tichitt in Mauritania: along the edge of a sandstone cliff overlooking a dry valley with a shallow lake, dry-stone walled villages with round compounds and cattle enclosures; herders driving cattle down to water and women pounding millet in wooden mortars. Late afternoon light on the cliffs. Painted in the style of Saharan rock paintings, red ochre and white, stylised figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-bantu-expansion: c. 1500 BCE, the Cameroon Grassfields: a small group of farming families in bark-cloth and leather, carrying baskets of yams, oil palm nuts and clay pots and stone hoes, walk along a path from rolling grassy highlands down towards a dense rainforest edge; a village of round thatched huts behind them, misty hills. Painted in the earthy palette of Central African rock art, ochre, red and black, simple figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-punt-expedition: c. 1470 BCE, the Land of Punt on the Red Sea coast: Egyptian ships with single square sails and oars are moored at the shore, where Egyptian sailors in white kilts load potted incense trees, ebony logs, baskets of gold and baboons up gangplanks; Puntite houses on stilts among palm trees, local people bringing goods. Painted in the style of the Deir el-Bahari reliefs, flat Egyptian painted relief, ochre, blue and green. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-dmt-yeha: c. 800 BCE, Yeha in the Tigray highlands: a tall rectangular temple of finely dressed limestone blocks rises on a platform, masons in white garments setting the last stones while priests carry offerings; rugged mountains and terraced fields around, clear highland light. Rendered in the style of South Arabian and Aksumite stone relief carving, softly tinted, simple figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-nok-culture: c. 500 BCE, the Nok region of central Nigeria: in a village of round thatched huts on wooded hills, craftsmen shape and fire terracotta heads with elaborate hairstyles and pierced eyes in an open kiln, and nearby a smith works a clay furnace for iron smelting, smoke rising; women carrying water pots. Painted in a warm earthy palette inspired by Nok terracotta, ochre, brown and charcoal, soft brushwork. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-urewe: c. 500 BCE, near Lake Victoria in Kenya: farmers in bark-cloth tend a tall clay iron-smelting furnace with goatskin bellows, sparks and smoke rising, while potters decorate bowls with dimpled bases nearby; banana groves and round thatched huts by the vast lake. Soft morning light. Painted as an earthy watercolour in the palette of East African rock art, red ochre and charcoal. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-djenne-djenno: c. 250 BCE, Djenne-Djenno on the inland Niger delta: a town of round mud-brick houses on a raised mound surrounded by floodwaters, fishermen in dugout canoes with nets, rice paddies and iron-workers at furnaces; traders unloading baskets of fish and rice from canoes. Golden evening light. Painted in an earthy palette inspired by West African mud cloth and rock art, ochre and black. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-meroitic-script: c. 200 BCE, Meroe in Sudan: beside steep-sided sandstone pyramids on a desert ridge, a scribe in a linen robe carves tiny illegible signs into a stone stela, while priests and officials watch; mud-brick temples and iron-slag heaps of the city by the Nile below, palm trees, hot clear sky. Painted in the style of a Meroitic temple relief with Egyptian influence, softly painted ochres and blues. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-periplus: c. 50 CE, the port of Adulis on the Red Sea coast: Greek and Roman merchant ships with square sails at anchor, Aksumite traders in white cloth carry elephant ivory tusks and tortoiseshell down a sandy beach to small boats, a Greek merchant in a tunic writing notes on a wax tablet. Stone warehouses and hills behind, bright hazy light. Painted in the style of a Roman fresco, earthy reds and ochres. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-aksum-coins: c. 270 CE, Aksum in Ethiopia: in a royal workshop, craftsmen strike small gold and bronze coins with hammers and dies on an anvil, a balance and trays of coins on a stone table, officials in white garments watching; stone buildings with wooden beam ends and highland mountains outside. Coin markings tiny and illegible. Painted in the style of an Ethiopian manuscript painting, bold outlines and bright flat colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-ghana-rises: A painting of an early Soninke town of Wagadu (ancient Ghana) in the western Sahel around 300 CE. Low drystone and mud-walled compounds with flat roofs and round thatched granaries, with no mosques, minarets or towers with protruding wooden beams. Soninke traders, bareheaded or in simple cloth wraps, weigh gold dust on small scales beside slabs of Saharan salt. Cattle and donkeys stand near acacia trees on dry savanna. No turbans, Muslim caps or Islamic architecture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-aksum-stelae: c. 300 CE, Aksum: on a field above royal tombs, hundreds of workers with ropes, wooden rollers and earthen ramps raise a giant carved granite stele decorated with false doors and windows, smaller stelae standing nearby; officials in white robes watch, highland mountains in the background. Bright highland light. Painted in the style of an Ethiopian manuscript painting, bold outlines and bright flat colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-trans-saharan-trade: c. 400 CE, Aoudaghost on the Sahara's southern edge: a long camel caravan winds across golden dunes towards a small oasis town of stone houses with date palms, the camels loaded with slabs of rock salt, Berber traders in indigo robes and veils leading them; local merchants with gold dust waiting at the town. Low evening sun. Painted in the style of Saharan rock art, ochre and white, stylised figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-kaleb-himyar: 525 CE, the Red Sea coast of Yemen: a fleet of Aksumite sewn-plank ships with square sails lands an army on a rocky shore, soldiers in white garments with spears, round shields and bows wading ashore, a few war elephants being led down; beyond, the stone tower houses of a South Arabian town and terraced mountains under a hot sky. Seen from a distance. Painted in the style of an Ethiopian manuscript painting, bold outlines and bright flat colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-baqt: 652 CE, Old Dongola on the Nile in Nubia: outside the mud-brick walls of a Christian town with a domed church, Nubian envoys in white robes and Arab commanders in turbans and mail sit facing each other on carpets under a canopy, exchanging gifts of grain and cloth; Nubian archers on the walls, date palms and the river with sailing boats. Bright clear light. Painted in the style of a Nubian church fresco from Faras, warm ochre, red and white. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-kanem-founded: c. 700 CE, northeast of Lake Chad: nomadic Kanuri herders with camels and cattle set up a camp of round grass-mat tents and thorn-fence enclosures on the dry plain near the lake's reedy shore, a chief seated under a canopy receiving clan leaders; acacia trees, dust and a low evening sun. Painted in an earthy palette inspired by Saharan rock art and Sahelian textiles, ochre, indigo and white. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-igbo-ukwu: c. 900 CE, Igbo-Ukwu in southeastern Nigeria: in a forest compound of mud-walled huts with thatched roofs, a craftsman pours molten bronze from a clay crucible into a lost-wax mould beside a small furnace, while finished intricate bronze vessels shaped like shells and bowls decorated with fine beads and insect motifs lie on a mat; oil palms and dense forest. Painted in an earthy palette inspired by Igbo uli wall painting, ochre and black lines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-benin-kingdom: c. 1180, the forest of southern Nigeria: a clearing where Edo people build the first earthen walls and dig a deep moat around a growing town of red-mud houses with steep thatched roofs; a chief in a coral-bead collar presides under a shade tree with attendants, and the dense rainforest rises all around. Morning mist. Rendered in the style of a Benin brass plaque relief, stylised figures on a textured background. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-lalibela: c. 1200, Lalibela in the Ethiopian highlands: workers with iron picks and chisels carve a cross-shaped church downward into a pit of solid red volcanic rock, its roof level with the ground, deep trenches around it; priests in white shammas with processional crosses watch from the rim, highland mountains and juniper trees beyond. Clear morning light. Painted in the style of an Ethiopian manuscript painting, bold outlines and bright flat colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-ife-heads: c. 1200, Ile-Ife in Yorubaland: inside a palace workshop courtyard of red-earth walls, artists shape a naturalistic terracotta head with fine striations and polish a copper-alloy head on a stand, a small clay furnace glowing; attendants in woven cloth watch, and a line of finished heads rests on a low bench. Forest trees beyond. Painted in a warm earthy palette inspired by Yoruba textiles and terracotta, soft brushwork. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-solomonic: c. 1270, Tegulet in Shewa: a highland royal camp of large white tents on a green plateau, priests in white with crosses and umbrellas and nobles in embroidered cloaks gather as a new king, small and seen from behind, sits under a red ceremonial parasol; soldiers with spears and round shields, mountains and juniper woods around. Painted in the style of an Ethiopian manuscript painting, bold outlines and bright flat colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-kongo-kingdom: c. 1390, Mbanza Kongo on a hilltop plateau in northern Angola: a royal town of rectangular thatched houses with woven palm-fibre walls inside a palisade, a large assembly of Kongo nobles in raffia cloth and caps gathering before a king seated under a tree with attendants holding fans and an ivory horn player; savannah and forested valleys below. Painted in an earthy palette inspired by Kongo raffia textile patterns, ochre and brown. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-mutapa: c. 1430, Mount Fura in northern Zimbabwe: a royal settlement of round thatched huts and dry-stone enclosures on a hillside, Shona miners carrying baskets of gold-bearing quartz, traders exchanging gold dust for glass beads and cloth with Swahili merchants in white robes; granite hills and savannah woodland beyond. Warm afternoon light. Painted in an earthy palette inspired by southern African rock art, ochre and red. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-ewuare: c. 1440, Benin City: thousands of labourers dig a deep moat and pile up huge earthen walls around the city, which has broad straight streets and red-earth palace compounds with steep roofs and turrets; chiefs in coral beads and attendants with fans supervise, forest beyond. Seen from a distance. Rendered in the style of a Benin brass plaque relief, stylised figures, textured background. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-dias-cape: 1488, the Cape of Good Hope: two small Portuguese caravels with lateen sails marked with red crosses battle rough grey-green seas off a rugged rocky headland, storm clouds clearing to reveal sunlight, seabirds overhead; distant mountains along the coast. No people close up. Painted in the style of a fifteenth-century Portuguese illuminated sea chart, decorative ships and waves. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-benin-bronzes: c. 1500, Benin City: in a guild workshop of the Oba's palace, brass-casters in wrappers pour molten brass into clay moulds, while finished rectangular brass plaques showing warriors and Portuguese traders in helmets hang on red-earth walls; a few Portuguese visitors in doublets and hats watching from the doorway. Rendered in the style of a Benin brass plaque relief, stylised figures with textured background. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-ethiopia-adal: A 16th-century Ethiopian manuscript-style painting of the Battle of Shimbra Kure, 1529, in the Ethiopian highlands. On one side Imam Ahmad Gragn's Adal army in white turbans and cotton robes, with a few matchlock musketeers firing and plain cloth or crescent-topped banners. On the other side Emperor Lebna Dengel's Ethiopian host with spears, round hide shields and processional crosses, under a red ceremonial umbrella. No national tricolour flags of any kind, no modern Ethiopian green-yellow-red flag and no European flags. A marshy stream between them, mountains behind. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-gondar: 1636, Gondar in the Ethiopian highlands: a stone castle with round domed towers and crenellated walls rises in a royal enclosure, masons on wooden scaffolding finishing it, priests in white and courtiers with umbrellas gathered; round thatched churches and the green hills around Lake Tana. Clear highland light. Painted in the style of a Gondarine church mural, bright flat colours and large-eyed figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-oyo-empire: c. 1650, Oyo-Ile on the West African savanna: a large army of Yoruba cavalry in quilted armour with spears and decorated bridles rides out from a walled town of red-earth houses with thatched roofs, drummers and foot soldiers following; baobab trees and open grassland, dust in the golden afternoon light. Painted in the style of a Yoruba textile and wall-painting palette, indigo, ochre and red. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-sokoto: c. 1804, the Hausa lands of northern Nigeria: Fulani horsemen in white robes and turbans with spears and banners without lettering ride across dry savanna towards a walled Hausa town of red mud-brick houses with pinnacled gates; a scholar on foot with followers carrying books walks at the front. Seen from a distance. Painted as a West African-inspired watercolour with earthy reds and indigo. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-mfecane: c. 1818, southeastern Africa: across grassy hills, long lines of displaced families with cattle herds, carrying rolled mats, pots and bundles, migrate towards distant mountains, while far off a regiment of warriors with tall cowhide shields and short spears crosses a ridge; smoke on the horizon. No violence shown. Painted as an early nineteenth-century travel watercolour, soft earth tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-liberia: 1847, Monrovia on Cape Mesurado: a small town of white frame houses with verandas on a green hill above the Atlantic, a gathering of men in dark frock coats and top hats and women in long dresses before a modest government building as a flag with stripes and a single star is raised; ships offshore and palms. Paper text illegible. Painted as a nineteenth-century American engraving with light watercolour tint. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-livingstone-falls: 1855, the Zambezi river: a small party, a Scottish explorer in a peaked cap and a group of Makololo guides in a dugout canoe, approaches an island at the lip of an immense waterfall, a vast column of spray rising like smoke with a rainbow, the river spilling into a deep chasm; lush riverine forest. Figures small. Painted as a nineteenth-century travel watercolour, misty and luminous. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-magdala: 1868, Magdala in the Ethiopian highlands: a flat-topped mountain fortress on a sheer cliff, with a long column of British troops in red coats and white helmets, elephants carrying artillery and mule trains winding up a mountain road below; puffs of cannon smoke near the fortress gate. Seen from a great distance, no wounded shown. Rendered as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine cross-hatching. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-anc-founded: 1912, Bloemfontein: a gathering of Black South African men in dark suits, waistcoats and collars, some in clerical dress, sits on benches in a simple church hall with tall windows, listening to a speaker at a table; outside, a dusty street of corrugated-iron roofs and veld under a vast blue sky. Figures small. Painted as an early twentieth-century documentary watercolour, muted tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-taung-child: 1924, Johannesburg: at a wooden desk by a window, a scientist in a shirt and waistcoat, seen from behind, chips away limestone from a small fossil skull with a knitting needle, lamp light falling on scattered tools, boxes of rock and a microscope; outside a dusk sky. Painted as a 1920s documentary watercolour, warm muted tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-freedom-charter: 1955, Kliptown near Johannesburg: a large open-air gathering of thousands of people of many backgrounds seated on a dusty field before a simple wooden stage with banners without lettering, women in headscarves, men in hats and suits; corrugated-iron houses and a few eucalyptus trees around, bright winter sun. Seen from a distance. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, warm tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-things-fall-apart: c. 1958, Igboland in southeastern Nigeria: a traditional Igbo village of red-earth compounds with thatched roofs and carved wooden doors, an elders' meeting under a great tree with a slit drum, yam barns full of stacked yams, and in the distance a small mission church with a cross beside a dirt road. Calm afternoon light. Painted in a muted woodcut style with earthy tones, quiet and literary. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-year-of-africa: 1960, Lagos: crowds in colourful agbada robes, wrappers and headwraps fill a racecourse field at night as a new green-and-white flag rises on a pole, fireworks bursting overhead, soldiers in formation and a brass band; palm trees and colonial buildings in the background. Seen from a distance, no faces close. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-arusha: 1967, rural Tanzania: a new ujamaa village of mud-brick houses with tin roofs in neat rows, villagers in kanga cloth and shirts hoeing a shared maize field and gathering at a meeting under a baobab tree, a schoolhouse being built; Mount Meru rising in the distance. Bright daylight. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, warm earth and green tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-tazara: c. 1970, the Tanzanian countryside: Chinese and Tanzanian workers in work clothes and caps lay rails and wooden sleepers across red earth through savanna and hills, a small diesel locomotive and wagons of rails behind them, a newly built concrete bridge spanning a river; acacia trees and wide sky. Small figures. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-lucy: 1974, Hadar in the Afar region of Ethiopia: in a barren, eroded landscape of grey and ochre gullies under a hot sky, a few researchers in hats kneel with brushes and small tools around fragments of fossil bone laid out on the ground, a Land Rover and tents in the distance. Figures small and seen from behind. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-angola: 1975, Luanda: the curving bay front with Portuguese colonial buildings, palm trees and a fort on a hill; crowds gather at a distance as a new flag rises, while ships in the harbour take away departing settlers with crates and luggage on the quay. Calm evening light. Painted as a neutral documentary watercolour, muted tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-ethiopian-famine: 1983, Korem in the Ethiopian highlands: a relief camp of tents and corrugated sheds on a bare, wind-swept plateau, long lines of people wrapped in white shawls waiting quietly at a food distribution point, aid workers unloading grain sacks from a truck; dry brown hills and a grey sky. No bodies shown. Painted as a sombre muted documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-somali-civil-war: 1991, Mogadishu: a quiet view of the Indian Ocean coastal city with white Italian-era buildings, many damaged and roofless, an empty street with a burnt-out truck, a few distant figures walking, and the blue sea beyond under a hot sky. No violence or bodies shown. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, pale ochre and blue. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-rwandan-genocide: 1994, Kigali: a calm view of the green terraced hills of Rwanda at dusk, scattered houses with tin roofs, banana groves and mist in the valleys, a single lit memorial candle lantern on a low stone wall in the foreground. Mournful and restrained, no people, no violence. Painted as a sorrowful muted documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-trc: 1996, a public hearing hall in South Africa: a large plain room with a long table draped in cloth where commissioners sit, a witness at a small table with headphones for translation, and rows of listeners on chairs; everyone seen from behind and at a distance, tall windows with soft light. Paper text illegible. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour, calm and dignified. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-second-congo-war: c. 1998, Goma on the shore of Lake Kivu: seen from a distance, a road crowded with displaced families carrying bundles and jerrycans, a few military trucks parked by the roadside, the volcano Nyiragongo rising behind the town under heavy clouds and the lake shining. No violence shown. Painted as a sombre muted documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-focac: 2000, Beijing: a broad view of a large modern conference hall with rows of flags without emblems along the walls, delegates in suits and African robes seated at long curved tables, interpreters in booths above; everyone small and seen from behind. Neutral, calm daylight from high windows. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-african-union: 2002, Durban: a large conference centre beside the Indian Ocean, delegates in suits and colourful African robes walking along a palm-lined promenade towards its entrance, rows of flags without detail fluttering, a ceremonial guard of honour in white uniforms at the steps, the sea, ships on the horizon and a sunny winter sky beyond. Small figures, no recognisable faces. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-darfur: c. 2003, near El Fasher in Darfur: a vast camp of makeshift tents and grass shelters on a dry plain, women in colourful wraps carrying water containers from a well, a few aid trucks, thorn trees and a dust-hazed sky. Seen from a distance, no violence or bodies shown. Painted as a sombre muted documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-boko-haram: c. 2009, Maiduguri in northeast Nigeria: a quiet, empty dusty street of single-storey houses and shops with closed shutters, a military checkpoint with sandbags and soldiers far off, a mosque minaret and neem trees in the background under a hazy sky. Tense but calm, no violence shown. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-south-sudan: 2011, Juba: a large crowd in colourful clothes celebrates on a dusty open ground beside the White Nile as a new flag rises on a pole, drummers and dancers at the edge, soldiers in formation; mango trees and low buildings, bright midday sun. Seen from a distance, no faces close. Painted as a muted documentary gouache illustration. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-mali-war: c. 2012, Gao on the Niger river: a quiet view of a Sahelian town of mud-brick houses and the stepped mud-brick pyramid tomb of the Askia, a few pick-up trucks parked at the edge of town, the broad river and sandbanks beyond under a dusty sky. No violence shown. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour in ochre and pale blue. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-ebola: 2014, Guéckédou in the forest region of Guinea: a health centre of tents and white tarpaulin shelters at the edge of a village of mud-brick houses with tin roofs, health workers in full protective suits walking along a fenced path, villagers watching from a distance; forested hills and humid haze. Painted as a muted documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-afcfta: 2018, Kigali: a modern domed convention centre lit at dusk on a green hill, flags without emblems lining the approach road, delegates in suits and robes small in the distance walking to the entrance; the city's hills and lights spreading around. Painted as a neutral documentary watercolour, calm blue and gold tones. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-tigray-war: c. 2020, the Tigray highlands near Mekelle: a quiet, bare mountain landscape of terraced fields and stone houses, a line of displaced families walking with donkeys and bundles on a dusty road far off, an aid truck parked by the roadside; clouds over flat-topped mountains. No violence shown. Painted as a sombre muted documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
af-sudan-war: 2023, Khartoum at the meeting of the Blue and White Nile: a distant view of the city skyline under a haze of smoke, empty streets in the foreground, and on a road leading out of the city a long line of buses, cars and people on foot carrying bundles; the rivers shining in the low sun. No violence shown. Painted as a sombre muted documentary watercolour. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.shang-bronze-cultures.1: About 1300 BCE, Wucheng on the Gan River, Jiangxi: a walled town of rammed earth on a low rise above the river, thatched timber houses on stilts and low platforms inside.
