Near the gate, workers in hemp tunics pour glowing bronze into clay moulds over a charcoal pit, while a potter beside them scratches small geometric signs into the shoulder of a grey stoneware jar. Green subtropical hills, paddy-like marshes and dugout canoes on the broad river. No tiled roofs, no iron tools, no legible text. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, jade green and ochre, humid haze. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.shang-bronze-cultures.2: About 1250 BCE, Yin near Anyang: a vast open-air foundry yard beside rammed-earth workshops with thatched hipped roofs. Rows of sectioned clay piece moulds are fitted around cores; teams of bronze-smiths in plain hemp tunics with hair in topknots tilt crucibles from glowing pit furnaces, pouring molten bronze into a large square cauldron mould while others polish finished ding, gu and jue vessels lined up in rows. Smoke drifts over the Huan River. Figures small, seen from a distance. No iron, no wheels on furnaces, no legible inscriptions. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, bronze browns and smoky ochres. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.shang-bronze-cultures.6: About 1100 BCE, Jinsha on the Chengdu plain: a riverside ritual ground among bamboo groves and wet rice fields at dawn. Priests in long patterned robes lay out yellow jade cong, jade blades and stacks of elephant tusks on the bank, while one raises a thin gold foil disc cut with a sun and four circling birds toward the rising sun. Thatched timber halls on stilts beyond, river mist. No giant bronze statues in this scene, no tiled roofs, no stirrups. Figures small, seen from behind. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, cinnabar and gold-ochre. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.wu-ding.5: About 1200 BCE, Yin near Anyang: a rectangular vertical shaft tomb inside the royal precinct, with a timber chamber at its base. Attendants in hemp and silk robes lower bronze battle-axes, ritual vessels, jade figurines and carved ivory cups into the chamber on ropes, while mourners and priests stand in ranks along the edge of the pit. Rammed-earth halls with thatched roofs and the Huan River behind, overcast morning. No bodies shown, no tiled roofs, no legible inscriptions. Figures small, frieze-like arrangement. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre, frieze composition. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.zhou-conquers-shang.7: 1046 BCE, Chaoge: evening falls over the Shang capital, and a tall rammed-earth terrace, the Deer Terrace, rises above the city with a timber pavilion on top now wreathed in flames. Smoke pours into a dark red sky; far below, chariots with spoked wheels and Zhou foot soldiers with dagger-axes and banners halt outside the walls, watching. No figures visible in the flames, no blood, no tiled roofs, no stirrups or ridden horses. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, muted ochre, cinnabar and black, distant figures, no blood. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.confucius-journey.3: 496 BCE, Kuang: on a dusty road outside a small walled town, a light two-horse carriage with an umbrella canopy is halted, ringed by local men with spears and staves. Confucius, an elderly scholar in a long robe and cap, sits calmly in the carriage seen from behind, his disciples standing close around him; one plays a zither. Village earthen walls and millet fields in hazy light. No stirrups, no ridden horses, no tiled roofs, no violence. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, warm ochres. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.confucius-journey.4: 492 BCE, Song: a huge old spreading tree on the edge of a field, under which a circle of disciples in long robes practise ritual bows while Confucius instructs them. Nearby, men sent by the minister Huan Tui swing axes at the trunk, chips flying, and the group quietly gathers up and walks away along a path toward distant hills, a carriage waiting. Late afternoon light. No violence shown, no tiled roofs, no stirrups. Figures small, seen from a distance. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, warm ochres and greens. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.confucius-journey.5: 489 BCE, between Chen and Cai: in a wild marshy plain, Confucius's small party sits camped beside two unhitched carriages, weary disciples lying in the grass, an empty cooking pot over a dead fire. Confucius sits upright playing a zither. On a low ridge around them a ring of armed men stands guard, while far off on the horizon a column of Chu chariots and banners approaches. Misty morning, muted greens and greys, figures small, seen from a distance. No stirrups, no tiled roofs. Ink and light colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.confucius-journey.6: 484 BCE, Qufu, state of Lu: a quiet courtyard of a modest thatched house with a timber veranda, apricot trees in blossom. An elderly Confucius sits on a mat surrounded by seated disciples in long robes, bundles of bamboo slips tied with cord stacked beside him, one disciple unrolling a slip bundle. The city's rammed-earth walls and gentle hills beyond. No paper, no books with covers, no legible text, no tiled pagodas. Figures small, seen from a distance. Soft spring light, muted greens and greys. Ink and light colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.wu-and-yue.4: About 490 BCE, Kuaiji, state of Yue: inside a plain timber hall with a thatched roof, a king in simple hemp robe sits on a mat on a bed of brushwood rather than cushions; a dried gall bladder hangs on a cord from the beam above his seat, and he reaches up toward it before a modest meal on a low table. Attendants wait by the door; through it, rice fields, canals and grey hills under overcast sky. Figure seen from the side at mid-distance, no close-up face. No chairs, no tiled roofs. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, blues and greys. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.qu-yuan-and-chu.1: About 311 BCE, Linzi, capital of Qi: a Chu envoy's carriage, drawn by four horses with a tall parasol, rolls through the great gate of Linzi's massive rammed-earth walls into a busy broad avenue. Crowds in Qi robes, market stalls, ox carts; Qu Yuan stands in the carriage in a tall hat and long sweeping Chu robe, seen from behind, with banners of his retinue. Grey sea haze beyond the city. No stirrups, no ridden cavalry saddles with stirrups, no tiled pagodas. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, flowing line, black, red and gold. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.qu-yuan-and-chu.4: About 296 BCE, crossing the Yangtze toward Lake Dongting: a small boat with a matting canopy crosses the wide brown river, a boatman poling at the stern. A lone figure in a tall hat and long sweeping robe, Qu Yuan, stands at the bow looking south toward a vast reed-fringed lake and misty hills. Behind, on the northern bank, the walls of a Chu town fade into haze. Autumn wind ripples the water, wild geese overhead. Figures small, no close-up face. No tiled pagodas. Painted in the style of a Warring States lacquerware scene, black, cinnabar and ochre. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.qu-yuan-and-chu.5: About 290 BCE, Xupu on the Yuan River: a narrow boat rowed upstream between towering dark forested cliffs, rain falling steadily, clouds hanging low among the trees. Gibbons swing and cluster in the branches overhead. A lone traveller in a tall hat and long robe sits under the boat's matting cover, seen from behind, gazing at the gloomy gorge ahead. Rushing water, mist, no villages. Figures small. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, black and red with drifting mist. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.qin-unification.6: 221 BCE, Linzi, state of Qi: the massive rammed-earth gates of Linzi stand open, and a column of Qin soldiers in black lamellar armour with crossbows and halberds marches in under black banners. Before them the last Qi king and his officials, bareheaded in plain robes, stand by the roadside in surrender, a carriage behind them. Crowds watch silently from the ramparts. No battle, no bodies, no stirrups. Painted in the style of Han-dynasty tomb murals, flat colours of black, red and ochre on plaster, figures small and seen from a distance, no faces in close-up. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.first-emperor-tours.0: 220 BCE, Longxi on the western frontier: a long imperial procession of black-lacquered carriages under parasols, flanked by Qin cavalry and foot guards with black banners, winds up a road through bare loess hills toward a narrow mountain pass. Watchtowers of rammed earth stand on the ridges, herds of horses graze in the valleys, and distant snow-dusted peaks rise on the horizon. The emperor's carriage is closed, no figure shown. No stirrups, no tiled pagodas. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, ochre, cinnabar and green on plaster, flat stylised mountains. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.first-emperor-tours.4: 215 BCE, Jieshi on the Bohai coast: on a rocky headland above the sea, stonemasons with mallets and chisels cut columns of characters into a smoothed cliff face, the marks shown only as blurred lines with no legible text. Below on the beach, a group of magicians in robes board small boats to sail out toward misty islands where the immortals are thought to live. The emperor's retinue with black banners and carriages waits on the slope. Waves, gulls. No stirrups. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.first-emperor-tours.5: 210 BCE, Mount Kuaiji: a solemn sacrifice on a forested southern mountain; an altar platform of earth with smoke rising from offerings, ranks of officials in black robes bowing, and the emperor, seen from behind under a canopy, facing the peak in honour of Yu the Great. Nearby, a tall stone stele stands newly erected, its surface showing no legible text. Below, green hills, rivers and the hazy sea to the east. No stirrups, no tiled pagodas. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, dark reds, ochre and black on plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.han-xiongnu.7: 119 BCE, Mount Langjuxu beyond the Gobi: on a bare windswept summit in the northern steppe, a Han general's retinue builds an earthen altar mound and burns offerings, smoke rising into a vast pale sky. Below, the Han cavalry army rests on the grassland, armoured horsemen with long halberds beside their mounts, red banners flapping, captured Xiongnu horses herded in the distance. Seen from far away, tiny figures, no stirrups, no bodies. Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing style, with galloping horses in silhouette like Han relief carvings. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.seven-states-rebellion.0: 155 BCE, Chang'an: a palace hall of timber columns on a raised terrace, its tiled roof seen from a distance. Inside, the emperor sits on a dais behind a low table, and an official in black robes and a tall cap kneels before him holding a bundle of bamboo slips, gesturing earnestly, while other ministers sit in rows on mats along the sides. Through open doors, the walls of the capital. No chairs, no paper, no legible text. Figures small, seen from a distance. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, earthy red, ochre and black pigments. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.seven-states-rebellion.2: 154 BCE, the eastern market of Chang'an: a wide market square lined with low tiled shops and closed stalls, a silent crowd held back by soldiers with halberds. In the centre an official in full black court robes and cap is led forward by guards on an ordinary winter morning; the execution itself is not shown. Far beyond the city walls, dust rises from marching armies in the east. No blood, no bodies. Figures small, seen from a distance. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.seven-states-rebellion.4: 154 BCE, Changyi: a fortified Han camp behind high earth walls and palisades, with watchtowers and banners, the gates closed; inside, soldiers drill calmly. A lone messenger rider from Liang gallops up to the shut gate. In the far distance, a column of light cavalry slips south through farmland toward a river, where a line of grain carts and boats is being cut off. Overcast sky, wide panoramic view. No stirrups, figures small, no gore. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.seven-states-rebellion.5: 154 BCE, near Xiayi: night attack on a large Han camp. At the south-east corner a noisy feint of torches and drums, but at the north-west corner Han soldiers with crossbows and shields hold the wall firm against massed rebel infantry with ladders, who fall back. Beyond, the rebel camps break up, men streaming away across the plain. Figures small, seen from a distance, no gore, no bodies, no stirrups. Torchlight against a dark sky. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.seven-states-rebellion.6: 154 BCE, Dantu on the lower Yangtze: a small party of fugitives in travel-worn robes crosses the broad grey river in a few boats toward the southern shore, where Yue warriors with bronze-tipped spears and tattooed arms wait among reeds and low thatched huts. Rain clouds, wind whipping the water. No violence shown, no bodies. Figures small, seen from far off. No stirrups. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.seven-states-rebellion.7: 154 BCE, Chang'an: in a large palace courtyard under clear autumn light, court officials appointed by the emperor receive seals and cords from a herald and set off in carriages toward the kingdoms, while kings' envoys bow in rows. Clerks at low tables tally bamboo slip registers. Tiled halls on raised terraces and the city walls behind. Calm, orderly mood. No legible text, no paper, no stirrups. Figures small, seen from a distance. Painted as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ink on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.zhang-qian.1: About 138 BCE, the Hexi Corridor: a Han envoy party of about a hundred men with pack horses is surrounded by Xiongnu horsemen in fur caps and felt coats on a dry plain between the Qilian snow peaks and the desert. In the background, a Xiongnu camp of round felt tents and herds; years later life there goes on. Zhang Qian, seen from behind, still holds his tall envoy's staff with yak-tail tassels. No stirrups, no violence. Figures small, clear dry light. Han tomb mural style, ochre ground, red and black lines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.zhang-qian.2: About 129 BCE, Dayuan (Ferghana): coming down from the snowy Tian Shan passes, a small party of travellers with an envoy's tassel staff arrives in a green valley of orchards, irrigation canals and walled towns of mud brick. Tall, splendid horses graze in meadows, herded by local riders in belted tunics and pointed caps. A local escort points the way west. No stirrups, no turbans, no domes, no mosques. Figures small, clear dry light. Han tomb mural style, ochre ground, red and black lines. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.zhang-qian.3: About 128 BCE, north of the Oxus: the Yuezhi in prosperous settled lands, a wide green river valley with mud-brick fortified towns, vineyards and orchards. Zhang Qian's small party with its tassel staff is received at a large felt tent beside a town by Yuezhi nobles in long belted caftans and trousers, who feast calmly and gesture refusal. Bactrian camels and horses nearby, distant arid mountains. No stirrups, no domes, no mosques. Evening light. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments, flat figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.zhang-qian.4: About 127 BCE, north of the Kunlun: a tiny party of travellers with pack animals crosses a narrow oasis track along the southern edge of the Tarim basin, the snowy Kunlun range towering to the south and endless sand dunes to the north. From a gully, Xiongnu horsemen in fur caps ride out to intercept them. Poplars and a mud-walled oasis town in the distance. No stirrups, no violence shown, figures small. Rendered in the style of a Han tomb mural, ochre, red and black pigments, flat figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sima-qian-travels.0: About 126 BCE, Chang'an: at dawn a young man in a plain travelling robe and cap, about twenty, sets out from one of the great gates of the Han capital in a light one-horse cart with a servant, bundles of bamboo slips and a few belongings tied on behind. Behind him, the high rammed-earth walls, gate towers and tiled roofs of palaces; ahead, a long road east across the Wei River plain toward distant hills. No stirrups, no paper books. Figures small, seen from behind. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red pigments, stylised peaks. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sima-qian-travels.1: About 126 BCE, Huaiyin: on a low hill above flat watery country of the Huai, a grave mound stands on high ground with open fields stretching around it. A young traveller in a plain robe sits on a stone beside a few elderly villagers who point toward the mound as they tell stories, his cart waiting below. Willows, rice paddies, thatched farmhouses and a river with boats. Afternoon light, figures small, seen from a distance. No stirrups. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red pigments, stylised peaks. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sima-qian-travels.2: About 126 BCE, Mount Kuaiji: a lone traveller with a walking staff climbs a steep stone path through dense green forest toward a dark cave mouth high on the mountainside, a local guide leading with a torch. Far below, the plains of Yue, rivers and the distant sea in drifting cloud. A small earthen altar marks the old shrine of Yu. Figures small, seen from behind. No tiled pagodas, no Buddhist temples. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red pigments, stylised peaks. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sima-qian-travels.3: About 126 BCE, the Miluo River near Changsha: a small boat moored at a quiet bend where the river widens into a still, deep pool shaded by maples and reeds. A young traveller in a plain robe stands alone on the bank with head bowed, seen from behind, his boatman waiting at the oars. Misty hills, autumn leaves drifting on the water. Melancholy calm, figures small. No Buddhist temples, no tiled pagodas. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red pigments, stylised peaks. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sima-qian-travels.4: About 126 BCE, Qufu: the courtyard of Confucius's old house turned shrine, a simple tiled hall where an old two-wheeled carriage and folded robes are displayed. Students in long robes and caps practise ritual bows and music with bells and chime stones in the courtyard, while a young traveller stands quietly at the edge watching, seen from behind. Cypress trees, low walls. No Buddhist elements, no legible text, no stirrups. Figures small. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red pigments. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sima-qian-travels.5: About 126 BCE, near Pengcheng: a lone traveller's cart with a broken wheel stuck in the mud on a rainy road across the flat plain of the lower Huai, the young man and his servant pushing it. In the distance, the walled town of Pengcheng and the villages of Feng and Pei among willows, farmers working their fields. Grey sky, wet earth. No stirrups. Figures small, seen from a distance. Painted in the manner of a Han tomb mural, ochre, green and red pigments, stylised landscape. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sima-qian-travels.7: 110 BCE, Luoyang: a dim room in a house at night, an oil lamp on a bronze stand. An old man lies on a low platform bed under a quilt, holding the hand of his son, who kneels beside him in travel-stained robes; bundles of bamboo slips are stacked on a low table nearby. Through the open lattice, the tiled roofs of the city at night. Mid-distance view, no close-up faces. No legible writing. Han tomb mural style, warm lamplit tones on plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.guangwu-restoration.2: 25 CE, Qianqiu pavilion south of Hao, Hebei: an open-air enthronement on a raised earthen altar with a small pavilion on top, red banners of Han on poles. Liu Xiu, in a black and red ceremonial robe and crown with hanging tassels, is seen from behind ascending the altar steps while generals in armour and officials kneel in rows below. Smoke rises from a sacrificial fire to Heaven; cavalry and carriages wait on the flat northern plain. No stirrups. Painted as a Han tomb mural, mineral red, black and ochre on whitewashed plaster, outlined figures in procession. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.eastern-han-learning.7: About 200, Qiao: a doctor's courtyard house with a tiled roof. In the yard, a white-haired physician in a long robe leads several pupils through slow exercises imitating animals: one crouches like a tiger, one stretches like a deer, another stands like a bird with arms spread. Inside the open hall a patient lies asleep on a mat, attendants beside a steaming herbal pot. Peaceful morning, figures small, seen from a distance, no surgery or blood shown. Painted as an Eastern Han tomb mural of daily life, soft ochre and red lines on plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.ban-chao.1: 73 CE, Shanshan near Lop Nur: at night in a strong wind, a few dozen Han soldiers set fire to the felt tents of an enemy embassy camp outside a mud-walled oasis town, beating drums upwind. Flames and smoke whip across the desert sand under a starry sky; distant horsemen scatter. Distant view, no bodies, no blood. No stirrups. One unbroken scene with no borders or registers. Rendered as an Eastern Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, grey ink on paper, galloping horses in strong silhouette. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.ban-chao.2: 73 CE, Khotan: before the mud-brick palace of an oasis kingdom, a confrontation in a wide courtyard. A Han officer in armour and a few soldiers stand firm; a shaman in a fringed robe who demanded a horse is led away by guards, not shown harmed. The king in a belted caftan, seated under an awning, gestures to his men, who march out foreign envoys. Poplars, mulberry orchards and the snowy Kunlun beyond a sandy plain under a pale sky. No blood, no stirrups. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on paper, flat silhouetted riders in a horizontal frieze. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.ban-chao.4: 87 CE, Yarkand: a large allied army of Han troops and local oasis contingents in caftans and felt caps camped on a desert plain; at dusk, part of the army marches openly away eastward as if retreating, while horsemen sent by Kucha follow far off. In the background the mud-brick walls of Yarkand with its gates opening and envoys emerging. Distant view, figures small, no bodies. No stirrups. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on paper, flat silhouetted riders in a horizontal frieze. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.ban-chao.5: 91 CE, Kucha: before the mud-brick walls and gate of the oasis city, a Han officer in armour sits under an awning on a low dais as the Protector General, while envoys of Kucha, Gumo and Wensu in belted caftans and felt caps bow and present horses, felt and jade. Han soldiers with red banners line the approach. Poplars, irrigation channels, reed beds and the snowy Tianshan behind. Bright day, figures small, seen from a distance. No stirrups, no domes. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, ochre, red and green pigments. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.guandu.3: 200, near Yanjin on the Yellow River: on a flat river road, abandoned baggage carts, chests and loose horses lie scattered as bait; Yuan cavalry riders have dismounted and break formation to loot them. From behind a low earth bank, a compact force of armoured horsemen with long lances bursts forth in a charge, the looters scattering. The wide yellow river and ferry boats behind. Small figures, seen from a distance, no gore. No stirrups. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing of cavalry battle, bold silhouettes in grey ink. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.guandu.4: Autumn 200, Guandu: two vast fortified camps face each other across a flat plain. On Yuan's side, tall earth mounds with wooden towers from which archers shoot volleys into the opposing camp; on Cao's side, soldiers shelter under shields while traction trebuchets pulled by teams of men hurl stones at the towers, and trench diggers work along a deep ditch. Dust and drifting arrows, autumn haze. No counterweight trebuchets, no stirrups, no gore. Figures small. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on paper, stylised figures in flat registers. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.guandu.5: Winter 200, Guandu: at night a lone horseman in a cloak gallops away from a great camp lit by braziers across the frozen plain toward the opposing camp's palisade, where sentries with torches open the gate. In the far distance, at Wuchao, long rows of grain carts and stacked granary sheds sit under guard. Cold starlight, bare trees. Figures small, seen from a distance. No stirrups. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on paper, stylised horses and fire in flat registers. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.guandu.7: 201, Cangting on the Yellow River: a great army marches in ordered ranks along the riverbank under many banners, then wheels to attack an enemy camp on the flats; the enemy's lines break and scatter across the plain toward distant city walls. Wide yellow river, grey late-summer sky. High distant view, figures small, no gore, no bodies. No stirrups. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, ordered rows of soldiers and city walls, grey ink. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.red-cliffs.1: Autumn 208, Xiangyang in Jing province: the great gate of a walled city on the Han River stands open; a young lord and his officials in plain robes walk out carrying seals and bundles of registers, bowing before the vanguard of a huge northern army with banners and armoured cavalry. Townspeople watch quietly from the walls. Broad river with boats behind, autumn trees. No battle, no stirrups. Small figures. Rendered as an Eastern Han tomb mural, quick ink and earthy red. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.red-cliffs.3: 208, Chaisang on the Yangtze: inside a large timber hall with a tiled roof open to the river, a young ruler stands and draws his sword to strike the corner of a low table, declaring for war; around him advisers in robes kneel on mats, some recoiling, while a commander in armour and a scholar in a light robe with a feather fan stand by. Through the open side, warships on the river. Mid-distance view, no close-up faces, no chairs. Rendered as an Eastern Han tomb mural, quick ink and earthy red. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.red-cliffs.5: Winter 208, Huarong: a defeated army struggles through vast reed marshes and mud on a narrow track; soldiers lay bundles of reeds and brushwood across the mire so horses and carts can pass, some men sinking to their knees. Wind and drizzle, smoke from burnt ships faint on the horizon. Seen from a high distance, small figures, no bodies, no individual faces. No stirrups. Painted in the style of a late Han tomb mural, cinnabar, black and ochre washes on plaster, sweeping rhythmic brushwork. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.red-cliffs.6: 209, the middle Yangtze: a wide river landscape divided by the great river. On the south bank, columns of soldiers under one set of banners march into walled commandery towns among green hills; downstream, warships of another lord patrol the lower river; on the far northern shore, a distant fortified line holds. A sense of three separate camps across one vast landscape. Seen from far above, small figures, no battle. No stirrups. Painted in the style of a late Han tomb mural, cinnabar, black and ochre washes on plaster, sweeping rhythmic brushwork. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.liu-bei-shu-hanzhong.0: 211, Fu in Sichuan: outside a walled town on the Fu River, a long banquet in the open air under awnings, low tables laden with food along rows of mats, two lords in robes seated side by side on a raised dais, musicians and dancers performing, soldiers of both armies relaxing nearby. Green hills of the Sichuan basin, bamboo and terraced fields. Mid-distance view, small figures, no chairs, no stirrups. Rendered as an Eastern Han tomb mural from Sichuan, warm red and ochre lines on pale plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.liu-bei-shu-hanzhong.1: 212, Jiameng Pass in northern Sichuan: an army camp in a narrow mountain valley; soldiers help local farmers bring in the harvest and share grain at a gate, while villagers bring gifts. In the foreground a messenger arrives, and the army begins to strike its tents and turn its banners south down the valley road. Steep forested mountains, a river below. Figures small, seen from a distance. No stirrups. Rendered as an Eastern Han tomb mural from Sichuan, warm red and ochre lines on pale plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.liu-bei-shu-hanzhong.2: 214, Luo near Chengdu: a long siege of a walled town on the plain, the army camped around it in earthworks. Assault troops with ladders and shields advance on the walls under a light rain of arrows; a mounted commander at their head is about to fall, shown only from a great distance. Defenders on the battlements. Smoke, overcast sky. No blood, no bodies, figures small. No stirrups. Rendered as an Eastern Han tomb mural from Sichuan, warm red and ochre lines on pale plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.liu-bei-shu-hanzhong.3: 214, Jiangzhou (Chongqing): a city on a rocky promontory where two rivers meet, with war boats along the Yangzi below. In a courtyard inside the captured walls, a big general in armour stands with sword lowered before an old white-bearded general who stands upright and refuses to kneel; the big general then steps forward to untie his bonds, soldiers looking on. Mid-distance view, no close-up faces. No stirrups. Rendered as an Eastern Han tomb mural from Sichuan, warm red and ochre lines on pale plaster. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.liu-bei-shu-hanzhong.7: Spring 219, Hanzhong: steep mountain passes with forts on the ridges held by troops under banners; below, along the narrow valley road, a huge army with carts and pack animals turns back and winds north out of the basin toward the Qinling mountains. Spring blossoms, river in the valley floor. Small figures, no gore, seen from a distance. No stirrups. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing of a long retreating column, strong diagonal composition, grey ink. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.yiling.1: Winter 219, the middle Yangzi: at night, a convoy of merchant boats with covered cargo holds glides along the river; men in white merchant robes row, while armoured soldiers hide beneath the matting. Ahead, small beacon watchtowers on the riverbank are quietly taken by men climbing up from the boats; the beacons stay dark. A walled river town in the distance, lights in its windows. Seen from far above, small figures only, no violence shown. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine line, ink and grey-blue washes on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.yiling.2: Winter 219, Maicheng: a small walled fort on a hill in bleak winter countryside; soldiers slip out of its gates in ones and twos and drift away along the roads. At dawn a small band of riders leaves by a side gate heading west into wooded hills, where ambushers lie hidden among the trees. Snow on the ground, grey sky. No capture or execution shown, no blood. Figures small. No stirrups. Rendered in Han pictorial brick relief style from Sichuan tombs, warm grey clay texture with ink-rubbing tones and touches of red. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.yiling.4: 221, the Three Gorges: a great Shu army descends the Yangzi through towering gorges, war boats and supply rafts on the river, infantry columns along cliff paths with banners. At the mouth of the gorges, a walled riverside town at Zigui is being occupied, and a defeated vanguard falls back downstream. Steep cliffs, mist, swirling water. Small figures, no gore. Rendered in Han pictorial brick relief style from Sichuan tombs, warm grey clay texture with ink-rubbing tones and touches of red. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.yiling.5: 222, Yiling in the Yangzi gorges: summer heat; dozens of wooden palisade camps strung out in a long line along wooded hillsides on the north bank of the river, tents among the trees, smoke from cooking fires. On the far plain downstream, a smaller army sits quietly behind its fortifications, waiting. Hazy heat, still air, dense forest. No battle shown, no fire yet. Small figures. Painted in the style of a late Han tomb mural, ochre and green on grey plaster, rhythmic repeated tents and mountains, no close figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.three-kingdoms-to-jin.2: 263, the Yinping mountains: a small army cuts its way through wild, empty mountains; soldiers hack a track along cliffs, build plank walkways over gorges, and at a steep drop the men wrap themselves in felt blankets and roll down the slope. Far below, the fortified town of Jiangyou on a green plain. Ragged clouds, pine forests. Small figures, seen from a distance. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and mineral colour on aged silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.three-kingdoms-to-jin.6: 280, the Yangzi at Xiling Gorge: a great fleet of Jin warships with multi-storey cabins sails downriver. Ahead, huge rafts loaded with straw dummies of soldiers drift into the water, snagging iron spikes; on burning rafts, huge torches soaked in oil melt the iron chains stretched across the river, sparks and smoke rising. A walled city on the bank in the distance. Small figures, no bodies. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, fine continuous lines, soft mineral colour on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.zhuge-liang-north.2: 228, Mount Qi: a large Shu army emerges from narrow mountain valleys onto the open hills above the Wei River, columns of infantry with crossbows and banners winding down the slopes, ox-drawn supply carts behind. In the distance, the walled towns of Tianshui and the Wei valley, where riders gallop with news. A chancellor in a light carriage with a feather fan watches from a ridge, seen from behind. Spring green hills. Figures small, seen from behind. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale mineral colour on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.eastern-jin-gentlemen.0: Around 318, Xinting outside Jiankang: a pavilion on a riverside hill, gentlemen in loose wide-sleeved robes and gauze caps sit on mats drinking wine from lacquer cups, some weeping into their sleeves. One man stands up and gestures firmly northward, rebuking them. The Yangtze, green hills and the walls of Jiankang in the distance, spring willows. Figures small, no close-up faces. No chairs, no tiled pagodas. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, fine gossamer lines, pale greens and ochres on aged silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.eastern-jin-gentlemen.2: 360, the Eastern Hills of Kuaiji: a mountain retreat among bamboo and pines, with a simple thatched villa; a gentleman in his forties in wide-sleeved robes leaves it, walking down a path toward a carriage and an official escort waiting below, while friends and singing girls watch from the terrace. Misty peaks and a lake behind. Figures small, seen from behind. No chairs, no tiled pagodas. Painted as a Gu Kaizhi-style handscroll, fine continuous gossamer line, delicate colour on aged silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.eastern-jin-gentlemen.4: 383, Jiankang: a quiet garden pavilion; two gentlemen in wide-sleeved robes kneel on mats facing each other over a weiqi board of black and white stones. A messenger in travel dress kneels at the pavilion edge, having handed over a letter, which one player has set aside without looking up, hand poised over the board. Attendants with an incense burner nearby, a bamboo garden outside. Mid-distance view, no close-up faces, no legible text. Painted as a Gu Kaizhi-style handscroll, fine continuous gossamer line, delicate colour on aged silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.eastern-jin-northern-campaigns.1: 354, the Wei valley near Lantian: an Eastern Jin army that has come through the Wu Pass marches out of mountain gorges onto the open loess plain, infantry in lamellar armour and archers advancing under banners while the enemy line in the distance gives way. Elders of the local villages line the road with food and wine to welcome them. Autumn light, the Qinling ridges behind. Small figures, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.eastern-jin-northern-campaigns.6: 416, Luoyang: an army arrives before the ruined but still vast walls of the old capital in late autumn; the gates open, and officials of Later Qin come out to surrender, bowing beside the road. Jin infantry and cavalry with banners file in, boats on the Luo River behind. Ruined palace terraces, bare trees. Distant view, no gore. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine line, ink and ochre on aged silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.fei-river.4: 383, the Huai plains: an enormous army of Former Qin marches south in a column stretching to the horizon, cavalry, infantry and supply carts kicking up dust, barbarian and Chinese soldiers mixed under many banners. In the foreground a small band of light cavalry gallops ahead of the main army along a road toward a walled town on the river. Late autumn, wide flat landscape. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and pale colour on aged silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.faxian.1: 400, Zhangye in the Hexi Corridor: a small Buddhist monastery of mud-brick walls and timber halls in a green oasis, snow-capped Qilian mountains behind. A group of shaven-headed monks in patched kasaya robes sit in meditation rows in a courtyard during the summer retreat, while new arrivals with walking staffs and bundles are greeted at the gate by fellow monks. Poplars, irrigated fields. Small figures. Painted in the style of an early Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, malachite green and lapis blue, flaking pigment texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.faxian.2: 400, Dunhuang: at the edge of the oasis town, a party of monks in patched robes is loaded with water skins and food by servants of the governor, camels and donkeys kneeling. Beyond lies the empty white desert of the Lop Nur road, no birds, no animals, only a faint track marked by scattered sun-bleached stones, the horizon shimmering. Tiny figures setting out. No bones or bodies shown. Painted in the style of an early Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, malachite green and lapis blue, flaking pigment texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.faxian.3: 401, Khotan: a grand Buddhist procession in a broad street of a mud-brick oasis city; a tall four-wheeled image cart, decorated like a moving hall with silk banners and canopies, carries Buddha images, pulled by crowds. Monks in robes walk in rows, the king in a belted robe walks barefoot behind with flowers, women scatter blossoms from balconies. Stupas and monasteries beyond, poplars and mountains. Small figures. Painted in the style of an early Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, malachite green and lapis blue, flaking pigment texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.faxian.4: 402, the Pamirs to the Indus: a narrow path cut into sheer rock cliffs high above a roaring gorge; a few monks in robes with staffs edge along a ledge, then cross a sagging rope bridge over the river far below. Snow peaks all around, swirling clouds. Tiny figures, vast mountains. Painted in the style of an early Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, malachite green and lapis blue, flaking pigment texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.faxian.5: About 405, Pataliputra: a monastery courtyard in the old Mauryan city, brick halls and a stupa, palm and banyan trees. Under a veranda, a lone Chinese monk in a patched robe sits on a mat copying texts onto palm leaves with a stylus, beside Indian monks in saffron robes who recite. Hot afternoon light, the Ganges plain beyond. Small figures, seen from a distance. No legible text, no domes or minarets. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and blue-green washes on aged silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.faxian.6: About 410, Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka: a vast white stupa rises above palm groves; in the great temple hall before a large jade-green stone Buddha image, a merchant kneels and offers a white silk fan. Off to one side an elderly Chinese monk in a patched robe, seen from behind, turns away overcome, wiping his eyes with his sleeve. Monks in saffron robes, frangipani trees. Small figures. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and blue-green washes on aged silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.faxian.7: 412, the South China Sea: a large merchant ship with mat sails and a high stern is tossed in a storm on huge dark waves under lightning; sailors fight the rigging and throw cargo overboard. In the background, distant palm-fringed island coasts of Java appear briefly in the gloom. A small figure of a monk clings to the mast clutching a bundle of scriptures. Tiny figures, vast sea. Painted in the manner of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer line, ink and blue-green washes on aged silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.cave-temples-road.1: 420, Binglingsi on the Yellow River: a huge natural cave high in a red sandstone cliff above the river, reached by wooden ladders and plank walkways; inside, painters on scaffolds paint a Buddha and attendants on the wall beside a clay statue, a donor kneels with incense while a scribe brushes a column of characters shown as unreadable marks, no legible text. Below, the Yellow River gorge and jagged peaks. Small figures. Painted in the style of an early Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, mineral greens and blues, rough flaking pigment texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.cave-temples-road.3: 500, Longmen near Luoyang: the limestone cliffs on the west bank of the Yi River, where stone carvers on bamboo scaffolding cut a large cave; inside, a seated Buddha with slender body and layered Chinese-style robes falling in pleated folds is emerging from the rock. Court officials and monks in long robes watch from the riverbank, carts of chips hauled away. Green hills, the river below. Small figures, no legible text. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei cave mural, mineral blues, greens and ochre, flat stylised figures with flaking pigment. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.cave-temples-road.4: 538, Mogao near Dunhuang: inside a square cave chamber lit by oil lamps, painters on low scaffolds paint the ceiling and walls: Indian-style gods of sun and moon, flying celestials, and slender Buddhist figures in flowing Chinese robes, against a blue and ochre ground. A painter brushes a short dedication panel shown as unreadable marks, no legible text. Through the cave mouth, sand dunes and poplars. Small figures, seen from behind. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei cave mural, mineral blues, greens and ochre, flat stylised figures with flaking pigment. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.cave-temples-road.5: 540, Maijishan near Tianshui: a dome-shaped rock peak rising out of forested green hills, its sheer cliff face honeycombed with caves and connected by plank walkways. A small funeral procession of monks and mourners in white climbs the zigzag walkways to a newly cut niche high on the cliff, where workers seal the entrance. Mist drifting through the pines. Tiny figures, no coffins opened, no bodies. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei cave mural, mineral blues, greens and ochre, flat stylised figures with flaking pigment. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.cave-temples-road.6: About 555, Xiangtang Shan on Mount Gu: a rocky hillside beside a road where columns of stone carvers work inside caves; a fuller, rounder Buddha figure with smooth thin robes sits in a niche, while masons carve dense columns of sutra text on the cliff, shown only as faint unreadable textured rows, no legible text. Outside, a Northern Qi courtly procession with carriages and horsemen passes on the road between Ye and Jinyang. Dry yellow hills, clear sky. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi cave mural, mineral blues, greens and ochre, flat stylised figures with flaking pigment. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.northern-wei-unifies-north.2: 397, Zhongshan on the Hebei plain: Tuoba cavalry pour out of the Taihang passes in long columns, riders in fur-trimmed caps and armour with lances, onto the flat farmland toward a walled city whose gates stand open as officials come out to submit. Armoured horses and banners, autumn dust. Small figures, no gore and no prisoners shown. Painted in the manner of a Northern Wei lacquer screen panel, black ground with cinnabar, yellow and white figures in fine line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sui-unification.4: Winter 588, the Yangtze: along the north bank of the great river, vast Sui armies gather at many points, armoured cavalry and infantry under banners, and large war boats with multiple decks lined up along the shore, sails furled. A prince's command tent with pennants sits on a rise. Across the wide grey river, the southern shore with its watchtowers is faint in mist. Seen from high above, many small figures, overcast morning. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, faded lapis and malachite, ochre ground. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sui-unification.5: Early 589, Caishi on the Yangtze: at night boats carry soldiers across the wide river under a crescent moon, landing on a rocky cliff shore below sleeping watchtowers; on the far horizon, another column marches toward the walled city of Jiankang from the east. Torches are dimmed, oars muffled. Small figures, no violence shown. Painted in the style of a Sui dynasty cave mural from Dunhuang, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sui-unification.7: 589, Jiankang: the walls and palaces of the southern capital are being torn down; workers pull down timber halls with ropes, fields are ploughed over inside the old city, and long columns of carts and captive officials file north along the road. Smoke and dust over the Yangtze, the green Zhongshan hills behind. Small figures, no violence. Painted in the style of a Sui dynasty cave mural from Dunhuang, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, many small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sui-reforms.5: 587, Daxing (Chang'an): in the courtyard of a government office, candidates from the prefectures in plain robes and caps line up before officials seated behind low tables, handing over scrolls of recommendation shown as blank pale sheets, no legible text. Carriages and travelling servants wait by the gate; through it, the new grid streets and tiled roofs of the capital. Mixed ages of candidates, clear daylight. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Sui-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, lively small figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sui-reforms.8: 618, Chang'an: in a great palace hall with red columns and a tiled roof, officials of the new Tang court in round-collared robes and black gauze hats sit at low tables, working through stacks of Sui registers and law scrolls carried in by clerks, the written pages shown only as blank pale sheets. Through the open doors, the palace courtyard and the city. Mid-distance, no close-up faces. Painted in Tang court painting style, fine line, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sui-grand-canal.2: 605, Shanyang (Huai'an): a wide straight channel being dug across flat wet land, thousands of labourers in hemp clothes with spades and baskets on carrying poles, digging and carrying earth in endless rows; overseers in round-collared robes stand on embankments. Willows, small boats waiting at the Huai end, the walled town in the distance. Hazy morning light. Painted in the style of a Sui-Tang Dunhuang mural, mineral greens and ochres, many tiny figures in rhythmic rows. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sui-grand-canal.3: Autumn 605, the Grand Canal near Jiangdu: an immense imperial flotilla sails down the canal, led by a towering four-storey dragon boat with red pillars and gilded dragon prow, followed by hundreds of smaller boats stretching to the horizon; teams of haulers in green on the towpaths pull with ropes, mounted guards ride along the banks. Willows line the canal. Hazy autumn light, vast scale, small figures. Painted in the style of a Sui blue-green landscape in the manner of Zhan Ziqian, fine line, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sui-grand-canal.5: 610, Yuhang (Hangzhou): the southern terminus of the canal, a busy harbour where the new canal meets a lake and river, with green hills around. Grain barges and passenger boats are loaded at stone embankments; warehouses and a small walled town with tiled roofs. The canal stretches away north in a straight line through rice paddies. Small figures, clear morning light. Painted in the style of a Sui blue-green landscape in the manner of Zhan Ziqian, fine line, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.sui-collapse.7: Spring 618, Jiangdu: a palace on the canal at night; soldiers of the guard with torches pour through the gates and across courtyards, attendants flee down corridors, and lamps are knocked over. In the middle distance, a small group of armed men surround a pavilion; nothing more is shown. The canal and boats glint in moonlight beyond the walls. Small figures, no bodies, no blood. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.xuanzang.1: 629, the Mokhayan desert beyond Yumen: a lone monk in a travel robe with a wooden backpack frame and a thin old red horse crosses endless gravel desert under a burning sky; behind him, tiny beacon towers on the horizon. His water skin lies spilled on the ground; heat haze and mirages shimmer. Tiny figure, vast emptiness, no bones or bodies. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, flaking pigment texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.xuanzang.2: 630, Gaochang (Turfan): inside a mud-brick palace hall with carpets and Buddhist banners, a monk sits motionless in meditation on a mat, refusing food set before him on a low table, while a king in a Central Asian robe kneels beside him pleading, courtiers watching. Through the doors, the oasis city walls, vineyards and the Flaming Mountains. Mid-distance view, no close-up faces. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, flaking pigment texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.xuanzang.3: 630, near Suyab in the Chu valley: a great Western Turk encampment of felt tents on green pasture, the khagan's large tent hung with gold ornaments. The khagan in green silk with his long hair bound, surrounded by hundreds of mounted warriors in braids and felt coats, greets a Chinese monk in robes. Snowy Tian Shan peaks behind, herds of horses. Small figures, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, flaking pigment texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.xuanzang.4: 631, Nalanda: the vast red brick monastery-university of Nalanda, with multi-storey monastic blocks, temples and a tall stupa, lotus ponds in between. Hundreds of monks in saffron robes sit in groups debating and studying palm-leaf manuscripts in courtyards; in one corner, an aged abbot teaches a Chinese monk in grey robes, seen from behind. Palms and mango trees. Small figures, no legible text, no domes or minarets. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, flaking pigment texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.xuanzang.5: 642, Kanyakubja on the Ganges: a great assembly under a vast pavilion and canopies by the river, a tall temple tower beside it, kings, Brahmins and monks seated in rows. A Chinese monk sits on a high dais expounding; a king in Indian royal dress and jewelled crown stands beside it with a parasol. Crowds, war elephants with howdahs, banners. Small figures, no domes or minarets. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, flaking pigment texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.xuanzang.6: 644, Khotan: a Chinese monk waits in a monastery guesthouse in the oasis city; in the courtyard his pack elephants and horses laden with sutras and images rest, while he watches a messenger ride off east across the desert road with a letter. Poplars, mulberry orchards, stupas and the white Kunlun range beyond. Small figures, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, flaking pigment texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.xuanzang.7: 645, Chang'an: through the wide avenues of the Tang capital, a great procession carries hundreds of sutra bundles and Buddha images on carts and litters, monks chanting; dense crowds line the streets and roofs, incense smoke rising. A monk walks humbly in the middle. The walls, gate towers and tiled roofs of the city. Small figures, festive spring light. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, flaking pigment texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.wencheng-tibet.0: 640, Chang'an: in a Tang palace courtyard with red columns, a Tibetan envoy in a red-trimmed robe and braided hair, followed by attendants carrying gold vessels and chests, bows before the emperor seated under a canopy on a raised hall, flanked by court officials in round-collared robes and black hats and ladies holding fans. Mid-distance view, no close-up faces. Painted in Tang court painting style in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral blues and greens on silk, fine line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.wencheng-tibet.1: Early 641, the road west of Chang'an: a long bridal procession winds through the loess hills of Longyou toward a frontier town; ox carts and covered carriages, riders with banners, a guard of armoured cavalry led by a prince, and camels laden with silks and books. Snow lingers on the hilltops. Small figures, seen from a distance. Painted in Tang court painting style in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral blues and greens on silk, fine line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.wencheng-tibet.2: 641, the Red Ridge (Riyue Shan): a pass between green farmland on one side and vast high grassland on the other; the bridal party pauses at the summit, where a lady in Tang dress stands by her carriage, seen from behind, looking back east. A fallen round mirror glints on the ground. Yak herds on the pasture beyond. Small figures. Painted in Tang court painting style in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral blues and greens on silk, fine line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.wencheng-tibet.3: 641, Madoi near the source of the Yellow River: a vast high-altitude plain of lakes and grassland; a Tibetan king and his troops in braids and fur-trimmed robes, mounted on horses with banners, meet the Tang bridal party. The king bows respectfully to the Tang prince, who leads the escort. Black yak-hair tents, snowy mountains beyond. Small figures. Painted in Tang court painting style in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral blues and greens on silk, fine line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.wencheng-tibet.5: 680, Lhasa: the Lhasa valley with a modest early fortress on the Red Hill and the Jokhang temple of stone and timber below; monks and townspeople in Tibetan robes gather with butter lamps and offerings outside the temple in mourning. On the road, Tang envoys and a yak caravan with goods arrive. Snowy peaks around, clear thin light. Not the later great white-and-red Potala palace, no prayer flags. Small figures, seen from a distance. Painted in Tang court painting style in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral blues and greens on silk, fine line. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.tang-western-regions.3: 692, Kucha: a Tang army victoriously returns to the oasis garrison city of Kucha, armoured cavalry and infantry with red banners entering through the gates of mud-brick walls; local people in Central Asian dress watch and musicians play. A large fortified military camp sits outside the walls. Snowy Tianshan behind, poplars and irrigation channels. Small figures, dramatic scale. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Zhaodao's Emperor Minghuang's Journey to Shu, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.tang-western-regions.5: 750, Chach (Tashkent): a Tang army camped around a mud-brick walled city in a green oasis; soldiers carry loot from the gates, and a captured king in a Sogdian robe is led away under guard on horseback. Off to the side, a young prince on a fast horse slips away into the hills to the west. Dust, harsh late light. Small figures, no gore. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Zhaodao's Emperor Minghuang's Journey to Shu, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.tang-western-regions.7: 751, Samarkand: in a workshop courtyard of a walled Sogdian city, captive Chinese craftsmen in Tang round-collared robes soak and pound fibres in vats, lift wet sheets of paper on bamboo screens and lay them to dry on walls in the sun, watched by Arab and Sogdian officials in robes and turbans. Mud-brick buildings, a citadel beyond. Small figures, harsh light. No minarets, no legible text. Painted in the style of a Dunhuang cave mural, mineral greens, ochre and faded red, flaking plaster texture. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.wu-zetian.0: 649, Ganye convent in Chang'an: a quiet Buddhist nunnery with tiled halls and a pagoda behind walls; a young nun with shaven head in grey robes stands in the courtyard among other nuns. At the gate, an imperial retinue arrives, a young emperor in yellow robes and black hat stepping from a carriage, attendants carrying incense. Willows and cherry blossoms. Small figures, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Zhang Xuan, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.wu-zetian.6: 698, Luoyang: in a palace hall with red columns, an old empress in imperial robes sits on a dais while an elderly minister in purple robes and black hat kneels before her, gesturing earnestly; court ladies and eunuchs stand by. Through the open hall doors, a carriage waits in the courtyard as if ready to recall someone. Mid-distance view, no close-up faces. Daylight, calm. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.wu-zetian.8: 706, Qianling northwest of Chang'an: a mountain tomb with a long spirit road flanked by stone figures of horses, winged horses and officials; a funeral procession with banners, carriages and many mourners in white moves up the road toward the mountain. On one side stands a tall stone stele with a blank face and no inscription. Loess hills, autumn light. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.tang-and-tibet.0: 663, Kokonor (Qinghai Lake): a vast blue lake surrounded by grassland and snow peaks; a Tibetan army of horsemen in leather armour and fur-trimmed robes sweeps across the plain, and the Tuyuhun people flee with their herds and felt tents toward the east. Many small figures, no gore. Black yak-hair tents of the Tibetans dot the far slopes. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, lapis, malachite and ochre. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.li-bai-travels.0: 701, Suyab on the Chu river: a Tang garrison town of mud-brick walls in a green valley below the snowy Tianshan; inside, a family courtyard house where a baby is presented to a merchant father in a Tang robe, Sogdian traders with camels in the street outside. Poplars, irrigation channels. Small figures, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.li-bai-travels.1: 705, Changlong in Mianzhou, Sichuan: a village among green hills and bamboo; a boy in a short robe practises swordplay in a courtyard, then climbs a mountain path to a thatched hut where a Daoist hermit sits among cranes and pines. Misty peaks, waterfalls, terraced fields. Small figures, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.li-bai-travels.2: 725, the Three Gorges to Jiangling: a small boat shoots down the rushing Yangzi between towering cliffs, a young man in a white robe standing at the bow. At the riverbank town of Jiangling, an elderly Daoist master in a feathered robe greets the young traveller on a stone landing. Gibbons in the cliffs, morning mist. Small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.li-bai-travels.3: 726, Yangzhou: a bustling canal city of tiled roofs, bridges and wine shops lit by lanterns; a young man in a white robe stands on a pavilion terrace pouring wine and handing over strings of coins to a group of poor scholars, while singing girls play music. Boats on the canal and the Yangzi beyond. Small figures, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.li-bai-travels.4: 742, Chang'an: the Hanlin Academy courtyard in the palace, under flowering peonies; a poet in a white robe stands with brush raised before a low table, other scholars around him; an elderly official raises a wine cup in praise. The emperor watches from a raised hall in the background. Mid-distance view, no close-up faces, no legible text. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.li-bai-travels.7: 759, Baidicheng: at dawn a small boat races down the Yangzi from the white walls of a hilltop town above the gorge, sails full and oarsmen pulling; a poet in a robe sits in the bow, looking back at the rising sun on the white town. Rose clouds, gibbons on the cliffs, rushing water. Distant panoramic view, small figures. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.li-bai-travels.8: 762, Dangtu: a magistrate's courtyard house on the bank of the Yangzi in late autumn; an old man in a robe lies in a pavilion, while a younger official at a low table gathers stacks of scrolls; servants carry in medicine. The river with boats and green mountains beyond, a full moon rising. Distant panoramic view, small figures, no legible text. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.du-fu-life.0: 712, Gong county near Luoyang: a gentry family compound of tiled halls in loess hills by the Luo River; in the courtyard, relatives gather around a nurse holding a newborn; ancestors' scrolls and books hang in a study. Elm and jujube trees, cave dwellings in the loess cliffs nearby. Small figures, seen from a distance, warm spring light. No legible text. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.du-fu-life.1: 746, Chang'an: a thin scholar in a worn robe stands at the gate of a grand mansion, holding a scroll of poems, while gatekeepers turn him away; behind him, a busy avenue with carriages of the wealthy and finely dressed riders. Tiled roofs and the palace towers beyond. Winter light. Small figures, seen from a distance. No legible text. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.du-fu-life.2: Late 755, Lishan: a frozen road at the foot of Mount Li; on the hillside above, the imperial hot spring palace glows with lanterns, steam rising, music drifting out. On the road below, a thin traveller in a worn robe trudges through snow past huddled poor people by the roadside. Bare trees, dark winter evening. Small figures, no bodies, no gore. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.du-fu-life.3: 757, Chang'an: spring in the occupied capital; a lone scholar stands on a broken wall, looking at overgrown streets, tall grass, and flowering trees among abandoned houses. Rebel soldiers patrol in the distance; smoke on the horizon. Birds in the sky. Small figures, seen from behind, melancholy. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.du-fu-life.4: 757, Fengxiang: the temporary court camp of the new emperor, tents and wooden halls on a loess plain with banners; a ragged traveller in hemp sandals and torn robes arrives at the gate and bows, officials receiving him. Soldiers drilling, horses tethered, autumn dust over the bare fields. Small figures, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Tang court painting, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.du-fu-life.5: 759, the road to Qinzhou and Tonggu: a scholar with his family and a few bundles trudges through bare autumn mountains on a narrow path, a child on a donkey; in a valley below, a few thatched huts and people digging for wild roots in the snow. Grey sky, cold wind. Small figures, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.du-fu-life.6: 760, Chengdu: a thatched cottage beside the Huanhua stream among bamboo and plum trees, with a small garden; a scholar stands in the garden looking up as autumn wind tears the thatch from his roof, while children run off with straw. Rain clouds, distant city walls. Small figures, seen from a distance. Painted in the style of a Tang blue-green landscape in the manner of Li Sixun, mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.du-fu-life.7: 766, Kuizhou at the head of the Three Gorges: on a high terrace above the walled town, a gaunt elderly poet in a plain Tang round-collared robe and soft black cap stands seen from behind, leaning on a staff, looking down at the Yangzi rushing into the dark cliffs of Qutang Gorge; autumn wind, falling leaves, wild geese and gibbons on the cliffs, small boats far below, Baidi city on its hill. Tang dress and timber architecture only, no Ming-style buildings, no legible text. Painted as a Tang-style blue-green landscape on silk, ink and mineral colour, figure tiny. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.du-fu-life.8: 770, the Xiang River between Tanzhou and Yuezhou: a small, worn wooden boat with a reed-mat cabin drifts on a wide grey winter river, a few family members in plain Tang clothing tending a brazier at the stern, the old poet only suggested lying under a quilt inside the shadowed cabin, not visible; bare reeds, snow on the far hills, a single crane overhead, cold mist. Quiet, mournful, no bodies shown. Painted as a Tang-style ink landscape on silk, sparse wash and light colour, figures tiny and distant. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jianzhen.0: 742, Daming Temple in Yangzhou: in a Tang temple courtyard with a tall timber hall, bracketed eaves and a stone lantern, two young Japanese monks in dark travelling robes bow deeply before an elderly Chinese Vinaya master in ochre robes seated on the hall steps, seen from the side at a distance; disciples stand in rows under blossoming trees, a bronze incense burner smokes. Spring daylight, solemn mood, no legible text. Painted in the style of a Japanese Nara-period illustrated sutra or Kamakura emakimono of Ganjin's voyage, fine line, mineral colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jianzhen.1: 744, the sea off Mingzhou (Ningbo): a Tang wooden ship with matting sails is driven onto black rocks by a storm among small islands, its mast cracked, monks in robes and sailors clinging to ropes and wading through surf to a stony shore with bundles of sutras; huge curling waves, dark low clouds, rain. All figures small and distant, no bodies, no gore. Painted in the style of a Kamakura emakimono of Ganjin's voyage, fine line, mineral colours, stylised waves. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jianzhen.2: 748, Zhenzhou at the southern tip of Hainan: after fourteen days adrift, a battered Tang sailing ship with torn matting sails lies beached in a turquoise bay; weary monks in robes carry sutra boxes across white sand, while local Li people in wrapped cloth and a few Tang officials come down through coconut palms to meet them. Bright tropical sun, green hills behind, figures small. Painted in the style of a Japanese Nara-period illustrated sutra or Kamakura emakimono, fine line, mineral colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jianzhen.3: 750, the road north through Guangxi toward Guangzhou: a small party of monks in dusty robes and straw sandals walks a narrow path between steep green karst peaks and rice fields, an elderly monk in front led by the hand by a disciple, his eyes cloth-bound, others carrying sutra boxes and a parasol; a simple new grave mound with a wooden marker under a tree by the path. Hot humid haze, figures small, no legible text. Painted in the style of a Kamakura emakimono, fine line, mineral colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jianzhen.4: 753, Huangsipu near Suzhou: at grey dawn a small rowing boat slips out from a reedy creek mouth toward a large Japanese embassy ship riding at anchor on the broad estuary, its hull painted, matting sails half raised; an old blind monk sits in the boat supported by two disciples, and Japanese envoys in Nara court robes and black caps wait at the ship's rail. Mist, calm water, distant flat shore. Figures small, no legible text. Painted in the style of a Kamakura emakimono of Ganjin's voyage, fine line, mineral colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jianzhen.6: 754, Todaiji in Nara: before the colossal timber Great Buddha Hall with its sweeping hipped roof and red columns, a raised square earthen ordination platform stands in the courtyard; an elderly monk in Tang robes presides from it while a retired emperor in plain monk's robes and kneeling courtiers and nuns receive the precepts, rows of Japanese monks in dark robes watching. Spring, cherry blossoms, incense smoke. Nara-period architecture only, figures small. Painted as a Kamakura-period emakimono, fine line and mineral colours on paper. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.jianzhen.7: 759, Toshodaiji in Nara: carpenters raise the timber frame of a new Tang-style golden hall with a broad colonnade and deep bracketed eaves, while in a nearby lecture hall monks study; in a garden plot disciples dry medicinal herbs on mats, and an elderly blind master in robes sits on a veranda, seen from behind, listening. Pines, autumn sunlight. No later pagodas, Nara-period dress only, no legible text. Painted in the style of a Japanese Nara-period illustrated sutra or Kamakura emakimono, fine line, mineral colours. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.huang-chao.1: 878, the hills of eastern Hubei after the defeat at Huangmei: ragged columns of rebel soldiers in mixed leather armour and peasant clothes trudge across a valley under torn banners, joining a large camp of tents and carts on a river plain where new banners are being raised; a mounted leader in a red cloak is seen from far behind at the camp gate. Overcast spring, smoke from cooking fires, figures small, no gore. Painted as a late Tang ink-and-colour handscroll on silk, mineral greens, figures small and distant. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.huang-chao.3: 880, Caishi on the Yangtze: a rebel army crosses the wide river in hundreds of commandeered boats and rafts below the steep wooded rock of Caishi, horses swimming beside the boats, banners crowding the decks, while Tang watchtowers on the far bank stand abandoned; misty green hills of the south behind. Autumn, choppy brown water, figures tiny and distant, no gore. Painted as a late Tang ink-and-colour handscroll on silk, mineral greens. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.huang-chao.5: 882, Tongzhou near the great bend of the Yellow River: through the opened gate of a walled town, a rebel commander with a small mounted escort rides out under a lowered banner toward a Tang army camp on the plain, where officers in lamellar armour and red robes wait in a line to receive his surrender; loess terraces and the river beyond. Autumn, pale light, figures small, no gore. Painted in late Tang court style, ink and mineral colours on silk, panoramic composition. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.ten-kingdoms.0: 907, Guangling (Yangzhou), seat of the Wu state: soldiers in lamellar armour drill on the rammed-earth walls of a canal city while salt barges and grain boats crowd the Grand Canal below; envoys' boats with different banners from rival southern courts moor at a wharf, and across the misty Huai plain watchtowers mark an armed frontier. Late summer haze, many small figures. Painted in the style of a Five Dynasties handscroll, fine line, ink and light colour on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.rise-of-khitan.0: 907, the Xar Moron river valley: beside felt tents and grazing horses, Han Chinese refugees in plain hemp clothing build rammed-earth walls of a new village, plough strips of land with oxen and set up a small smithy, while a troop of Khitan horsemen with shaved crowns and side locks, in left-closing robes and boots, watch from the riverbank. Wide steppe sky, early summer. Painted in the style of Hu Gui's Khitan horsemen paintings, ink and colour on silk, fine detailed figures. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.bianjing-prosperity.0: 960, Kaifeng: a high bird's-eye view of a great walled city spread across a flat plain with no hills anywhere on the horizon; the Bian canal runs in from the southeast through a water gate, crowded with grain barges, and the palace roofs rise at the centre amid dense wards. Early Song timber and rammed-earth architecture, no Ming brick gates. Clear spring morning, tiny figures. Painted as a Northern Song court genre painting, fine line and mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.bianjing-prosperity.1: 976, Luoyang: from a terrace of the old palace, an emperor in a yellow robe and his brother in a purple robe, both seen from behind with attendants, gaze across the ruined capital toward the wooded Mang hills and the twin cliffs of the Yi Que gorge; courtiers in black caps stand in a cluster, one gesturing back to the east. Late spring, peonies in bloom below. Figures small, no faces. Painted as a Northern Song court genre painting, fine line and mineral colours on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.bianjing-prosperity.2: About 1007, Sizhou where the Bian canal leaves the Huai River: long convoys of flat grain barges with matting sails and lowered masts queue at a lock gate, teams of trackers haul them on towpaths, clerks with scales check sacks of rice at a waterside granary; the broad Huai and the pagoda of Sizhou behind. Bright autumn day, many tiny figures. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, fine line, ink and light colour on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
tour.bianjing-prosperity.6: Early 1100s, Kaifeng: the night market by Zhou Bridge, lanes lined with open-fronted shops and food stalls lit by paper lanterns, cooks at steaming woks, crowds of townspeople in Song dress, a timber bridge over the Bian canal; beyond the rooftops the great halls of Daxiangguo Temple loom in the dark. Late night, warm lantern glow, many small figures. No ward walls, no legible signboards. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, fine line, ink and light colour on silk. One single unified scene, no panels or insets.
